editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination: the negation-sensitive lines survive intact ("jika batasan coupling map tidak terpenuhi, jalur swap yang sesuai diidentifikasi"), the TransformationPass/AnalysisPass contrast keeps the "hanya dimaksudkan untuk mengekstrak informasi" restriction, and the layer definition keeps the "set qubit yang terpisah sehingga bisa dieksekusi secara independen" justification. Two editor-level slips: (1) the file consistently keeps "Circuit" capitalized in English, but one sentence near the dag_to_circuit section switches to "Sebuah sirkuit diambil" — the same concept under two spellings inside one paragraph pair; (2) "Membuat dan mentranspilasi terhadap Backend kustom" is a word-for-word calque of English "transpile against", where Indonesian would use "untuk" ("mentranspilasi untuk Backend kustom"). Neither misleads a learner; terminology (qubit, Gate, coupling map, transpiler pass, subcircuit, sub-DAG, node/simpul) is otherwise correct and stable.

examples.suggested: Sebuah Circuit diambil, diproses dalam bentuk DAG, dan Circuit yang sudah ditransformasi dihasilkan sebagai output.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries are the two sub-headings under "Menghapus akses functions": "Catalog Functions" → "Fungsi Katalog" (line 497) and "Custom Functions" → "Fungsi Kustom" (line 526). Neither misleads — the renderings are transparent and the anchors are untouched — but they are inconsistent with the rest of the page, which keeps these two product names in English everywhere else, including in the very next sentence under each heading ("Untuk menghapus Catalog Functions dari sebuah instance…", "Untuk menghapus Custom Functions dari sebuah instance…") and in Step 4 ("memberikan akses ke Catalog Functions dan Custom Functions", line 412). Since these are Qiskit Functions product/feature names tied to the `functions` and `custom_functions` JSON keys, the file should pick one convention; the surrounding prose already picked English, so the headings are the outliers. Also note line 524 mixes both registers in one sentence ("menghapus Catalog Functions") while line 553 lowercases it ("menghapus custom functions"), which the heading change now sits on top of.

examples.suggested: Catalog Functions {#catalog-functions}

A reader matching the heading to the prose and to the `functions` key sees two names for one feature. Not misleading, but a native technical editor would align them.

examples.suggested: Custom Functions {#custom-functions}

editor_note: No misleading drift or hallucination: every card description matches its English setup, and the register is consistently informal ("kamu", "Bangun…", "Kurangi…"). Three wording problems a native technical editor would fix: (1) in the Shaded lightcones card, "noise model terms" is rendered "istilah model noise" — "istilah" means *terminology/vocabulary*, while the mathematical sense here requires "suku (model noise)"; (2) "entangling gates" becomes "Gate yang saling mengait", which reads as gates hooked to each other rather than gates that entangle qubits (conventional: "gerbang/Gate yang membelitkan" or "…yang menimbulkan keterbelitan"); (3) "plug into a workflow to scale … new quantum algorithms" is softened to "untuk mengembangkan … algoritma kuantum baru", losing the specific sense of scaling up. Additionally the "Postselection with bit-flip checks" card description is still fully in English while every neighbouring card is translated, and "circuit" is rendered as lowercase "sirkuit" inside the Qiskit Fermions card but as "Circuit" everywhere else in the file.

examples.source: Reduce probabilistic error cancellation (PEC) sampling overhead by removing noise model terms that have low impact on the observable estimation.
examples.translation: Kurangi overhead sampling probabilistic error cancellation (PEC) dengan menghapus istilah model noise yang berdampak kecil pada estimasi observable.
examples.suggested: … dengan menghapus suku-suku model noise yang berdampak kecil pada estimasi observable.
examples.why: "istilah" is the false-friend rendering of "term" (vocabulary item). The mathematical term of a noise model is "suku"; as written the sentence reads as deleting naming/labels rather than terms of the model.

examples.source: Reduce the depth of transpiled circuits by decomposing entangling gates between non-adjacent qubits.
examples.translation: Kurangi kedalaman Circuit yang sudah ditranspilasi dengan menguraikan Gate yang saling mengait antara Qubit yang tidak berdekatan.
examples.suggested: … dengan menguraikan Gate yang membelitkan (entangling) Qubit yang tidak berdekatan.
examples.why: "saling mengait" (mutually hooked) suggests gates linked to one another; the English says the gates entangle non-adjacent qubits. Conventional Indonesian for entanglement is keterbelitan/membelitkan.

examples.source: can plug into a workflow to scale or design new quantum algorithms
examples.translation: bisa dipasang ke dalam sebuah alur kerja untuk mengembangkan atau merancang algoritma kuantum baru
examples.suggested: bisa dipasang ke dalam alur kerja untuk menskalakan atau merancang algoritma kuantum baru
examples.why: "to scale" (scale up to utility scale — the page's whole premise) is flattened to the generic "mengembangkan" (to develop), and it then duplicates "merancang".

examples.source: Filter out non-Markovian noise in sampled bitstrings by incorporating bit-flip checks into a circuit.
examples.translation: Filter out non-Markovian noise in sampled bitstrings by incorporating bit-flip checks into a circuit.
examples.suggested: Saring noise non-Markovian pada bitstring hasil sampling dengan menyisipkan pemeriksaan bit-flip ke dalam Circuit.
examples.why: This card description was left entirely untranslated while every other card on the page is in Indonesian; its linkText ("Read the documentation") and the Paulice card's ("Browse documentation") are also still English where the rest use "Jelajahi dokumentasi".

examples.suggested: struktur data untuk operator dan Circuit fermionik … sintesis Circuit
examples.why: Within-file inconsistency: "circuit" is kept as "Circuit" everywhere else (headings, AQC-Tensor, MPF, OBP, cutting, utilities) but appears as lowercase "sirkuit" twice in this one card.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the three `layout_mode` descriptions, the `replace_only_if_better=False` caveat, the "connected subgraph / raises a warning and leaves the sub-circuit unchanged" paragraph and the thread-pool default (jumlah core ditambah empat) all survive intact, and the informal "kamu" convention holds file-wide. Two drift-adjacent slips: the block-size limits are rendered "mendukung hingga sembilan blok qubit" / "hingga enam blok qubit", which in Indonesian word order reads as a cap on the NUMBER of blocks rather than on block size, while the very next bullet uses the correct shape "blok 65, 33, dan 27 qubit" — an internal inconsistency the reader must resolve from the following sentence about "ukuran blok"; and "We expect to gradually increase" is firmed up to "Kami berencana" (we plan to). Naturalness slips are the redundant "menghasilkan hasil yang lebih baik / lebih buruk" (twice), the calqued instantiation family "instantiasi / meng-instantiasi / di-instantiasi" and "men-sintesis ulang" with nonstandard hyphenation, and "`qiskit-ibm-transpiler` package" left in English word order where earlier in the file the same thing is correctly "paket `qiskit-ibm-transpiler`". None of these teaches a false concept, so this stays below FAIL.

examples.source: Currently up to nine qubit blocks. / Currently up to six qubit blocks.
examples.translation: Saat ini mendukung hingga sembilan blok qubit. / Saat ini mendukung hingga enam blok qubit.
examples.suggested: Saat ini mendukung blok hingga sembilan qubit. / ... blok hingga enam qubit.
examples.why: In Indonesian, numeral + classifier ('sembilan blok qubit') reads as nine blocks, not blocks of nine qubits, so the cap appears to be on block count rather than block size. The third bullet in the same list uses the correct shape ('blok 65, 33, dan 27 qubit'), making the list internally inconsistent.

examples.source: We expect to gradually increase the size of the supported blocks.
examples.translation: Kami berencana untuk secara bertahap meningkatkan ukuran blok yang didukung.
examples.suggested: Kami memperkirakan ukuran blok yang didukung akan bertambah secara bertahap.
examples.why: 'expect' (an expectation) is upgraded to 'berencana' (we plan to), turning a forecast into a commitment — a mild strengthening of a forward-looking claim.

examples.source: They often produce better results ... / It often produces worse results ...
examples.translation: Pass ini sering menghasilkan hasil yang lebih baik ... / Mode ini sering menghasilkan hasil yang lebih buruk ...
examples.suggested: sering memberikan hasil yang lebih baik / sering memberi hasil yang lebih buruk
examples.why: 'menghasilkan hasil' is a tautology no Indonesian technical writer would produce; it appears twice in the file.

examples.source: with the `max_threads` argument at pass instantiation ... all synthesis passes instantiated after that ... by re-synthesizing them
examples.translation: dengan argumen `max_threads` saat instantiasi pass ... semua pass sintesis yang di-instantiasi setelahnya ... dengan cara men-sintesis ulang
examples.suggested: saat pass dibuat (diinstansiasi) ... semua pass sintesis yang dibuat setelah itu ... dengan mensintesis ulang
examples.why: 'instantiasi / meng-instantiasi / di-instantiasi' is a raw calque of the English noun/verb, and 'men-sintesis' uses nonstandard hyphenation for a prefix that attaches directly ('mensintesis'); both read as machine output rather than native technical prose.

examples.source: If you use any AI-powered feature from the `qiskit-ibm-transpiler` package in your research

examples.suggested: Jika kamu menggunakan fitur berbasis AI apa pun dari paket `qiskit-ibm-transpiler` dalam penelitianmu
examples.why: English head-noun order ('`...` package') is kept even though line 38 of the same file already uses the correct Indonesian 'paket `qiskit-ibm-transpiler`'; the quantifier 'any' is also dropped.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the conditional final bullet ("Untuk Flex Plan, instans tidak bisa memproses job lebih lanjut kecuali batasnya sudah ditingkatkan, atau untuk Premium Plan, setelah jendela penggunaan berikutnya dimulai") keeps both plans' conditions correctly attributed, and the caveat "jika alokasi tidak ditetapkan sebagai batas, instans bisa menggunakan lebih dari jatah waktunya" survives intact. Three editor-level slips, none misleading: (1) the core noun "instance" is rendered "instans" everywhere except the "Set different values" section, where it flips to the untranslated "instance" three times in one paragraph; (2) second person alternates between "Anda" (paras 1 and 3) and "kamu" (line 18 and the whole "Set different values" paragraph) — both are acceptable informal register, but the switch mid-document is unedited; (3) the Next-steps link text "meminimalkan waktu kuantum job" adds "kuantum", a word absent from the English "minimize job usage", and narrows "usage" to "waktu". Terminology is otherwise correct and idiomatic (QPU, workload, job, antrean for queue, algoritma fair-share).

examples.source: When you set the allocation limit for an instance in IBM Quantum Platform, the same value is set as the instance's usage limit.
examples.translation: Saat kamu menetapkan batas alokasi untuk sebuah instance di IBM Quantum Platform, nilai yang sama ditetapkan sebagai batas penggunaan instance.
examples.suggested: Saat Anda menetapkan batas alokasi untuk sebuah instans di IBM Quantum Platform, nilai yang sama ditetapkan sebagai batas penggunaan instans tersebut.
examples.why: The rest of the file consistently uses "instans" (lines 10, 14, 18, 28); this paragraph alone leaves "instance" in English three times, so the same concept appears under two names within one short page. Not misleading, but an editor would unify it.

examples.source: You can optionally set the time allocation as a limit for the instance.
examples.translation: Kamu bisa secara opsional menetapkan alokasi waktu sebagai batas untuk instans.
examples.suggested: Anda bisa menetapkan alokasi waktu sebagai batas untuk instans (opsional).
examples.why: Paragraphs 1 and 3 address the reader as "Anda"; from line 18 onward it switches to "kamu" and never switches back. Also "secara opsional" is a stiff calque of the English adverb-fronted "can optionally" — Indonesian technical prose puts the option at the end instead.

examples.source: Review suggestions to [minimize job usage](minimize-time).
examples.translation: Tinjau saran untuk [meminimalkan waktu kuantum job.](minimize-time)
examples.suggested: Tinjau saran untuk [meminimalkan penggunaan job](minimize-time).
examples.why: "kuantum" is not in the English link text, and "usage" is narrowed to "waktu". Harmless in context because the target page is about run time, but it is an addition plus a narrowing rather than a translation of the source phrase.

editor_note: The single prose paragraph is faithful and idiomatic ("Tinjau peran yang tersedia dan tindakan yang dipetakan ke masing-masing peran untuk membantumu menetapkan akses"), the informal register ("membantumu", "milikmu") holds, and no semantic drift, dropped caveat or hallucination appears anywhere — every table row maps one-to-one onto its English counterpart with the right verb aspect (Cancel→Membatalkan, Run→Menjalankan, Delete→Menghapus, Update→Memperbarui). The one thing a native technical editor would change is the six rows where the API verb "List" is rendered "Mendaftar" ("Mendaftar Backend milikmu", "Mendaftar detail job", "Mendaftar log job", "Mendaftar hasil job", "Mendaftar job", "Mendaftar tag"): although KBBI allows mendaftar = "membuat daftar", in current usage it reads first as "to register / sign up", so a read-only GET endpoint momentarily looks like an enrolment action; "Menampilkan daftar …" or "Mencantumkan …" is the conventional rendering. It is also slightly inconsistent with the neighbouring row "Get list of backends → Mendapatkan daftar Backend", which uses the noun "daftar" correctly. The HTTP method shown in each row keeps this from actually misleading a learner, so it stays MINOR.

examples.source: List your backends (`GET /v1/backends`)
examples.translation: Mendaftar Backend milikmu (`GET /v1/backends`)
examples.suggested: Menampilkan daftar Backend milikmu (`GET /v1/backends`)
examples.why: "Mendaftar" is read in modern Indonesian as "to register/sign up", so a read-only GET row briefly looks like an enrolment action; the noun-phrase form "menampilkan daftar" is the conventional rendering for the API verb "List".

examples.source: List job details / List job logs / List job results / List jobs / List tags
examples.translation: Mendaftar detail job / Mendaftar log job / Mendaftar hasil job / Mendaftar job / Mendaftar tag
examples.suggested: Menampilkan daftar detail job / … log job / … hasil job / … job / … tag
examples.why: The same calqued verb repeats five more times, and sits inconsistently beside line 50 where "Get list of backends" is correctly rendered with the noun "Mendapatkan daftar Backend".

editor_note: No semantic drift: every ordering claim survives intact — bit $0$ = "bit paling tidak signifikan" / bit $n-1$ = "paling signifikan", topmost/bottommost, leftmost/rightmost, the `reverse_bits` caveat ("hanya mempengaruhi diagram ... Gate X tetap bekerja pada qubit $0$") and the closing "Gate X bekerja pada qubit $1$" are all faithful, and the informal "kamu" register holds throughout. What a native technical editor would still change: "resources" is calqued as "sumber daya" (which in Indonesian means resources in the manpower/energy sense, not reference material — should be "referensi" or "sumber rujukan"); "when coding" becomes "pengkodean", which Indonesian developers read as *encoding* rather than the act of writing code; and "computational basis state" is rendered "basis komputasional" where the settled Indonesian physics term is "basis komputasi". All three are wording slips only — none would lead a learner to a false belief about bit ordering.

examples.source: Different softwares and resources must choose how they order these bits
examples.translation: Berbagai perangkat lunak dan sumber daya harus memilih cara pengurutan bit-bit ini
examples.suggested: Berbagai perangkat lunak dan referensi harus memilih cara pengurutan bit-bit ini
examples.why: "resources" here means documentation/reference material; "sumber daya" in Indonesian denotes resources in the manpower/energy sense and reads as a direct calque a native technical writer would not produce.

examples.source: This is helpful when coding because each bit has the value $2^\text{label}$
examples.translation: Ini memudahkan pengkodean karena setiap bit memiliki nilai $2^\text{label}$
examples.suggested: Ini memudahkan saat menulis kode karena setiap bit memiliki nilai $2^\text{label}$
examples.why: "pengkodean" is the standard Indonesian word for *encoding*, not for programming; in a page about bit representations that collision is actively distracting, though the surrounding sentence keeps the meaning recoverable.

examples.source: the amplitude at index $x$ represents the computational basis state $|x\rangle$
examples.translation: amplitudo pada indeks $x$ merepresentasikan keadaan basis komputasional $|x\rangle$
examples.suggested: amplitudo pada indeks $x$ merepresentasikan keadaan basis komputasi $|x\rangle$
examples.why: The established Indonesian rendering of "computational basis" is "basis komputasi"; "komputasional" is an English-shaped adjective that is recognizable but not the conventional domain term.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every quantity, condition and caveat survives intact ($T_2 \le 2T_1$, "reset ke 1 alih-alih 0 dengan probabilitas `p_reset`", the qubit-order caveat "error yang diterapkan pada qubit [0, 1] ... berbeda dengan yang diterapkan pada qubit [1, 0]", and the $P(A|B)$ recorded-vs-true bit distinction). The main defect is terminological: "noisy" is rendered as "bersuara" (literally "audible / making sound") in four headings and links — "Menjalankan simulasi bersuara", "Circuit bersuara", "Simulasi eksak dan bersuara" — and once as "berisik" ("simulasi berisik", line 65), while the noun stays English ("model noise"); a native quantum writer would use "berderau"/"bernoise" or simply "dengan noise", and would not split it three ways. Secondary: "circuit" alternates between "sirkuit kuantum" (line 35) and the kept "Circuit" (lines 366, 570) within the same file, and the hedge in "That suggests you should write your own transpiler pass" is hardened to "Artinya, kamu perlu ..." ("that means you need to"). Register is correct throughout: informal "kamu", never bapak/ibu.

examples.source: Execute a noisy simulation with a noise model / To simulate noisy circuits
examples.translation: Menjalankan simulasi bersuara dengan noise model / Untuk mensimulasikan Circuit bersuara
examples.suggested: Menjalankan simulasi berderau (bernoise) dengan noise model / Untuk mensimulasikan Circuit yang terkena noise
examples.why: "bersuara" means "making sound / having a voice" — the acoustic sense of noise, not the signal/error sense. Recognizable only because "noise model" sits untranslated beside it, but no Indonesian quantum engineer would write it.

examples.source: The NoiseModel class which stores a noise model used for noisy simulation.
examples.translation: Kelas `NoiseModel` yang menyimpan model noise yang digunakan untuk simulasi berisik.
examples.suggested: ... yang digunakan untuk simulasi bernoise (berderau).
examples.why: Third rendering of the same adjective in one file: "berisik" here, "bersuara" in every later heading, plain "noise" in the noun phrases. Within-file inconsistency for one core concept.

examples.source: That suggests you should write your own transpiler pass (TransformationPass) and run the pass just before running the simulator if you need to insert your quantum errors...
examples.translation: Artinya, kamu perlu [membuat transpiler pass sendiri] ... jika ingin menyisipkan quantum error ...
examples.suggested: Ini menyiratkan bahwa kamu sebaiknya membuat transpiler pass sendiri ...
examples.why: "That suggests you should" is a recommendation; "Artinya, kamu perlu" states it as a requirement. A hedge dropped — not misleading about the mechanism, but the emphasis is strengthened.

examples.source: we must specify the type of instruction that it acts on and what qubits to apply it to
examples.translation: kita harus menentukan jenis *instruksi* yang diterapkan dan qubit mana yang dikenai error tersebut
examples.suggested: kita harus menentukan jenis *instruksi* yang dikenai error tersebut dan pada qubit mana error itu diterapkan
examples.why: "jenis instruksi yang diterapkan" reads as "the type of instruction that is applied", losing the it-acts-on relation; the second half then carries the error relation, so the sentence is lopsided. Calqued word order rather than a meaning error.

examples.source: quantum circuits / a simple test circuit / noisy circuits
examples.translation: sirkuit kuantum (l.35) ... Circuit uji sederhana (l.366) ... Circuit bersuara (l.570)
examples.suggested: Pick one: keep "Circuit" throughout, or use "sirkuit" throughout.
examples.why: The same core term appears both translated and kept in English inside one page; a native editor would normalise it.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat: the Paulice entry keeps "single-shot access to the quantum state" and the both/and scope ("baik dalam alur kerja berbasis sampling maupun berbasis nilai ekspektasi"), PNA keeps "menyerap invers dari kanal noise yang dipelajari ke dalam observable menggunakan propagasi Pauli", and SLC keeps the comparative "secara lebih ketat" plus "dengan varians yang berkurang". Terminology is correct and consistent (nilai ekspektasi, kanal noise, observable, fidelitas, propagasi Pauli), and the register stays neutral-informative with no deferential slips. The only thing a native technical editor would change is the closing clause of the June 2026 bullet: "untuk cara memulai hari ini" is a word-for-word calque of "for how to get started today" and is missing the governing verb Indonesian needs (e.g. "untuk mengetahui cara memulai" / "untuk mulai menggunakannya hari ini"). That is stiffness only and does not mislead.

examples.source: Check out the [blog](...) and [documentation](...) for how to get started today.
examples.translation: Lihat [blog](...) dan [dokumentasi](...) untuk cara memulai hari ini.
examples.suggested: Lihat [blog](...) dan [dokumentasi](...) untuk mengetahui cara memulai hari ini.
examples.why: "untuk cara memulai" is a direct calque of "for how to get started"; Indonesian needs a verb (mengetahui/mempelajari) before the nominalized clause, otherwise the preposition dangles. Meaning is still clear, so this is cosmetic only.

editor_note: Meaning is fully faithful throughout this short changelog: the sunset entry ("Layanan pratinjau telah dihentikan dan ekstensi Visual Studio Code serta JupyterLab telah diarsipkan"), the rationale sentence ("semakin banyak pengguna yang menjalankan model Qiskit Code Assistant secara lokal"), and the caveat that the models stay available locally are all preserved with no drift, inversion or added claim. The one thing a native technical editor would change is the calqued verb in "Kami telah membuka sumber (open-source) dua model baru untuk inferensi lokal" — "membuka sumber" is a literal rendering of "open-sourced" that Indonesian tech writing does not use; the parenthetical gloss shows the translator sensed it. Idiomatic would be "Kami telah merilis dua model baru sebagai open source…". No terminology or register problems otherwise (no deferential bapak/ibu forms; "inferensi lokal", "alur kerja pengembangan" are correct and consistent).

examples.source: We have open-sourced two new models for local inference in Hugging Face:
examples.translation: Kami telah membuka sumber (open-source) dua model baru untuk inferensi lokal di Hugging Face:
examples.suggested: Kami telah merilis dua model baru sebagai open source untuk inferensi lokal di Hugging Face:
examples.why: "Membuka sumber" is a word-for-word calque of the English verb "open-sourced" and is not idiomatic Indonesian; the bracketed English gloss confirms it does not stand on its own. Meaning is still clear, so this is a naturalness slip only, not misleading.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the three pre-flight checks, the `usage()`/`backends()`/`backend()`/`least_busy()` list, the "fewest pending jobs" wording and the TEM-vs-PEC "lebih sedikit shot" comparison all match the English, and the informal "Anda" register holds everywhere. Two editorial slips remain. (1) The relative-clause calque "dengan mana pengguna dapat…" appears twice (Q-CTRL circuit function, Q-CTRL optimization solver) as a literal rendering of English "with which"; no Indonesian technical writer would use it — "sehingga pengguna dapat…" is the natural form. (2) "eksekusi dari representasi ISA circuit" turns the English adjective "representative ISA circuit" into a noun ("the ISA circuit representation"); the sense survives but the intended "ISA circuit yang representatif" is lost. Also "Get started" is rendered as the imperative "Mulai sekarang" ("start now") where the section is a heading for setup steps ("Memulai"). None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: Q-CTRL is releasing a circuit function that applies AI-driven quantum control techniques, with which users can scale successfully to larger problems.
examples.translation: Q-CTRL merilis fungsi circuit yang menerapkan teknik kontrol kuantum berbasis AI, dengan mana pengguna dapat berhasil menskalakan ke masalah yang lebih besar.
examples.suggested: …teknik kontrol kuantum berbasis AI, sehingga pengguna dapat menskalakan ke masalah yang lebih besar dengan sukses.
examples.why: 'dengan mana' is a direct calque of English 'with which'; it is not idiomatic Indonesian and reads as machine output. Occurs again in the Q-CTRL application-function bullet ('solver optimasi dengan mana pengguna dapat memberikan sebuah graph…').

examples.source: …then manage synthesis, optimization, and execution of the representative ISA circuit.
examples.translation: …lalu mengelola sintesis, optimasi, dan eksekusi dari representasi ISA circuit.
examples.suggested: …lalu mengelola sintesis, optimasi, dan eksekusi ISA circuit yang representatif.
examples.why: The adjective 'representative' became the noun 'representasi', so the phrase reads 'the ISA circuit representation' rather than 'the representative ISA circuit'. The overall sense is close enough not to mislead, but the qualifier is lost.

examples.source: **Get started**
examples.translation: **Mulai sekarang**
examples.suggested: **Memulai**
examples.why: As a section label introducing installation steps, the English is a gerund heading, not an exhortation; 'Mulai sekarang' ('start now') reads as marketing copy. Cosmetic only.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout this very short changelog page — no drift, no dropped caveat, no hallucination; version numbers, dates and links match, and core terms are correct and consistent ("transpilasi", "pass transpiler berbasis AI", "pustaka Python", "klien Qiskit Transpiler Service"). Two wording slips a native technical editor would fix in the single prose paragraph: "menghasilkan hasil yang lebih baik" is a tautology (menghasilkan + hasil) where Indonesian would use "memberikan/memberi hasil yang lebih baik", and "seamlessly integrate" is flattened to "dengan mudah mengintegrasikan" ("easily"), losing the seamless/frictionless nuance that "dengan mulus" would carry. Neither would mislead a learner; the rest of the paragraph reads naturally and the em-dash appositive ("alat mutakhir yang mungkin lebih cepat…") preserves the English emphasis.

examples.source: cutting-edge tools that might be faster and produce better results than traditional transpilation methods
examples.translation: alat mutakhir yang mungkin lebih cepat dan menghasilkan hasil yang lebih baik dibandingkan metode transpilasi tradisional
examples.suggested: alat mutakhir yang mungkin lebih cepat dan memberikan hasil yang lebih baik dibandingkan metode transpilasi tradisional
examples.why: "menghasilkan hasil" repeats the same root (hasil) and reads as a tautology no Indonesian technical writer would leave in; "memberikan hasil" is the idiomatic pairing.

examples.source: a Python library that helps users seamlessly integrate the service into their current Qiskit patterns and workflows
examples.translation: pustaka Python yang membantu pengguna dengan mudah mengintegrasikan layanan ke dalam pola dan alur kerja Qiskit mereka saat ini
examples.suggested: pustaka Python yang membantu pengguna mengintegrasikan layanan secara mulus ke dalam pola dan alur kerja Qiskit mereka saat ini
examples.why: "seamlessly" is about frictionless integration, not ease of use; "dengan mudah" softens it to "easily" and the pre-verb placement is calqued English word order.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every claim, version number (`qiskit-ibm-runtime` 0.47.0/0.46.0/0.45.0), caveat ("saat ini dalam versi beta"), and conditional ("Jika Anda lebih memilih tingkat abstraksi yang lebih tinggi") matches the English, and the informal "Anda" register holds throughout. Three editorial slips remain. (1) The entire lead sentence of the April 2026 bullet is left untranslated English — "**Introducing the Executor primitive**: We're excited to announce the release of the new `Executor` primitive and a new version of the noise-learning helper class, `NoiseLearnerV3`, both of which were first previewed at QDC 2025." — while the following paragraph ("Bersama dengan Samplomatic, keduanya membentuk...") is in Indonesian and depends on it, so the section opens mid-thought for an Indonesian reader. (2) "Building on the momentum established across the v2.x series" is calqued as "Membangun momentum yang telah dibentuk di seluruh seri v2.x", which reads as "building momentum" rather than "building *on* it" (natural: "Berlandaskan/Bertumpu pada momentum yang telah terbangun"). (3) "Upgrades and Rust-driven performance enhancements" becomes the awkward doubling "Peningkatan dan peningkatan performa berbasis Rust". Domain terms are otherwise correct and consistent (qubit, quantum circuit, transpiler/transpilasi, pipeline, fidelitas, mitigasi error, catatan rilis).

examples.source: **Introducing the Executor primitive**: We're excited to announce the release of the new `Executor` primitive and a new version of the noise-learning helper class, `NoiseLearnerV3`, both of which were first previewed at QDC 2025.
examples.translation: **Introducing the Executor primitive**: We're excited to announce the release of the new `Executor` primitive and a new version of the noise-learning helper class, `NoiseLearnerV3`, both of which were first previewed at QDC 2025.
examples.suggested: **Memperkenalkan primitive Executor**: Kami dengan senang hati mengumumkan rilis primitive `Executor` baru dan versi baru dari kelas helper noise-learning, `NoiseLearnerV3`, yang keduanya pertama kali ditampilkan di QDC 2025.
examples.why: The whole announcement sentence that opens the April 2026 entry was never translated. It is not a kept English term but the topic sentence the next Indonesian paragraph refers back to ("keduanya membentuk..." = "together they make up..."), so the section begins with an unexplained antecedent for a reader who does not read English.

examples.source: Building on the momentum established across the v2.x series, which has centered on positioning Qiskit as the leading platform for hybrid quantum-HPC workflows, ...
examples.translation: Membangun momentum yang telah dibentuk di seluruh seri v2.x, yang berfokus pada memposisikan Qiskit sebagai platform terdepan untuk alur kerja hybrid quantum-HPC, ...
examples.suggested: Berlandaskan momentum yang telah terbangun sepanjang seri v2.x, yang berfokus pada menempatkan Qiskit sebagai platform terdepan untuk alur kerja hybrid quantum-HPC, ...
examples.why: "Building on" is calqued to "Membangun momentum", which reads as "building momentum" (creating it) rather than "building upon existing momentum"; "di seluruh seri" is a literal rendering of "across the series" where "sepanjang" is the natural Indonesian, and "memposisikan" is stiffer than "menempatkan".

examples.source: Upgrades and Rust-driven performance enhancements to `VF2Layout` and `VF2PostLayout` improve the speed and scalability of circuit-to-hardware layout selection ...
examples.translation: Peningkatan dan peningkatan performa berbasis Rust pada `VF2Layout` dan `VF2PostLayout` meningkatkan kecepatan dan skalabilitas pemilihan layout circuit-ke-hardware ...
examples.suggested: Pembaruan serta peningkatan performa berbasis Rust pada `VF2Layout` dan `VF2PostLayout` mempercepat dan memperbaiki skalabilitas pemilihan layout circuit-ke-hardware ...
examples.why: "Peningkatan dan peningkatan ... meningkatkan" repeats the same stem three times in one sentence; a native technical writer would vary it ("Pembaruan serta peningkatan performa ... mempercepat ..."). Meaning is intact, but the sentence reads as machine output.

editor_note: One genuine status-strengthening drift drives the FAIL: in the 2 February 2025 entry, EN "the following capabilities are now deprecated and will be no longer supported on or around 2 June 2025" became "kemampuan berikut kini tidak lagi didukung dan tidak akan didukung lagi pada atau sekitar 2 Juni 2025" — it tells the reader `while`/`for`/`switch` and nested control flow are ALREADY unsupported, and the sentence contradicts its own date clause. The same file renders "deprecated" correctly four other times ("tidak lagi digunakan (deprecated)" at lines 629/642/647/652), so this is an error rather than a house convention. Secondary: two chunks are left wholly in English — the heading "### `ibm_torino` to retire" (line 234) and the entire bullet "The new dynamic circuits is now available to all users on all backends…" (line 373), the latter being the lead sentence of its section. Also "circuit" is split against "sirkuit" inside the same file (circuit at lines 41/49/127/202/291, sirkuit at 375/379/383/412/437/455/590/595), one register slip to "Kamu" at line 615 against "Anda" everywhere else, and "2,477" (line 313) keeps the English thousands comma while line 23 correctly localizes "100.000".

examples.source: To accelerate the rollout, the following capabilities are now deprecated and will be no longer supported on or around 2 June 2025:
examples.translation: Untuk mempercepat peluncuran, kemampuan berikut kini tidak lagi didukung dan tidak akan didukung lagi pada atau sekitar 2 Juni 2025:
examples.suggested: Untuk mempercepat peluncuran, kemampuan berikut kini tidak lagi digunakan (deprecated) dan tidak akan didukung lagi pada atau sekitar 2 Juni 2025:
examples.why: "deprecated" was rendered as "kini tidak lagi didukung" (= already unsupported), strengthening the claim: the reader concludes while/for/switch and nested control flow stopped working at announcement time, not on 2 June 2025. The sentence also contradicts itself (already unsupported AND will be unsupported in June). The file translates "deprecated" correctly elsewhere.

examples.source: The new dynamic circuits is now available to all users on all backends, except some QPUs under the On-Prem Plan.
examples.translation: The new dynamic circuits is now available to all users on all backends, except some QPUs under the On-Prem Plan.
examples.suggested: Dynamic circuits versi baru kini tersedia untuk semua pengguna di semua backend, kecuali beberapa QPU di bawah On-Prem Plan.
examples.why: The whole lead sentence of the section — the one carrying the availability statement and its exception — is untranslated English; the Indonesian text that follows ("Dengan versi baru ini…") refers back to a claim the reader of the ID page never gets in their language.

examples.source: ### `ibm_torino` to retire
examples.translation: ### `ibm_torino` to retire
examples.suggested: ### `ibm_torino` akan dipensiunkan
examples.why: Section heading left in English while its body paragraph is translated ("QPU `ibm_torino` akan dipensiunkan pada atau sekitar 1 April 2026"); every sibling heading in the same February 2026 block is translated.

examples.source: circuit / dynamic circuits
examples.translation: "circuit"/"Circuit dinamis" in the 2026 sections vs "sirkuit"/"sirkuit dinamis" throughout the 2025 accordion
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering (the kept English "circuit", used in the newer sections) and apply it file-wide.
examples.why: The same core term is split two ways within one page; a reader scrolling from the 2026 entries into the 2025 accordion meets "sirkuit dinamis" and "Circuit dinamis" for the identical feature. Recognizable, so MINOR.

examples.source: You can also force the Gen3 path using the `gen3-turbo` experimental option.
examples.translation: Kamu juga bisa memaksa jalur Gen3 dengan menggunakan opsi eksperimental `gen3-turbo`.
examples.suggested: Anda juga dapat memaksa jalur Gen3 dengan menggunakan opsi eksperimental `gen3-turbo`.
examples.why: Lone "Kamu" in a file that uses "Anda" everywhere else (lines 33, 124, 242, 291, 462, …); an isolated register switch inside one changelog bullet.

examples.source: to take advantage of the lower error rates (approximately 5x lower EPLG) and faster gates (nearly 8x faster)
examples.translation: untuk memanfaatkan tingkat error yang lebih rendah (sekitar 5x lebih rendah EPLG) dan gate yang lebih cepat (hampir 8x lebih cepat)
examples.suggested: untuk memanfaatkan tingkat error yang lebih rendah (EPLG sekitar 5x lebih rendah) dan gate yang lebih cepat (hampir 8x lebih cepat)
examples.why: "sekitar 5x lebih rendah EPLG" keeps English adjective-before-noun order; Indonesian puts the head noun first ("EPLG sekitar 5x lebih rendah"). Reads as MT, not as something a native technical writer would produce.

editor_note: No semantic drift: every translated paragraph tracks the English faithfully ("continues to provide" → "tetap menyediakan", "to further improve the result quality" → "untuk lebih meningkatkan kualitas hasil", the 0.47.0-or-higher beta caveat intact), and the informal "kamu" register is consistent. Two things a native editor would change. First, the lead bullet of the April 2026 entry — "**Introducing the Executor primitive**: We're excited to announce the release of the new `Executor` primitive and a new version of the noise-learning helper class, `NoiseLearnerV3`, both of which were first previewed at QDC 2025." — is left entirely in English, so the sentence that actually introduces the whole entry is unreadable to an Indonesian-only learner and the following "keduanya membentuk..." has no visible antecedent. Second, "Noise learning helper" is rendered "Pembantu noise learning"; "pembantu" in everyday Indonesian reads as domestic helper and is not the idiomatic word for a helper class — "Kelas bantu noise learning" or keeping "Helper noise learning" is what a technical writer would use.

examples.source: **Introducing the Executor primitive**: We're excited to announce the release of the new `Executor` primitive and a new version of the noise-learning helper class, `NoiseLearnerV3`, both of which were first previewed at QDC 2025.
examples.translation: (identical English text, untranslated)
examples.suggested: **Memperkenalkan primitive Executor**: Kami dengan senang hati mengumumkan rilis primitive `Executor` yang baru dan versi baru dari kelas bantu noise learning, `NoiseLearnerV3`, yang keduanya pertama kali ditampilkan di QDC 2025.
examples.why: The entry's topic sentence is the only place the Executor primitive and NoiseLearnerV3 are introduced; leaving it in English breaks the reference chain for the next paragraph, which opens with "Bersama dengan Samplomatic, keduanya membentuk..." and now points at nothing an Indonesian reader has been told about.

examples.source: Noise learning helper
examples.translation: Pembantu noise learning
examples.suggested: Kelas bantu noise learning
examples.why: "Pembantu" carries a domestic-help sense in ordinary Indonesian and is not the conventional rendering of a helper class; "kelas bantu" (or simply keeping "helper") is what Indonesian software documentation uses, and this is a link label a learner will click.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, no swapped quantities, no hallucinated claims; the optimization_level=0 vs 3 comparison, the CNOT error-rate rationale, the dynamical-decoupling paragraph and the "higher is better, 1 is perfect fidelity" caveat all land correctly, and the informal "kamu" register holds consistently. What an editor would change is internal consistency: within one sentence (line 36) the file writes "satu sirkuit" and "Circuit lain" for the same noun, splitting the term between the Indonesianized and kept-English forms; "device" is rendered "perangkat" in the Transpile section but left as bare "device run" at line 190; and the verb is inflected three ways — "men-transpilasi" (34), "men-transpilasikan" (89), "transpilasikan" (83, 236). One small nuance is dropped at line 60: English "what you'd expect to measure" becomes only "apa yang kamu harapkan", losing "mengukur" — harmless but the measurement framing is part of the pedagogy.

examples.source: Note that the same setting could improve the results of one circuit while hindering another.
examples.translation: Perhatikan bahwa pengaturan yang sama bisa meningkatkan hasil satu sirkuit sementara menghambat Circuit lain.
examples.suggested: Perhatikan bahwa pengaturan yang sama bisa meningkatkan hasil satu Circuit sementara menghambat Circuit lain.
examples.why: The same noun appears as both "sirkuit" and "Circuit" inside a single sentence; the file otherwise uses "Circuit" everywhere, so the split is a visible inconsistency (not misleading — the concept stays identifiable).

examples.source: plot the results from the device runs against the ideal distribution
examples.translation: plot hasil dari device run terhadap distribusi ideal
examples.suggested: plot hasil eksekusi pada perangkat terhadap distribusi ideal
examples.why: "device" is translated as "perangkat" earlier in the same file (line 83: "memetakan qubit Circuit ke qubit perangkat"), so leaving "device run" bare here is inconsistent and reads as untranslated residue rather than a kept term of art.

examples.source: the ideal distribution (what you'd expect to measure if you ran this on a perfect quantum computer an infinite number of times)
examples.translation: distribusi ideal (apa yang kamu harapkan jika kamu menjalankan ini pada komputer kuantum sempurna sebanyak tak terhingga kali)
examples.suggested: distribusi ideal (apa yang kamu harapkan untuk diukur jika kamu menjalankan ini pada komputer kuantum sempurna sebanyak tak terhingga kali)
examples.why: "to measure" is dropped, so the gloss says only "what you'd expect" rather than "what you'd expect to measure". The learner still gets the right idea, but the explicit link between the ideal distribution and measurement outcomes — the point of the parenthetical — is flattened.

examples.source: The lowest optimization level does the bare minimum needed to get the circuit running on the device
examples.translation: Level optimasi terendah hanya melakukan yang minimum yang diperlukan agar Circuit bisa berjalan di perangkat
examples.suggested: Level optimasi terendah hanya melakukan hal minimum yang diperlukan agar Circuit bisa berjalan di perangkat
examples.why: "melakukan yang minimum yang diperlukan" stacks two "yang" clauses and reads as a calque of "the bare minimum needed"; a native technical writer would insert a head noun ("hal minimum" / "upaya minimum"). Defensible but stiff.

editor_note: The three rewritten headings are faithful and idiomatic and follow the file's own localized-heading convention: "Pernyataan switch", "Perulangan for", "Perulangan while" sit alongside the existing "Pernyataan `if`", "Ekspresi klasik" and "Langkah selanjutnya", with anchors ({#switch-statement}, {#for-loop}, {#while-loop}) intact and "perulangan"/"pernyataan" the standard Indonesian renderings of loop/statement.

Semantically faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat: the 32-digit feature code, the "tidak akan diaktifkan tanpa langkah terakhir ini" warning, the credit-card caution, the 10-minutes-per-28-day rolling window (both occurrences, with "hingga" correctly kept only where EN says "up to"), and the full instance-prefix example (`physics-101-john-doe` / default `open-student-john-doe`) all match the source exactly. Register is consistently informal "kamu", never deferential. What a native technical editor would still change are three English-shaped constructions: "di mana mereka akan melihat instance Akun Kelas mereka" (calqued relative "where they will see" — Indonesian prose would use "dan mereka akan melihat"), "salin Account ID (ditemukan di bawah Details)" (literal "found under Details"; natural is "terdapat di bagian Details"), and "Periksa kotak masuk email kamu untuk kode verifikasi tujuh digit" (calqued "check X for Y"). None of these mislead; the page teaches as clearly as the English.

examples.source: …they can navigate to IBM Quantum Platform, where they will see their Classroom Account instance in the account switcher in the page header.
examples.translation: …mereka bisa membuka IBM Quantum Platform, di mana mereka akan melihat instance Akun Kelas mereka di pengalih akun pada header halaman.
examples.suggested: …mereka bisa membuka IBM Quantum Platform, dan instance Akun Kelas mereka akan muncul di pengalih akun pada header halaman.
examples.why: "di mana" as a relative pronoun is a direct calque of English "where"; Indonesian technical writers split the clause or use "dan" instead. Meaning is unaffected.

examples.source: …and copy the Account ID (found under Details).
examples.translation: …dan salin Account ID (ditemukan di bawah Details).
examples.suggested: …dan salin Account ID (terdapat di bagian Details).
examples.why: "ditemukan di bawah" is a literal rendering of "found under"; "di bawah" reads as physical position rather than "in the Details section". A native would write "terdapat di bagian Details".

examples.source: Check your email inbox for a seven-digit verification code, then return to the account creation form.
examples.translation: Periksa kotak masuk email kamu untuk kode verifikasi tujuh digit, lalu kembali ke formulir pembuatan akun.
examples.suggested: Periksa kotak masuk email kamu, cari kode verifikasi tujuh digit, lalu kembali ke formulir pembuatan akun.
examples.why: The "check X for Y" pattern does not map onto Indonesian "periksa X untuk Y", which reads as purpose rather than search target. Stiff but not ambiguous.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every claim in the approximation-degree section (0.0 = maximum approximation, 1.0 = default/no approximation, "paling banyak tiga CX Gate", "lebih sedikit kesalahan dari hardware, tetapi lebih banyak dari aproksimasi") matches the English exactly, terminology is consistent ("sintesis uniter", "tingkat aproksimasi", "qubit virtual"/"qubit fisik"), and the informal "kamu" register holds throughout. What a native technical editor would change is translationese: "Mereka mempengaruhi cara kerja Transpiler" uses the human pronoun "Mereka" for inanimate options (a direct calque of English "They"); "menghasilkan hasil yang berbeda" / "akan menghasilkan hasil yang sama" repeats the root twice in one clause where a native writer would write "memberikan hasil yang berbeda/sama"; "kesalahan yang dimasukkan" for "error is introduced" reads as literal MT ("ditimbulkan" is the domain norm). The `initial_layout` list sentence, "qubit fisik yang harus dipetakan oleh qubit ke-$i$", uses an "oleh" agent-passive that grammatically makes the physical qubit the thing being mapped by the virtual one — the pairing a learner extracts is still correct, but the direction is muddled and should read "qubit fisik tempat qubit ke-$i$ harus dipetakan". None of these would teach a false concept.

examples.source: They influence how the transpiler works and are used to try and get better, different, or specific output from the transpiler.
examples.translation: Mereka mempengaruhi cara kerja Transpiler dan digunakan untuk mencoba mendapatkan output yang lebih baik, berbeda, atau spesifik dari Transpiler.
examples.suggested: Opsi ini mempengaruhi cara kerja Transpiler dan digunakan untuk mencoba mendapatkan output yang lebih baik, berbeda, atau spesifik dari Transpiler.
examples.why: "Mereka" is the human third-person plural pronoun; applying it to a list of options is a direct calque of English "They" that no Indonesian technical writer would use for inanimate referents.

examples.source: repeated transpilation runs may return different results ... Repeated runs using the same seed will return the same results.
examples.translation: transpilasi yang diulang mungkin menghasilkan hasil yang berbeda ... Eksekusi berulang menggunakan seed yang sama akan menghasilkan hasil yang sama.
examples.suggested: transpilasi yang diulang mungkin memberikan hasil yang berbeda ... Eksekusi berulang dengan seed yang sama akan memberikan hasil yang sama.
examples.why: "menghasilkan hasil" repeats the root hasil in the same clause, twice in one paragraph; stiff and avoidable with "memberikan hasil".

examples.source: the $i$-th element of the list contains the physical qubit that the $i$-th qubit should be mapped to
examples.translation: elemen ke-$i$ dari daftar berisi qubit fisik yang harus dipetakan oleh qubit ke-$i$
examples.suggested: elemen ke-$i$ dari daftar berisi qubit fisik tempat qubit ke-$i$ harus dipetakan
examples.why: The "oleh" agent-passive makes the physical qubit the object being mapped by the virtual qubit, blurring the virtual→physical direction the section just established; the pairing survives but the explanation is harder to parse than the English.

examples.source: That is, how much error is introduced when a matrix representation of a circuit is converted to discrete gates.
examples.translation: Artinya, seberapa besar kesalahan yang dimasukkan ketika representasi matriks sebuah sirkuit dikonversi menjadi gate diskrit.
examples.suggested: Artinya, seberapa besar kesalahan yang ditimbulkan ketika representasi matriks sebuah sirkuit dikonversi menjadi gate diskrit.
examples.why: "dimasukkan" (inserted/put in) is a literal rendering of "introduced"; Indonesian technical prose uses "ditimbulkan" or "muncul" for error introduced by a process.

editor_note: Nothing here misleads: every technical claim I checked paragraph-by-paragraph is faithful (reduced purity "[0.5, 1]; nilai satu menunjukkan bahwa qubit tidak terjerat dengan pihak lain mana pun", the CZ example state and "Probabilitas untuk masing-masing keadaan komputasi adalah 1/4", SXdg "karena gate NOT adalah inversnya sendiri", the q-sphere vs Bloch sphere admonition, Toffoli "hanya ketika kedua kontrol berada dalam keadaan |1>"), and the informal "kamu" register holds throughout. What a native editor would change is consistency: "qubit state" is rendered "status qubit" in the first half (§Apa yang bisa dilakukan, item 4/5 of the interface tour) but "keadaan qubit" from the Visualisasi section onward — "keadaan" is the right physics term and "status" should go; likewise "phase" splits between Indonesian ("cakram fase", "Gate fase", "fase relatif/global" in the glossary) and English ("phase disk", "phase kuantum", "sudut phase") in the Cakram fase / Statevector sections, so the same object is named two ways within one page. Three phrasings also read as MT rather than as written Indonesian: "Garis putus-putus akan menggaris bawahi kumpulan operasi" (menggarisbawahi = to underline; the English says the dashed line *outlines* the selection — should be "mengelilingi/membatasi"), "lebih berwawasan untuk mengambil tampilan *global*" for "more insightful", and "Umum untuk menyebut ... sebagai amplitudo kuantum" for "It is common to call". Minor dropped nuance: item 6 of the tour loses the contrastive "instead" in "Sign in and click Run circuit to get results from the specified backend instead."

examples.source: See how changes to your circuit affect the state of qubits … the state of the qubits as the computation evolves
examples.translation: Lihat bagaimana perubahan pada Circuit-mu memengaruhi status qubit … (later) keadaan qubit
examples.suggested: Use "keadaan qubit" everywhere; drop "status qubit".
examples.why: "state" is rendered two ways in the same file; "keadaan" is the conventional Indonesian physics term, "status" reads as UI status and weakens the concept.

examples.source: phase disk / quantum phase
examples.translation: "cakram fase", "Gate fase", "fase relatif" (tour + glossary) vs "phase disk", "phase kuantum", "sudut phase" (Visualisasi/Statevector sections)
examples.suggested: Pick one — either keep "phase disk" as a kept English term throughout, or use "cakram fase"/"fase kuantum" throughout.
examples.why: The same visualization and the same physical quantity are named in two languages within one page, including in the heading ("### Cakram fase") whose body then says "Phase disk".

examples.source: A dashed line outlines the set of operations you are selecting
examples.translation: Garis putus-putus akan menggaris bawahi kumpulan operasi yang sedang kamu pilih
examples.suggested: Garis putus-putus mengelilingi kumpulan operasi yang sedang kamu pilih
examples.why: "menggarisbawahi" means to underline/emphasize, not to outline; the UI draws a dashed box around the selection, so the verb describes the wrong visual.

examples.source: it is more insightful to take a global view and look at the quantum state in its entirety
examples.translation: lebih berwawasan untuk mengambil tampilan *global* dan melihat keadaan kuantum secara keseluruhan
examples.suggested: lebih memberi pemahaman (atau: lebih informatif) untuk mengambil sudut pandang *global* …
examples.why: "berwawasan" describes a person as broad-minded, not an approach as insightful; the calque reads as machine translation in an otherwise well-written admonition.

examples.source: It is common to call sqrt(p_k)e^{i phi_k} the quantum amplitude.
examples.translation: Umum untuk menyebut $\sqrt{p_k}e^{i\varphi_k}$ sebagai amplitudo kuantum.
examples.suggested: $\sqrt{p_k}e^{i\varphi_k}$ biasa disebut amplitudo kuantum.
examples.why: Word-for-word calque of the English cleft; Indonesian technical prose puts the term first with "biasa disebut".

examples.source: Sign in and click **Run circuit** to get results from the specified backend instead.
examples.translation: Masuk dan klik **Run circuit** untuk mendapatkan hasil dari Backend yang ditentukan.
examples.suggested: … untuk mendapatkan hasil dari Backend yang ditentukan sebagai gantinya (alih-alih dari simulator).
examples.why: The dropped "instead" removes the contrast with the single-shot simulator that the rest of the bullet sets up; the reader loses the reason for signing in.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries are heading renderings of IBM product names, and both are semantically faithful — nothing here misleads a learner. The defect is within-file inconsistency: the headings translate the product names ("Layanan Komputasi IBM Quantum", "Platform IBM Quantum") while every occurrence in the body of the same page keeps them in English and untranslated — "IBM Quantum Compute Service, sebelumnya disebut Qiskit Runtime Service..." immediately under the first heading, and "IBM Quantum Platform menyediakan lingkungan terpadu...", "...menjadikan IBM Quantum Platform sebagai pusat kendali...", "...memulai dengan IBM Quantum Platform" under the second. A reader scanning the sidebar/TOC sees a name that does not textually match the product named in the prose (and the anchor slugs stay English). Indonesian technical docs conventionally leave vendor product names intact; the fix is to keep the headings as "IBM Quantum Compute Service" and "IBM Quantum Platform" so heading and body agree. Everything else in these two entries — the anchors, the order of the brand tokens — is correct.

examples.source: IBM Quantum Compute Service {#ibm-quantum-compute-service}
examples.translation: Layanan Komputasi IBM Quantum {#ibm-quantum-compute-service}
examples.suggested: IBM Quantum Compute Service {#ibm-quantum-compute-service}
examples.why: The heading translates the product name, but the very next paragraph and the open-source subsection both keep it as the English proper noun ("IBM Quantum Compute Service, sebelumnya disebut Qiskit Runtime Service"; "...untuk mengakses IBM Quantum Compute Service"). Same product, two spellings in one page; headings should match the body's convention of leaving IBM product names untranslated.

examples.source: IBM Quantum Platform {#ibm-quantum-platform}
examples.translation: Platform IBM Quantum {#ibm-quantum-platform}
examples.suggested: IBM Quantum Platform {#ibm-quantum-platform}
examples.why: The body uses the untranslated "IBM Quantum Platform" four times (lines 34, 36, 38, plus the frontmatter description), so the reordered heading form is the odd one out. Not misleading, but a native editor would align the heading with the prose rather than re-order the brand tokens only in the heading.

editor_note: Semantically faithful throughout: the negation in "Tidak seperti kebijakan IAM, pembatasan berbasis konteks tidak memberikan hak akses" is preserved, the three role requirements (Administrator on IBM Quantum Compute Service; Editor *or* Administrator for network zones; Viewer can only add zones to a rule) are rendered exactly, and the "bukan dari IBM Quantum Compute Service" contrast in the Activity Tracker paragraph is intact. Two things a native technical editor would still change. (1) "meskipun kredensial bocor atau salah kelola" is ungrammatical adjectival stacking — Indonesian needs "meskipun kredensial telah disusupi atau salah dikelola"; "bocor" also narrows "compromised" (leaked only) rather than covering compromise generally. (2) The comma in "kebijakan IAM tradisional yang berbasis identitas, untuk memberikan lapisan perlindungan tambahan" splits the purpose clause from its verb — a calque of the English appositive commas; drop it. Neither misleads a learner.

examples.source: context-based restrictions offer protection even in the face of compromised or mismanaged credentials
examples.translation: pembatasan berbasis konteks tetap memberikan perlindungan meskipun kredensial bocor atau salah kelola
examples.suggested: pembatasan berbasis konteks tetap memberikan perlindungan meskipun kredensial telah disusupi atau salah dikelola
examples.why: "bocor atau salah kelola" stacks bare verb roots as adjectives, which Indonesian does not allow without "yang" + passive ("yang bocor atau salah dikelola"); it reads as clipped MT. "bocor" (leaked) also narrows "compromised", which covers stolen or misused credentials, not just disclosed ones.

examples.source: These restrictions work with traditional IAM policies, which are based on identity, to provide an extra layer of protection.
examples.translation: Pembatasan ini bekerja bersama kebijakan IAM tradisional yang berbasis identitas, untuk memberikan lapisan perlindungan tambahan.
examples.suggested: Pembatasan ini bekerja bersama kebijakan IAM tradisional yang berbasis identitas untuk memberikan lapisan perlindungan tambahan.
examples.why: The comma is carried over from the English non-restrictive clause, but in the Indonesian sentence it now separates the purpose clause from the verb it modifies. A native technical writer would drop it.

editor_note: The single delta entry — the frontmatter title "Integrate external quantum resources with Qiskit" → "Integrasikan sumber daya kuantum eksternal dengan Qiskit" — is faithful and idiomatic: correct Indonesian imperative (Integrasikan), correct post-nominal adjective order in "sumber daya kuantum eksternal", and Qiskit left untranslated as the surrounding page does; it matches the body H1 "Mengintegrasikan sumber daya kuantum eksternal dengan Qiskit" in meaning with no drift or added claim.

Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination: the quantities and conditions survive exactly ("paling banyak 3 Qubit" for "at most 3 qubits", "max_trials" prose, "`coupling_map` … hanya digunakan ketika `target` tidak ditentukan", "Mengembalikan `None` juga diperbolehkan"), and the `supports_*` caveat and backward-compatibility promise are intact. What a native technical editor would change is terminology consistency: the two plugin families are named two ways each in the same file — "plugin unitary synthesis" / "plugin high-level synthesis" in the intro bullets and reserved-names list, but "plugin sintesis unitary" / "plugin sintesis tingkat tinggi" from the section headings onward; likewise "matriks uniter" (intro) vs "matriks unitary" (body). "Reserved" is rendered as "dipesan" ("booked/ordered") in the reserved-names section and table header, while the correct sense "dicadangkan" is used later in the `supports_` note. Also a first-person slip in one sentence that mixes exclusive "kami" with inclusive "kita" where the English has a single "we". None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: unitary synthesis plugin / high-level synthesis plugin
examples.translation: "Plugin unitary synthesis" / "Plugin high-level synthesis" in the intro bullets and reserved-names list, but "plugin sintesis unitary" / "plugin sintesis tingkat tinggi" from the section headings onward
examples.suggested: Pick one convention per family and keep it file-wide (e.g. "plugin sintesis unitary" and "plugin sintesis tingkat tinggi" everywhere, including the three intro bullets and the reserved-names list)
examples.why: The same two plugin kinds are named two different ways in one short how-to; a reader scanning back from the section heading to the intro bullet may not immediately see they are the same item. Recognizable, so MINOR.

examples.source: whose names are also reserved. The reserved names are: / Reserved names / are reserved on a `UnitarySynthesisPlugin` derived class
examples.translation: "yang namanya juga sudah dipesan. Nama-nama yang dipesan adalah:" and table header "Nama yang dipesan", versus "dicadangkan" in the `supports_` note
examples.suggested: "…yang namanya juga sudah dicadangkan. Nama-nama yang dicadangkan adalah:" / table header "Nama yang dicadangkan"
examples.why: "Dipesan" is the booking/ordering sense (memesan tiket, meja); the namespace sense of "reserved" is "dicadangkan", which the file itself uses correctly later. Imperfect but still understood as "taken", so MINOR, not FAIL.

examples.source: takes as input a unitary matrix … a Numpy array storing a unitary matrix
examples.translation: "matriks uniter" in the intro bullet, "matriks unitary" twice in the unitary-synthesis section
examples.suggested: Use one form consistently — "matriks uniter" is the standard Indonesian physics term; apply it in both places (or keep "unitary" in both)
examples.why: Same concept spelled two ways within the file; the split is between the definition (intro) and the worked example, exactly where a learner cross-references.

examples.source: In the next sections, we show examples of these steps for the different types of plugins. In these examples, we assume that we are creating a Python package called `my_qiskit_plugin`.
examples.translation: "Di bagian selanjutnya, kami menampilkan contoh langkah-langkah ini … kami mengasumsikan bahwa kita membuat paket Python bernama `my_qiskit_plugin`."
examples.suggested: "Di bagian selanjutnya, kita akan menampilkan contoh … kita mengasumsikan bahwa kita membuat paket Python bernama `my_qiskit_plugin`."
examples.why: Exclusive "kami" (we-not-you) and inclusive "kita" (we-including-you) appear in the same sentence for one English "we"; the rest of the guide uses inclusive "kita" ("kita membuat plugin", "kita ekspos plugin"), which is the right voice for a walkthrough the reader follows along with.

editor_note: No misleading drift: all quantities, conditions and examples survive intact (CZ within chips / CX between chips, qubits 6→21 and 25→40, the four BackendV2 parts, the SWAP-insertion explanation), and the informal "kamu" register holds throughout. The one real terminology slip is graph-theory "graph" rendered as "grafik" (= chart/diagram) instead of the standard Indonesian "graf" — "grafik konektivitas" (~line 213) and "pustaka berbagai grafik yang besar" (~line 348), where the latter also reads ambiguously as "library of various large graphs" rather than "large library of different graphs". Two small fidelity/naturalness slips: "This class serves a single purpose: to get backend objects that you provide" becomes the circular "menyediakan objek backend yang kamu sediakan" (provide → provide), and "acquire/instantiate backends" uses the business-flavoured "mengakuisisi" where "memperoleh" is the natural technical verb. Minor intensity creep in two hedged sentences ("one of the more powerful" → superlative "yang paling canggih"; "it is straightforward" → "sangat mudah"), recognizable but not misleading.

examples.source: You can view the connectivity graph of this new class … The [rustworkx] package contains a large library of different graphs and enables the creation of custom graphs.
examples.translation: Kamu bisa melihat grafik konektivitas dari kelas baru ini … Paket [rustworkx] mengandung pustaka berbagai grafik yang besar dan memungkinkan pembuatan grafik kustom.
examples.suggested: Kamu bisa melihat graf konektivitas dari kelas baru ini … Paket rustworkx berisi pustaka besar berisi bermacam graf dan memungkinkan pembuatan graf kustom.
examples.why: In Indonesian technical usage the graph-theory object is "graf"; "grafik" means chart/graphic. Recognizable in context, so MINOR, but it is the wrong domain term and it is used for every occurrence in the file. The second sentence also attaches "yang besar" to the graphs rather than to the library.

examples.source: This class serves a single purpose: to get backend objects that you provide.
examples.translation: Kelas ini memiliki satu tujuan: menyediakan objek backend yang kamu sediakan.
examples.suggested: Kelas ini memiliki satu tujuan: mengambil objek backend yang kamu sediakan.
examples.why: "to get" is turned into "menyediakan" (to provide), producing the circular "provide the backend objects that you provide" and blurring the Provider's actual role (retrieving the backends the implementer supplies). Does not teach a false concept, so MINOR.

examples.source: …as well as the ability to acquire/instantiate backends.
examples.translation: …serta kemampuan untuk mengakuisisi/menginstansiasi backend.
examples.suggested: …serta kemampuan untuk memperoleh/menginstansiasi backend.
examples.why: "mengakuisisi" carries a corporate-takeover flavour in Indonesian; a native technical writer would use "memperoleh" or "mengambil" here. Pure calque of "acquire".

examples.source: One of the more powerful features of Qiskit … it is straightforward to transpile quantum circuits against this backend
examples.translation: Salah satu fitur Qiskit yang paling canggih … sangat mudah untuk melakukan Transpile Circuit kuantum terhadap Backend ini
examples.suggested: Salah satu fitur Qiskit yang cukup ampuh … cukup mudah untuk melakukan transpilasi sirkuit kuantum terhadap backend ini
examples.why: Two hedged English claims are strengthened: the comparative "more powerful" becomes the superlative "paling canggih", and "straightforward" becomes "sangat mudah" (very easy). Both are defensible idiomatic choices and do not mislead about the mechanics, so MINOR only.

editor_note: The prose is accurate, natural and consistently informal ("kamu"/"-mu"); domain terms are handled well and consistently (Pauli twirling → "Pauli twirling", error suppression → "strategi penekanan error", "coherent error menjadi stochastic error", "Setiap two-qubit gate kini diapit oleh dua Pauli"), and the tricky left/right-twirl passage in the PauliTwirl section is rendered faithfully including the *sebelum*/*setelah* contrast. One real defect: the entry for the English sentence "This example illustrates the DAG by creating a simple circuit that prepares a Bell state and applies an $R_Z$ rotation…" (PO entry at line 98 of i18n/id/po/guides/custom-transpiler-pass.po) has an image markdown line as its msgstr instead of a translation, so the framing sentence is lost and the DAG_circ.avif image renders twice in a row (translated alt text before the code cell, English alt text after). The learner is not actively misled — the injected caption still says the circuit prepares a Bell state and applies an R_Z rotation depending on the measurement outcome — but the explanatory lead-in is gone and the duplicated figure is visible on the page. Second, smaller point: "instal [`graphviz` library]" keeps English noun order; a native writer would write "pustaka `graphviz`" or "library `graphviz`".

examples.source: This example illustrates the DAG by creating a simple circuit that prepares a Bell state and applies an $R_Z$ rotation, depending on the measurement outcome.
examples.translation: ![Circuit yang mempersiapkan Bell state dan menerapkan rotasi $R_Z$ tergantung pada hasil pengukuran.](/docs/images/guides/custom-transpiler-pass/DAG_circ.avif "Circuit")
examples.suggested: Contoh ini mengilustrasikan DAG dengan membuat sirkuit sederhana yang menyiapkan Bell state dan menerapkan rotasi $R_Z$, tergantung pada hasil pengukuran.
examples.why: The msgstr for this sentence is an image line, not a translation: the introductory sentence that tells the reader what the upcoming example does is dropped, and DAG_circ.avif is emitted twice (again at ID line 65 with the English alt text). Content loss plus a visible duplicate figure; not misleading because the injected caption repeats the same facts.

examples.source: install the [`graphviz` library](https://graphviz.org/download/) for the DAG plotting functions
examples.translation: instal [`graphviz` library](https://graphviz.org/download/) untuk fungsi plotting DAG
examples.suggested: instal [pustaka `graphviz`](https://graphviz.org/download/) untuk fungsi plotting DAG
examples.why: English modifier-noun order left intact; Indonesian puts the head noun first. Small calque, does not affect meaning.

editor_note: No semantic drift: the three guideline thresholds (">90% → mitigasi kemungkinan tidak akan membantu", "<90% → PEA", "<80% → ZNE dengan gate folding") are all rendered with the correct comparison direction, the caution block keeps its full hedge ("hanya mensimulasikan sebagian dari noise tersebut, sehingga kemungkinan besar kurang parah dibandingkan noise pada QPU sungguhan"), and the closing sentences of Application 1 and 2 match the source. Two modal hedges are dropped, both making the English weaker claim sound firmer: "This *can be* useful to set up expectations" becomes the flat "Ini berguna untuk menetapkan ekspektasi", and "use `Neat` to *help* determine which noise amplification factors will work best" becomes "untuk menentukan faktor amplifikasi noise mana yang paling cocok" — neither misleads, but a native editor would restore "bisa berguna" and "membantu menentukan". Terminology is also split within the file: "circuit" appears as Indonesian "sirkuit" in the opening two paragraphs (lines 42, 83) but as kept-English "Circuit" everywhere after (lines 163–426), and "job" is "pekerjaan" in the title/description yet "job" in the body ("sebelum menjalankan job pada QPU"). Core domain terms are otherwise correct and consistent (observable, gate, noise, transpiler pass, kedalaman Circuit for depth, tolok ukur for figure of merit), and the informal "kamu" register holds throughout.

examples.source: This can be useful to set up expectations on the quality of the experimental results before running a job on a QPU.
examples.translation: Ini berguna untuk menetapkan ekspektasi kualitas hasil eksperimen sebelum menjalankan job pada QPU.
examples.suggested: Ini bisa berguna untuk menetapkan ekspektasi kualitas hasil eksperimen sebelum menjalankan job pada QPU.
examples.why: The English modal "can be" is dropped, turning a hedged suggestion into a flat assertion. Not misleading, but a strengthened claim relative to the source.

examples.source: You can use `Neat` to help determine which noise amplification factors will work best
examples.translation: Kamu bisa menggunakan `Neat` untuk menentukan faktor amplifikasi noise mana yang paling cocok
examples.suggested: Kamu bisa menggunakan `Neat` untuk membantu menentukan faktor amplifikasi noise mana yang paling cocok
examples.why: "help determine" is rendered as plain "menentukan", removing the qualifier that Neat assists rather than decides. Same softened-claim class as above.

examples.source: circuit
examples.translation: "sirkuit" in the first two body paragraphs ("Sirkuit Clifford mengalami tingkat noise yang serupa", "sebuah sirkuit enam-Qubit") vs "Circuit" from the Cliffordize section onward ("Circuit PUB ... bukan Clifford", "kedalaman Circuit", "ukuran Circuit")
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering and use it throughout the file.
examples.why: Within-file inconsistency for the single most frequent domain term; the concept stays identifiable, so MINOR, but a native technical editor would unify it. Same pattern for job: "pekerjaan" in title/description, "job" in the body.

editor_note: No semantic drift: every claim, condition and caveat survives intact (the NoiseLearner-vs-NoiseLearnerV3 contrast, the "Pauli-Lindblad if the set contains one- and two-qubit gates / TREX if it contains measurements" split, and the client-side-inspection caveat are all faithful), and the informal "kamu" register holds throughout. Three editorial slips: (1) "performant" is rendered "performatif", which in Indonesian means "performative" (speech-act), not high-performing — the correct rendering is "berkinerja tinggi"/"tetap berkinerja baik"; (2) "post-process" is left as a raw English verb and inflected as "mem-post-process data yang dikumpulkan…", which no Indonesian technical writer would write (use "memproses lebih lanjut" or "melakukan pascaproses"); (3) "should be treated as having a stable noise context" is calqued word-for-word into "yang harus diperlakukan sebagai memiliki konteks noise yang stabil", and the parenthetical "other than having different parameter values assigned to it" loses "assigned to it" ("selain memiliki nilai parameter yang berbeda"). None of these would mislead a learner about the physics or the API.

examples.source: so that the process is transparent yet performant
examples.translation: sehingga prosesnya transparan namun tetap performatif
examples.suggested: sehingga prosesnya transparan namun tetap berkinerja tinggi
examples.why: "Performatif" is a false friend — in Indonesian it means "performative" (of a speech act), not "high-performance". The intended sense is kinerja/performa.

examples.source: These fields can be used to post-process data collected from executing the bound template circuit.
examples.translation: Field-field ini dapat digunakan untuk mem-post-process data yang dikumpulkan dari eksekusi template Circuit yang telah di-bind.
examples.suggested: Field-field ini dapat digunakan untuk memproses lebih lanjut (pascaproses) data yang dikumpulkan dari eksekusi template Circuit yang telah di-bind.
examples.why: Prefixing an untranslated English verb with meN- ("mem-post-process") is not something a native technical writer would write; step 4 leaves the same verb bare as "Post-process hasil eksekusi", so the file is also inconsistent with itself.

examples.source: to reason about collections of circuit operations that should be treated as having a stable noise context
examples.translation: untuk memahami kumpulan operasi Circuit yang harus diperlakukan sebagai memiliki konteks noise yang stabil
examples.suggested: untuk menalar kumpulan operasi Circuit yang dianggap memiliki konteks noise yang stabil
examples.why: "diperlakukan sebagai memiliki" is a word-for-word calque of "treated as having" that reads stiffly; "memahami" also flattens "reason about" (the library operates on them, it does not comprehend them).

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, no swapped quantities, no dropped caveats; the tricky YGate paragraph ("bukan basis Gate, sedangkan `XGate` adalah" ... "meskipun itu bukan basis Gate sebenarnya dari `ibm_fez`") and the BasisTranslator re-application rationale ("ini adalah pass default, tetapi dieksekusi sebelum penjadwalan, sehingga perlu diterapkan lagi") both land correctly, and the informal "Anda" register holds. What a native technical editor would still change is physics word choice and a few calques: "membatalkan efek noise channel" uses the "cancel an appointment" sense of membatalkan where physics cancellation calls for "meniadakan"/"saling meniadakan"; "membaliknya di sekitar Bloch sphere" is a word-for-word trace of "flip them around the Bloch sphere" (natural Indonesian would be "memutarnya pada Bloch sphere"); and "ditempatkan secara teratur dalam waktu" / "dua-Qubit" are stiff calqued forms ("berjarak teratur", "dua-qubit"). One small pronoun drift: EN "basis gates of our target" becomes "basis Gate dari target Anda". None of these would give a learner a false belief.

examples.source: which cancels the effect of noise channels, thereby suppressing decoherence
examples.translation: yang membatalkan efek noise channel sehingga menekan dekoherensi
examples.suggested: yang meniadakan efek noise channel sehingga menekan dekoherensi
examples.why: "Membatalkan" is the administrative sense of cancel (cancel a booking/order). For physical cancellation of an effect, Indonesian physics writing uses "meniadakan" or "saling meniadakan". Meaning survives, but the register is wrong for a technical text.

examples.source: to idle qubits to flip them around the Bloch sphere
examples.translation: ke qubit yang menganggur untuk membaliknya di sekitar Bloch sphere
examples.suggested: ke qubit yang menganggur untuk memutarnya pada Bloch sphere
examples.why: "di sekitar" is a literal trace of the English preposition "around" and reads as "in the vicinity of the Bloch sphere" rather than rotation on it; a native writer would use "memutarnya pada/di Bloch sphere".

examples.source: a series of gates that compose to the identity and are spaced regularly in time
examples.translation: serangkaian Gate yang bersama-sama membentuk identitas dan ditempatkan secara teratur dalam waktu
examples.suggested: serangkaian Gate yang komposisinya membentuk identitas dan berjarak teratur dalam waktu
examples.why: "ditempatkan secara teratur dalam waktu" is calqued English word order; "berjarak teratur" is the idiomatic rendering of "regularly spaced" and matches the later "berjarak teratur" used at line 115/133, so the file is also internally inconsistent on this phrase.
