editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every claim tracks the English, including the delicate ones (ZNE "tidak dijamin menghasilkan hasil yang tidak bias", PEC "mengembalikan estimasi ... yang tidak bias. Namun, umumnya menimbulkan overhead yang lebih besar", the quadratic-in-γ / exponential-in-depth scaling, the 3x overhead, the "bisa memperburuk performa" caveat on dynamical decoupling). The informal "kamu" register holds throughout. What a native technical editor would change: (1) "noisy" is rendered two ways — "Circuit berisik" in the PEC section vs "nilai ekspektasi yang noisy" in ZNE/PEA; "berisik" is the auditory sense of noisy and reads wrong for a noise channel. (2) "circuit" splits between "sirkuit" (lines 83, 87) and the kept "Circuit" everywhere else, inside the same sentence at line 83. (3) "some qubits sit idle" is calqued as "beberapa qubit duduk diam" — a native writer would write "menganggur" / "tidak melakukan operasi apa pun". (4) "one of several functional forms" loses "several": "memilih dari salah satu bentuk fungsional" drops the qualifier that there is a menu to pick from. None of these would make a learner believe something false.

examples.source: the effect of an ideal target circuit is expressed as a linear combination of noisy circuits that are actually implementable in practice
examples.translation: efek dari Circuit target ideal dinyatakan sebagai kombinasi linier dari Circuit berisik yang sebenarnya dapat diimplementasikan dalam praktik
examples.suggested: ... kombinasi linier dari Circuit ber-noise (atau: Circuit yang terdampak noise) yang ...
examples.why: "berisik" is the auditory/annoying sense of noisy; the rest of the file keeps "noisy"/"noise" (e.g. line 156 "nilai ekspektasi yang noisy"), so the same concept is rendered two ways.

examples.source: The result is that a single circuit is replaced with a random ensemble of circuits, all with the same ideal effect.
examples.translation: Hasilnya adalah satu sirkuit digantikan dengan ansambel Circuit acak, semuanya dengan efek ideal yang sama.
examples.suggested: Hasilnya adalah satu Circuit digantikan dengan ansambel Circuit acak, ...
examples.why: "sirkuit" and the kept term "Circuit" appear in the same sentence (and again at line 87, "Setiap sirkuit dalam satu baris"); one convention should win within the file.

examples.source: circuits containing gaps in which some qubits sit idle without any operations acting on them
examples.translation: Circuit yang mengandung celah di mana beberapa qubit duduk diam tanpa operasi apa pun yang bekerja pada mereka
examples.suggested: Circuit yang memiliki celah saat sebagian qubit menganggur tanpa ada operasi yang dikenakan padanya
examples.why: "duduk diam" is a word-for-word calque of "sit idle", and "bekerja pada mereka" uses the animate pronoun "mereka" for qubits — an Indonesian technical writer would use "menganggur" and "padanya".

examples.source: For the extrapolation, you can choose from one of several functional forms, including a linear fit or an exponential fit.
examples.translation: Untuk ekstrapolasi, kamu dapat memilih dari salah satu bentuk fungsional, termasuk fit linier atau fit eksponensial.
examples.suggested: Untuk ekstrapolasi, kamu dapat memilih salah satu dari beberapa bentuk fungsional, termasuk fit linier atau fit eksponensial.
examples.why: "several" is dropped, so the sentence no longer conveys that there is a set of forms to pick from; it also leaves "memilih dari salah satu" ungrammatical in Indonesian. Dropped qualifier, not misleading.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the failed/canceled-job rules, the 28-day Instances-vs-Analytics distinction, the 2 s per-sub-job overhead, the 250-microsecond default `rep_delay`, the "56 kali lebih lama daripada Gate `x`" comparison and the `2+0.00035*<num executions>` shortcut all survive intact, and the informal "kamu" register holds everywhere. Two genuine editorial slips: (1) "at the expense of increased state preparation error rate" is softened to "dengan risiko meningkatnya error rate persiapan state" ("with the risk of"), turning a stated cost into a mere possibility; (2) "after PUB elements are broadcasted" becomes "setelah elemen PUB disiarkan", where "disiarkan" is the radio/TV sense of broadcast rather than the array-broadcasting sense (Indonesian Qiskit usage keeps "di-broadcast"). Plus within-file term splits: "job" is kept in English everywhere except "untuk satu pekerjaan" in the `job.usage()` bullet, and "workload" is kept in English (title, "Setelah workload selesai") but rendered "beban kerja" in the opening definition sentence. None of these would teach a false concept, so MINOR rather than FAIL.

examples.source: Note that lowering `rep_delay` decreases the total QPU execution time, but at the expense of increased state preparation error rate
examples.translation: Perlu diperhatikan bahwa menurunkan `rep_delay` mengurangi total waktu eksekusi QPU, tetapi dengan risiko meningkatnya error rate persiapan state
examples.suggested: ... tetapi dengan konsekuensi meningkatnya error rate persiapan state
examples.why: "dengan risiko" (at the risk of) softens a stated, definite trade-off into a possible side effect; the English presents the higher state-preparation error rate as the price you pay, not a chance outcome.

examples.source: where the circuits are those generated after PUB elements are broadcasted
examples.translation: di mana Circuit adalah yang dihasilkan setelah elemen PUB disiarkan
examples.suggested: di mana Circuit adalah yang dihasilkan setelah elemen PUB di-broadcast
examples.why: "disiarkan" is the broadcast-a-signal/air-a-programme sense; here "broadcast" is the array-shape-broadcasting operation on PUB elements, which Indonesian Qiskit material keeps in English.

examples.source: run [`job.usage()`](...) for a single job
examples.translation: jalankan [`job.usage()`](...) untuk satu pekerjaan
examples.suggested: jalankan [`job.usage()`](...) untuk satu job
examples.why: "job" is kept in English in every other occurrence in the file ("Usage single job", "job yang gagal atau dibatalkan", "untuk melihat usage untuk satu job" two bullets later); this single "pekerjaan" breaks the file's own convention.

examples.source: determined by the amount of time a QPU is locked to execute workloads
examples.translation: ditentukan oleh jumlah waktu QPU dikunci untuk mengeksekusi beban kerja
examples.suggested: ... untuk mengeksekusi workload
examples.why: The file's title and body otherwise keep "workload" in English ("Penggunaan workload", "apakah workload sedang berjalan", "Setelah workload selesai"); "beban kerja" in the defining first sentence is the one divergence, right where the term is introduced.

editor_note: No semantic drift: the five-step precision-precedence list, the "job akan gagal jika `twirling` diaktifkan dan hasil perkalian ... lebih kecil dari jumlah shot yang dibutuhkan" caveat, and "Presisi berbanding terbalik dengan penggunaan" all carry the English conditions and quantities intact, and register is uniformly informal "kamu". Four editorial slips: (1) `resilience.pec` is glossed "Opsi mitigasi error probabilistik", which drops "cancellation" and back-reads as "mitigation of probabilistic errors" rather than probabilistic error cancellation — recognizable from the option key, but the descriptive phrase misparses; (2) "Daftar nama gate basis untuk di-unroll ke" is a word-order calque of "to unroll to" that leaves "ke" dangling with no object; (3) a repeated stiff double-relativizer cleft — "maka nilai presisi dari opsi yang digunakan", "yang memiliki prioritas tertinggi (...) yang digunakan", "yang ditentukan sebagai opsi `twirling`, yang digunakan" — where a native writer would use "akan digunakan"; (4) the `zne.noise_factors` default "`(1, 1.5, 2)` untuk `PEA`, dan `(1, 3, 5)` lainnya" omits the head noun ("untuk kasus lainnya"), so "lainnya" hangs off the value. Core terminology is otherwise correct and consistent (presisi, opsi, sirkuit, pengukuran, qubit/gate/shots/backend kept in English).

examples.source: Probabilistic error cancellation mitigation options.
examples.translation: Opsi mitigasi error probabilistik.
examples.suggested: Opsi mitigasi probabilistic error cancellation (PEC).
examples.why: "Cancellation" is dropped, so the phrase reads as "mitigation of probabilistic errors" instead of naming the PEC technique; the option key `resilience.pec` is what keeps it recoverable.

examples.source: List of basis gate names to unroll to
examples.translation: Daftar nama gate basis untuk di-unroll ke
examples.why: Direct calque of the English stranded preposition; Indonesian leaves "ke" with no object and the phrase is ungrammatical.
examples.suggested: Daftar nama basis gate sebagai target unroll

examples.source: then the precision value from the options is used, most notably `default_precision`
examples.translation: maka nilai presisi dari opsi yang digunakan, terutama `default_precision`
examples.suggested: maka nilai presisi dari opsi akan digunakan, terutama `default_precision`
examples.why: Cleft "yang digunakan" without a copula reads stiff; the same pattern recurs in list item 3 and in the "keempat tempat" sentence.

examples.source: `(1, 1.5, 2)` for `PEA`, and `(1, 3, 5)` otherwise
examples.translation: `(1, 1.5, 2)` untuk `PEA`, dan `(1, 3, 5)` lainnya
examples.suggested: `(1, 1.5, 2)` untuk `PEA`, dan `(1, 3, 5)` untuk kasus lainnya
examples.why: "lainnya" is left without a head noun, so it reads as "and other (1, 3, 5)" rather than "otherwise"; meaning is still inferable from context.

editor_note: Judging only the re-written entry 26: the section heading "Dynamical Decoupling" is now rendered "Dekopling Dinamis", which is recognizable and not misleading (the anchor #dynamical-decoupling and the option key `dynamical_decoupling` still carry the English), but it breaks consistency twice inside this same file. The lead-in sentence one screen above it lists the three techniques in English — "opsi default untuk dynamical decoupling, twirling, dan TREX + ZNE" — and its two sibling headings are left untranslated ("### Twirling", "### TREX + ZNE"), so a reader scanning the page sees two English technique headings and one half-Indonesianized one for a term the prose itself just used in English. "Dekopling" is also an ad-hoc loan rather than an established Indonesian rendering; either keep "Dynamical Decoupling" like the siblings, or translate all three consistently. Everything else on the page (nilai ekspektasi, observabel, mitigasi error, informal "kamu" throughout) is faithful and reads naturally.

examples.source: ### Dynamical Decoupling {#dynamical-decoupling}
examples.translation: ### Dekopling Dinamis {#dynamical-decoupling}
examples.suggested: ### Dynamical Decoupling {#dynamical-decoupling}
examples.why: Sibling headings in the same section are left in English (### Twirling, ### TREX + ZNE), and the introductory sentence at line 142 names the technique in English ("opsi default untuk dynamical decoupling, twirling, dan TREX + ZNE"). Translating only this one heading, and with an ad-hoc loan ("dekopling") rather than an established Indonesian term, makes the heading harder to match to the prose and to the `dynamical_decoupling` option key in the code block below it. Not misleading, but a native technical editor would restore the English form or translate all three.

editor_note: No semantic drift: every yes/no answer keeps its polarity (session mode "Ya … waktu jam dinding" vs batch "Tidak. … hanya waktu yang dihabiskan di perangkat keras kuantum"), the "whichever happens last" caveat survives as "mana pun yang terjadi **terakhir**", and the five-lane / two-occupied / three-started example arithmetic is intact. What a native technical editor would change is fluency and register: the "next in line to be run" construction is rendered twice as a predicate-less noun phrase ("job batch Anda berikutnya dalam antrian", "Batch Anda yang berisi enam job berikutnya dalam antrian"), which momentarily reads as "your next batch job in the queue" instead of "is next in line"; "the QPU is committed to the session" becomes the active, slightly off "QPU **berkomitmen ke Session**" (the QPU commits itself) where "dialokasikan/didedikasikan untuk Session" is the natural passive; and the informal-"Anda" convention breaks once inside a single sentence with "Minta administratormu untuk menghubungi dukungan IBM jika Anda membutuhkan…". Minor calques remain ("waktu jam dinding" for wall clock time, "kapasitas yang dipesan" where "dicadangkan" is the standard term for reserved capacity). None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: If there are one or more execution lanes available, and your batch jobs are next in line to be run… Your batch of six jobs is next in line to be run.
examples.translation: Jika ada satu atau lebih execution lanes yang tersedia, dan job batch Anda berikutnya dalam antrian… Batch Anda yang berisi enam job berikutnya dalam antrian.
examples.suggested: …dan job batch Anda berada di urutan berikutnya untuk dijalankan… Batch Anda yang berisi enam job berada di urutan berikutnya untuk dijalankan.
examples.why: "berikutnya dalam antrian" is left without a predicate, so the clause reads as the noun phrase "your next batch job in the queue" rather than the assertion "is next in line"; a native writer would add berada di urutan berikutnya.

examples.source: usage is the wall clock time the QPU is **committed to the session**
examples.translation: penggunaan adalah waktu jam dinding ketika QPU **berkomitmen ke Session**
examples.suggested: penggunaan adalah waktu jam dinding selama QPU **didedikasikan untuk Session**
examples.why: English is passive — the QPU is committed (allocated) to the session; "berkomitmen ke" makes the QPU the one making a commitment, which is unidiomatic for resource allocation, though the relation is still recoverable.

examples.source: Ask your administrator to contact IBM support if you need a different interactive TTL…
examples.translation: Minta administratormu untuk menghubungi dukungan IBM jika Anda membutuhkan interactive TTL…
examples.suggested: Minta administrator Anda untuk menghubungi dukungan IBM jika Anda membutuhkan interactive TTL…
examples.why: The file's convention is "Anda" throughout; the clitic "-mu" appears once in the same sentence as "Anda", an internal register inconsistency.

examples.source: IBM Quantum Network members gain reserved capacity on IBM Quantum QPUs.
examples.translation: Anggota IBM Quantum Network mendapatkan kapasitas yang dipesan di QPU IBM Quantum®.
examples.suggested: …mendapatkan kapasitas yang dicadangkan pada QPU IBM Quantum®.
examples.why: "dipesan" reads as "ordered/booked"; the standard Indonesian rendering of reserved capacity in an infrastructure sense is "kapasitas yang dicadangkan".

editor_note: No semantic drift: every claim tracks the English, including the precedence rule ("nilai yang ditetapkan setelah menginisialisasi primitif yang digunakan"), the copy-semantics caveat ("mengubah dictionary atau instansi opsi asli tidak mempengaruhi opsi yang dimiliki primitif"), and all option defaults/ranges (10800 (3 jam), init_qubits, rep_delay). Register is consistently informal ("Kamu bisa…"), and domain terms are left in English per convention (qubit, shot, ground state, quantum circuit, backend, dictionary, primitif). Two things a native technical editor would change: (1) "instance" is rendered as "instansi" three times — in Indonesian "instansi" means a government agency/institution; the field uses "instance" (or "instans"), so "instansi kelas opsi" reads as a false friend; (2) the precedence sentence at line 50 is a stiff calque with a dangling cleft ("…baik saat maupun setelah…, nilai yang ditetapkan setelah menginisialisasi primitif yang digunakan") — grammatical and correct, but not how a native writer would build it. Neither misleads the learner.

examples.source: You can pass in an instance of the options class … changing the original dictionary or options instance doesn't affect the options owned by the primitive.
examples.translation: Kamu bisa meneruskan instansi kelas opsi atau dictionary … mengubah dictionary atau instansi opsi asli tidak mempengaruhi opsi yang dimiliki primitif.
examples.suggested: Kamu bisa meneruskan instance dari kelas opsi … mengubah dictionary atau instance opsi asli tidak memengaruhi opsi yang dimiliki primitif.
examples.why: "Instansi" in Indonesian means a government body/agency; the programming sense of "instance" is normally kept in English (or "instans"). Recognizable in context, so MINOR, but a native technical editor would not write "instansi kelas Executor" (also at line 58).

examples.source: If an option is specified both during and after primitive initialization, the value set after initializing the primitive is used.
examples.translation: Jika suatu opsi ditentukan baik saat maupun setelah inisialisasi primitif, nilai yang ditetapkan setelah menginisialisasi primitif yang digunakan.
examples.suggested: Jika sebuah opsi ditentukan saat inisialisasi primitif sekaligus setelahnya, yang dipakai adalah nilai yang ditetapkan setelah inisialisasi.
examples.why: Word-order calque of the English: "baik … maupun …" plus a trailing "yang digunakan" leaves the clause hanging, and "inisialisasi primitif" is repeated verbatim. Meaning is correct — only the phrasing is stiff.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every claim (28-day rolling window, the Flex Plan caveat repeated in both bullets, "twice the minutes → twice the workloads", enterprise child-account two-step distribution, FIFO within an instance) matches the English, and the informal "Anda" register holds throughout. Three editorial slips remain. (1) "the scheduler will select the oldest workload first" is rendered "memilih workload yang paling lama terlebih dahulu" — bare "paling lama" reads more naturally as "the longest(-running)" than "the oldest (queued)"; "workload tertua" or "yang paling lama menunggu" is the unambiguous rendering (recoverable from the FIFO sentence that follows, hence minor). (2) "With all else being equal" is calqued as "Dengan semua hal lain yang sama" instead of idiomatic "Jika hal lain sama" / "dengan asumsi kondisi lainnya sama". (3) "base-level construct" → "Konstruk tingkat dasar" and "overarching account" → "akun utama" are stiff/flattened; a native technical writer would write "konstruk paling dasar" and "akun induk/menyeluruh".

examples.source: If the selected instance has submitted more than one workload, the scheduler will select the oldest workload first.
examples.translation: Jika instance yang dipilih telah mengirimkan lebih dari satu workload, penjadwal akan memilih workload yang paling lama terlebih dahulu.
examples.suggested: ... penjadwal akan memilih workload tertua (yang paling lama menunggu) terlebih dahulu.
examples.why: Bare 'paling lama' most readily means 'the longest (in duration)' rather than 'the oldest (earliest submitted)'. The following FIFO sentence rescues the meaning, so it is a minor ambiguity, not a misleading claim.

examples.source: With all else being equal, an instance with twice the number of minutes can execute twice the number of workloads.
examples.translation: Dengan semua hal lain yang sama, instance dengan dua kali jumlah menit dapat mengeksekusi dua kali jumlah workload.
examples.suggested: Jika hal lainnya sama, instance dengan jumlah menit dua kali lipat dapat mengeksekusi workload dua kali lebih banyak.
examples.why: 'Dengan semua hal lain yang sama' is a word-for-word calque of 'all else being equal'; 'dua kali jumlah menit' is likewise English word order. Indonesian technical prose puts the multiplier after the noun ('dua kali lipat').

examples.source: The base-level construct to which time is allocated from the overarching account to a set of QPUs
examples.translation: Konstruk tingkat dasar yang menerima alokasi waktu dari akun utama untuk sejumlah QPU
examples.suggested: Konstruk paling dasar yang menerima alokasi waktu dari akun induk untuk sekumpulan QPU
examples.why: 'Konstruk tingkat dasar' is a stiff calque of 'base-level construct', and 'akun utama' flattens 'overarching account' (the parent/umbrella account) into a vaguer 'main account'. Defensible but not what a native technical writer would write.

editor_note: The one re-written entry (the sample citation sentence, line 28) is semantically faithful: "salah satu prosesor IBM Quantum Canary" correctly renders "one of the IBM Quantum Canary processors" — no drift, no invented claim, `ibmq_vigo` and the Canary family name preserved verbatim, and the informal "kami" (authorial we) matches the quoted-paper voice. The only editorial slip is within-file term inconsistency: this entry says "Dalam paper ini", while the surrounding paragraphs of the same section consistently use "makalah" for paper ("Untuk makalah penelitian", "Referensi makalah harus menggunakan kutipan berikut", "Unit pemrosesan kuantum dalam makalah"). A native technical editor would align it to "Dalam makalah ini kami menggunakan ..." so the sample citation matches the guidance immediately above it. This misleads no learner — it is a consistency nit only.

examples.source: > In this paper we used `ibmq_vigo`, which is one of the IBM Quantum Canary processors.
examples.translation: > Dalam paper ini kami menggunakan `ibmq_vigo`, salah satu prosesor IBM Quantum Canary.
examples.suggested: > Dalam makalah ini kami menggunakan `ibmq_vigo`, salah satu prosesor IBM Quantum Canary.
examples.why: "paper" is left in English here while the same section renders it "makalah" three times (lines 18, 22, 26). Meaning is correct either way, so this is a consistency nit, not a drift: the sample citation should use the same word as the instruction paragraph that introduces it.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the angle constraint ($0 \lt \theta \leq \pi/2$), the "only if the related real backend supports them" conditional, the FoldRzzAngle caveat and the "measurement twirling with TREX *is* supported" exception all survive intact, and the informal "kamu" register is consistent. Four editorial slips: (1) "arbitrary angle" is rendered "sudut yang sewenang-wenang" twice (§Cara menggunakan) — "sewenang-wenang" carries the sense of arbitrary-as-despotic; the mathematical term a native technical writer uses is "sudut sembarang". (2) "Example:" before the FakeBoston snippet is left untranslated ("Contoh:"). (3) "circuit" is rendered "Circuit" everywhere except inside the Admonition, where it becomes "sirkuit" — one stray split. (4) "error-suppressed" is softened to "lebih tahan error" (error-tolerant), which shifts the claim from errors being suppressed to the circuit resisting them. None of these would mislead a learner about how fractional gates work.

examples.source: directly executing an $R_{ZZ}(\theta)$ and $R_X(\theta)$ rotation for an arbitrary angle
examples.translation: langsung menjalankan rotasi $R_{ZZ}(\theta)$ dan $R_X(\theta)$ untuk sudut yang sewenang-wenang
examples.suggested: langsung menjalankan rotasi $R_{ZZ}(\theta)$ dan $R_X(\theta)$ untuk sudut sembarang
examples.why: "sewenang-wenang" is arbitrary in the sense of high-handed/capricious; Indonesian technical writing uses "sembarang" for the mathematical sense. Same slip repeats in the next sentence ("rotasi satu-Qubit dengan sudut sewenang-wenang").

examples.source: Example:
examples.translation: Example:
examples.suggested: Contoh:
examples.why: A plain prose label left in English between two translated paragraphs; it is not a kept domain term.

examples.source: especially when the dominant source of error in a circuit is due to relaxation
examples.translation: terutama ketika sumber error dominan dalam sebuah sirkuit disebabkan oleh relaksasi
examples.suggested: terutama ketika sumber error dominan dalam sebuah Circuit disebabkan oleh relaksasi
examples.why: The file otherwise renders "circuit" as "Circuit" (durasi Circuit, kedalaman Circuit, Circuit kuantum); this is the single place it becomes "sirkuit".

examples.source: create a more efficient (and thus error-suppressed) quantum circuit
examples.translation: menciptakan Circuit kuantum yang lebih efisien (dan dengan demikian lebih tahan error)
examples.suggested: menciptakan Circuit kuantum yang lebih efisien (dan dengan demikian errornya lebih tertekan / lebih rendah error)
examples.why: "lebih tahan error" says the circuit tolerates errors better (an error-resilience claim, cf. error correction), whereas the English says fewer errors are introduced in the first place. The nuance flattens but does not invert the lesson.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every quantity survives intact (1000 randomization → 11 PUB × 1000 ≈ 11.000 instance sirkuit; 100 × 200 = 20.000 shot per observable; 26,8 juta instruksi per qubit, "per job bukan per PUB"; `batches=4` → "kira-kira tiga PUB per job alih-alih sebelas"), the "replaces the defaults wholesale rather than merging" caveat is restated correctly in both places ("mengganti default secara keseluruhan alih-alih digabung ke dalamnya"), and register is consistently informal ("kamu"/"-mu"). What a native technical editor would change is a cluster of literal calques: "Bake any local kick into this circuit" is rendered as the oven-sense "Panggang (bake) kick lokal apa pun ke dalam sirkuit ini" (native: "Sertakan/masukkan"); "The `[extras]` syntax is honored" as "Sintaks `[extras]` dihormati" (native: "didukung"); and two English imperative-plus-"and" constructions are transplanted whole — "Melebihi kapasitas yang bisa ditampung sistem kontrol dan job akan gagal" and "hilangkan dan fungsi akan mengambil yang paling tidak sibuk" — where Indonesian needs "Jika ...". Also "langkah-langkah selanjutnya yang lebih terentangle" (English stem with an Indonesian affix), "siklus hidup job secara kasar" for "coarse lifecycle" (kasar reads as rough/rude; "garis besar" is the idiom), and "Tempel ID yang kamu simpan di atas placeholder", which reads as "paste above the placeholder" rather than "paste over/replacing it" — the only spot that could briefly misdirect, though the untranslated code comment in the next cell ("Replace the ID that follows with your own") resolves it.

examples.source: Bake any local kick into this circuit.
examples.translation: Panggang (bake) kick lokal apa pun ke dalam sirkuit ini.
examples.suggested: Sertakan kick lokal apa pun ke dalam sirkuit ini.
examples.why: "Panggang" is the oven sense of "bake"; the English here is the idiom "build in / incorporate". The parenthetical "(bake)" rescues the meaning, but a native technical writer would use "sertakan"/"masukkan".

examples.source: Exceed what the control system holds and the job fails with error 6073.
examples.translation: Melebihi kapasitas yang bisa ditampung sistem kontrol dan job akan gagal dengan [error 6073].
examples.suggested: Jika kapasitas yang bisa ditampung sistem kontrol terlampaui, job akan gagal dengan [error 6073].
examples.why: The English imperative-plus-"and" conditional is transplanted verbatim; Indonesian has no equivalent construction, so the clause reads as a dangling gerund. Same pattern again at line 335: "hilangkan dan fungsi akan mengambil yang paling tidak sibuk".

examples.source: Paste your saved ID over the placeholder in the following reconnect cell.
examples.translation: Tempel ID yang kamu simpan di atas placeholder pada cell sambung kembali berikut.
examples.suggested: Ganti placeholder pada cell sambung kembali berikut dengan ID yang kamu simpan.
examples.why: "di atas placeholder" is naturally read as "above the placeholder" (position), not "over/replacing it". The only rendering in the file with any potential to misdirect an action; the English code comment in the next cell still says "Replace the ID that follows with your own", so it does not actually mislead.

examples.source: The `[extras]` syntax is honored
examples.translation: Sintaks `[extras]` dihormati
examples.suggested: Sintaks `[extras]` didukung
examples.why: "dihormati" is the social sense of "honored" (to show respect); for a package-manager feature Indonesian uses "didukung"/"diperhatikan". Same calque family as "dipin ke versi yang diizinkan" in the same sentence ("disematkan"/"dikunci" is the term).

examples.source: later, more-entangled steps need a deeper one
examples.translation: langkah-langkah selanjutnya yang lebih terentangle membutuhkan yang lebih dalam
examples.suggested: langkah-langkah selanjutnya yang keterjeratannya lebih tinggi membutuhkan ansatz yang lebih dalam
examples.why: "terentangle" welds an Indonesian passive prefix onto an English stem — a hybrid no Indonesian technical writer would produce; the file elsewhere keeps the noun "entanglement" unchanged, so the verb form is also internally inconsistent.

examples.source: `status()` reports both the coarse job lifecycle and the per-stage sub-status
examples.translation: `status()` melaporkan baik siklus hidup job secara kasar maupun sub-status per tahap
examples.suggested: `status()` melaporkan siklus hidup job secara garis besar sekaligus sub-status per tahap
examples.why: "secara kasar" primarily reads as rough/crude (or rude) rather than "coarse-grained"; "garis besar" carries the granularity contrast the English draws against the per-stage sub-status.

examples.source: Nothing about the science code changes.
examples.translation: Tidak ada yang berubah tentang kode ilmiahnya.
examples.suggested: Kode ilmiahnya sendiri tidak berubah sama sekali.
examples.why: "tentang" calques the English "about"; in Indonesian "tidak ada yang berubah tentang X" is not idiomatic. Meaning is preserved, but the sentence reads as machine output at a point where the English is deliberately emphatic.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — every quantitative claim survives intact (20.000–200.000 shots for <16 orbital molekul, 600/1500/6000/16000 sampel per batch for metanol/metilamina/air/etanol, "hanya memiliki koneksi di setiap qubit keempat", "batch energi terendah diambil sebagai solusi"), the conditionals and caveats are preserved, and the informal "kamu" register holds consistently. What a native technical editor would still change: (1) "distribusi angka okupersi ground-state" (line 62) — "okupersi" is not an Indonesian word; the term for occupation/occupancy is "okupansi" (and elsewhere in the guide the concept is left untranslated), so the learner meets a malformed term; (2) "studi SQD [non-kovalent]" (line 64) — the Indonesian adjective is "kovalen", not "kovalent"; (3) two AccordionItem titles use "Klik untuk memperluas demi detail/info lebih lanjut" — "demi" is a purpose-with-sacrifice preposition and reads wrong here, a native writer would write "untuk detail lebih lanjut"; (4) "parameter SQD run" (line 51) leaves "run" as a raw English noun inside an Indonesian noun phrase, a calque of "SQD run parameters"; (5) "informasi yang berguna tentang kemajuan workflow" (line 310) flattens the English "actionable information" to merely "useful". None of these would mislead a learner about the physics or the workflow.

examples.source: to obtain the initial approximation to the ground-state occupation number distribution
examples.translation: untuk mendapatkan aproksimasi awal distribusi angka okupersi ground-state
examples.suggested: untuk mendapatkan aproksimasi awal distribusi bilangan okupansi ground-state
examples.why: "okupersi" is not a word in Indonesian — the loan from "occupancy/occupation" is "okupansi". Recognizable from context (so MINOR, not FAIL), but it is a malformed term in the one sentence that explains why the shot count must be large. "angka" is also weaker than "bilangan" for a quantum occupation number.

examples.source: [non-covalent](...), [fragment-based](...), and [implicit solvent](...) SQD studies suggest
examples.translation: studi SQD [non-kovalent](...), [berbasis fragmen](...), dan [pelarut implisit](...) menyarankan
examples.suggested: studi SQD [nonkovalen](...), [berbasis fragmen](...), dan [pelarut implisit](...) menunjukkan
examples.why: The Indonesian adjective is "kovalen" (nonkovalen), not "kovalent" — the trailing -t is an English/German spelling carried over. Note the sibling term in the same list, "berbasis fragmen", is correctly nativized, so the file is inconsistent about nativizing chemistry adjectives.

examples.source: Click to expand for more details on the required options:
examples.translation: Klik untuk memperluas demi detail lebih lanjut tentang opsi yang diperlukan:
examples.suggested: Klik untuk melihat detail lebih lanjut tentang opsi yang diperlukan:
examples.why: "demi" means "for the sake of" and carries a connotation of sacrifice or lofty purpose — no Indonesian technical writer would use it to render the purposive "for" in a UI affordance. It appears twice (also "demi info lebih lanjut" at line 83), so the calque is systematic rather than a one-off slip.

examples.source: For this template you must specify options for generating the LUCJ circuit, and SQD run parameters.
examples.translation: Untuk template ini kamu harus menentukan opsi untuk menghasilkan Circuit LUCJ, dan parameter SQD run.
examples.suggested: Untuk template ini kamu harus menentukan opsi untuk menghasilkan Circuit LUCJ dan parameter untuk menjalankan SQD.
examples.why: "parameter SQD run" transplants the English noun-stack word order intact; "run" is a bare English noun with no Indonesian syntactic anchor, unlike the deliberately kept brand/domain terms (Circuit, Sampler, shots). A native writer would verbalize it as "parameter untuk menjalankan SQD" or "parameter eksekusi SQD".

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I checked the tip block on `run()` ("langsung memunculkan error alih-alih membiarkan job gagal di antrean", `suppress_low_usage_warning=True` → "untuk mematikannya"), the whole job-status list, and the runtime-jobs note ("hanya melaporkan runtime job-nya ketika ia mengirimkannya melalui runtime service yang diterima fungsi tersebut saat runtime"); no inverted condition, swapped quantity or hallucinated claim, and the informal "kamu" register holds. The real defect is incompleteness, not drift: the two paragraphs that begin with an inline `<span id="…">` anchor are left entirely in English — the trusted-environment `save_account()` paragraph (translation line 76, "If you are working in a trusted Python environment…") and the security caveat at line 103 ("Avoid executing code on an untrusted machine or an external cloud Python environment…"), which also carries the advice to rotate the API key after each use. An Indonesian-only reader gets no guidance at exactly the two security-relevant spots, and this looks systematic (both untranslated blocks are the span-prefixed ones), so it is worth a pipeline check rather than a per-file patch. Smaller: "function" is rendered as English `function` everywhere except the runtime-jobs Admonition, where it switches to "fungsi" twice; and "partner" (line 42) vs "mitra" (line 38) for the same catalog-partner concept.

examples.source: **If you are working in a trusted Python environment (such as on a personal laptop or workstation),** use the `save_account()` method to save your credentials locally. ([Skip to the next step](#functions-untrusted) if you are not using a trusted environment…)
examples.translation: **If you are working in a trusted Python environment (such as on a personal laptop or workstation),** use the `save_account()` method to save your credentials locally. ([Skip to the next step](#functions-untrusted) if you are not using a trusted environment…)
examples.suggested: **Jika kamu bekerja di environment Python yang tepercaya (misalnya di laptop atau workstation pribadi),** gunakan metode `save_account()` untuk menyimpan kredensialmu secara lokal. ([Lompat ke langkah berikutnya](#functions-untrusted) jika kamu tidak menggunakan environment tepercaya, seperti komputer bersama atau komputer publik, untuk mengautentikasi ke IBM Quantum Platform.)
examples.why: Paragraph left wholly untranslated. It is the branch point of the whole authentication section — an Indonesian-only reader cannot tell which of the two code paths applies to them. Both untranslated blocks start with an inline `<span id=…>` anchor, suggesting the extractor skipped them.

examples.source: **Avoid executing code on an untrusted machine or an external cloud Python environment to minimize security risks.** If you must use an untrusted environment … change your API key after each use by deleting it on the IBM Cloud API keys page to reduce risk.
examples.translation: **Avoid executing code on an untrusted machine or an external cloud Python environment to minimize security risks.** If you must use an untrusted environment … change your API key after each use by deleting it on the IBM Cloud API keys page to reduce risk.
examples.suggested: **Hindari menjalankan kode di mesin yang tidak tepercaya atau di environment Python cloud eksternal untuk meminimalkan risiko keamanan.** Jika kamu terpaksa menggunakan environment yang tidak tepercaya (misalnya di komputer publik), ganti API key kamu setelah setiap penggunaan dengan menghapusnya di halaman [IBM Cloud API keys](…) untuk mengurangi risiko.
examples.why: Second untranslated paragraph, and the one carrying the security caveat (rotate/delete the API key after use on an untrusted machine). The neighbouring danger Admonition *is* translated, so the page reads as if the caveat were incidental English boilerplate.

examples.source: A function reports its runtime jobs only when it submits them through the runtime service … and some functions do not submit runtime jobs directly.
examples.translation: Sebuah fungsi hanya melaporkan runtime job-nya ketika ia mengirimkannya melalui runtime service … dan beberapa fungsi tidak mengirimkan runtime job secara langsung.
examples.suggested: Sebuah function hanya melaporkan runtime job-nya ketika ia mengirimkannya melalui runtime service … dan beberapa function tidak mengirimkan runtime job secara langsung.
examples.why: Every other occurrence in the file keeps the product term as English `function` ("memilih function", "Setiap Qiskit Function", "function tertentu"); this Admonition alone switches to "fungsi", which reads as the generic mathematical/programming sense rather than a Qiskit Function. Same pattern as "mitra" (line 38) vs "partner" (line 42).

editor_note: No misleading drift: every provider row's claims survive intact (Qedma's "unbiased expectation values" → "nilai ekspektasi tak bias", Q-CTRL's "zero-overhead ... compatible with any weight of observables" → "kompatibel dengan observable berbobot apa pun", Kipu's "solved within hours" → "diselesaikan dalam hitungan jam"), register is consistently neutral-informal, and no hallucinated sentences appear. Three editor-level slips: (1) the two section headings half-translate the product terms ("Fungsi circuit" / "Fungsi aplikasi") while every table cell keeps them untranslated as "Circuit function" / "Application function", so the same concept is named two ways within the file; (2) "deep circuits" is rendered "Circuit dalam", which in Indonesian reads ambiguously as "circuit inside/within" rather than "circuit berkedalaman tinggi" — a native writer would add "yang dalam" or rephrase; (3) Qunova's unbounded "by orders of magnitude" becomes the capped "hingga beberapa orde besaran" ("up to several orders of magnitude"), a small softening of the claim. None of these would cause a learner to form a false belief.

examples.source: ### Circuit functions / ### Application functions (vs. table cells "Circuit function", "Application function")
examples.translation: ### Fungsi circuit / ### Fungsi aplikasi (tabel: "Circuit function", "Application function")
examples.suggested: Pick one convention: either "Circuit function"/"Application function" in the headings too, or "Fungsi sirkuit"/"Fungsi aplikasi" throughout.
examples.why: The headings coin a half-translated hybrid that never reappears in the body, so the reader sees the same product category named two different ways on one page.

examples.source: Workloads that contain parametric circuits, deep circuits, or require many circuit executions.
examples.translation: Beban kerja yang mengandung Circuit parametrik, Circuit dalam, atau memerlukan banyak eksekusi Circuit.
examples.suggested: ... Circuit parametrik, Circuit dengan kedalaman tinggi, atau yang memerlukan banyak eksekusi Circuit.
examples.why: "Circuit dalam" is a calque; without a qualifier "dalam" reads first as the preposition "inside/within", not as circuit depth.

examples.source: ... outperforming some classical solutions on supercomputers or standard SQD in convergence speed or accuracy, respectively, by orders of magnitude.
examples.translation: ... melampaui beberapa solusi klasik di superkomputer atau SQD standar dalam kecepatan konvergensi atau akurasi, masing-masing hingga beberapa orde besaran.
examples.suggested: ... masing-masing sebesar beberapa orde besaran.
examples.why: "hingga" turns an unqualified "by orders of magnitude" into a ceiling ("up to"), slightly softening the vendor claim.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat: the mode/object mapping in step 3 ("objek `batch`, `session`, atau `backend` untuk mode eksekusi batch, session, dan job, masing-masing") preserves the "respectively" pairing, the Open Plan restriction and the "fitur eksperimental dan mungkin berubah" caveat both survive, and the informal "kamu/-mu" register holds from start to finish. The one editorial defect is a within-file split on the core term "circuit": it is kept as "Circuit" everywhere (intro, step 2 heading, ISA paragraph, step 4) but rendered as Indonesian "sirkuit" once, in the very first sentence of step 2 — the same referent named two ways two lines apart, which a native technical editor would normalize. Not misleading (the concept stays identifiable), so MINOR only. A secondary nit worth mentioning but not counted: "Tinjau [contoh-contoh] detail" in Next steps postposes the adjective onto a reduplicated noun and reads slightly stiff versus "Tinjau contoh detail".

examples.source: You need at least one circuit and one observable as inputs to the Estimator primitive.
examples.translation: Kamu membutuhkan setidaknya satu sirkuit dan satu observabel sebagai input ke primitif Estimator.
examples.suggested: Kamu membutuhkan setidaknya satu Circuit dan satu observabel sebagai input ke primitif Estimator.
examples.why: "circuit" is rendered "sirkuit" here but "Circuit" in the intro ("Circuit bisa terparameterisasi"), in the heading directly above it ("Buat Circuit dan observabel"), in the ISA paragraph and in step 4. One term, two spellings, two lines apart — inconsistent, though the concept stays identifiable.

examples.source: Review detailed [examples](/guides/estimator-examples).

examples.suggested: Tinjau [contoh detail](/guides/estimator-examples).

editor_note: The one re-written entry (the H1) is semantically faithful — "Quantum Portfolio Optimizer: Sebuah Qiskit Function oleh Global Data Quantum" preserves the product name, the "Qiskit Function" kept term, the attribution to Global Data Quantum and the heading anchor; nothing here could mislead a learner. The only thing a native technical editor would change is the article calque "Sebuah" in a heading: Indonesian headings normally drop the English indefinite "A", so "Quantum Portfolio Optimizer: Qiskit Function dari Global Data Quantum" reads like an Indonesian-written title while "Sebuah …" reads as translated-from-English. It is consistent with the frontmatter description ("Sebuah Qiskit Function untuk menyelesaikan …"), where the article sits more naturally in running prose, so this is cosmetic only. Surrounding context (unjudged) is sound: informal "kamu" register holds throughout, and domain terms (qubit, ansatz, optimizer, trajektori investasi, "diproses pasca-komputasi dengan SQD") are correct and consistent.

examples.source: Quantum Portfolio Optimizer: A Qiskit Function by Global Data Quantum
examples.translation: Quantum Portfolio Optimizer: Sebuah Qiskit Function oleh Global Data Quantum
examples.suggested: Quantum Portfolio Optimizer: Qiskit Function dari Global Data Quantum
examples.why: "Sebuah" is a direct calque of the English indefinite article "A"; Indonesian headings and titles normally omit it. Meaning is unaffected — purely a fluency/register polish, not a semantic defect.

editor_note: Faithful and natural throughout: the HA/DR framing is preserved exactly ("tetap beroperasi dan dapat diakses meski terjadi kegagalan yang tidak terduga", "Pelanggan ... tidak bertanggung jawab atas perencanaan atau tindakan disaster recovery"), the zonal-failure claim keeps its strength ("Tidak ada penurunan layanan yang terasa selama kegagalan zona"), and infrastructure terms are correctly kept in English and used consistently (high availability, disaster recovery, load balancer, node instans HA, region multi-zona).

No semantic drift or hallucination: every quantitative and conditional claim survives intact (⟨Z1Z0⟩ "seharusnya 1" vs. the product "seharusnya nol"; "lebih dari 100 qubit dan lebih dari 1000 Gate"; "menurun seiring meningkatnya $i$, meskipun dalam simulasi ideal semua ... seharusnya 1"; the "hanya memungkinkan untuk Circuit kecil" caveat is kept). What a native technical editor would change: (1) "entangled/entanglement" is rendered two ways — "dua qubit saling terjalin sepenuhnya" / "keadaan terjalin" early on, then "keterikatan kuantum" at the Step-4 payoff line, so the file's headline concept does not carry one label; "terjalin" (= interwoven) is also a weak choice next to the established "keterbelitan/keterikatan". (2) The Anda/kamu register flips inside single paragraphs ("Komputer kuantum ... jadi biasanya Anda mengumpulkan sampel ... Kamu bisa memperkirakan nilai observabel"; same in Step 4). (3) "Ini memerlukan bahwa Anda sudah ..." is a literal calque of "It requires that you have already ...", used twice. (4) Two stiff spots: the stacked relative clauses in "Nilai ekspektasi antara qubit yang jauh yang semakin tidak akurat (rusak)" and the non-standard "Saat Anda melakukan skalasi" (should be "penskalaan"/"menskalakan"). None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: two qubits are fully entangled with each other … If the state is entangled … This is a hallmark of quantum entanglement.
examples.translation: dua qubit saling terjalin sepenuhnya … Jika keadaannya terjalin … Ini adalah ciri khas keterikatan kuantum.
examples.suggested: Pick one convention and use it throughout, e.g. "dua qubit saling terbelit sepenuhnya" / "Jika keadaannya terbelit" / "ciri khas keterbelitan kuantum" (or keterikatan/terikat consistently).
examples.why: The file's central concept is labelled "terjalin" (interwoven) in Step 1 and "keterikatan" in the Step-4 conclusion, so the learner cannot connect the setup to the payoff by term alone. Still recognizable from context, so MINOR.

examples.source: You can estimate the value of the observable by using the `Estimator` class. … You might feed these results into another workflow for further analysis
examples.translation: Kamu bisa memperkirakan nilai observabel menggunakan kelas `Estimator`. … Kamu bisa memasukkan hasil ini ke dalam alur kerja lain untuk analisis lebih lanjut
examples.suggested: Anda bisa memperkirakan nilai observabel … / Anda bisa memasukkan hasil ini …
examples.why: Both sentences sit inside paragraphs that otherwise address the reader as "Anda" ("biasanya Anda mengumpulkan sampel", "langkah ini spesifik untuk masalahmu"), so the second-person form flips mid-paragraph.

examples.source: It requires that you have already saved your credentials
examples.translation: Ini memerlukan bahwa Anda sudah [menyimpan kredensialmu](/guides/cloud-setup).
examples.suggested: Kode ini mengharuskan Anda sudah menyimpan kredensial Anda.
examples.why: "memerlukan bahwa" is a direct calque of the English "requires that"; Indonesian technical writing uses "mengharuskan Anda sudah …". Appears identically in both Step 2 sections.

examples.source: Increasingly inaccurate (corrupted) expectation values between distant qubits would reveal the level of noise present.
examples.translation: Nilai ekspektasi antara qubit yang jauh yang semakin tidak akurat (rusak) akan mengungkapkan tingkat noise yang ada.
examples.suggested: Nilai ekspektasi antar-qubit yang berjauhan akan semakin tidak akurat (rusak), dan itu menunjukkan tingkat noise yang ada.
examples.why: Two stacked "yang" clauses make the subject hard to parse on first read; the meaning is right but a native technical writer would split the modifier off.

examples.source: When you scale up in the next section, you will need to use a real device.
examples.translation: Saat Anda melakukan skalasi di bagian berikutnya, Anda perlu menggunakan perangkat nyata.
examples.suggested: Saat Anda menskalakan program di bagian berikutnya, Anda perlu menggunakan perangkat nyata.
examples.why: "skalasi" is not a standard Indonesian noun; the file itself uses the correct verb form elsewhere ("Skalakan ke jumlah qubit yang besar", "menskalakan program sederhana tersebut").

editor_note: Judging only the two rewritten Card entries ("Learning" / "Learning paths"): both descriptions are semantically faithful and read naturally — "Jelajahi penawaran pembelajaran gratis kami, seperti kursus lengkap dan modul kelas." and "…rangkaian pembelajaran, dokumentasi, dan konten tutorial yang dikurasi…" carry the English meaning with no drift, invention or dropped caveat, and "Jalur pembelajaran" is the right rendering of "Learning paths". Two editorial slips remain, neither misleading. (1) The visible call-to-action text is left in English in exactly these two cards — linkText="Visit IBM Quantum Learning" and linkText="Explore learning paths" — while every neighbouring card on the same page translates it ("Mulai membangun", "Jelajahi tutorial", "Baca ikhtisar", "Dapatkan bantuan"), so the reader hits two untranslated buttons in an otherwise Indonesian card group. (2) In entry 13 the qualifier "designed to" is compressed away ("designed to facilitate knowledge and skill-building" → "untuk membantu membangun pengetahuan dan keterampilan"), losing the sense that the sequences are deliberately curated for that purpose; "dirancang untuk memfasilitasi…" would restore it.

examples.translation: linkText="Visit IBM Quantum Learning"
examples.suggested: linkText="Kunjungi IBM Quantum Learning"
examples.why: Visible button text left untranslated in the rewritten card, while all other cards on the page translate linkText ("Mulai membangun", "Jelajahi tutorial"). Inconsistent UI language within one card group; product name IBM Quantum Learning should stay English, the verb should not.

examples.translation: linkText="Explore learning paths"

examples.why: Plain English call-to-action with no brand component left untranslated, even though the card's own title was translated to "Jalur pembelajaran" two lines above — a within-file inconsistency a native editor would fix.

examples.source: Explore curated sequences of learning, documentation, and tutorial content designed to facilitate knowledge and skill-building in specific interest areas.
