examples.why: "designed to" is dropped, softening the claim that the sequences were deliberately built for skill-building into a vaguer "untuk membantu". Meaning is still recognizable, so minor rather than misleading.

editor_note: Judging only the delta entry: the section heading "UNIX-like" was rewritten to "Mirip UNIX", which is semantically accurate and not misleading. The problem is consistency of the section's own name inside this file: the body sentence directly under it still reads "instruksi build untuk sistem UNIX-like", and the two cross-references that point at this exact section keep the English label — "seperti yang dilakukan pada bagian [UNIX-like](#unix)" (Windows intro) and "seperti dijelaskan di bagian [UNIX-like](#unix)" (Build the standalone library). A reader following either link lands on a heading called "Mirip UNIX", so the section is referred to by two different names. Either translate the link labels to "Mirip UNIX" as well, or leave the heading as "UNIX-like" like the surrounding prose. No drift, no hallucination, informal "kamu" register holds throughout.

examples.source: ## UNIX-like  …  build instructions for UNIX-like systems  …  as is done in the [UNIX-like](#unix) section
examples.translation: ## Mirip UNIX  …  instruksi build untuk sistem UNIX-like  …  seperti yang dilakukan pada bagian [UNIX-like](#unix)
examples.suggested: Align the section's name: either heading "## UNIX-like", or translate the link labels and body to "Mirip UNIX" too
examples.why: The delta rewrote only the heading, so the same section is now named "Mirip UNIX" at its title and "UNIX-like" at both cross-references and in the sentence right beneath it — a within-file naming split a native technical editor would normalize. Meaning is unaffected.

editor_note: Semantically faithful throughout — no drift, no dropped caveat, no hallucination; the prerequisite ordering ("Sebelum menginstal `qiskit-ibm-runtime`, ikuti instruksi di panduan-panduan berikut"), the periodic-check advice, and the four "Rekomendasi" bullets all match the English exactly, and the informal register (kamu / -mu: "akun IBM Cloud-mu", "program pertamamu", "kebutuhanmu") is consistent with no deferential slips. The one thing a native technical editor would change is "memperbarui kebutuhanmu untuk `qiskit-ibm-runtime`" for "updating your requirements for qiskit-ibm-runtime": here "requirements" means the pinned dependency/version requirement (requirements.txt), and "kebutuhan" ("needs") is a calque — Indonesian devs would write "persyaratan versi" or simply keep "requirements". It is understandable in context and does not teach a false concept, so it stays MINOR. Nothing else in the file warrants a change.

examples.source: We recommend frequently updating your requirements for `qiskit-ibm-runtime` by running `pip install -U qiskit-ibm-runtime`.
examples.translation: Kami menyarankan untuk sering memperbarui kebutuhanmu untuk `qiskit-ibm-runtime` dengan menjalankan `pip install -U qiskit-ibm-runtime`.
examples.suggested: Kami menyarankan untuk sering memperbarui persyaratan versi (requirements) `qiskit-ibm-runtime` dengan menjalankan `pip install -U qiskit-ibm-runtime`.
examples.why: "requirements" here is the packaging term (the pinned dependency spec), not the user's "needs"; "kebutuhanmu" is a literal calque that an Indonesian developer would not write. Meaning is still recoverable from context, so MINOR.

editor_note: The one re-written entry ("Install Qiskit" → "Instal Qiskit") is semantically faithful — nothing is added, dropped, negated or softened, and the anchor is preserved — so it cannot mislead a learner. The only editorial slip is spelling consistency: this heading now reads "Instal Qiskit" while the two sibling headings in the same file still read "Install Qiskit SDK dari sumber" (line 14) and "Install compiler Rust" (line 72), and the body mixes both forms too ("Install `qiskit`", "install persyaratan developer" vs. "menginstal Qiskit", "menginstal ulang"). Either spelling is defensible on its own — "instal" is the KBBI form, "install" the widely used borrowing — but a native technical editor would normalize the file to one of them, most naturally to the KBBI "instal"/"menginstal" that the prose already prefers. Register is consistently informal ("kamu", "proyekmu", "sistemmu"), and the surrounding prose (e.g. the editable-mode admonition about rebuilding the Rust extension) is accurate and reads natively.

examples.source: Install Qiskit {#install-qiskit}
examples.translation: Instal Qiskit {#install-qiskit}
examples.suggested: Instal Qiskit {#install-qiskit} — and align lines 14/72 to "Instal Qiskit SDK dari sumber" / "Instal compiler Rust"
examples.why: Meaning is exact, but this heading is now the only one using the KBBI form "Instal" while the other two headings in the same file keep "Install"; the same verb should be spelled one way throughout the page.

editor_note: The translation is faithful in substance, informal-register consistent ("kamu" throughout), and nothing is hallucinated; core terms are handled sensibly (importer/exporter kept, "instruksi khusus" for custom instruction, "fungsi klasik khusus" for custom classical function, "mode ketat" for strict mode). Four editorial slips, none of which makes the page teach a false concept on its own: (a) the QASM2ParseError condition "does not match both the number of parameters and the number of qubits" is rendered with a negated "maupun" ("tidak cocok dengan jumlah parameter maupun jumlah qubit"), whose canonical Indonesian reading is "matches neither", narrowing the error condition from "at least one mismatch" to "both mismatch"; (b) "a later release of Qiskit" becomes "rilis Qiskit berikutnya" (= the NEXT release) in both warning admonitions, a mild over-commitment; (c) "circuit" is kept as English "Circuit" everywhere (headings, "Circuit yang dihasilkan") except one place where it becomes "sebuah sirkuit"; (d) the EN sentence "a program exported by our importer" is silently corrected to "diekspor oleh exporter kita" — the right meaning, but a deviation from the source a reviewer should know about.

examples.source: If a `gate` statement is encountered that matches the `name` of a custom instruction, but does not match both the number of parameters and the number of qubits, the importer will raise a `QASM2ParseError`
examples.translation: Jika pernyataan `gate` ditemukan yang cocok dengan `name` instruksi khusus, tapi tidak cocok dengan jumlah parameter maupun jumlah qubit, importer akan memunculkan [`QASM2ParseError`]
examples.suggested: ... tapi jumlah parameter dan jumlah qubitnya tidak cocok sekaligus (salah satu saja sudah cukup), importer akan memunculkan ...
examples.why: Negated 'maupun' reads as 'matches neither', so the learner may conclude the error fires only when BOTH counts differ; the source means a mismatch in either one is enough.

examples.source: it will be resolved in a later release of Qiskit
examples.translation: akan diselesaikan pada rilis Qiskit berikutnya
examples.suggested: akan diselesaikan pada rilis Qiskit mendatang
examples.why: 'berikutnya' promises the very next release; the English only says some later release. Appears in both warning admonitions.

examples.source: they accept a circuit and, only in the case of `qasm2.dump()`, a location to write the output to
examples.translation: mereka menerima sebuah sirkuit dan, hanya untuk [`qasm2.dump()`], lokasi untuk menulis outputnya
examples.suggested: mereka menerima sebuah Circuit dan, hanya untuk [`qasm2.dump()`], lokasi untuk menulis outputnya
examples.why: The file otherwise keeps 'Circuit' in English (heading 'Ekspor Circuit Qiskit ke OpenQASM 2', 'Circuit yang dihasilkan'); this single 'sirkuit' breaks the in-file convention.

examples.source: the default settings of the importer might not be able to import a program exported by our importer
examples.translation: pengaturan default importer mungkin tidak bisa mengimpor program yang diekspor oleh exporter kita
examples.suggested: (keep, but flag) — matches intent; note the deviation from the source wording
examples.why: The translation silently fixes an upstream slip ('our importer' → 'exporter kita'). Semantically correct and clearer, but it is an unflagged departure from the English a reviewer should be aware of.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: all four pattern steps, the ISA-circuit definition, the Batch/Session contrast, and the Sampler→bitstring / Estimator→nilai ekspektasi split are all faithful, and the informal "kamu" register holds throughout. What a native technical editor would change is syntax, not meaning. The closing sentence (line 47) collapses the English relative clause ("the flexibility and ease with which Qiskit patterns allow users to compose…") into an unparsable run-on — "fleksibilitas dan kemudahan pola Qiskit memungkinkan pengguna menyusun berbagai langkah pola membuka komputasi kuantum ke berbagai aplikasi" — where the subject of "membuka" is lost; a reader can recover the intent only by consulting the English. Smaller slips: the English noun-first calque "dari `qiskit-ibm-runtime` package" (should be "paket `qiskit-ibm-runtime`"), the animate pronoun "pada mereka" used for circuits, and "di bagian bawah" ("at the bottom") for "in the sections below" instead of "di bagian-bagian berikut". Domain terminology is correct and internally consistent (qubit, nilai ekspektasi, observabel, peta kopling, di-transpile, primitif Sampler/Estimator).

examples.source: the flexibility and ease with which Qiskit patterns allow users to compose the different steps of the pattern opens quantum computing to a wide variety of applications and techniques
examples.translation: fleksibilitas dan kemudahan pola Qiskit memungkinkan pengguna menyusun berbagai langkah pola membuka komputasi kuantum ke berbagai aplikasi dan teknik
examples.suggested: fleksibilitas dan kemudahan yang ditawarkan pola Qiskit dalam menyusun berbagai langkah pola tersebut membuka komputasi kuantum bagi beragam aplikasi dan teknik
examples.why: The English relative clause ('the ease with which … allow users to compose') is flattened into a chain of verbs, leaving 'membuka' without a clear subject. The sentence is syntactically broken and has to be re-parsed against the English; meaning is recoverable, so MINOR, but no native technical writer would leave it.

examples.source: a Sampler or Estimator primitive from the `qiskit-ibm-runtime` package
examples.translation: primitif Sampler atau Estimator dari `qiskit-ibm-runtime` package
examples.suggested: primitif Sampler atau Estimator dari paket `qiskit-ibm-runtime`
examples.why: English noun-modifier order carried over verbatim; Indonesian places the head noun first ('paket X'). A visible calque in an otherwise clean paragraph.

examples.source: perform a series of optimizations on them
examples.translation: melakukan serangkaian optimasi pada mereka
examples.suggested: melakukan serangkaian optimasi terhadap Circuit tersebut
examples.why: 'mereka' is the animate third-person plural; used here for circuits it reads as machine translation. Native technical prose would repeat the noun or use 'terhadapnya'.

examples.source: Each step is detailed in the sections below.
examples.translation: Setiap langkah dijelaskan secara rinci di bagian bawah.
examples.suggested: Setiap langkah dijelaskan secara rinci di bagian-bagian berikut.
examples.why: 'di bagian bawah' reads as 'at the bottom (of the page)' rather than 'in the sections that follow', so the navigational cue to the four following headings is weakened. Not misleading about content, but the pointer is duller than the English.

editor_note: Meaning is substantially faithful — all quantities (10 juta eksekusi, 26,8 juta instruksi, 30/20 juta Gate RZ/SX, lima juta Gate dua-Qubit), the ISA instruction table and the per-job-not-per-PUB caveat all survive intact, and the informal "kamu" register holds throughout. Four editorial slips: (1) the opening paragraph drops the English hedge "to decrease the likelihood that your job fails" and restates it as an absolute purpose ("sehingga kamu tidak perlu menunggu dalam antrean lalu menghadapi kegagalan job"), overstating what validation guarantees — the retained "berusaha memastikan" keeps it from actually misleading, but the qualifier should be restored (e.g. "untuk mengurangi kemungkinan job kamu gagal setelah kamu menunggu di antrean"). (2) "noise factors" is rendered "faktor kebisingan", the acoustic-noise word; the signal/quantum convention is "derau" or simply keeping "noise". (3) "introduce additional gates" is calqued as "memperkenalkan Gate tambahan" (twice) where a native writer would use "menambahkan"/"menghasilkan". (4) "circuit" is lowercase "sirkuit" once in the PUB example while the rest of the file uses "Circuit", an in-file inconsistency in one sentence. None of these changes what the reader learns about the limits.

examples.source: it is first validated to try to ensure that the job can run on the QPU, to decrease the likelihood that your job fails after you've waited for it to go through the queue
examples.translation: Layanan ini berusaha memastikan bahwa job dapat berjalan di QPU sehingga kamu tidak perlu menunggu dalam antrean lalu menghadapi kegagalan job.
examples.suggested: Layanan ini berusaha memastikan bahwa job dapat berjalan di QPU, untuk mengurangi kemungkinan job kamu gagal setelah kamu menunggu di antrean.
examples.why: The probabilistic hedge "decrease the likelihood" becomes an absolute outcome ("so you won't have to wait in the queue and then face failure"). Validation only reduces the chance of post-queue failure; the page itself later says jobs over the limit "biasanya akan gagal".

examples.source: The number of two-qubit gates is multiplied by the sum of noise factors requested in gate-folding ZNE.
examples.translation: Jumlah Gate dua-Qubit dikalikan dengan jumlah faktor kebisingan yang diminta dalam gate-folding ZNE.
examples.suggested: ... dikalikan dengan jumlah faktor derau (noise factor) yang diminta dalam gate-folding ZNE.
examples.why: "Kebisingan" is acoustic noise/noise pollution; the signal-processing and quantum-error convention in Indonesian is "derau", or the term is kept as "noise factor". Recognizable in context, so minor, but it is the wrong register of the word.

examples.source: Dynamical decoupling and gate-folding ZNE introduce additional gates ...
examples.translation: Dynamical decoupling dan gate-folding ZNE memperkenalkan Gate tambahan ...
examples.suggested: ... menambahkan Gate tambahan ... / menghasilkan Gate tambahan ...
examples.why: "Memperkenalkan" is a direct calque of "introduce" and in Indonesian means introducing a person or a concept, not adding elements to a circuit. Occurs twice in the same admonition.

examples.source: if you have a PUB with one circuit and parameters with shape (4, 1), this would render 4 circuits
examples.translation: jika kamu memiliki PUB dengan satu sirkuit dan parameter berbentuk (4, 1), ini akan menghasilkan 4 Circuit
examples.suggested: jika kamu memiliki PUB dengan satu Circuit dan parameter berbentuk (4, 1), ini akan menghasilkan 4 Circuit
examples.why: The same noun appears as lowercase "sirkuit" and as "Circuit" within one sentence; the file otherwise uses "Circuit" consistently. Cosmetic inconsistency only, the concept stays identifiable.

editor_note: No semantic drift and no hallucination: every claim matches the English, including the retirement date (15 Mei 2024), the "sekitar 50 qubit" ceiling, the Open Plan caveat ("hanya dapat berjalan dalam mode job atau mode batch"), and the table rows; the informal "kamu" register holds throughout. What a native editor would change is consistency and one calque: the AccordionItem titles use the English-borrowed "hardware kuantum" and "skill" ("Menggunakan hardware kuantum membangun skill yang unik", "Algoritma harus disesuaikan untuk hardware kuantum") while every body paragraph under them says "perangkat keras kuantum" and "keterampilan"; the section heading is translated "Backend tiruan" but the body and table then say "fake backend"/"Fake Backends" untranslated. "melakukan simulasi berisik QPU" is a literal calque of "noisy simulations of the QPU" — "berisik" means acoustically noisy in everyday Indonesian and a technical writer would write "simulasi QPU dengan noise". The H1 is also expanded to "Migrasi dari simulator cloud ke simulator lokal" where the English (and the frontmatter title) is just "Migrate to local simulators" — harmless, but it makes H1 and frontmatter disagree.

examples.source: Using quantum hardware builds unique skills / Interacting with quantum hardware grows skills and experience
examples.translation: Menggunakan hardware kuantum membangun skill yang unik / Berinteraksi dengan perangkat keras kuantum mengembangkan keterampilan dan pengalaman
examples.suggested: Menggunakan perangkat keras kuantum membangun keterampilan yang unik
examples.why: The accordion title borrows 'hardware' and 'skill' while the very next line of its own body uses 'perangkat keras kuantum' and 'keterampilan'; same split recurs at the third accordion title ('Algoritma harus disesuaikan untuk hardware kuantum' vs 'perangkat keras kuantum' in its body).

examples.source: ### Fake backends — The fake backends mimic the behaviors of IBM QPUs
examples.translation: ### Backend tiruan — [Fake backend] meniru perilaku QPU IBM
examples.suggested: Keep one form: either '### Fake backend' or 'Backend tiruan' in heading, body and table alike
examples.why: The heading translates the term but the body, the admonition ('fake backend mungkin menjadi pilihan yang lebih baik') and the table column ('Fake Backends') leave it in English, so the heading and the content read as two different things.

examples.source: which are useful for testing the transpiler and performing noisy simulations of the QPU
examples.translation: yang berguna untuk menguji Transpiler dan melakukan simulasi berisik QPU
examples.suggested: yang berguna untuk menguji Transpiler dan menjalankan simulasi QPU dengan noise
examples.why: 'berisik' is the everyday acoustic sense of noisy; as a calque here it reads as machine translation, and the file elsewhere consistently keeps the term as 'noise' ('model noise', 'simulasi bebas noise').

examples.source: # Migrate to local simulators
examples.translation: # Migrasi dari simulator cloud ke simulator lokal
examples.suggested: # Migrasi ke simulator lokal
examples.why: The H1 adds a source ('dari simulator cloud') the English heading does not state, and now disagrees with this page's own frontmatter title 'Migrasi ke simulator lokal'; content-wise accurate, so cosmetic only.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I checked every claim in the simulation-method list and the last 40% (the noise caution, the Clifford section, Next steps) against the English and found no drift, no dropped caveat and no hallucination: "all options except shots are ignored" → "semua opsi kecuali shots diabaikan", "it does not support measurements" (superop) and "it does not support measurement, reset, or noise" (unitary) are both rendered with the negation and the correct exception list intact, and "likely to be less severe than the noise on a real QPU" → "kemungkinan besar tidak separah noise pada QPU sungguhan" keeps the hedge. Informal register ("kamu", "programmu") holds consistently. Two editorial nits: (1) "noise" is kept in English as a noun ("model noise", "dampak noise") but its adjective is rendered with the KBBI word "derau" — "simulasi berderau", "Circuit *berderau*", "Gate dan reset ideal maupun berderau" — a split a native technical editor would standardize, since "berderau" reads dated next to the untranslated noun in the same sentence; (2) in Next steps, "Review detailed Sampler examples" became "Tinjau contoh Sampler secara detail", moving the qualifier from the examples to the act of reviewing. Neither misleads a learner.

examples.source: performing noisy simulations of the QPU / noise model / the noise impact
examples.translation: melakukan simulasi berderau dari QPU / model noise / dampak noise
examples.suggested: melakukan simulasi dengan noise dari QPU (or consistently use derau for both noun and adjective)
examples.why: Within one file the same concept is split between the untranslated noun 'noise' and the derau-derived adjective 'berderau'; 'berderau' is correct KBBI but reads archaic next to 'model noise' in the same paragraph. Clear, not misleading — a consistency slip only.

examples.source: Review detailed Sampler examples. / Review detailed Estimator examples.
examples.translation: Tinjau contoh Sampler secara detail. / Tinjau contoh Estimator secara detail.
examples.suggested: Tinjau contoh Sampler yang mendetail. / Tinjau contoh Estimator yang mendetail.
examples.why: The qualifier moves from the examples (which are detailed) to the reading (do it in detail). Same destination, same action, so it cannot mislead, but it is not what the English says.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination; the cost caveat ("mungkin dikenakan biaya") and the dynamic-rules tip both survive intact, and all three connection options map one-to-one to the English. What a native editor would change: (1) the second-person register flips inside a single paragraph — "Kamu bisa mengintegrasikan… Dengan menggunakan provider eksternal, Anda bisa menyediakan… bagi pengguna di perusahaanmu… Kamu bisa menghubungkan" — three forms (Kamu / Anda / -mu) in three consecutive sentences; the same flip repeats in the Admonition ("Setelah menghubungkan IDP, Anda bisa…"), so pick one and hold it. (2) "mengintegrasikan dengan identity provider (IDP) eksternal" is a calque of "integrate with": mengintegrasikan is transitive and left objectless here; "berintegrasi dengan" or "melakukan integrasi dengan" is what an Indonesian technical writer would write. (3) In the last bullet the sentence-final period was pulled inside the link text ("dokumentasi lengkap [App ID.](…)"), so the rendered link reads "App ID." — it belongs after the closing parenthesis.

examples.source: You can integrate with your external identity provider (IDP) … you can provide a way for users in your company to use single sign-on (SSO). You can connect your cloud account…
examples.translation: Kamu bisa mengintegrasikan dengan identity provider (IDP) eksternal … Dengan menggunakan provider eksternal, Anda bisa menyediakan cara bagi pengguna di perusahaanmu … Kamu bisa menghubungkan akun cloud…
examples.suggested: Kamu bisa berintegrasi dengan identity provider (IDP) eksternal … kamu bisa menyediakan cara bagi pengguna di perusahaanmu … Kamu bisa menghubungkan akun cloud…
examples.why: Three second-person forms (Kamu, Anda, -mu) alternate across three consecutive sentences of one paragraph; the file's own convention is informal, so Anda is the outlier. Register slip only — meaning is unaffected.

examples.source: You can integrate with your external identity provider (IDP)
examples.translation: Kamu bisa mengintegrasikan dengan identity provider (IDP) eksternal
examples.suggested: Kamu bisa berintegrasi dengan identity provider (IDP) eksternal
examples.why: Calqued from English 'integrate with': the meN-…-kan form is transitive and is left without an object, which reads as MT. The intransitive berintegrasi dengan (or melakukan integrasi dengan) is the idiomatic form.

examples.source: After connecting your IDP, you can set up dynamic rules so you don't have to manually add every user…
examples.translation: Setelah menghubungkan IDP, Anda bisa menyiapkan aturan dinamis sehingga tidak perlu menambahkan setiap pengguna…
examples.suggested: Setelah menghubungkan IDP, kamu bisa menyiapkan aturan dinamis sehingga tidak perlu menambahkan setiap pengguna…
examples.why: Formal 'Anda' in the tip block against the informal 'Kamu' used in the body — same file, two conventions. Minor consistency slip, not misleading.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every claim, caveat and quantity matches the English (the beta caveat, "belum ada backend simulator untuk Executor", "Kamu perlu menerapkannya secara manual; tidak ada yang dikoreksi secara implisit", the XOR/measurement_flips step, and the "shots berlaku untuk seluruh job" restriction are all faithful), and the informal "kamu" register holds throughout. What a native technical editor would change: (1) the results table renders "Multiple registers" as "Register ganda", which reads as "double/dual register" rather than "beberapa register" — imprecise though recoverable from the adjacent `result[0]["<name>"] per register` cell; (2) two prose labels are left untranslated, "Examples:" (before the shots/meas_type table in Langkah 5) and "**Example:**" (before the ExecutorOptions snippet), while every other label in the file is translated; (3) "directed execution model" is kept in English everywhere in the body but translated as "Model eksekusi terarah" in the Next-steps list — an in-file inconsistency for the file's central concept name; (4) calqued/stiff phrasing: "kamu menangkap maksud desainmu di sisi client" for "capture your design intent" (a native would write "menyatakan/mendefinisikan maksud desainmu"), "Ada juga perbedaan struktural dalam di mana pengaturan berada" (double preposition, "mengenai di mana pengaturan disimpan"), and "Harus dikomposisi secara manual" for "Must be manually composed" ("disusun" is the natural verb); (5) the "post-" prefix is dropped twice — "Post-process the array manually" → "Proses array secara manual" and "results are shaped and post-processed" → "dibentuk dan diproses" — harmless here but it flattens the Sampler/Executor contrast the section is making. None of these would lead a learner to a false belief.

examples.source: Multiple registers | `result[0].data.<name>` per register | `result[0]["<name>"]` per register
examples.translation: Register ganda | `result[0].data.<name>` per register | `result[0]["<name>"]` per register
examples.suggested: Beberapa register
examples.why: "ganda" means double/dual, implying exactly two registers; the English means an arbitrary number of registers. Recoverable from the code cells, so minor, but wrong as a term.

examples.source: Examples: … **Example:**
examples.translation: Examples: … **Example:**
examples.suggested: Contoh: … **Contoh:**
examples.why: Two plain-English prose labels left untranslated while every other label in the file (Catatan, Rekomendasi, Catatan versi, Langkah 1…) is translated.

examples.source: Directed execution model
examples.translation: Model eksekusi terarah (Next steps) vs. "directed execution model" kept in English in all five body occurrences
examples.suggested: Keep "directed execution model" in the Next-steps link too, matching the body
examples.why: The file's central concept name is rendered two ways; a reader following the link may not connect it to the model discussed above.

examples.source: Instead, you capture your design intent on the client side (by using circuit annotations and a *samplex*)
examples.translation: Sebagai gantinya, kamu menangkap maksud desainmu di sisi client (dengan menggunakan anotasi circuit dan *samplex*)
examples.suggested: Sebagai gantinya, kamu menyatakan maksud desainmu di sisi client …
examples.why: "menangkap maksud desain" is a word-for-word calque of "capture intent"; in Indonesian technical prose the writer declares/expresses intent, not captures it.

examples.source: There is also a structural difference in where settings live.
examples.translation: Ada juga perbedaan struktural dalam di mana pengaturan berada.
examples.suggested: Ada juga perbedaan struktural mengenai tempat pengaturan disimpan.
examples.why: "dalam di mana" stacks two prepositions — grammatically tolerated but unmistakably machine-shaped; no native technical writer would leave it.

editor_note: The Indonesian reads naturally and nothing in it would teach a false concept, but four small editorial slips remain. (1) Address form is inconsistent: the file uses "Anda" in the intro bullet, bullet 1 and bullet 4, but switches to "Kamu bisa membatasi berapa lama..." in bullet 2 — pick one within the file. (2) The EN's generic "usage" / "a job's QPU consumption" is twice narrowed to "waktu kuantum" (frontmatter description, and "Waktu kuantum yang digunakan sebuah job") — upstream deliberately says *usage*, of which quantum time is only the unit, so the rendering over-specifies. (3) "scales with the number of shots" is strengthened to "berbanding lurus dengan jumlah shots" (strictly *directly proportional*); "meningkat seiring jumlah shots" keeps the EN's looser claim. (4) "a noise model becomes stale after a certain time" is both softened and blurred as "noise model bisa menjadi tidak relevan" — EN asserts it *does* become stale, and "kedaluwarsa"/"usang" carries the staleness sense better than "tidak relevan" (irrelevant). Core kept terms (shots, Estimator, session, batch, noise model, error mitigation/suppression) are consistent throughout.

examples.source: You can limit how long each job, batch, or session runs.
examples.translation: Kamu bisa membatasi berapa lama setiap job, batch, atau session berjalan.
examples.suggested: Anda bisa membatasi berapa lama setiap job, batch, atau session berjalan.
examples.why: Every other bullet in the file uses "Anda"; this lone "Kamu" is an in-file register inconsistency, not a deliberate choice.

examples.source: A job's QPU consumption (and therefore, its cost) scales with the number of shots.
examples.translation: Waktu kuantum yang digunakan sebuah job (dan oleh karena itu, biayanya) berbanding lurus dengan jumlah shots.
examples.suggested: Konsumsi QPU sebuah job (dan oleh karena itu, biayanya) meningkat seiring dengan jumlah shots.
examples.why: Two shifts in one sentence: "QPU consumption" is narrowed to "waktu kuantum", and the loose "scales with" is hardened into strict direct proportionality ("berbanding lurus").

examples.source: Note that a noise model becomes stale after a certain time, so this is only practical if there is no long delay between jobs.
examples.translation: Perlu diingat bahwa noise model bisa menjadi tidak relevan setelah jangka waktu tertentu, jadi ini hanya praktis jika tidak ada jeda panjang antar job.
examples.suggested: Perlu diingat bahwa noise model menjadi kedaluwarsa setelah jangka waktu tertentu, ...
examples.why: EN states the model does go stale; "bisa menjadi" downgrades it to a possibility, and "tidak relevan" (irrelevant) misses the time-decay sense of "stale".

examples.source: description: How to minimize the amount of usage spent processing and running a job.
examples.translation: description: 'Cara meminimalkan jumlah waktu kuantum yang digunakan untuk memproses dan menjalankan sebuah job.'
examples.suggested: Cara meminimalkan jumlah penggunaan (usage) untuk memproses dan menjalankan sebuah job.
examples.why: Upstream moved from "quantum time" to the broader billing concept "usage"; rendering it back as "waktu kuantum" reintroduces the superseded term.

editor_note: Judging only the rewritten method table (entry 11): all four descriptions are semantically faithful — `job.result()` keeps the "(blocking call hingga selesai)" caveat and `job.wait_for_final_state()` correctly says the call blocks until a final state, so nothing here misleads. Two editorial slips remain. (1) The table's own header row is still English, "| Method | Description |", while the surrounding prose consistently uses "metode" ("Gunakan metode `service.usage()`", "metode manajemen job tambahan") and the page translates every other label — it should read "| Metode | Deskripsi |". (2) "Blokir hingga job mencapai status akhir" uses the bare imperative "Blokir", which in Indonesian reads as "ban/block (someone)" and sounds like an instruction to the reader rather than a description of the call's behavior; a native technical writer would write "Memblokir hingga job mencapai keadaan terminal/status akhir" (also matching the nominal style a description column wants). Neither changes the meaning a learner takes away.

examples.source: | Method | Description |
examples.translation: | Method | Description |
examples.suggested: | Metode | Deskripsi |
examples.why: The table header was left in English while the body prose of the same page uses "metode" (e.g. "Gunakan metode `service.usage()`"); the column labels are ordinary UI-free prose and should be translated for consistency.

examples.source: | `job.wait_for_final_state()` | Block until the job reaches a terminal state |
examples.translation: | `job.wait_for_final_state()` | Blokir hingga job mencapai status akhir |
examples.suggested: | `job.wait_for_final_state()` | Memblokir hingga job mencapai keadaan terminal |
examples.why: Bare imperative "Blokir" reads in Indonesian as "ban/block someone" and addresses the reader, whereas the English describes what the method does; the nominal "Memblokir" is the natural register for a description column, and "keadaan terminal" is the more precise rendering of "terminal state".

editor_note: No semantic drift: every claim tracks the English, including the tricky ones — the version gates (`NoiseLearner` hanya berfungsi dengan EstimatorV2 / `NoiseLearnerV3` hanya berfungsi dengan Executor), "tiga kotak, dua di antaranya mengandung anotasi `InjectNoise` ... (karena tidak setara)", and the Pauli-Lindblad formula gloss ("$r_j$ adalah `LayerError.rates`"). Register is consistently informal ("kamu bisa memilih", "memberi kamu kemampuan"). What a native technical editor would still change: (1) "box" is rendered two ways in the same section — "box beranotasi" / "ke box yang berisi entangler" (lines ~347-350) but "berisi tiga kotak" at line ~362; pick one. (2) "fitted" is rendered as the colloquial anglicism "difit" ("model noise yang telah difit", lines 35 and 170) where "dicocokkan"/"hasil pencocokan" is the normal written-technical form. (3) English noun-phrase order is calqued in a few places — "IBM Quantum `EstimatorV2` primitive" and "sebelum membuat instance Estimator primitive" (line 208) instead of "primitive `EstimatorV2` IBM Quantum"; likewise the bullet calque "menentukan untuk menambahkan anotasi..." for "specifies to add...". None of these mislead.

examples.source: The circuit from the previous example contains three boxes, two of which contain `InjectNoise` annotations
examples.translation: Circuit dari contoh sebelumnya berisi tiga kotak, dua di antaranya mengandung anotasi `InjectNoise`
examples.suggested: Circuit dari contoh sebelumnya berisi tiga box, dua di antaranya mengandung anotasi `InjectNoise`
examples.why: The same section already keeps the API-bound term untranslated ("box beranotasi", "ke box yang berisi entangler", "ke sebuah box"); switching to "kotak" only here is a within-file inconsistency for a term that maps to the `BoxOp` object.

examples.source: without any local access to the fitted noise model / the fitted Pauli Lindblad model
examples.translation: tanpa akses lokal ke model noise yang telah difit / model Pauli Lindblad yang telah difit
examples.suggested: tanpa akses lokal ke model noise hasil pencocokan / model Pauli Lindblad yang telah dicocokkan
examples.why: "difit" is a spoken-register anglicism (di- + English "fit"); recognizable but not what an Indonesian technical writer would put in documentation prose.

examples.source: can also be used as an input to the IBM Quantum `EstimatorV2` primitive ... before instantiating an Estimator primitive
examples.translation: bisa digunakan sebagai input ke IBM Quantum `EstimatorV2` primitive ... sebelum membuat instance Estimator primitive
examples.suggested: bisa digunakan sebagai input ke primitive `EstimatorV2` IBM Quantum ... sebelum membuat instance primitive Estimator
examples.why: English head-final noun order is carried over; Indonesian puts the head noun first ("primitive EstimatorV2"), and the file itself does this correctly elsewhere ("Mirip dengan primitive", "kompatibel dengan primitive Executor").

examples.source: `inject_noise_targets="gates"` specifies to add the `InjectNoise` annotations to boxes that contain entanglers.
examples.translation: `inject_noise_targets=”gates”` menentukan untuk menambahkan anotasi `InjectNoise` ke box yang berisi entangler.
examples.suggested: `inject_noise_targets="gates"` membuat anotasi `InjectNoise` ditambahkan ke box yang berisi entangler.
examples.why: "menentukan untuk + verb" is a direct calque of "specifies to <verb>" and is not idiomatic Indonesian; both bullets repeat the pattern.

editor_note: Nothing in this short IBM Cloud Activity Tracker page would mislead a learner — the action/trigger table, the endpoint glosses ("Ambil konfigurasi backend", "Batalkan job") and the two repeated IBM Cloud Logs sentences are faithful. Three editorial slips: (1) register breaks mid-sentence in the third paragraph — "Kamu bisa menggunakan … di akunmu ke tujuan yang Anda pilih" mixes kamu and Anda in one clause; (2) "routed" is rendered two different ways in adjacent sentences, the correct verb "merutekan" in para 3 but the raw English calque "diroute" in paras 4 and 6, where "dirutekan" is what an Indonesian technical writer would write; (3) "abnormal activity" becomes "aktivitas yang mencurigakan" (suspicious), a narrower notion than "abnormal/tidak normal", and the sentence's "and … and" structure is flattened into a single comma list. "event auditing" also keeps the English gerund where "event audit" is the natural Indonesian noun phrase.

examples.source: to route auditing events in your account to destinations of your choice
examples.translation: untuk merutekan event auditing di akunmu ke tujuan yang Anda pilih
examples.suggested: untuk merutekan event audit di akunmu ke tujuan yang kamu pilih
examples.why: The file's convention is informal "kamu/-mu"; "Anda" appears once, inside the very sentence that already used "akunmu", so the register flips mid-clause.

examples.source: events that are generated in your account and routed by IBM Cloud Activity Tracker Event Routing
examples.translation: event yang dihasilkan di akunmu dan diroute oleh IBM Cloud Activity Tracker Event Routing
examples.suggested: event yang dihasilkan di akunmu dan dirutekan oleh IBM Cloud Activity Tracker Event Routing
examples.why: "diroute" is an un-assimilated English stem with an Indonesian prefix; the same file already uses the proper form "merutekan" two paragraphs earlier, so the term is rendered inconsistently.

examples.source: You can use the events to investigate abnormal activity and critical actions and to comply with regulatory audit requirements.
examples.translation: Kamu bisa menggunakan event ini untuk menginvestigasi aktivitas yang mencurigakan, tindakan kritis, dan untuk memenuhi persyaratan audit regulasi.
examples.suggested: Kamu bisa menggunakan event ini untuk menyelidiki aktivitas tidak normal dan tindakan kritis, serta untuk memenuhi persyaratan audit regulasi.
examples.why: "abnormal" (anything out of the ordinary) is narrowed to "mencurigakan" (suspicious, i.e. implying intent); the original's two coordinated purposes are also collapsed into one comma list.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner: every claim, quantity and qualifier in the three English paragraphs survives intact (2016, "most popular quantum framework" → "framework kuantum paling populer", "thanks in part to" correctly hedged as "sebagian berkat"), and the informal "kamu" register holds throughout. Three things a native technical editor would still change. (1) "open-sourcing key parts of the quantum software stack" is rendered as "pengembangan open-source untuk bagian-bagian penting dari stack perangkat lunak kuantum" — that reads as "open-source development *for* key parts", i.e. an ongoing activity, rather than the act of releasing those parts as open source; the idiomatic rendering is "menjadikan bagian-bagian penting ... bersifat open source" / "merilis ... sebagai open source". (2) The page names itself two ways: frontmatter `title` stays English "Open source" while the H1 is translated "Sumber terbuka" — sidebar/tab and heading will disagree. (3) The frontmatter description narrows "get involved with the Qiskit open-source community" to "berkontribusi dalam komunitas open-source Qiskit" (contribute), dropping the broader "join in / take part" sense that the body's own "bergabung dalam komunitas" gets right.

examples.source: This groundbreaking initiative includes open-sourcing key parts of the quantum software stack and introducing Qiskit, a versatile quantum computing framework.
examples.translation: Inisiatif terobosan ini mencakup pengembangan open-source untuk bagian-bagian penting dari stack perangkat lunak kuantum dan memperkenalkan Qiskit, sebuah framework komputasi kuantum yang serbaguna.
examples.suggested: Inisiatif terobosan ini mencakup menjadikan bagian-bagian penting dari stack perangkat lunak kuantum sebagai open source dan memperkenalkan Qiskit, sebuah framework komputasi kuantum yang serbaguna.
examples.why: "open-sourcing X" is the act of releasing X under an open-source license; "pengembangan open-source untuk X" shifts it to doing open-source development on X. The historical fact (IBM opened up existing stack components) is blurred into a generic development activity.

examples.source: title: Open source / # Open source
examples.translation: title: 'Open source' / # Sumber terbuka {#open-source}
examples.suggested: title: 'Sumber terbuka' (or leave the H1 as "Open source" to match)
examples.why: The same page name is rendered two different ways in the same file — untranslated in the frontmatter, translated in the H1 — so the sidebar/browser-tab label and the on-page heading disagree. Within-file inconsistency, not misleading.

examples.source: description: Learn how to get involved with the Qiskit open-source community to shape the future of quantum computing.
examples.translation: Pelajari cara berkontribusi dalam komunitas open-source Qiskit untuk membentuk masa depan komputasi kuantum.
examples.suggested: Pelajari cara terlibat dalam komunitas open-source Qiskit untuk membentuk masa depan komputasi kuantum.
examples.why: "get involved" is deliberately broader than contributing code — the body itself lists Slack community support alongside pull requests. "berkontribusi" narrows the invitation; "terlibat" keeps it open.

editor_note: No semantic drift: every load-bearing claim survives intact — the index convention (`A.tensor(B)` = B on subsistem 0, A on subsistem 1), `A.compose(B)` → matriks $B.A$ vs `front=True` → $A.B$, the dimension-matching caveat with its `front=True` parenthetical, "kombinasi linear tidak [mempertahankan keunitaran]", the global-phase inequality, and the closing CP caveat ("pengecualian akan dimunculkan jika input tidak CP") are all faithful. Terminology is sound ("uniter"/"keunitaran", "pengecualian dimunculkan", "fidelitas proses") and the informal "kamu" register holds throughout. What an editor would still change: the tensor term is split within the file — the heading is "Produk tensor" but the body twice keeps raw "tensor product" ("operator tensor product $A\otimes B$", "bekerja seperti tensor product"); "information-theoretic quantity" is calqued as "besaran teoritis-informasi", which no Indonesian physicist writes (it should be "besaran teori-informasi" / "besaran dalam teori informasi"); and "circuit" is rendered three ways in the prose ("sirkuit kuantum", lowercase "circuit", capitalized "Circuit").

examples.source: Two operators $A$ and $B$ can be combined into a tensor product operator … acts like a tensor product but in the reverse order
examples.translation: ### Produk tensor … digabungkan menjadi operator tensor product $A\otimes B$ … bekerja seperti tensor product tetapi dalam urutan terbalik
examples.suggested: digabungkan menjadi operator produk tensor $A\otimes B$ … bekerja seperti produk tensor tetapi dalam urutan terbalik
examples.why: The heading establishes 'produk tensor' as the chosen convention, then the body reverts to the English phrase twice — within-file inconsistency for a core term. Concept stays identifiable, so MINOR.

examples.source: This is an information-theoretic quantity for how close two quantum channels are to each other
examples.translation: Ini adalah besaran teoritis-informasi untuk seberapa dekat dua kanal kuantum satu sama lain
examples.suggested: Ini adalah besaran dalam teori informasi yang mengukur seberapa dekat dua kanal kuantum satu sama lain
examples.why: 'teoritis-informasi' is a word-order calque of the English compound adjective; Indonesian post-modifies ('teori informasi'). The added 'yang mengukur' also repairs the verbless 'besaran … untuk seberapa dekat', which reads as raw MT.

examples.source: quantum circuit … added to the circuit … inserted into the circuit itself
examples.translation: sirkuit kuantum … ditambahkan ke circuit … dimasukkan ke dalam Circuit itu sendiri
examples.suggested: Pick one convention and hold it across the file (e.g. 'sirkuit' throughout, or the kept English term throughout)
examples.why: Three renderings of the same everyday term in one page. Not misleading — a learner still identifies the concept — so MINOR; the capitalized 'Circuit' form itself belongs to the deterministic kept-term sweep.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries are the two plan-name headings, and both are semantically faithful — "Paket Bayar Sesuai Pemakaian" is an accurate gloss of Pay-As-You-Go and "Paket Premium" of Premium; nothing misleading, no drift, no dropped caveat. The defect is consistency: these two headings now localize IBM's product names while every other heading and every in-body reference in the same file keeps them in English — sibling headings read "## Open Plan", "## Flex Plan", "## On-Prem Plan", and the prose says "instance Pay-As-You-Go Plan" (intro), "pertimbangkan Pay-As-You-Go Plan sebagai alternatif" and "langganan Premium Plan" (Flex section), "tersedia untuk pengguna Premium Plan" (inside the very section now titled "Paket Premium"). A reader scanning the page sees the Premium section headed one way and named another two lines later, and the Flex section's cross-reference to Pay-As-You-Go no longer matches the heading it points at. The fix a native technical editor would make is to restore "## Pay-As-You-Go Plan" and "## Premium Plan" (these are product names, and the file's established convention is to keep them), or else localize all five plan names and every in-body mention together. Both entries remain recognizable, so this is cosmetic, not misleading.

examples.source: Pay-As-You-Go Plan {#pay-as-you-go-plan}
examples.translation: Paket Bayar Sesuai Pemakaian {#pay-as-you-go-plan}
examples.suggested: Pay-As-You-Go Plan {#pay-as-you-go-plan}
examples.why: The rest of the file keeps IBM's plan names in English — sibling headings are "## Open Plan", "## Flex Plan", "## On-Prem Plan", and the prose refers to "instance Pay-As-You-Go Plan" (intro) and "pertimbangkan Pay-As-You-Go Plan sebagai alternatif" (Flex section). Localizing only this heading makes the Flex section's cross-reference point at a section whose title no longer matches the name used. Meaning is accurate, so this is a consistency slip, not a mistranslation.

examples.source: Premium Plan {#premium-plan}
examples.translation: Paket Premium {#premium-plan}
examples.suggested: Premium Plan {#premium-plan}
examples.why: Same convention break, and here it collides inside its own section: the heading reads "Paket Premium" while the first paragraph under it says "tersedia untuk pengguna Premium Plan", and the Flex section says "langganan Premium Plan". One product, two names two lines apart.

editor_note: The two labels introducing the broadcasting examples are swapped, which teaches the NumPy broadcasting rule backwards: the block showing successful broadcasts (1 vs 3x5 → 3x5; 11x2x7 vs 11x1x7 → 11x2x7) is captioned "Contoh pasangan array yang tidak bisa di-broadcast:" ("pairs that do NOT broadcast"), while the block of incompatible pairs (5 vs 3; 2x1 vs 6x5x4, with the embedded comment saying it would only work if the middle dimension were 2) is captioned "Contoh pasangan array yang bisa di-broadcast:". A learner reading the rules immediately above ("Dua dimensi kompatibel jika ukurannya sama atau salah satunya adalah 1") then hits examples that contradict them — this is a directly misleading inversion and the only reason for the FAIL. Beyond that the page is faithful and readable; the residual nits are minor: the "circuit" term splits between "sirkuit" (Gambaran umum PUB) and "Circuit" elsewhere, "standard deviations" is rendered as the word-order-reversed "standar deviasi" instead of "deviasi standar"/"simpangan baku", and "dictionary of counts" is left wholly untranslated in the post-processing section while "dictionary yang memetakan bitstring" is translated around it.

examples.source: Examples of array pairs that broadcast:
examples.translation: Contoh pasangan array yang tidak bisa di-broadcast:
examples.suggested: Contoh pasangan array yang bisa di-broadcast:
examples.why: Inverted negation: this caption sits above the pairs that DO broadcast (1 vs 3x5 → 3x5; 11x2x7 vs 11x1x7 → 11x2x7), so the learner is told that valid broadcasts are invalid — the opposite of the rule stated two lines earlier.

examples.source: Examples of array pairs that do not broadcast:
examples.translation: Contoh pasangan array yang bisa di-broadcast:
examples.suggested: Contoh pasangan array yang tidak bisa di-broadcast:
examples.why: The mirror half of the same swap: it labels the incompatible pairs (5 vs 3, and 2x1 vs 6x5x4) as broadcastable, even though the code comment inside the block explains it would only work if the middle dimension were 2 instead of 5.

examples.source: one for each circuit being executed by the primitive
examples.translation: satu untuk setiap sirkuit yang dieksekusi oleh primitif
examples.suggested: pick one convention for 'circuit' and hold it for the whole file
examples.why: The file uses the Indonesian 'sirkuit' once in the PUB overview and the untranslated 'Circuit' everywhere else ('dengan Circuit yang sama', 'diikat ke Circuit', 'Circuit sepuluh-Qubit'); the concept stays identifiable, so this is minor, but a native technical editor would unify it.

examples.source: standard deviations
examples.translation: standar deviasi
examples.suggested: deviasi standar (or simpangan baku)
examples.why: Indonesian noun-adjective order makes 'standar deviasi' a calque of the English word order; the conventional technical renderings are 'deviasi standar' or 'simpangan baku'. Recognizable, hence minor.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, swapped quantities or hallucinated claims; the deprecation timeline (Qiskit SDK v1.3.0 → removal in v2.0.0, awal 2025), the `use_fractional_gates` flag on Heron, and the "calibration = pemetaan antara `ScheduleBlock` dan sebuah gate dalam `QuantumCircuit`" definition all land correctly, and the informal "Anda" register is consistent. Three editorial slips: (1) "our ongoing focus" is rendered "fokus kami yang terus berkembang" ("our ever-growing focus"), which shifts a statement of continuity into one of growth; (2) "deprecated" is rendered with the coined anglicism "dideprekasi" twice, where Indonesian technical writing would normally say "tidak digunakan lagi"/"usang" (or keep the English verb); (3) "the calibration builder passes" is flattened to "pass kalibrasi", dropping the fact that these are the *builder* passes (`RXCalibrationBuilder`/`RZXCalibrationBuilder`) just named in the same sentence. None of these would teach a learner something false.

examples.source: This change was motivated by our ongoing focus on utility-scale experiments
examples.translation: Perubahan ini didorong oleh fokus kami yang terus berkembang pada eksperimen skala utilitas
examples.suggested: Perubahan ini didorong oleh fokus kami yang berkelanjutan pada eksperimen skala utilitas
examples.why: "terus berkembang" means "ever-growing/evolving"; the English only claims the focus is ongoing, not that it is expanding. A small strengthening of the claim, not misleading.

examples.source: has been deprecated ... has been deprecated as of the Qiskit SDK v1.3.0
examples.translation: telah dideprekasi ... telah dideprekasi sejak Qiskit SDK v1.3.0
examples.suggested: sudah tidak digunakan lagi (deprecated) ... / dinyatakan usang sejak Qiskit SDK v1.3.0
examples.why: "dideprekasi" is a coined anglicism, not established Indonesian technical usage; recognizable but a calque a native technical editor would rewrite. Used consistently at least.

examples.source: build a transpilation pipeline containing the calibration builder passes to calibrate the single- and two-qubit rotations
examples.translation: membangun pipeline transpilasi yang berisi pass kalibrasi untuk mengkalibrasi rotasi qubit tunggal dan dua qubit
examples.suggested: membangun pipeline transpilasi yang berisi pass calibration builder tersebut untuk mengkalibrasi ...
examples.why: Drops "builder", loosening the link to the `RXCalibrationBuilder`/`RZXCalibrationBuilder` passes named earlier in the same sentence; the reader can still follow, so it is a dropped qualifier rather than a false statement.

editor_note: No misleading drift or hallucination: the benchmark numbers (30 shot vs 170.000 shot, ambang kepercayaan 99%), the $A$ metric definition, the error-suppression-vs-mitigation contrast ("bekerja di level Gate dan pulse ... mencegah kemungkinan terjadinya error") and the changelog all track the English exactly, and the informal "kamu" register holds throughout. Four editorial slips remain. (1) "sehingga kamu bisa dengan mudah mengganti Sampler dan Estimator Q-CTRL" loses the direction of "swap in the Q-CTRL Sampler and Estimator" — without "dengan"/"beralih ke" it reads as replacing Q-CTRL's primitives rather than dropping them in for IBM's. (2) "Bagian selanjutnya memberikan detail lebih lanjut" says "the next section" where the English says "The rest of this section" (the detail is in this same Benchmarks section). (3) "out of the box" is flattened to "langsung dari awal", losing the no-configuration-needed sense a native writer would render as "tanpa perlu konfigurasi tambahan". (4) "pengujian di luar batas ini didorong" is a bare calqued passive that no Indonesian technical writer would produce ("kamu dianjurkan untuk menguji di luar batas ini").

examples.source: Fire Opal Performance Management has two options for execution that are similar to the IBM Quantum primitives, so you can easily swap in the Q-CTRL Sampler and Estimator.
examples.translation: Fire Opal Performance Management memiliki dua opsi eksekusi yang mirip dengan primitif IBM Quantum, sehingga kamu bisa dengan mudah mengganti Sampler dan Estimator Q-CTRL.
examples.suggested: ... sehingga kamu bisa dengan mudah beralih ke Sampler dan Estimator Q-CTRL.
examples.why: "mengganti X" in Indonesian means "replace X", so the sentence reads as replacing Q-CTRL's primitives instead of substituting them in place of IBM's. The direction of the swap is inverted/ambiguous; context still lets a reader recover it, so MINOR.

examples.source: The rest of this section provides more details about types of algorithms you can run, as well as the expected performance and runtimes.
examples.translation: Bagian selanjutnya memberikan detail lebih lanjut tentang jenis algoritma yang bisa kamu jalankan, serta performa dan runtime yang diharapkan.
examples.suggested: Sisa bagian ini memberikan detail lebih lanjut tentang ...
examples.why: "Bagian selanjutnya" points the reader to the NEXT section (Get started), but the details are in the remainder of the Benchmarks section itself. A dropped scope qualifier, not a false claim.

examples.source: All Fire Opal pipeline methods are pre-configured and algorithm-agnostic, meaning you always get the best performance out of the box.
examples.translation: Semua metode pipeline Fire Opal sudah dikonfigurasi sebelumnya dan bersifat agnostik terhadap algoritma, artinya kamu selalu mendapatkan performa terbaik langsung dari awal.
examples.suggested: ... artinya kamu selalu mendapatkan performa terbaik tanpa perlu konfigurasi tambahan.
examples.why: "langsung dari awal" (right from the start) is a temporal reading; "out of the box" here means without any setup on the user's part — the selling point of the zero-configuration pipeline is flattened.

examples.source: Larger problem sizes have been successfully solved, and testing beyond these limits is encouraged.
examples.translation: Ukuran masalah yang lebih besar telah berhasil dipecahkan, dan pengujian di luar batas ini didorong.
examples.suggested: ... dan kamu dianjurkan untuk menguji di luar batas tersebut.
examples.why: A bare agentless passive calqued on English "is encouraged"; "didorong" stranded at the end of the clause is not something an Indonesian technical writer would write, and it breaks the "kamu" address used elsewhere in the paragraph.

editor_note: No semantic drift: all nine notes track the English claim-for-claim (note 4's "hanya memiliki dukungan sangat terbatas untuk parsing ekspresi variabel", note 8's "tidak memenuhi syarat untuk eksekusi di perangkat keras", note 9's `input float[64]` sentence all preserve scope, negation and caveats), and the informal "kamu" register holds in the Admonition. What a native technical editor would change is surface: the proper name "Live Specification" is rendered "Spesifikasi Langsung" (reads as "live broadcast", not "continuously updated spec") in two places; note 7 leaves the English adverb inside Indonesian syntax as "mengevaluasi modifier Gate secara eagerly"; note 7 also calques "precludes ... from being valid" into "mengecualikan ... agar tidak valid", which is stiff enough to make the reader re-parse; and the product name is split — the table header says "Layanan Komputasi IBM Quantum" while every prose mention keeps "IBM Quantum Compute Service". Also "klasikal" is used throughout where Indonesian technical writing uses "klasik" ("register klasik", "ekspresi klasik"). None of these would make a learner form a false belief.

examples.source: OpenQASM 3.X Live Specification
examples.translation: Spesifikasi Langsung OpenQASM 3.X
examples.suggested: Spesifikasi Live OpenQASM 3.X (or keep the English title)
examples.why: "Langsung" reads as "live broadcast/direct"; here "Live" names a continuously-updated spec document, so the translated title misnames a proper resource.

examples.source: will eagerly evaluate gate modifiers during the parse
examples.translation: akan mengevaluasi modifier Gate secara eagerly selama parsing
examples.suggested: akan langsung mengevaluasi modifier gate saat parsing
examples.why: An untranslated English adverb bolted onto Indonesian syntax ("secara eagerly"); no Indonesian technical writer would leave it, and the reader gains nothing over "langsung/sedini mungkin".

examples.source: This precludes custom `gate` definitions and higher-level constructs like gate modifiers (such as `inv @`) from being valid for execution on hardware verbatim
examples.translation: Ini mengecualikan definisi `gate` kustom dan konstruksi tingkat tinggi seperti modifier Gate (seperti `inv @`) agar tidak valid untuk eksekusi langsung di perangkat keras
examples.suggested: Akibatnya, definisi `gate` kustom dan konstruksi tingkat tinggi seperti modifier gate (misalnya `inv @`) tidak valid untuk dieksekusi apa adanya di perangkat keras
examples.why: "mengecualikan ... agar tidak valid" is a word-for-word calque of "precludes ... from being valid"; the meaning survives but the clause has to be re-read. Purely a fluency slip, not drift.

examples.source: IBM Quantum Compute Service
examples.translation: table header: "Layanan Komputasi IBM Quantum"; prose: "IBM Quantum Compute Service"
examples.suggested: Keep "IBM Quantum Compute Service" in the table header too
examples.why: The same product name appears translated in the column header and untranslated in every prose mention, so the header column and the bullet explaining it no longer visibly refer to the same thing.

examples.source: classical registers / classical expressions / classical type
examples.translation: register klasikal / ekspresi klasikal / tipe klasikal
examples.suggested: register klasik / ekspresi klasik / tipe klasik
examples.why: "Klasikal" is chiefly used for classical music in Indonesian; the established rendering for the classical/quantum contrast in technical prose is "klasik". Consistent within the file, so recognizable — a polish item only.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the tricky V1→V2 primitives passages (vectorized inputs / "primitive unified bloc (pub)", the `shots` vs `precision` distinction, "fase `2\pi` bergeser satu siklus penuh, berbeda dari versi diskretnya") all land correctly, and no caveat or negation is inverted. What a native editor would still change: (1) the informal "kamu" convention breaks once into "Anda" in the V1-updates bullet ("Anda harus secara eksplisit mengonversi ke `SparsePauliOp`") while the very next bullet is back to "kamu harus"; (2) three in-file term splits — "primitif" vs "primitives" ("primitif Sampler"/"Primitif V2" vs "primitives V2"/"Primitives V2"), "antarmuka" vs untranslated "Interface" ("Interface V1 tidak mengizinkan fleksibilitas yang sama" against "antarmuka V1" everywhere else), and "pustaka" vs "library" ("Pustaka pulse diskret" vs "circuit library"/"library khusus"); (3) two small nuance shifts: "straightforward" strengthened to "sangat mudah", and "the module you are interested in" narrowed to "modul yang kamu butuhkan". None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: You should explicitly convert to a `SparsePauliOp` by using `SparsePauliOp.from_operator(operator)` instead.
examples.translation: Anda harus secara eksplisit mengonversi ke `SparsePauliOp` dengan menggunakan `SparsePauliOp.from_operator(operator)` sebagai gantinya.
examples.suggested: Kamu harus secara eksplisit mengonversi ke `SparsePauliOp` ...
examples.why: Single 'Anda' slip in an otherwise consistently 'kamu' file — the adjacent bullet eight lines later uses 'kamu harus mengonversi argumen secara eksplisit'.

examples.source: The V1 interface didn't allow for the same flexibility.
examples.translation: Interface V1 tidak mengizinkan fleksibilitas yang sama.
examples.suggested: Antarmuka V1 tidak mengizinkan fleksibilitas yang sama.
examples.why: 'interface' is rendered 'antarmuka' everywhere else in the file (e.g. 'antarmuka primitives V2', 'di antarmuka V1' two paragraphs later); this one leaves it as English 'Interface'.

examples.source: the Sampler primitive … The new V2 primitives … V2 primitives accept multiple PUBs
examples.translation: primitif [Sampler] … Primitif V2 baru dirancang … Primitives V2 menerima beberapa PUB
examples.suggested: Pick one: either 'primitif' throughout or keep 'primitives' throughout.
examples.why: The same concept alternates between the Indonesianized 'primitif' and the English 'primitives' within a few paragraphs; the concept stays identifiable, so this is cosmetic.

examples.source: The migration to the new paths is straightforward.
examples.translation: Migrasi ke jalur baru sangat mudah.
examples.suggested: Migrasi ke jalur baru cukup sederhana.
examples.why: 'straightforward' (uncomplicated) is upgraded to 'sangat mudah' (very easy) — a mild strengthening of the claim, harmless but not what the English says.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout this very short page: the compatibility break, the three link descriptions ("Perubahan paket yang memutus kompatibilitas di Qiskit v1.0" for "Breaking package changes") and the blog pointer all match the English, and the informal register ("proyekmu", "kode kamu") is consistent. The one editorial slip is an added sentiment word: "tapi sayangnya memutus kompatibilitas" injects "unfortunately", which the English ("but it does break compatibility with all previous versions") does not say — the English emphasis is factual ("does break"), not regretful. A native technical editor writing IBM-style release docs would drop "sayangnya" (e.g. "tetapi memang memutus kompatibilitas ..."), which preserves the emphatic "does" without editorializing. Nothing here misleads a learner.

examples.source: Qiskit 1.0 brings new stability guarantees and performance improvements, but it does break compatibility with all previous versions of Qiskit.
examples.translation: Qiskit 1.0 hadir dengan jaminan stabilitas baru dan peningkatan performa, tapi sayangnya memutus kompatibilitas dengan semua versi Qiskit sebelumnya.
examples.suggested: Qiskit 1.0 hadir dengan jaminan stabilitas baru dan peningkatan performa, tetapi memang memutus kompatibilitas dengan semua versi Qiskit sebelumnya.
examples.why: "sayangnya" (unfortunately) adds a regretful sentiment absent from the source; the English "does break" is emphatic-factual, best rendered with "memang". Tone-only, not a meaning change.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every claim (c_if removal, the "only IfElseOp and WhileLoopOp may have a condition" restriction, the v1.x bug-fix-until-September-2024 / security-until-March-2025 dates, the QPY/ScheduleBlock caveat) tracks the English exactly, and "kamu" is used consistently throughout. What a native editor would change is phrasing and one term split: "circuit" is rendered as the kept "Circuit" almost everywhere but slips to "sirkuit" inside a single sentence at line 124 ("eksekusi Circuit, 'durasi' sebuah sirkuit"). Several calques read as translationese rather than Indonesian technical prose — "sudah lebih direpresentasikan" for "preferentially represented" (line 29), "secara ketat lebih sedikit fiturnya" for "strictly less featureful" (line 39), and "mengquery"/"indeks Target pertama dengan nama operasi" (lines 108–109), where the imperative "index" is left as the noun "indeks". Line 192 drops the subject ("memungkinkan untuk membangun" where "dimungkinkan" is required), and line 104 drops the qualifier "directly" from "did not directly need to touch the information". None of these would lead a learner to a false belief.

examples.source: In general, as classical control-flow becomes more common within circuit executions, the "duration" of a circuit will become less and less well defined.
examples.translation: Secara umum, seiring control-flow klasik menjadi lebih umum dalam eksekusi Circuit, "durasi" sebuah sirkuit akan semakin tidak terdefinisi dengan baik.
examples.suggested: ... dalam eksekusi Circuit, "durasi" sebuah Circuit akan semakin tidak terdefinisi dengan baik.
examples.why: Within one sentence 'circuit' is rendered twice, once as the kept term 'Circuit' and once as 'sirkuit'. The file otherwise keeps 'Circuit' (lines 101, 104); the concept stays identifiable, so this is a consistency slip, not a misleading one.

examples.source: Classical conditions in Qiskit have been preferentially represented by the instruction IfElseOp since before Qiskit v1.0.
examples.translation: Kondisi klasik di Qiskit sudah lebih direpresentasikan oleh instruksi IfElseOp sejak sebelum Qiskit v1.0.
examples.suggested: Sejak sebelum Qiskit v1.0, kondisi klasik di Qiskit lebih dianjurkan untuk direpresentasikan dengan instruksi IfElseOp.
examples.why: 'sudah lebih direpresentasikan' is a word-for-word calque of 'preferentially represented' that no Indonesian technical writer would produce; 'lebih' dangles without a point of comparison.

examples.source: This was strictly less featureful than the full control-flow form, and was never well-supported on hardware.
examples.translation: Cara ini secara ketat lebih sedikit fiturnya dibandingkan bentuk control-flow penuh, dan tidak pernah didukung dengan baik pada hardware.
examples.suggested: Cara ini jelas lebih terbatas fiturnya dibandingkan bentuk control-flow penuh, dan tidak pernah didukung dengan baik di hardware.
examples.why: 'secara ketat' is a literal rendering of the mathematical sense of 'strictly' that reads as robotic here; 'jelas'/'benar-benar' carries the intended emphasis.

examples.source: You can retrieve the hardware-specified duration ... by querying the Target. To do this, index the Target first with the operation's name, and then the indices of the hardware qubits as a tuple.
examples.translation: ... dengan mengquery Target. Caranya, indeks Target pertama dengan nama operasi, lalu indeks qubit hardware sebagai tuple.
examples.suggested: ... dengan melakukan kueri ke Target. Caranya, indeks-kan Target terlebih dahulu dengan nama operasi, lalu dengan indeks Qubit hardware sebagai tuple.
examples.why: 'mengquery' is an unassimilated hybrid, and 'indeks Target pertama' parses more readily as the noun phrase 'the first index of Target' than as the imperative 'index the Target first'; the step is recoverable from context but the instruction is stiff.

examples.source: The alternatives are constructing a custom Target from scratch, constructing a generic backend, and, in addition to these, it is possible to build a custom target with instruction_durations and/or timing_constraints ...
examples.translation: Alternatifnya adalah membangun Target kustom dari awal, membangun Backend generik, dan, selain itu, memungkinkan untuk membangun target kustom dengan instruction_durations dan/atau timing_constraints ...
examples.suggested: ... dan, selain itu, dimungkinkan untuk membangun target kustom dengan instruction_durations dan/atau timing_constraints ...
examples.why: Active 'memungkinkan' needs a subject; the impersonal 'it is possible' requires the passive 'dimungkinkan'. A grammar slip, not a meaning change.

examples.source: Storing the information separately for each individual instruction significantly increased the memory demands of Qiskit and slowed down even circuit operations that did not directly need to touch the information.
examples.translation: Menyimpan informasi secara terpisah untuk setiap instruksi individual secara signifikan meningkatkan kebutuhan memori Qiskit dan memperlambat bahkan operasi Circuit yang tidak perlu menyentuh informasi tersebut.
examples.suggested: ... dan memperlambat bahkan operasi Circuit yang tidak secara langsung perlu menyentuh informasi tersebut.
examples.why: The qualifier 'directly' is dropped, so the translation says those operations did not need the information at all rather than did not need it directly. A dropped qualifier, but it does not change the takeaway (the cost hit unrelated operations).

editor_note: Judging only the two delta entries. Entry 70 (the llama.cpp AccordionItem title) is faithful and consistent with its siblings — "Deploy model Qiskit Code Assistant secara lokal melalui llama.cpp secara manual" matches the pattern used for the Ollama and `llama-cpp-python` accordions; the repeated "secara ... secara" is slightly heavy but defensible and carries "manually ... in local" correctly. Entry 141 (the benchmark table) preserves every model name, every score, the em-dashes for missing values, and both trailing columns, and localizes the headers sensibly ("Metrik Benchmark", "Tanggal rilis", "Dilatih pada versi Qiskit"); nothing here misleads. The one thing a native editor would change is that the **Release date** cell values stay English ("January 2026", "June 2025", "February 2025", "November 2024") while the very same dates are localized a few lines above in the model lists ("Dirilis Oktober 2025", "Juni 2025", "Februari 2025", "November 2024") — a within-file inconsistency in date rendering, not a factual error.

examples.source: | **mistral-small-3.2-24b-qiskit** | ... | **January 2026** | **2.2** |  ... | granite-8b-qiskit-rc-0.10 | ... | February 2025 | 1.3 |
examples.translation: | **mistral-small-3.2-24b-qiskit** | ... | **January 2026** | **2.2** |  ... | granite-8b-qiskit-rc-0.10 | ... | February 2025 | 1.3 |

examples.why: The month names in the 'Tanggal rilis' column are left in English while the same release dates are rendered in Indonesian in the adjacent lists (lines 437-443, 450-464, 486-488: 'Dirilis Oktober 2025', 'Juni 2025', 'Februari 2025'). The header was localized but its data was not, so one page shows two conventions for the same dates. No factual drift — scores, model names and Qiskit versions are byte-identical to the English.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries are headings that reorder an English product name into Indonesian head-initial order ("Qiskit MCP Servers" → "Server MCP Qiskit", "Qiskit Gym MCP Server" → "Server MCP Qiskit Gym"). Neither misleads — meaning is intact and the anchors are untouched — but both are now inconsistent with the rest of the same page, which keeps every other server name verbatim in English: the four sibling headings read "### Qiskit MCP Server", "### Qiskit Runtime MCP Server", "### Qiskit Docs MCP Server", "### Qiskit IBM Transpiler MCP Server", and the running prose says "Qiskit MCP Servers adalah kumpulan server…", "MCP server berikut ini tersedia", "Instal Qiskit MCP Servers". The H1 "Server MCP Qiskit" also contradicts the page's own frontmatter title 'Qiskit MCP Servers' and the section heading two screens down, so the same product appears under two names; entry 28 is doubly awkward because the installable package is literally `qiskit-gym-mcp-server`. Recommend restoring both to the English product names to match the file's established convention.

examples.source: Qiskit MCP Servers {#qiskit-mcp-servers}
examples.translation: Server MCP Qiskit {#qiskit-mcp-servers}
examples.suggested: Qiskit MCP Servers {#qiskit-mcp-servers}
examples.why: The H1 translates the product name while the frontmatter title (line 3) keeps 'Qiskit MCP Servers' and the section heading at line 42 keeps '### Qiskit MCP Server' — the same product is named two different ways on one page. Not misleading, but a native technical editor would keep the product name verbatim as the rest of the file does.

examples.source: Qiskit Gym MCP Server {#qiskit-gym-mcp-server}
examples.translation: Server MCP Qiskit Gym {#qiskit-gym-mcp-server}
examples.suggested: Qiskit Gym MCP Server {#qiskit-gym-mcp-server}
examples.why: This is the only server heading in the file that is reordered; its four siblings (Qiskit Runtime / Docs / IBM Transpiler MCP Server) stay in English, and the package the reader installs is `qiskit-gym-mcp-server`. Reordering breaks the visual match between heading and command without adding clarity.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the QPU-versioning rules (major/minor tidak dijamin bisa berjalan vs revision tetap bisa berjalan), the EPLG 4/5(1-LF^(1/99)) passage, prob_meas0_prep1/prep0 conditionals and the init-error vs prob_meas1_prep0 contrast all survive intact, and the informal "kamu/-mu" register holds consistently. What a native technical editor would change is consistency, not accuracy. (1) "gate" is rendered as "Gate" almost everywhere but slips to "gerbang" twice ("Durasi operasi gerbang dua-qubit", "gerbang Hadamard"). (2) Parallel table row headers are half-translated: "Lihat dengan Qiskit" / "Lihat di IBM Quantum Platform" in most blocks, but raw "View with Qiskit" / "View on IBM Quantum Platform" left in the prob-meas0-prep1, Gate length (2Q) and MCPS tables, plus one stray "Lihat di Platform IBM Quantum" word-order variant in the init-error block. (3) Accordion titles are inconsistently translated — "`T1` (Waktu relaksasi)" but "`T2` (Dephasing time)", "Panjang readout" in the body but "Readout length" in the title, "Initialization error" untranslated. (4) "state" vs "keadaan" splits within the init-error block. (5) One dropped qualifier: "necessarily" is lost in the `error = 1` note. None of these mislead; they are polish items.

examples.source: Duration of the two-qubit gate operation. / … reinitialization of a circuit with a Hadamard gate …
examples.translation: Durasi operasi gerbang dua-qubit. / … reinisialisasi circuit dengan gerbang Hadamard …
examples.suggested: Durasi operasi Gate dua-qubit. / … reinisialisasi circuit dengan Gate Hadamard …
examples.why: The file otherwise uses "Gate" consistently (Gate satu-qubit, Gate basis, Gate RZZ, Gate √X); these two "gerbang" instances are the only Indonesian-calque exceptions, so the same concept appears under two labels within one page.

examples.source: View with Qiskit / View on IBM Quantum Platform
examples.translation: View with Qiskit / View on IBM Quantum Platform (left in English in the prob-meas0-prep1, Gate length (2Q) and MCPS tables)
examples.suggested: Lihat dengan Qiskit / Lihat di IBM Quantum Platform
examples.why: Every other instance of these two identical row headers is translated, so the reader hits the same label in two languages inside adjacent accordion tables; also line 643 renders it as "Lihat di Platform IBM Quantum", a third variant of the product name's word order.

examples.source: This is not an indication that the qubit or edge is necessarily non-working or that the error is 1
examples.translation: Ini bukan indikasi bahwa qubit atau edge tersebut tidak berfungsi atau bahwa errornya adalah 1
examples.suggested: Ini bukan indikasi bahwa qubit atau edge tersebut pasti tidak berfungsi atau bahwa errornya adalah 1
examples.why: "necessarily" is dropped. The hedge matters here: the English says a stale value does not prove the qubit is broken, while the Indonesian reads closer to a flat denial. The following clause ("error dianggap tidak terdefinisi dan kamu harus berhati-hati") still carries the caveat, so this does not mislead, but the qualifier should be restored.

examples.source: `T1` (Relaxation time) … `T2` (Dephasing time) … Readout length … Initialization error

examples.source: the percentage of the population in the |1⟩ state … discriminating between the |0⟩ and |1⟩ states
