editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination: the no-cloning theorem and "ketidakmungkinan untuk membedakan dengan sempurna keadaan kuantum yang tidak ortogonal" both track the English exactly, and the informal "kamu" register holds. Two things a native technical editor would change, neither misleading. (1) *pengukuran projektif* is misspelled for Indonesian orthography — the adjective of "proyeksi" is *proyektif*, and the same sentence already writes *proyeksi* correctly, so the file is internally inconsistent on the same root. (2) "inner products" is rendered *perkalian dalam*; the settled Indonesian mathematical term is *hasil kali dalam* (perkalian dalam is understandable but non-standard). Minor extra nit in the same clause: *antar vektor* should be written closed as *antarvektor*.

examples.source: *projections* and *projective measurements*, which generalize standard basis measurements
examples.translation: *proyeksi* dan *pengukuran projektif*, yang menggeneralisasi pengukuran basis standar
examples.suggested: *proyeksi* dan *pengukuran proyektif*, yang menggeneralisasi pengukuran basis standar
examples.why: Indonesian derives the adjective from *proyeksi* → *proyektif*; the spelling *projektif* is a Dutch/English-influenced form and clashes with *proyeksi* written correctly two words earlier in the same sentence.

examples.source: *inner products* between vectors
examples.translation: *perkalian dalam* antar vektor
examples.suggested: *hasil kali dalam* antarvektor
examples.why: *Hasil kali dalam* is the conventional Indonesian term for inner product in linear-algebra/quantum texts; *perkalian dalam* is recognizable but non-standard. Also, the prefix *antar-* is written closed (*antarvektor*).

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no dropped caveat, no hallucination — and core terms are right ("matriks uniter", "keadaan kuantum", "vektor keadaan klasik dan kuantum", informal "kamu"/"kita" held consistently). Three editorial slips remain, none misleading. (1) "multiple systems" is rendered "sistem ganda", which in Indonesian reads as "double/dual (two) systems"; the source means several interacting systems, so "beberapa sistem" or "sistem majemuk" is the right rendering. (2) "the comparatively simple setting" is calqued as "pengaturan yang relatif sederhana" — "pengaturan" in Indonesian means device settings/configuration, not an intellectual setting; "situasi"/"kasus yang relatif sederhana" is what a native technical writer would use, and the clause also uses the calqued relative "di mana" for a non-place antecedent. (3) "operations ... described by unitary matrices" becomes "operasi ... yang dijelaskan oleh matriks uniter" ("explained by"), where "digambarkan"/"dinyatakan oleh" carries the mathematical sense of "described". Also note "in isolation" flattened to "secara terpisah" rather than "secara terisolasi".

examples.source: In the next lesson, we'll expand our view to *multiple systems,* which can interact with one another and be correlated.
examples.translation: Dalam pelajaran berikutnya, kita akan memperluas pandangan kita ke *sistem ganda,* yang bisa berinteraksi satu sama lain dan berkorelasi.
examples.suggested: ... ke *beberapa sistem,* yang dapat berinteraksi satu sama lain dan saling berkorelasi.
examples.why: "ganda" means double/dual in Indonesian and narrows "multiple" to exactly two; the lesson covers systems in general, so "beberapa sistem" (or "sistem majemuk") is the conventional rendering.

examples.source: We will restrict our attention in this lesson to the comparatively simple setting in which a *single system* is considered in isolation.
examples.translation: Kita akan membatasi perhatian kita dalam pelajaran ini pada pengaturan yang relatif sederhana di mana *satu sistem* dipertimbangkan secara terpisah.
examples.suggested: Dalam pelajaran ini kita membatasi pembahasan pada kasus yang relatif sederhana, yaitu ketika *satu sistem* ditinjau secara terisolasi.
examples.why: "pengaturan" is a calque of "setting" that in Indonesian means configuration/settings; "di mana" as a relative pronoun for a non-place antecedent and "dipertimbangkan" for "is considered" (here: "ditinjau") are English syntax showing through.

examples.source: operations on quantum states that are described by unitary matrices
examples.translation: operasi pada keadaan kuantum yang dijelaskan oleh matriks uniter
examples.suggested: operasi pada keadaan kuantum yang digambarkan (dinyatakan) oleh matriks uniter
examples.why: "dijelaskan" = "explained"; the mathematical sense of "described by" is "digambarkan/dinyatakan oleh". Meaning survives, but the technical idiom is off.

editor_note: Delta entry 87 only: "National Academies / Standards Bodies" → "Akademi Nasional / Badan Standardisasi" is faithful and idiomatic — "Badan Standardisasi" is the standard Indonesian term for standards bodies, and the generic "Akademi Nasional" matches the sibling reference-category italics in the same section ("Laporan Pemerintah / Resmi", "Organisasi Antar Pemerintah / Kebijakan"), so the grouping label stays consistent and nothing misleads; the entry it labels (National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine) correctly keeps its proper name untranslated.

Nothing in this short overview page misleads a learner: the audience list, the "no technical prerequisite" statement, the 4-hour estimate and the Quantum Business Foundations pointer all match the English exactly, and the informal "kamu" / "tapi" register is held consistently. Two small qualifier losses are what a native editor would still change: the adverb "effectively" in "assist teams and organizations to effectively build the necessary capabilities" has no counterpart in "membantu tim dan organisasi dalam membangun kapabilitas yang diperlukan" (only "successfully" survives, as "dengan sukses"), and "It will be of particular use to organizations new to quantum computing" becomes "Kursus ini sangat berguna bagi…", trading the comparative "particular(ly)" for a plain intensifier "sangat". Secondary, non-blocking: "academic faculty" → "staf akademis" reads as university staff generally rather than teaching faculty ("dosen" would be sharper), and "concerns" → "kekhawatiran" is a slightly literal rendering where "masukan" would sound more like a native contact line — both defensible as they stand.

examples.source: This course is designed to assist teams and organizations to effectively build the necessary capabilities to successfully kick-start quantum initiatives.
examples.translation: Kursus ini dirancang untuk membantu tim dan organisasi dalam membangun kapabilitas yang diperlukan agar bisa memulai inisiatif kuantum dengan sukses.
examples.suggested: Kursus ini dirancang untuk membantu tim dan organisasi membangun kapabilitas yang diperlukan secara efektif, agar bisa memulai inisiatif kuantum dengan sukses.
examples.why: The qualifier "effectively" (which modifies how the capabilities are built) is dropped; only "successfully" is carried over. Non-misleading, but a lost nuance of the source claim.

examples.source: It will be of particular use to organizations new to quantum computing.
examples.translation: Kursus ini sangat berguna bagi organisasi yang baru mengenal komputasi kuantum.
examples.suggested: Kursus ini akan terutama bermanfaat bagi organisasi yang baru mengenal komputasi kuantum.
examples.why: "of particular use" singles out that group relative to others; "sangat berguna" only asserts a high degree of usefulness, flattening the comparative emphasis the English uses to steer the reader.

examples.source: including academic faculty, project leaders in large enterprises, startup leadership
examples.translation: termasuk staf akademis, manajer proyek di perusahaan besar, pimpinan startup
examples.suggested: termasuk dosen dan peneliti, pemimpin proyek di perusahaan besar, pimpinan startup
examples.why: "staf akademis" covers university staff in general (including administrative), whereas "academic faculty" means teaching/research faculty; "dosen" is the conventional Indonesian term. Recognizable, so MINOR only.

editor_note: The only entry under judgment (entry 33, the section heading) renders "Global systems integrators" as "Integrator sistem global" — the correct, natural Indonesian noun phrase with the unmarked plural and the adjective order a native technical writer would use; the anchor {#global-systems-integrators} is preserved and the heading matches the section body that follows (integrasi teknologi kuantum ke dalam sistem klien).

Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination: the syndrome/collapse argument, the product-state conclusion ("Yang paling penting, ini adalah keadaan produk"), the |α|²…|δ|² probability caveat, the single-qubit-operation argument in the last 40%, and the Kraus/generalization sections all track the English exactly, and register is consistently "kita" with no deferential slips. What a native technical editor would change is wording. "Arbitrary" is rendered everywhere as "sembarangan" ("kesalahan yang sembarangan", "channel qubit sembarangan"), which in Indonesian reads as "careless/haphazard"; the mathematical determiner is "sebarang"/"sembarang" — recognizable in context, so not misleading, but non-standard in every occurrence. Two calques stand out: "ada kemungkinan kesalahan yang tak terbatas" for "there are infinitely many possible errors like this" ("tak terbatas" = unbounded, not "tak hingga", and "like this" is dropped), and "probabilitas dimana keadaan yang di-encode kolaps" for "the probabilities with which…" (English relative-clause syntax, plus "dimana" should be "di mana"). Terminology is also mixed in convention: "uniter" and "matriks densitas" are Indonesianized while "channel" and "encoding" are kept in English, where "kanal" and "pengodean/penyandian" are the usual domain renderings.

examples.source: …in this section we'll consider arbitrary errors.
examples.translation: …di bagian ini kita akan mempertimbangkan kesalahan yang sembarangan.
examples.suggested: …di bagian ini kita akan meninjau kesalahan sebarang.
examples.why: "sembarangan" is the adverb "carelessly/haphazardly"; the mathematical "arbitrary" is "sebarang" (or "sembarang"). Used this way in every occurrence, incl. the heading "Kesalahan qubit sembarangan" and "channel qubit sembarangan". Recognizable, so not misleading, but consistently off-register for a maths text.

examples.source: After all, there are infinitely many possible errors like this, and it's inconceivable that we could somehow identify each error exactly and then undo it.
examples.translation: Lagi pula, ada kemungkinan kesalahan yang tak terbatas, dan tidak terbayangkan bahwa kita bisa mengidentifikasi setiap kesalahan secara tepat dan kemudian membatalkannya.
examples.suggested: Lagi pula, ada tak hingga banyaknya kesalahan semacam ini, dan tidak terbayangkan kita dapat mengidentifikasi setiap kesalahan secara persis lalu membatalkannya.
examples.why: "tak terbatas" means unbounded/unlimited; the count sense is "tak hingga". "kemungkinan kesalahan yang tak terbatas" also reads as "unlimited error possibility" rather than "infinitely many errors", and the qualifier "like this" (semacam ini) is dropped.

examples.source: …the values … are the probabilities with which the encoded state collapses to one for which the corresponding Pauli error has occurred.
examples.translation: …adalah probabilitas dimana keadaan yang di-encode kolaps ke keadaan di mana kesalahan Pauli yang bersesuaian telah terjadi.
examples.suggested: …adalah peluang bahwa keadaan terkode kolaps ke keadaan yang mengalami kesalahan Pauli bersesuaian.
examples.why: "probabilitas dimana" is a direct calque of "the probabilities with which" — a native writer uses "peluang bahwa…". It also stacks two relative clauses in one sentence, and "dimana" is misspelled (should be "di mana").

examples.source: …an error described by an arbitrary qubit channel Φ … this could be a dephasing or depolarizing channel, a reset channel…
examples.translation: …kesalahan yang dideskripsikan oleh channel qubit sembarangan $\Phi$ … ini bisa berupa channel dephasing atau depolarizing, channel reset…
examples.suggested: …kanal qubit sebarang $\Phi$ … kanal dephasing atau depolarizing, kanal reset…
examples.why: The file Indonesianizes "unitary"→"uniter" and "density matrix"→"matriks densitas" but leaves "channel" (and "encoding") in English; "kanal" is the conventional Indonesian term for a quantum channel, so the convention is internally inconsistent.

examples.source: …even errors that are tiny and hardly noticeable on their own. / …we've simply expanded out all of our Kraus matrices…
examples.translation: …bahkan kesalahan yang sangat kecil dan hampir tidak terasa sendiri. / Singkatnya, kita hanya mengekspansi semua matriks Kraus kita…
examples.suggested: …bahkan kesalahan yang sangat kecil dan nyaris tak terdeteksi jika berdiri sendiri. / Singkatnya, kita hanya menjabarkan semua matriks Kraus…
examples.why: "hampir tidak terasa sendiri" is stiff and ambiguous ("sendiri" dangles); "mengekspansi" is a borrowed verb Indonesian maths prose renders as "menjabarkan"/"menguraikan". Both are stylistic, meaning is intact.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every claim (fragility, the isolation-vs-control tension, "little doubt" → "hampir tidak ada keraguan", the 9-qubit Shor code and *diskretisasi kesalahan*) matches the English, and the informal "kamu" register holds throughout. The one real terminology slip is "environmental noise" → "kebisingan lingkungan": *kebisingan* is acoustic loudness, while the field's Indonesian rendering is "derau lingkungan" (or simply "noise lingkungan") — recognizable in context but the wrong domain word. Two qualifiers are silently dropped: "reliably implement" loses *andal* (the translation just says "bisa mengimplementasikan"), and "you can literally ruin it" loses *secara harfiah*. Finally, "we'll take a first look at quantum error correction" is calqued as "kita akan melihat pertama kali koreksi kesalahan kuantum", which a native technical writer would phrase "kita akan melihat sekilas untuk pertama kalinya…". None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: its susceptibility to both inaccuracies and environmental noise
examples.translation: kerentanannya terhadap ketidakakuratan dan kebisingan lingkungan
examples.suggested: kerentanannya terhadap ketidakakuratan dan derau lingkungan
examples.why: 'Kebisingan' means audible/acoustic noise; the physics sense of noise is 'derau' (or kept as 'noise') in Indonesian technical writing.

examples.source: before we can reliably implement the sorts of large-scale quantum computations
examples.translation: sebelum kita bisa mengimplementasikan komputasi kuantum berskala besar
examples.suggested: sebelum kita bisa mengimplementasikan secara andal komputasi kuantum berskala besar
examples.why: The qualifier 'reliably' is dropped; reliability is precisely the property this error-correction course is about, so the sentence loses its point.

examples.source: you can literally ruin it just by looking at it
examples.translation: kamu bisa merusaknya hanya dengan melihatnya
examples.suggested: kamu benar-benar bisa merusaknya hanya dengan melihatnya
examples.why: 'Literally' carries the rhetorical punch of the sentence (measurement really does destroy the state); without it the line reads as a loose figure of speech.

examples.source: we'll take a first look at quantum error correction
examples.translation: kita akan melihat pertama kali koreksi kesalahan kuantum
examples.suggested: kita akan melihat sekilas untuk pertama kalinya koreksi kesalahan kuantum
examples.why: Calqued word order; 'melihat pertama kali' reads as broken Indonesian rather than 'a first look at'.

editor_note: Semantically faithful throughout — every quantitative claim survives intact (3p²(1-p)+p³ discussion, "lebih kecil dari setengah" for p<1/2, the syndrome tables, "jumlah ganjil kesalahan phase-flip", the no-cloning caveat, and the crucial reversal that the modified code "sekarang tidak lagi bisa mengoreksi kesalahan bit-flip"); no inverted conditions, dropped caveats or hallucinated sentences, and register is consistently the informal "kita". What a native technical editor would change is a cluster of English-shaped calques: "Setaranya, kita bisa *mendekode*" (line 37) for "Equivalently"; "dalam kasus yang ada di tangan kita" (line 106), a word-for-word rendering of "in the case at hand"; "encoding yang sempurna valid" (line 159) instead of "sepenuhnya valid/sah"; and "Namun semua tidak hilang." (line 226), a literal calque of "All is not lost" that reads as broken Indonesian rather than the intended "Namun, belum semuanya hilang". Two smaller slips: "kesalahan kuantum sembarangan" (line 146) where the domain form is "sembarang" ("sembarangan" colloquially means careless/haphazard), and "tabel yang analogi dengan" (line 216) where it should be "analog/serupa dengan". Also "mengulang setiap bit beberapa kali yang tetap" (line 23) is a stiff rendering of "some fixed number of times" — "sejumlah kali tertentu" would be idiomatic. None of these mislead; they are polish items.

examples.source: All is not lost, however.
examples.translation: Namun semua tidak hilang.
examples.suggested: Namun, belum semuanya hilang.
examples.why: Word-for-word calque of the English idiom; the negation scope in Indonesian lands wrong and reads as broken prose, where the English is a reassuring aside.

examples.source: which, in the case at hand, would cause us to see $010$ or $101$
examples.translation: yang dalam kasus yang ada di tangan kita, akan menyebabkan kita melihat $010$ atau $101$
examples.suggested: yang, dalam kasus ini, akan membuat kita melihat $010$ atau $101$
examples.why: "kasus yang ada di tangan kita" is a literal rendering of "the case at hand"; a native technical writer would simply write "dalam kasus ini".

examples.source: the ability to correct an arbitrary quantum error on a single qubit
examples.translation: kemampuan untuk mengoreksi kesalahan kuantum sembarangan pada satu qubit
examples.suggested: kemampuan mengoreksi kesalahan kuantum sembarang pada satu qubit
examples.why: The technical sense "arbitrary" is "sembarang"; "sembarangan" in ordinary usage means careless/haphazard, which subtly mis-colours a key theoretical statement (still recognizable, hence minor).

examples.source: Equivalently, we can *decode* by computing the majority value
examples.translation: Setaranya, kita bisa *mendekode* dengan menghitung nilai mayoritas
examples.suggested: Dengan kata lain / Secara setara, kita bisa *mendekode* dengan menghitung nilai mayoritas
examples.why: "Setaranya" is not idiomatic as a sentence-initial discourse marker in Indonesian technical prose.

examples.source: one can easily deduce from the measurement outcomes the location of the bit-flip
examples.translation: seseorang bisa dengan mudah menyimpulkan dari hasil pengukuran lokasi bit-flip
examples.suggested: kita bisa dengan mudah menyimpulkan lokasi bit-flip dari hasil pengukuran
examples.why: The English fronted-object word order is copied verbatim, leaving "hasil pengukuran lokasi bit-flip" momentarily readable as one noun phrase; "seseorang" for generic "one" is also stiff next to the file's consistent "kita".

editor_note: Semantically faithful throughout — every load-bearing claim survives intact (syndrome $11$ → blok tengah, "empat gate CNOT lebih sedikit", anti-komut $XZ=-ZX$, break-even $0{,}0323$, "paling banyak satu blok mengalami jumlah ganjil"), and the degeneracy aside and the closing "bukan kode yang sangat bagus dari segi praktis" both land. The defects are editorial, not misleading. (1) "arbitrary" is rendered "sembarangan" (careless/haphazard) three times — lines 47, 92, 178 — where Indonesian technical prose needs "sembarang"; "vektor keadaan qubit sembarangan" reads as "a carelessly-made state vector". (2) The italicized term of art *concatenating* collapses into "*menggabungkan*", the exact generic verb already used for "combining together" two sentences earlier, so the QEC concept of code concatenation loses its name (the following sentence still defines it, so the concept stays identifiable). (3) "Three and a quarter percent or so" becomes "Tiga dan seperempat persen atau lebih" — "or more" instead of "or thereabouts", an altered qualifier. Plus scattered calques: "dalam beberapa keadaan tertentu" for "in some particular state", "jumlah ganjil dari mereka" (inanimate "mereka"), and "Circuit yang disederhanakan kita" word order.

examples.source: how an arbitrary qubit state vector is encoded / an arbitrary qubit state $\vert\psi\rangle$ / arbitrary quantum errors
examples.translation: bagaimana vektor keadaan qubit sembarangan di-encode / keadaan qubit sembarangan $\vert\psi\rangle$ / kesalahan kuantum sembarangan
examples.suggested: vektor keadaan qubit sembarang / keadaan qubit sembarang / kesalahan kuantum sembarang
examples.why: In Indonesian "sembarangan" is adverbial and means careless/haphazard; the mathematical sense "arbitrary" is "sembarang". Repeated three times, so it reads as a systematic MT habit rather than a typo.

examples.source: the code we obtain by *concatenating* the two codes from the previous section
examples.translation: kode yang kita peroleh dengan *menggabungkan* dua kode dari bagian sebelumnya
examples.suggested: kode yang kita peroleh dengan *mengonkatenasi* (concatenating) dua kode dari bagian sebelumnya
examples.why: The English italicizes *concatenating* precisely because it is the QEC term of art (code concatenation). "Menggabungkan" is the same generic verb already used for "combining together" in the opening paragraph, so the named concept disappears; the next sentence still explains the mechanism, which keeps this MINOR.

examples.source: Three and a quarter percent or so may not seem like a very good break-even point
examples.translation: Tiga dan seperempat persen atau lebih mungkin tidak terlihat seperti titik impas yang sangat bagus
examples.suggested: Sekitar tiga seperempat persen mungkin tidak terlihat sebagai titik impas yang sangat bagus
examples.why: "or so" is an approximation hedge; "atau lebih" asserts "or more". The exact figure 0,0323 was just given, so no learner is actually misled, but the qualifier is altered rather than translated.

examples.source: supposing that $\mathsf{Q}$ is a qubit in some particular state that we'd like to protect against errors
examples.translation: misalkan $\mathsf{Q}$ adalah qubit dalam beberapa keadaan tertentu yang ingin kita lindungi dari kesalahan
examples.suggested: misalkan $\mathsf{Q}$ adalah qubit dalam suatu keadaan tertentu yang ingin kita lindungi dari kesalahan
examples.why: "beberapa" = several, a literal calque of English "some"; it implies the single qubit occupies multiple states. Indonesian wants "suatu" for the indefinite-singular sense.

examples.source: our simplified circuit ... an odd number of them ... so long as at most one of the nine qubits is affected by an error
examples.translation: Circuit yang disederhanakan kita ... jumlah ganjil dari mereka ... selama paling banyak satu dari sembilan qubit yang terpengaruh oleh kesalahan
examples.suggested: Circuit kita yang disederhanakan ... jumlah kesalahan yang ganjil ... selama paling banyak satu dari sembilan qubit terpengaruh oleh kesalahan
examples.why: Three small calqued-syntax slips: possessive after the relative clause, inanimate "mereka" for "them" (Indonesian repeats the noun), and a stray "yang" in line 198 that turns the clause into a noun phrase with no predicate.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the exam facts survive intact (20 pertanyaan, "setidaknya 16 dengan benar untuk lulus", "Jika kamu tidak mendapat nilai lulus dalam dua percobaan, ujian akan terkunci sementara"), and the full Credly/IBM privacy NOTICE paragraph is rendered completely with no dropped caveat; informal register ("kamu"/"-mu") holds everywhere. Two editorial slips, neither misleading: (1) "course" is left untranslated twice in the survey paragraph ("menyelesaikan course ... dari IBM", "meningkatkan course ini") while the very next section correctly uses "kursus ini" — the same word rendered two ways within the file; (2) the course title is kept in English in one place ("Foundations of quantum error correction") but translated in another ("ujian lencana untuk Fondasi koreksi kesalahan kuantum"), so a learner sees two names for the same course. Cosmetic aside (not counted): the trailing period is placed inside the link text in "[di sini.](…)" twice in the notice.

examples.source: Congratulations on completing the "Foundations of quantum error correction" course by IBM! Please take a moment to help us improve our course…
examples.translation: Selamat telah menyelesaikan course "Foundations of quantum error correction" dari IBM! Luangkan waktu sejenak untuk membantu kami meningkatkan course ini…
examples.suggested: Selamat telah menyelesaikan kursus "Foundations of quantum error correction" dari IBM! … membantu kami meningkatkan kursus ini…
examples.why: "course" is left in English here but rendered "kursus" in the next section ("dalam kursus ini"); Indonesian has a settled everyday term and the file should pick one.

examples.source: the "Foundations of quantum error correction" course … the badging exam for Foundations of quantum error correction
examples.translation: course "Foundations of quantum error correction" … ujian lencana untuk Fondasi koreksi kesalahan kuantum
examples.suggested: Keep one form for the course name in both places (either the English title throughout, or "Fondasi koreksi kesalahan kuantum" throughout, matching the page title).
examples.why: The same course is named two different ways in adjacent sections, which reads as two different courses; the frontmatter title already commits to "Fondasi koreksi kesalahan kuantum".

editor_note: No semantic drift: every quantitative and conditional claim survives intact (five physical qubits per logical qubit, "hanya lokasi kesalahan yang independen" vs correlated errors, the 9-qubit Shor break-even condition "jika probabilitas kesalahan pada setiap qubit di atas titik impas", and the below-threshold conditional in the closing paragraph). The recurring defect is a calque of English "suggest": "Diagram menyarankan bahwa lima qubit fisik digunakan" and "seperti yang disarankan oleh kotak biru berlabel \"EC\"" both use menyarankan (= to recommend/advise) where the English means "indicates/shows"; a native technical writer would write mengisyaratkan or ditunjukkan. Two more translationese spots: "Mungkin lebih mungkin, ada kesalahan yang terlokalisir" (stuttering rendering of "Perhaps more likely") and "sebagai contoh yang terus berjalan" for "running example" (idiomatic Indonesian would be "contoh acuan"). Also "sangat wajar untuk menolak model tersebut" slightly overstates "reasonable to object to such a model" (menolak = reject rather than raise an objection), and the DefinitionTooltip definition prop is still English ("Entropy is a measure of randomness…") while the visible word is translated to "entropi". Terminology is otherwise correct and consistent: qubit, gate, uniter, dekoherensi, noise kept, kode koreksi kesalahan, gadget.

examples.source: The diagram suggests that five physical qubits are used for each logical qubit… / as suggested by the blue boxes labeled "EC"
examples.translation: Diagram menyarankan bahwa lima qubit fisik digunakan untuk setiap qubit logis… / seperti yang disarankan oleh kotak biru berlabel "EC"
examples.suggested: Diagram mengisyaratkan bahwa lima qubit fisik digunakan… / seperti ditunjukkan oleh kotak biru berlabel "EC"
examples.why: "menyarankan" in Indonesian means to recommend or advise; a diagram does not advise. English "suggest" here means indicate. Calque, repeated twice in the same section.

examples.source: Perhaps more likely, there could be errors that are localized but that nevertheless affect multiple components in a quantum computer.
examples.translation: Mungkin lebih mungkin, ada kesalahan yang terlokalisir tetapi tetap mempengaruhi beberapa komponen dalam komputer kuantum.
examples.suggested: Yang mungkin lebih sering terjadi, ada kesalahan yang terlokalisir tetapi tetap mempengaruhi beberapa komponen dalam komputer kuantum.
examples.why: "Mungkin lebih mungkin" repeats the same root twice and reads as raw word-for-word MT; no Indonesian technical writer would produce it.

examples.source: We'll use the teleportation circuit above as a running example to illustrate the strategy
examples.translation: Kita akan menggunakan Circuit teleportasi di atas sebagai contoh yang terus berjalan untuk mengilustrasikan strategi
examples.suggested: Kita akan menggunakan Circuit teleportasi di atas sebagai contoh acuan untuk mengilustrasikan strategi
examples.why: "contoh yang terus berjalan" is a literal calque of "running example" and reads as a circuit that keeps executing, not as a recurring illustrative example.

examples.source: Now, it is certainly reasonable to object to such a model, because there probably will be correlations among errors in real physical devices.
examples.translation: Sekarang, sangat wajar untuk menolak model tersebut, karena mungkin akan ada korelasi di antara kesalahan dalam perangkat fisik nyata.
examples.suggested: Sekarang, sangat wajar untuk mengajukan keberatan terhadap model tersebut, karena mungkin akan ada korelasi di antara kesalahan dalam perangkat fisik nyata.
examples.why: "menolak" = reject outright; the English only concedes that one may raise an objection, and the next paragraphs go on to defend keeping the model. Mild strengthening of the claim, not enough to mislead on its own.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, no hallucinated claims, and the threshold-theorem paragraph correctly keeps "berhingga" for *finite* and the critical negation ("tetapi yang krusial *tidak* bergantung pada ukuran Circuit kuantum"). The one substantive slip is a dropped qualifier repeated twice: English "arbitrarily large" (quantum computations / quantum circuits) is rendered both times as "yang sangat besar" ("very large"), which weakens the theorem's actual claim of unbounded size; "sebesar apa pun" or "berukuran sembarang" would be correct. Secondary: encode/decode is rendered three ways in adjacent sentences — "di-encode", "meng-encode ulang", "mendekode" — an inconsistent mix of hyphenated borrowing and Indonesianized verb; and "itu sendiri akan tidak sempurna" is stiff translationese where a native writer would write "pun tidak sempurna". Informal register ("kamu", "kita") holds consistently; core terms (qubit, gate, noise, propagasi kesalahan, nilai ambang, magic state, transversal) are correct and stable.

examples.source: it is possible in theory to perform arbitrarily large quantum computations reliably using noisy hardware. / arbitrarily large quantum circuits can be implemented reliably
examples.translation: secara teori dimungkinkan untuk melakukan komputasi kuantum yang sangat besar secara andal menggunakan perangkat keras yang noisy. / Circuit kuantum yang sangat besar bisa diimplementasikan secara andal
examples.suggested: komputasi kuantum sebesar apa pun … / Circuit kuantum berukuran sembarang (sebesar apa pun) …
examples.why: "sangat besar" = "very large", a bounded intensifier; "arbitrarily large" is the load-bearing claim of the threshold theorem (no bound on size). Dropping it softens the theorem into a vaguer statement, twice.

examples.source: qubits that have been encoded using a quantum error correcting code … decoding qubits … re-encoding once we're done
examples.translation: qubit yang telah di-encode … mendekode qubit … meng-encode ulang setelah selesai
examples.suggested: Pick one convention, e.g. "dikodekan / mendekodekan / mengodekan ulang" or consistently hyphenated "di-encode / men-decode / meng-encode ulang".
examples.why: Three different morphological treatments of the same encode/decode pair within two adjacent sentences; recognizable but visibly inconsistent to a native technical editor.

examples.source: the quantum gates, measurements, and state initializations used to implement quantum computations will themselves be imperfect
examples.translation: gate kuantum, pengukuran, dan inisialisasi keadaan yang digunakan untuk mengimplementasikan komputasi kuantum itu sendiri akan tidak sempurna
examples.suggested: … yang digunakan untuk mengimplementasikan komputasi kuantum pun tidak sempurna
examples.why: "akan tidak sempurna" is a calque of the English future "will themselves be"; Indonesian technical prose uses "pun tidak sempurna" for this emphatic-inclusive construction, and the future marker is unnatural here.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: the theorem statement, the p < p_th = 1/C condition, the Cp^2 bound, the doubly-exponential-in-k error decay vs. singly-exponential size growth, and the 0.1%–1% surface-code estimate all match the English exactly, and the informal "kamu" register holds in the survey block. What a native technical editor would change is a handful of calques. "On the order of" is rendered literally as "urutan" (line 21 "dalam urutan $N$ dikalikan dengan…", line 89 "berada pada urutan 0,1% hingga 1%"), which in Indonesian reads as "sequence", not magnitude — the domain word is "orde" (or "sekitar"/"berkisar"). English "translate to" is likewise carried over as literal "diterjemahkan" twice (line 26 "tidak selalu diterjemahkan ke pendekatan praktis", line 48 "ini diterjemahkan ke pengurangan kesalahan") where Indonesian wants "berujung pada" / "berarti". Smaller slips: "3.23% or so" becomes "di atas 3,23% atau lebih" ("or more" instead of "sekitar"), line 53 drops the copula in "seolah-olah Circuit lain mana pun" (needs "seolah-olah itu adalah Circuit kuantum lain mana pun"), and "rather cavalier about the noise model" is flattened to "cukup tidak peduli tentang model noise". None of these would make a learner believe something false.

examples.source: the size of the noisy circuit required is on the order of $N$ times some constant power of the logarithm of $N$ … the threshold has been estimated to be on the order of 0.1% to 1%.
examples.translation: ukuran Circuit noisy yang diperlukan adalah dalam urutan $N$ dikalikan dengan beberapa pangkat konstan dari logaritma $N$ … ambangnya diperkirakan berada pada urutan 0,1% hingga 1%.
examples.suggested: ukuran Circuit noisy yang diperlukan berorde $N$ dikali suatu pangkat konstan dari logaritma $N$ … ambangnya diperkirakan berkisar antara 0,1% hingga 1%.
examples.why: "Urutan" means sequence/ordering in Indonesian; the magnitude sense of "on the order of" is "orde" (or simply "sekitar"/"berkisar"). Recognizable from context and the adjacent formula, so imperfect rather than misleading, but it is not how an Indonesian technical writer would phrase a scaling statement.

examples.source: the most typical way it is proved doesn't necessarily translate to a practical approach … this translates to a reduction in error.
examples.translation: cara paling umum pembuktiannya tidak selalu diterjemahkan ke pendekatan praktis … ini diterjemahkan ke pengurangan kesalahan.
examples.suggested: cara pembuktian yang paling umum tidak selalu berujung pada pendekatan praktis … ini berarti adanya pengurangan kesalahan.
examples.why: "Diterjemahkan" is the linguistic sense of "translate" and is a direct calque here; Indonesian uses "berujung pada", "berarti" or "menghasilkan" for this figurative sense. Twice in the same file, so it reads as machine output rather than authored prose.

examples.source: just like the $9$-qubit Shor code doesn't help if the error probability is above 3.23% or so.
examples.translation: sama seperti kode Shor $9$-Qubit tidak membantu jika probabilitas kesalahan di atas 3,23% atau lebih.
examples.suggested: sama seperti kode Shor $9$-Qubit tidak membantu jika probabilitas kesalahan berada di atas sekitar 3,23%.
examples.why: "Or so" is an approximation hedge on the number (≈3.23%), but "atau lebih" renders it as "or more", attaching a redundant quantity clause to "di atas". The hedge on the value is lost; the claim itself still points the right way, so it is a dropped qualifier rather than an inverted fact.

examples.source: we can think of the *fault-tolerant* implementation of the original circuit as if it were any other quantum circuit
examples.translation: kita bisa memikirkan implementasi *toleran terhadap kesalahan* dari Circuit asli seolah-olah Circuit lain mana pun
examples.suggested: kita bisa memandang implementasi *toleran terhadap kesalahan* dari Circuit asli seolah-olah ia adalah Circuit kuantum lain mana pun
examples.why: The copula after "seolah-olah" is dropped, leaving a clause that stops short grammatically; "memikirkan" also mis-fits — the idiom for "think of X as Y" is "memandang/menganggap X sebagai Y". The intended meaning is still recoverable.

examples.source: This explanation will also be rather cavalier about the noise model
examples.translation: Penjelasan ini juga akan cukup tidak peduli tentang model noise
examples.suggested: Penjelasan ini juga akan bersikap cukup longgar terhadap model noise
examples.why: "Tidak peduli" (does not care) is a blunt literalization of "cavalier"; the pedagogical self-deprecation of the English ("we'll be loose about this") flattens into something closer to indifference. Nuance softened, not reversed.

editor_note: Meaning is fully faithful — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat; the load-bearing specifics all survive (the 9/7/5-qubit code list, "satu kesalahan dari lima, tujuh, atau sembilan", CSS as *pasangan* tertentu of classical codes, and the toric code as "keluarga kode yang tak terbatas, satu untuk setiap bilangan bulat positif yang lebih besar dari satu"). Terminology is correct and consistent throughout (kode koreksi kesalahan kuantum, kode CSS, kode torik, kode permukaan, kode warna) and the Anda register holds. What a native technical editor would change is translationese: "merepresentasikan tempat yang alami untuk memulai" is a word-for-word calque of "represent a natural place to begin" (native: "merupakan titik awal yang wajar"), "mereka" is used as an English-style pronoun for the inanimate codes, "memungkinkan seseorang untuk mengambil" calques "allows one to take", and "melihat pertama kali" is a stiff rendering of "take a first look". Also "mentoleransi" (3x) instead of the KBBI-standard "menoleransi" — consistent and recognizable, so cosmetic only.

examples.source: These codes are undoubtedly interesting and represent a natural place to begin an exploration of quantum error correction, but a problem with them is that they can only tolerate a very low error rate.
examples.translation: Kode-kode ini tidak diragukan lagi menarik dan merepresentasikan tempat yang alami untuk memulai eksplorasi koreksi kesalahan kuantum, tetapi masalah dengan kode-kode ini adalah bahwa mereka hanya bisa mentoleransi tingkat kesalahan yang sangat rendah.
examples.suggested: Kode-kode ini memang menarik dan merupakan titik awal yang wajar untuk mendalami koreksi kesalahan kuantum, tetapi masalahnya, kode-kode ini hanya mampu menoleransi tingkat kesalahan yang sangat rendah.
examples.why: Two calques in one sentence: 'merepresentasikan tempat yang alami untuk memulai' is a literal transfer of 'represent a natural place to begin', and 'mereka' is used as an English-style pronoun for inanimate codes, which Indonesian technical prose avoids (it drops the pronoun or repeats the noun). Meaning is intact — this is style only.

examples.source: The CSS code construction allows one to take certain *pairs* of classical error correcting codes and combine them into a single quantum error correcting code.
examples.translation: Konstruksi kode CSS memungkinkan seseorang untuk mengambil *pasangan* tertentu dari kode koreksi kesalahan klasik dan menggabungkannya menjadi satu kode koreksi kesalahan kuantum.
examples.suggested: Konstruksi kode CSS memungkinkan kita mengambil *pasangan* tertentu kode koreksi kesalahan klasik dan menggabungkannya menjadi satu kode koreksi kesalahan kuantum.
examples.why: 'memungkinkan seseorang untuk' is a direct calque of the impersonal English 'allows one to'. Indonesian instructional prose uses 'kita' (which the rest of this page already uses: 'Kita akan mulai...') or an agentless construction. The technical content, including the emphasis on *pasangan*, is correct.

examples.source: In this lesson, we'll take a first look at some more sophisticated quantum error correcting code constructions...
examples.translation: Dalam pelajaran ini, kita akan melihat pertama kali beberapa konstruksi kode koreksi kesalahan kuantum yang lebih canggih...
examples.suggested: Dalam pelajaran ini, kita akan menengok sekilas untuk pertama kalinya beberapa konstruksi kode koreksi kesalahan kuantum yang lebih canggih...
examples.why: 'melihat pertama kali' renders 'take a first look' word-by-word and reads as converted rather than written; the adverbial 'pertama kali' attaches awkwardly to 'melihat' here. No loss of meaning.

examples.source: tolerate a very low error rate / tolerate a lot more errors / tolerate a much higher error rate
examples.translation: mentoleransi tingkat kesalahan yang sangat rendah / mentoleransi jauh lebih banyak kesalahan / mentoleransi tingkat kesalahan yang jauh lebih tinggi
examples.suggested: menoleransi (all three occurrences)
examples.why: The KBBI-standard prefixed form of 'toleransi' is 'menoleransi' (the initial t assimilates); 'mentoleransi' is a widespread but non-standard variant. It is used consistently across all three occurrences and is immediately understood, so this is cosmetic polish, not a comprehension risk.

editor_note: The rewritten entry 47 is semantically faithful: the negation scope of "it is not the case that every closed loop ... is contained in the stabilizer" survives correctly as "bukan berarti setiap lingkaran tertutup kesalahan $X$ termasuk dalam stabilizer" (it negates the universal, not each instance), and the disambiguating caveat "(bukan segmen garis dari lingkaran qubit yang terpengaruh oleh kesalahan X)" is preserved whole, including "satu baris/kolom penuh qubit dalam kisi periodik" for "a full row/column of qubits". The one slip is terminology consistency the rewrite introduced: it renders "contained in the stabilizer" as "termasuk dalam stabilizer", while the untouched surrounding prose uses "terkandung dalam stabilizer" four times (numbered items 1 and 2, and the two paragraphs after the X-error-logical figure). Both are understandable and neither misleads, but within a single page describing one membership relation the file should settle on "terkandung dalam stabilizer". Nothing here would cause a learner to form a false belief.

examples.source: and it is not the case that every closed loop of $X$ errors is contained in the stabilizer.
examples.translation: dan bukan berarti setiap lingkaran tertutup kesalahan $X$ termasuk dalam stabilizer.
examples.suggested: dan tidak setiap lingkaran tertutup kesalahan $X$ terkandung dalam stabilizer.
examples.why: The rest of the page renders "contained in the stabilizer" as "terkandung dalam stabilizer" (four occurrences: items 1 and 2 of the list, plus the two paragraphs following the X-error-logical figure). This rewritten entry switches to "termasuk dalam" for the same relation, creating a within-file inconsistency. Meaning and negation scope are correct, so this is cosmetic, not misleading.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination; the hedges ("Tidak semua kode ... adalah kode stabilizer, tapi banyak yang memang demikian", "tampaknya cocok") and the observable/Pauli-matrix framing all survive, terminology is consistent (qubit, kode stabilizer, matriks Pauli, produk tensor, observable kept in English), and the informal "kamu" convention holds. What a native technical editor would change is phrasing: three calqued English constructions. "kita sudah melihat pertama kali koreksi kesalahan kuantum" and "melihat kedua kalinya kode repetisi" transplant English "took a first/second look at" word order into Indonesian, where the object ends up stranded after the adverbial; and "Ini akan menginformasikan dan mengarah ke diskusi umum" uses "menginformasikan" for English "inform" in the sense of "provide a basis for", which in Indonesian only means "to inform someone of something". None of these would mislead a learner about the physics.

examples.source: In the previous lesson, we took a first look at quantum error correction, focusing specifically on the 9-qubit Shor code.
examples.translation: Di pelajaran sebelumnya, kita sudah melihat pertama kali koreksi kesalahan kuantum, dengan fokus khusus pada kode Shor 9-qubit.
examples.suggested: Di pelajaran sebelumnya, kita untuk pertama kalinya melihat koreksi kesalahan kuantum, dengan fokus khusus pada kode Shor 9-qubit.
examples.why: "melihat pertama kali koreksi kesalahan kuantum" copies the English "took a first look at X" order and leaves the object stranded after the adverbial; an Indonesian writer would front "untuk pertama kalinya" (or use "melihat sekilas").

examples.source: We'll then go back and take a second look at the repetition code and see how it can be described in terms of Pauli matrix observables.
examples.translation: Kita kemudian akan kembali dan melihat kedua kalinya kode repetisi serta melihat bagaimana kode itu bisa dijelaskan dalam bentuk observable matriks Pauli.
examples.suggested: Kita kemudian akan kembali meninjau kode repetisi untuk kedua kalinya dan melihat bagaimana kode itu bisa dijelaskan dalam bentuk observable matriks Pauli.
examples.why: Same calqued "take a second look at" pattern; "melihat kedua kalinya kode repetisi" is ungrammatical-sounding word order, and the doubled "melihat ... serta melihat" in one sentence is stiff.

examples.source: This will both inform and lead into a general discussion of stabilizer codes...
examples.translation: Ini akan menginformasikan dan mengarah ke diskusi umum tentang kode stabilizer...
examples.suggested: Ini akan menjadi landasan sekaligus mengantar ke diskusi umum tentang kode stabilizer...
examples.why: English "inform" here means "provide the basis for"; Indonesian "menginformasikan" only means "to convey information to someone", so the sentence reads as a false friend rather than the intended sense.

editor_note: No misleading content: every numbered condition, the $2^{n-r}$ dimension argument, the three error-detection cases, the distance-3 Steane argument and the $CE$ proof all match the English, and the informal "kita/kamu" register holds throughout. The main defect is a hard terminology split at the "Operasi Clifford dan pengkodean" section: the first half consistently uses Indonesian ("kode stabilizer", "generator stabilizer", "ruang kode", "sindrom error", "kode Shor 9-Qubit"), the second half abruptly switches to English ("stabilizer code", "stabilizer generators", "code space", "syndrome", "9-qubit Shor code"), so the same concept carries two names inside one lesson. Three phrases also read as raw MT: "hanya ada *finitely many* operasi Clifford" leaves English prose untranslated, "berikut bahwa setiap operasi koreksi" is a literal calque of "it follows that", and "di mana kasus mana pun salah satunya bisa dipilih" is a garbled rendering of "in which case any one of them may be selected". Additionally "fixed by" is rendered throughout as "ditetapkan oleh" (= "determined/specified by") rather than "tetap/tidak berubah oleh", and the anti-commutation cleft at the "kasus kedua" paragraph lost its main verb and reads as a sentence fragment.

examples.source: stabilizer code / stabilizer generators / code space / syndrome
examples.translation: second half: "stabilizer code", "stabilizer generators", "code space", "syndrome" — first half: "kode stabilizer", "generator stabilizer", "ruang kode", "sindrom error"
examples.suggested: Pick one convention for the whole file; the first half's Indonesian set is the stronger one (keep only "stabilizer" itself untranslated).
examples.why: The same concepts are named two different ways within one lesson, and headings like "Jarak stabilizer code" mix both; a learner meeting "sindrom" in section 1 and "syndrome" in section 5 has to re-anchor the vocabulary mid-lesson.

examples.source: there are only *finitely many* $n$-qubit Clifford operations
examples.translation: hanya ada *finitely many* operasi Clifford $n$-qubit
examples.suggested: hanya ada *berhingga banyak* operasi Clifford $n$-qubit
examples.why: An English phrase is left untranslated in running prose (and italicized as if it were a technical term), which no Indonesian technical writer would leave standing.

examples.source: it follows that each correction operation $C$ corrects … / in which case any one of them may be selected
examples.translation: berikut bahwa setiap operasi koreksi $C$ mengoreksi … / di mana kasus mana pun salah satunya bisa dipilih
examples.suggested: maka setiap operasi koreksi $C$ mengoreksi … / dan dalam kasus seperti itu salah satunya boleh dipilih
examples.why: "berikut bahwa" is a word-for-word calque of "it follows that" and is not grammatical Indonesian; "di mana kasus mana pun" is a botched "in which case" that briefly reads as a quantifier over cases.

examples.source: At least one quantum state vector is fixed by all of the stabilizer generators
examples.translation: Setidaknya ada satu vektor state kuantum yang ditetapkan oleh semua generator stabilizer
examples.suggested: … yang tetap tak berubah oleh semua generator stabilizer (yaitu $P\vert\psi\rangle=\vert\psi\rangle$)
examples.why: "ditetapkan" means "determined/specified", not "left invariant"; the accompanying equation rescues the meaning, so it is recognizable rather than misleading, but the core notion of a fixed (+1-eigen) vector is not carried by the word chosen.

examples.source: It's the *anti-commutation* of an error with a stabilizer generator that causes a $-1$ to appear somewhere in the syndrome, signaling an error, but that doesn't happen in this case.
examples.translation: *Anti-komutasi* suatu error dengan stabilizer generator yang menyebabkan $-1$ muncul di suatu tempat dalam syndrome, yang menandakan error, tapi itu tidak terjadi dalam kasus ini.
examples.suggested: Justru *anti-komutasi* antara error dan generator stabilizer-lah yang membuat $-1$ muncul di syndrome sebagai penanda error — dan itulah yang tidak terjadi di kasus ini.
examples.why: The English cleft ("It's X that causes…") became a relative clause, leaving the sentence without a main predicate; the emphasis that anti-commutation is the *only* trigger for a $-1$ — the point of the paragraph — is flattened.

examples.source: we rule out this possibility by requiring this condition as a part of the definition
examples.translation: kita menyingkirkan kemungkinan ini dengan menjadikannya bagian dari definisi
examples.suggested: kita menyingkirkan kemungkinan ini dengan mensyaratkan kondisi tersebut sebagai bagian dari definisi
examples.why: "-nya" has no antecedent but "kemungkinan ini", so it reads as "we rule out this possibility by making it part of the definition" — the referent "kondisi" was dropped and the sentence briefly says the opposite of what it means.

examples.source: choose specific codes for which good corrections can be computed efficiently … devising stabilizer codes for which good correction operations can be computed efficiently
examples.translation: memilih kode-kode tertentu yang koreksinya bisa dihitung secara efisien … merancang stabilizer codes yang operasi koreksinya bisa dihitung secara efisien
examples.suggested: … yang operasi koreksi yang *baik* bisa dihitung secara efisien
examples.why: The qualifier "good" is dropped in both closing sentences; the lesson's point is that the correction must be both computable and a good (lowest-weight-like) choice, not merely computable.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: the exam facts survive intact (20 pertanyaan, "setidaknya 16 dengan benar", the two-attempt lock, the Credly data-sharing notice all match the English exactly). The defects are consistency and polish. (1) Second person is split arbitrarily between the -mu clitic and "Anda", sometimes inside one sentence: "Informasi pribadimu digunakan untuk menerbitkan badge Anda" (line 28), where the surrounding paragraph is "untukmu / informasi pribadimu / Kamu akan menerima" but this clause switches to "Anda"; §"Uji pengetahuanmu" (heading, -mu) then runs three paragraphs entirely on "Anda". (2) "course" is left untranslated twice in line 14 ("menyelesaikan course ini", "meningkatkan course kami") while line 18 and the section heading use the correct Indonesian "kursus" — the same word rendered two ways in adjacent paragraphs. (3) Minor translationese/orthography: "klik tombol di bawah untuk membuka IBM Training, di mana Anda bisa..." calques "where you can" (a native writer would use "untuk mengikuti ujian badging..."), and "Survei pasca kursus" should be the bound prefix "pascakursus"; the final link also swallows the period, "[di sini.](…)" instead of "[di sini](…)."

examples.source: Your personal information is used to issue your badge and for program reporting and operational purposes.
examples.translation: Informasi pribadimu digunakan untuk menerbitkan badge Anda dan untuk pelaporan program serta tujuan operasional.
examples.suggested: Informasi pribadimu digunakan untuk menerbitkan badge-mu dan untuk pelaporan program serta tujuan operasional.
examples.why: Informal -mu and formal "Anda" collide inside a single sentence; the rest of the paragraph (untukmu, informasi pribadimu, Kamu akan menerima) is consistently informal, so "badge Anda" is the outlier.

examples.source: Congratulations on completing this course! Please take a moment to help us improve our course...
examples.translation: Selamat telah menyelesaikan course ini! Luangkan waktu sejenak untuk membantu kami meningkatkan course kami...
examples.suggested: Selamat telah menyelesaikan kursus ini! Luangkan waktu sejenak untuk membantu kami meningkatkan kursus kami...
examples.why: "course" is left in English here but rendered "kursus" in the next section ("dalam kursus ini", line 18) and in the heading "Survei pasca kursus" — the same everyday term is split two ways within the file.

examples.source: click the button below to navigate to IBM Training, where you can take the badging exam for...
examples.translation: klik tombol di bawah untuk membuka IBM Training, di mana Anda bisa mengambil ujian badging untuk...
examples.suggested: klik tombol di bawah untuk membuka IBM Training dan mengikuti ujian badging untuk...
examples.why: "di mana Anda bisa" is a direct calque of English relative "where you can"; Indonesian technical prose normally chains with "dan"/"untuk" rather than a locative relative clause. Also "mengambil ujian" is a literal take-an-exam calque — the idiom is "mengikuti ujian".

examples.source: ## Post-course survey
examples.translation: ## Survei pasca kursus
examples.suggested: ## Survei pascakursus
examples.why: "pasca-" is a bound prefix in standard Indonesian orthography (pascakursus, pascasarjana); writing it as a separate word is a spelling slip a native editor would correct.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the optimality claim, the "known before Grover / matched an already-known lower bound" remark, the quadratic amplitude-amplification statement and the closing hedge all survive intact, with no inverted negation, swapped quantity or hallucinated sentence, so nothing here would mislead a learner. What a native technical editor would change is word choice: "in a variety of different settings" becomes "dalam berbagai pengaturan yang berbeda", where "pengaturan" is the configuration/settings false friend — the sense here is contexts/situations ("berbagai konteks"); "to get an improvement" becomes "untuk mendapatkan perbaikan" ("repair/fix") where "peningkatan" is the right word; "matched an already-known lower bound" is rendered with the flat calque "cocok dengan batas bawah" instead of "menyamai/mencapai batas bawah"; and the last sentence doubles the same hedge ("mungkin tidak segera menghasilkan ... dalam waktu dekat"), where the English says it once. Core domain terms are fine and consistent (algoritma query, batas bawah, percepatan akar kuadrat, subrutin, refleksi/diiterasi, amplitude amplification kept in English), and register is neutral-informal with no deferential slips.

examples.source: the square-root speed-up that it offers can be obtained in a variety of different settings
examples.translation: percepatan akar kuadrat yang ditawarkannya bisa diperoleh dalam berbagai pengaturan yang berbeda
examples.suggested: ... bisa diperoleh dalam berbagai konteks yang berbeda
examples.why: "pengaturan" is the UI/configuration sense of "settings"; the English means contexts or situations. Recognizable but a classic false-friend calque.

examples.source: sometimes it's possible to use Grover's algorithm in conjunction with another algorithm to get an improvement
examples.translation: terkadang memungkinkan untuk menggunakan algoritma Grover bersama dengan algoritma lain untuk mendapatkan perbaikan
examples.suggested: terkadang dimungkinkan untuk menggunakan algoritma Grover bersama algoritma lain untuk memperoleh peningkatan
examples.why: Two slips in one sentence: "memungkinkan" (enables) should be passive "dimungkinkan" for "it's possible", and "perbaikan" means repair/fix where the English means a performance improvement ("peningkatan").

examples.source: Grover's algorithm matched an already-known lower bound
examples.translation: algoritma Grover cocok dengan batas bawah yang sudah diketahui sebelumnya
examples.suggested: algoritma Grover menyamai batas bawah yang sudah diketahui sebelumnya
examples.why: "cocok dengan" is the literal "matches/fits"; for a complexity bound an Indonesian technical writer says "menyamai" or "mencapai". Meaning survives, but it reads as MT.

examples.source: although Grover's algorithm may not lead to a practical quantum advantage for searching any time soon
examples.translation: meskipun algoritma Grover mungkin tidak segera menghasilkan keunggulan kuantum praktis untuk pencarian dalam waktu dekat
examples.suggested: meskipun algoritma Grover mungkin belum menghasilkan keunggulan kuantum praktis untuk pencarian dalam waktu dekat
examples.why: "segera" and "dalam waktu dekat" express the same "any time soon" hedge twice; the redundancy is stylistic clutter, not a meaning change.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: the Z_f / Z_OR definitions, the OR case split (0 for x = 0^n, 1 otherwise), the three algorithm steps, the query-cost comparison ("$Z_f$ membutuhkan satu query sementara $Z_{\mathrm{OR}}$ tidak membutuhkan query"), and the closing $t = O(\sqrt{N})$ claim all match the English exactly, and the f(x)=1 / f(x)=0 branches keep their correct polarity. Three native-editor fixes remain, all word-choice calques. English "suggest" (in the sense of "indicate/imply") is twice rendered with "menyarankan/disarankan", which in Indonesian means "to recommend/advise" — "seperti yang disarankan diagram ini" and "untuk menyarankan bahwa operasi itu kemungkinan..." should be "seperti yang diisyaratkan/ditunjukkan diagram ini" and "untuk mengisyaratkan bahwa...". The English pronoun "one" in "larger and more complicated than one for $Z_{\mathrm{OR}}$" is calqued literally as "lebih rumit dari satu untuk $Z_{\mathrm{OR}}$", where "satu" reads as the numeral. Terminology is otherwise consistent (qubit, state, register, iterasi, operasi uniter, pengukuran basis standar) and register is uniformly the informal "kita".

examples.source: The operation $Z_f$ can be implemented using one query gate $U_f$ as this diagram suggests / as an informal visual clue to suggest that it is likely to be the more costly operation
examples.translation: Operasi $Z_f$ bisa diimplementasikan menggunakan satu Gate query $U_f$ seperti yang disarankan diagram ini / sebagai petunjuk visual informal untuk menyarankan bahwa operasi itu kemungkinan merupakan operasi yang lebih mahal biayanya
examples.suggested: seperti yang diisyaratkan diagram ini / sebagai petunjuk visual informal yang mengisyaratkan bahwa operasi itu kemungkinan lebih mahal
examples.why: "menyarankan/disarankan" in Indonesian means to recommend or advise, not to indicate or imply; a diagram does not "recommend" anything. Recognizable but a clear calque of English "suggest" that a native technical writer would replace with mengisyaratkan/menunjukkan.

examples.source: we can reasonably expect that the resulting quantum circuit will be larger and more complicated than one for $Z_{\mathrm{OR}}$
examples.translation: kita bisa dengan wajar mengharapkan bahwa Circuit kuantum yang dihasilkan akan lebih besar dan lebih rumit dari satu untuk $Z_{\mathrm{OR}}.$
examples.suggested: kita bisa mengharapkan bahwa rangkaian kuantum yang dihasilkan akan lebih besar dan lebih rumit daripada rangkaian untuk $Z_{\mathrm{OR}}$
examples.why: The English pro-form "one" is translated literally as "satu", which Indonesian readers parse as the numeral, so the comparison momentarily reads as "more complicated than one (unit) for Z_OR". Also "dengan wajar mengharapkan" is a stiff calque of "reasonably expect".

examples.source: requires that one workspace qubit, initialized to a $\vert -\rangle$ state, is made available
examples.translation: membutuhkan satu qubit ruang kerja, diinisialisasi ke state $\vert -\rangle$, untuk tersedia
examples.suggested: membutuhkan tersedianya satu qubit ruang kerja yang diinisialisasi ke state $\vert -\rangle$
examples.why: "untuk tersedia" is not idiomatic Indonesian — it mirrors the English passive "is made available" word for word. Meaning is preserved, but the sentence reads as machine output rather than something a native technical writer would compose.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the square-root/square inversion in para 1, the "sure to be washed away by staggering clock speeds" caveat, and the "slightly less than quadratic" FFT/sorting comparison all survive intact, and the informal "kamu" convention holds in the video paragraph. What a native editor would change is three calques: "pada permukaannya" for "on the surface" (Indonesian would say "sekilas" / "pada pandangan pertama"; the literal form reads as surface-of-an-object); "masih sangat dalam masa pertumbuhannya" for "still very much in its infancy", where the adverb placement before "dalam" is ungrammatical-sounding and "masih berada pada tahap sangat awal" is the idiom; and "menawarkan sedikit kurang dari keunggulan kuadratik" for "offer slightly less than a quadratic advantage", a word-order transplant that a technical writer would recast as "menawarkan keunggulan yang sedikit di bawah kuadratik". Separately, "compelling" is softened to "cukup menarik" ("quite interesting"), a mild register flattening but not misleading. No drift, no hallucination, no term taught falsely.

examples.source: ...many interesting computational tasks that may not initially look like unstructured search problems on the surface.
examples.translation: ...banyak tugas komputasi menarik yang mungkin awalnya tidak terlihat seperti masalah pencarian tak terstruktur pada permukaannya.
examples.suggested: ...yang sekilas mungkin tidak terlihat seperti masalah pencarian tak terstruktur.
examples.why: "pada permukaannya" is a literal calque of "on the surface" and in Indonesian reads as the physical surface of a thing; the idiomatic rendering is "sekilas" or "pada pandangan pertama". Meaning survives, but it marks the sentence as translated.

examples.source: While this technology is still very much in its infancy in comparison to classical computing...
examples.translation: Meskipun teknologi ini masih sangat dalam masa pertumbuhannya dibandingkan komputasi klasik...
examples.suggested: Meskipun teknologi ini masih berada pada tahap yang sangat awal dibandingkan komputasi klasik...
examples.why: "sangat" modifying the prepositional phrase "dalam masa pertumbuhannya" is not a construction a native technical writer uses; the intensifier has nothing to attach to. Reads as machine-placed emphasis.

examples.source: ...offer slightly less than a quadratic advantage over naive approaches to the problems they solve.
examples.translation: ...menawarkan sedikit kurang dari keunggulan kuadratik dibanding pendekatan naif terhadap masalah yang mereka selesaikan.
examples.suggested: ...menawarkan keunggulan yang sedikit di bawah kuadratik dibandingkan pendekatan naif terhadap masalah yang diselesaikannya.
examples.why: English word order transplanted directly; "sedikit kurang dari keunggulan kuadratik" is parseable but stiff, and "yang mereka selesaikan" anthropomorphizes the algorithms where "-nya" is the Indonesian norm.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, no swapped quantities, no dropped caveats: the $N=2^n$ / $O(N)$ / $O(\sqrt{N})$ claims, the "bukan masalah promise" negation, the "tepat satu string $z$" promise and the "jika tidak ada solusi, maka jawaban yang benar mengharuskan kita melaporkan bahwa tidak ada solusi" caveat all survive intact, and "mencari jarum dalam tumpukan jerami" lands the analogy well. What a native technical editor would change is a layer of English-shaped syntax: "Beroperasi di bawah asumsi bahwa…" is a word-for-word calque of "Operating under the assumption that…" (Indonesian: "Dengan asumsi bahwa…"), "sebagai lawan dari benar-benar menemukan solusinya" calques "as opposed to", and "salah satu dari mereka" uses the animate pronoun *mereka* for inanimate strings where "salah satunya" is required. Two smaller slips: "model query komputasi" inverts the head of "query model of computation" (should be "model komputasi query"), and "$f$ mengevaluasi ke $1$" is a calque of "evaluates to 1" that reads as if $f$ were evaluating something else ("bernilai $1$" is the idiom). Also "dengan memeriksa" at the end of the Boolean-circuit paragraph drops its object suffix ("memeriksanya"), and "demi kenyamanan" renders "for the sake of convenience" as physical comfort rather than notational ease. None of these would lead a learner to a false belief.

examples.source: Operating under the assumption that we're limited to evaluating $f$ on chosen inputs, this is the best we can do with a deterministic algorithm
examples.translation: Beroperasi di bawah asumsi bahwa kita terbatas hanya mengevaluasi $f$ pada input yang dipilih, ini adalah yang terbaik yang bisa kita lakukan dengan algoritma deterministik
examples.suggested: Dengan asumsi bahwa kita hanya bisa mengevaluasi $f$ pada input yang kita pilih, inilah yang terbaik yang bisa kita lakukan dengan algoritma deterministik
examples.why: "Beroperasi di bawah asumsi" is a literal calque of "operating under the assumption"; no Indonesian technical writer opens a sentence this way. "Dengan asumsi" is the standard construction.

examples.source: If there are multiple solutions, then any one of them is considered to be a correct output
examples.translation: Jika ada beberapa solusi, maka salah satu dari mereka dianggap sebagai output yang benar
examples.suggested: Jika ada beberapa solusi, maka salah satunya dianggap sebagai output yang benar
examples.why: "mereka" is the animate third-person plural pronoun; using it for inanimate solutions/strings is a hallmark of machine translation from English "them". "salah satunya" is the natural form.

examples.source: the goal is simply to determine whether or not a solution exists, as opposed to actually finding a solution
examples.translation: tujuannya adalah sekadar menentukan apakah solusi ada atau tidak, sebagai lawan dari benar-benar menemukan solusinya
examples.suggested: tujuannya sekadar menentukan ada atau tidaknya solusi, alih-alih benar-benar menemukan solusinya
examples.why: "sebagai lawan dari" is a word-for-word rendering of "as opposed to" and reads as an opposition/adversary rather than a contrast; "alih-alih" is the idiomatic contrastive connector.

examples.source: We'll formalize the problem that Grover's algorithm solves using the query model of computation.
examples.translation: Kita akan memformalisasi masalah yang diselesaikan algoritma Grover menggunakan model query komputasi.
examples.suggested: … menggunakan model komputasi query (query model of computation).
examples.why: Indonesian is head-initial, so "model query komputasi" parses as a "computation query model" and detaches *komputasi* from *model*. The established rendering is "model komputasi" modified by *query*.

examples.source: a string $x$ that causes $f$ to evaluate to $1$
examples.translation: string $x$ yang menyebabkan $f$ mengevaluasi ke $1$
examples.suggested: string $x$ yang membuat $f$ bernilai $1$
examples.why: "mengevaluasi" is transitive in Indonesian ("to evaluate something"), so "$f$ mengevaluasi ke $1$" reads as $f$ performing an evaluation rather than taking the value 1. The idiom is "bernilai $1$" / "menghasilkan nilai $1$".

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat; the Credly privacy notice tracks the English clause by clause and the informal "kamu"/"-mu" register holds consistently ("badge kamu", "informasi pribadimu"). Three things a native technical editor would still change: (1) "It will be handled in a manner consistent with IBM privacy practices" becomes "Hal ini akan ditangani dengan cara yang konsisten dengan praktik privasi IBM" — "Hal ini" shifts the referent from the personal information to the act of sharing, and "dengan cara yang konsisten dengan" is a word-for-word calque where "sesuai dengan praktik privasi IBM" is the idiomatic form; (2) "Ujian ini dimaksudkan untuk diambil setelah membaca pelajaran" is stiff double-passive translationese ("sebaiknya dikerjakan/diikuti setelah…" is what a native writer uses); (3) the sentence-final period was pulled inside the link text twice — "[di sini.](…)" — so the rendered anchor reads "di sini." Also the flattening of "eager to gain knowledge" to plain "ingin mendapatkan pengetahuan" loses the English's enthusiasm, though that is defensible. None of this would mislead a learner.

examples.source: It will be handled in a manner consistent with IBM privacy practices.
examples.translation: Hal ini akan ditangani dengan cara yang konsisten dengan praktik privasi IBM.
examples.suggested: Informasi tersebut akan ditangani sesuai dengan praktik privasi IBM.
examples.why: "Hal ini" points at the preceding act of sharing rather than at the personal information the English "It" refers to, and "dengan cara yang konsisten dengan" is a literal calque; "sesuai dengan" is the standard Indonesian legal/privacy phrasing.

examples.source: This exam is intended to be taken after reading the lessons in this course.
examples.translation: Ujian ini dimaksudkan untuk diambil setelah membaca pelajaran dalam kursus ini.
examples.suggested: Ujian ini sebaiknya dikerjakan setelah kamu membaca seluruh pelajaran dalam kursus ini.
examples.why: "dimaksudkan untuk diambil" stacks two passives in a calque of "is intended to be taken"; no Indonesian technical writer would phrase an exam instruction this way.

examples.source: The IBM Privacy Statement can be viewed [here](https://www.ibm.com/privacy/us/en/).
examples.translation: Pernyataan Privasi IBM dapat dilihat [di sini.](https://www.ibm.com/privacy/us/en/)
examples.suggested: Pernyataan Privasi IBM dapat dilihat [di sini](https://www.ibm.com/privacy/us/en/).
examples.why: The sentence period was moved inside the link label (twice in this paragraph), so the rendered hyperlink text is "di sini." instead of "di sini".

editor_note: Meaning is fully faithful throughout this short page — no drift, no hallucination: the Shor tooltip keeps both the discrete-logarithm contrast and the 1994 conference / 1997 journal dates exactly, "masalah estimasi fase", "faktorisasi bilangan bulat" and "transformasi Fourier kuantum" are the correct conventional Indonesian renderings, and the informal "Anda" register holds. What a native technical editor would change is phrasing: two English idioms are calqued word-for-word — "Along the way" → "Sepanjang jalan" (reads as "along the road"; idiomatically "Dalam prosesnya" / "Di sepanjang perjalanan ini") and "With this in hand" → "Dengan ini di tangan" (natural: "Berbekal itu"). A third, recurring slip is the locative preposition: "Di pelajaran ini", "Di video berikut", "di pelajaran ini tentang estimasi fase" — Indonesian technical prose uses "Dalam/Pada pelajaran ini", "Pada video berikut"; "di" here is a calque of English "in/on". None of these mislead a learner.

examples.source: Along the way, we'll encounter the quantum Fourier transform, and we'll see how it can be implemented efficiently by a quantum circuit.
examples.translation: Sepanjang jalan, kita akan menemui transformasi Fourier kuantum, dan kita akan melihat bagaimana itu bisa diimplementasikan secara efisien oleh Circuit kuantum.
examples.suggested: Dalam prosesnya, kita akan menemui transformasi Fourier kuantum, dan melihat bagaimana transformasi ini dapat diimplementasikan secara efisien oleh sirkuit kuantum.
examples.why: "Sepanjang jalan" is a literal calque of "along the way" and reads as physical travel along a road; the bare pronoun "itu" for the transform is also stiffer than repeating the noun. Meaning is intact, so this is style only.

examples.source: With this in hand, John moves on to Shor's algorithm.
examples.translation: Dengan ini di tangan, John beralih ke algoritma Shor.
examples.suggested: Berbekal itu, John beralih ke algoritma Shor.
examples.why: Word-for-word calque of the English idiom "with this in hand"; Indonesian uses "berbekal" or simply "Setelah itu". No loss of meaning, purely translationese.

examples.source: In this lesson, we'll discuss... / In the following video, John Watrous steps you through the content in this lesson...
examples.translation: Di pelajaran ini, kita akan mendiskusikan... / Di video berikut, John Watrous memandu Anda melalui konten di pelajaran ini...
examples.suggested: Dalam pelajaran ini, kita akan membahas... / Pada video berikut, John Watrous memandu Anda melalui materi dalam pelajaran ini...
examples.why: "Di" is the physical-location preposition; for abstract containers (a lesson, a video) Indonesian technical prose takes "dalam" or "pada". The slip repeats three times in the file, which makes it a consistent register flaw rather than a one-off.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I checked the whole analytic tail (the 4/π² ≈ 0.405 lower bound, the ≤ 1/4 upper bound, the "off by more than 2^-m ... dibatasi oleh 25%" summary, and the arc/chord inequalities) and found no inverted condition, swapped quantity or hallucinated claim; the m=2 special case, the recursive QFT steps 1–4 and the s_m = s_{m-1} + (2m-1) = m² count are all correct. The defects are lexical, not semantic. (a) "inequality" is rendered "ketidaksetaraan" (lines 813, 847) and "equality" as "kesetaraan" (583) — those are the social/equivalence words; the Indonesian math terms are "pertidaksamaan" and "kesamaan/persamaan". (b) "arbitrary" is "sembarang" everywhere (307, 343, 403, 469, 573, 718, 765) except line 290, where it becomes "sewenang-wenang" (= high-handed/capricious). (c) further within-file splits: inner product "produk dalam" (236) vs "hasil kali dalam" (411); "discrete" spelled "diskret" (265, 267) vs "diskrit" (310–349); "outcome" left in English (88, 96, 104, 120, 164, 296) while "hasil pengukuran" is used at 101 and 717; plus "probabilitas nonzero" (115) and the calque "berikut bahwa" for "it follows that" (800), and the dropped hedge "arguably" in line 507.

examples.source: Putting these two inequalities to use on $p_y$ reveals … where the second equality makes use of the observation that
examples.translation: Memanfaatkan kedua ketidaksetaraan ini pada $p_y$ mengungkapkan … di mana kesetaraan kedua memanfaatkan pengamatan bahwa
examples.suggested: Memanfaatkan kedua pertidaksamaan ini pada $p_y$ … di mana kesamaan kedua memanfaatkan pengamatan bahwa
examples.why: "ketidaksetaraan"/"kesetaraan" are the social-equality / equivalence words; Indonesian mathematical usage is "pertidaksamaan" for inequality and "kesamaan" (or "persamaan") for equality. Recognizable from the displayed formulas, so not misleading, but no Indonesian maths writer would use them.

examples.source: Here's a plot of the output probabilities the circuit produces for arbitrary choices of $\theta$.
examples.translation: Berikut adalah plot probabilitas output yang dihasilkan sirkuit untuk pilihan $\theta$ yang sewenang-wenang.
examples.suggested: … untuk pilihan $\theta$ yang sembarang.
examples.why: "sewenang-wenang" means arbitrary in the sense of high-handed/capricious; the mathematical sense is "sembarang", which this same file uses correctly at lines 307, 343, 403, 469, 573, 718 and 765 — so it is both the wrong word and the one outlier.

examples.source: inner product … discrete Fourier transform … measurement outcome
examples.translation: produk dalamnya (236) / hasil kali dalam (411); transformasi Fourier diskret (265, 267) / diskrit (310, 316, 349); outcome pengukuran (104, 120, 164, 296) / hasil pengukuran (101, 717)
examples.suggested: Pick one per concept: "hasil kali dalam", "diskret", "hasil pengukuran".
examples.why: Three core terms each appear in two forms inside one lesson. Each variant is understandable, so the concept stays identifiable, but the inconsistency is exactly what a technical editor would normalize — and "outcome" has a perfectly standard Indonesian equivalent already used in the same file.

examples.source: By the assumption we're considering, it follows that $\vert 2^m \theta - y \vert \leq 1/2$
examples.translation: Berdasarkan asumsi yang kita pertimbangkan, berikut bahwa $\vert 2^m \theta - y \vert \leq 1/2$
examples.suggested: Berdasarkan asumsi yang kita pertimbangkan, diperoleh bahwa $\vert 2^m \theta - y \vert \leq 1/2$
examples.why: "berikut bahwa" is a word-for-word calque of "it follows that" and is not idiomatic Indonesian — "berikut" is the adjective "following", not the verb. "maka"/"diperoleh"/"dapat disimpulkan" is what a native writer would use.

examples.source: There are, in fact, multiple ways to implement the quantum Fourier transform, but this is arguably the simplest method known.
examples.translation: Sebenarnya ada beberapa cara untuk mengimplementasikan transformasi Fourier kuantum, tetapi ini adalah metode paling sederhana yang dikenal.
examples.suggested: … tetapi ini bisa dibilang metode paling sederhana yang dikenal.
examples.why: The hedge "arguably" is dropped, turning the author's guarded claim into a flat assertion that this IS the simplest known method. A dropped qualifier rather than a reversed meaning, so minor, but it removes the author's deliberate caution.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, no swapped quantities, no dropped caveats (the "which seems extremely unlikely to happen any time soon, if ever" hedge and the "narrow application domain" concession both survive intact), and no hallucinated claims; the informal "Anda" register and the kept terms (oracle, instance, subrutin, kotak hitam for black box) are right.
