(4) "Map problem to quantum circuits and operators" becomes the noun phrase "Peta masalah ke circuit dan operator kuantum" in both the step list and the §1 heading, where the English is imperative — "Petakan/Memetakan masalah…" is what a native writer would put. (5) "one- and two-body electronic integrals" → "integral elektronik satu- dan dua-badan" is a calque; Indonesian physics writing uses "dua-benda"/"dua-partikel" or keeps the English term.

examples.source: Sampling the LUCJ ansatz in the computational basis generates a pool of noisy configurations $\tilde{\mathcal{\chi}}$, which are used in the post-processing routine. It involves a method called (details discussed later) _configuration recovery_ … Each batch of samples defines a subspace ($\mathcal{S^{(k)}}$).
examples.translation: Sampling the LUCJ ansatz in the computational basis generates a pool of noisy configurations $\tilde{\mathcal{\chi}}$, which are used in the post-processing routine. It involves a method called (details discussed later) _configuration recovery_ … Each batch of samples defines a subspace ($\mathcal{S^{(k)}}$).
examples.suggested: Pengambilan sampel ansatz LUCJ dalam basis komputasi menghasilkan kumpulan konfigurasi bising $\tilde{\mathcal{\chi}}$, yang digunakan dalam rutinitas pascaproses. Rutinitas ini melibatkan metode bernama _configuration recovery_ (dibahas rinci nanti) untuk mengoreksi konfigurasi dengan jumlah elektron yang salah secara probabilistik. Hanya konfigurasi dengan jumlah elektron yang benar $\tilde{\mathcal{\chi}}_{R}$ yang kemudian di-subsample dan dibagi ke beberapa batch berdasarkan frekuensi kemunculan tiap konfigurasi unik. Setiap batch sampel mendefinisikan sebuah subspace ($\mathcal{S^{(k)}}$). Selanjutnya, Hamiltonian molekuler $H$ diproyeksikan ke subspace tersebut:
examples.why: The whole paragraph that introduces the entire post-processing workflow of section 4 was never translated — it sits in English between two Indonesian paragraphs, so an Indonesian-only learner loses the conceptual map of the SQD loop right where it is introduced.

examples.source: **Hexagonal**: Every other orbital, such as 0th, 2nd, and 4th indexed orbitals, becomes nearest neighbors when $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are laid out in two adjacent linear chains.
examples.translation: **Hexagonal**: Setiap orbital lainnya, seperti orbital berindeks ke-0, ke-2, dan ke-4, menjadi tetangga terdekat ketika $\alpha$ dan $\beta$ disusun dalam dua rantai linier yang berdekatan.
examples.suggested: **Hexagonal**: Setiap orbital kedua (selang-seling), yaitu orbital berindeks ke-0, ke-2, ke-4, dan seterusnya, menjadi tetangga terdekat ketika $\alpha$ dan $\beta$ disusun dalam dua rantai linier yang berdekatan.
examples.why: "Every other" (alternating) became "setiap orbital lainnya" (= each of the remaining orbitals), which asserts a different α-β connectivity than the English in a bullet list whose whole point is which orbitals connect on each topology.

examples.source: self-consistent configuration recovery loop … configuration recovery step … 4.1 Configuration recovery: overview … Number of self-consistent configuration recovery iterations
examples.translation: loop pemulihan konfigurasi self-consistent … langkah configuration recovery … 4.1 Configuration recovery: gambaran umum … Jumlah iterasi configuration recovery self-consistent
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering and keep it: e.g. "pemulihan konfigurasi (configuration recovery)" on first use, then "pemulihan konfigurasi" throughout — including the 4.1 heading and the ``iterations`` bullet.
examples.why: The central named technique of the lesson is split between a translated form and the bare English form within the same file; the reader has to infer they are the same thing.

examples.source: Step 1: Map problem to quantum circuits and operators / ## 1. Map problem to quantum circuits and operators
examples.translation: Langkah 1: Peta masalah ke circuit dan operator kuantum / ## 1. Peta masalah ke circuit dan operator kuantum
examples.suggested: Langkah 1: Petakan masalah ke sirkuit dan operator kuantum
examples.why: "Peta" is the noun "a map", so the step reads as a sentence fragment rather than the instruction the English gives; an Indonesian technical writer would use the imperative "Petakan" (or "Memetakan") for a Qiskit-pattern step title.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — every numeric claim, condition and caveat survives (the −0.2111 vs −0.5357 mismatch in Case-2, the "amplitudo vektor yang tidak diinginkan ke $0$" noise-tolerance argument, the 49%/1%/0.01% sampling probabilities, the SQD "selalu menghasilkan batas atas" bound, and the explicit "seringkali lebih baik untuk **tidak** menyiapkan dan sampling dari ground state eksak" negation are all intact), so nothing here would mislead a learner. The one real editorial defect is in §5: the mathematical sense of "term" is rendered as "istilah" ("Banyak istilah Pauli", "$2951$ istilah Pauli unik", "istilah $X$ dan $Y$") — "istilah" means terminology/nomenclature, not a summand; Indonesian technical writing uses "suku" (or keeps "term"), and the slip repeats roughly eight times in that one table. The same table also splits "circuit" three ways within a few sentences ("Circuit pengukuran", "satu sirkuit", "beberapa sirkuit", "jumlah Circuit"), an internal inconsistency a native editor would unify. Register is consistently the informal "kita" convention with no deferential slips.

examples.source: Many Pauli terms, many measurement circuits: The Hamiltonian for the molecule has $2951$ unique Pauli terms. As the Pauli terms can contain $X$ and $Y$ terms…
examples.translation: Banyak istilah Pauli, banyak Circuit pengukuran: Hamiltonian untuk molekul memiliki $2951$ istilah Pauli unik. Karena istilah Pauli bisa mengandung istilah $X$ dan $Y$…
examples.suggested: Banyak suku Pauli, banyak sirkuit pengukuran: … memiliki $2951$ suku Pauli unik. Karena suku Pauli bisa mengandung suku $X$ dan $Y$…
examples.why: "istilah" is Indonesian for a term-of-vocabulary; the mathematical term (summand) of a Hamiltonian is "suku". Recognizable in context, so not misleading, but it is the classic literal-homonym slip and it repeats ~8 times in this one table.

examples.source: …we need at least $1187$ unique circuits … Typically, we measure a single circuit for a fixed number of shots … the number circuit remains much smaller than VQE.
examples.translation: …kita memerlukan setidaknya $1187$ Circuit unik … Biasanya, kita mengukur satu sirkuit untuk jumlah shots yang tetap … tetapi jumlah Circuit tetap jauh lebih kecil dari VQE.
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering ("sirkuit" throughout, or keep "circuit" throughout) and apply it consistently in the table and in §3/§3.2 ("Circuit kuantum yang sesuai", "memanfaatkan Circuit kuantum").
examples.why: The same concept alternates between "Circuit" and "sirkuit" within adjacent sentences of one table cell; the concept stays identifiable, so this is a consistency slip rather than a comprehension problem.

examples.source: The gap between full Hilbert space and feasible subspace dimensions, brings another important aspect of SQD, and that is the sparsity of the wave function.
examples.translation: Kesenjangan antara dimensi ruang Hilbert penuh dan dimensi subspace yang layak, membawa aspek penting lain dari SQD, yaitu sparsity dari fungsi gelombang.
examples.suggested: Kesenjangan antara dimensi ruang Hilbert penuh dan dimensi subspace yang layak membawa aspek penting lain dari SQD, yaitu sparsity fungsi gelombang.
examples.why: The subject–verb comma is carried over verbatim from the English source (itself non-standard); Indonesian never separates subject from predicate this way, and the trailing "sparsity dari fungsi gelombang" is a calqued of-genitive that the section heading itself already renders correctly as "Sparsity fungsi gelombang".

editor_note: The physics is faithful throughout — the variational principle ("tidak ada fungsi gelombang variasional yang bisa menghasilkan nilai ekspektasi energi ... lebih rendah dari ... ground state"), the commuting-Pauli worked example (`IZIZ`/`ZZXZ` yes, `ZZZZ`/`ZZZX` and `ZZZZ`/`ZZXX` no), the O(N²) vs N_GCP cost shift, and the QPE O(1/ε) vs VQE O(1/ε²) contrast all carry the English meaning, and the informal "kamu" register holds. What a native technical editor would change: two outright typos in running prose — "Bentuk jamul" for "jamak" (plural, line 117) and "masalah keterlatiahan" for "keterlatihan" (trainability, line 289); an MT calque of English "some" that turns a singular argument into a plural ("Beberapa fungsi yang akan diminimalkan" for "Some function to be minimized", line 166; same at line 163 "beberapa fungsi yang diminati"); a dropped-precision rendering at line 702 where "for substantial parts of the algorithm" becomes "untuk sebagian besar algoritma", which reads as "for most algorithms"; stiff calqued syntax ("Optimizer klasik berbasis gradien maupun bebas gradien ada.", line 289; "merelokasikan bagian perhitungan ini ke komputer kuantum" for "relegating", line 247); and mild within-file term drift — "keadaan" in §1–2 vs "state" in §3–4, and "komutasi" everywhere except "operator Pauli yang komut" at line 746. None of these would make a learner form a false belief, so the verdict is MINOR_ISSUES, not FAIL.

examples.source: The correct plural in German is "ansätze"
examples.translation: Bentuk jamul yang benar dalam bahasa Jerman adalah "ansätze"
examples.suggested: Bentuk jamak yang benar dalam bahasa Jerman adalah "ansätze"
examples.why: "jamul" is a typo; the Indonesian word for plural is "jamak". Visible misspelling in body prose.

examples.source: Both suffer from potential trainability issues
examples.translation: Keduanya rentan terhadap masalah keterlatiahan
examples.suggested: Keduanya rentan terhadap masalah ketertatihan → "masalah kemampuan pelatihan (trainability)"
examples.why: "keterlatiahan" is a misspelling of "keterlatihan"; the coined noun is also opaque here — spelling it out as "kemampuan pelatihan (trainability)" reads like a native technical writer.

examples.source: Some function to be minimized. This is often the energy expectation value.
examples.translation: Beberapa fungsi yang akan diminimalkan. Ini sering berupa nilai ekspektasi energi.
examples.suggested: Suatu fungsi yang akan diminimalkan. Ini sering berupa nilai ekspektasi energi.
examples.why: English "some function" is singular — this bullet describes ONE argument of scipy's minimize. "Beberapa" means "several", implying the call takes multiple functions. Same calque at line 163 ("beberapa fungsi yang diminati").

examples.source: ...still depend on classical computers, not just for operating the quantum computer, but for substantial parts of the algorithm.
examples.translation: ...masih bergantung pada komputer klasik, bukan hanya untuk mengoperasikan komputer kuantum, tapi untuk sebagian besar algoritma.
examples.suggested: ...tapi untuk bagian-bagian penting dari algoritmanya.
examples.why: "sebagian besar algoritma" reads as "most algorithms" (or "most of the algorithm"), a quantitative strengthening of "substantial parts". The file itself uses the better "komponen algoritma yang substansial" later, so it is also inconsistent.

examples.source: Both gradient-based, and gradient-free classical optimizers exist.
examples.translation: Optimizer klasik berbasis gradien maupun bebas gradien ada.
examples.suggested: Ada optimizer klasik berbasis gradien maupun yang bebas gradien.
examples.why: Word-for-word English order with a trailing "ada"; Indonesian puts the existential "Ada" first. Reads as machine output rather than written prose.

examples.source: relatively few groups of commuting Pauli operators
examples.translation: relatif sedikit kelompok operator Pauli yang komut
examples.suggested: relatif sedikit kelompok operator Pauli yang saling komutasi
examples.why: The rest of the file consistently uses "komutasi" ("tidak saling komutasi", "kelompok Pauli yang komutasi"); the bare verb "komut" appears only here. Concept still identifiable, so MINOR.

editor_note: Of the three re-written headings, two are clean and idiomatic: "Quantum kernels" → "Kernel kuantum" and "Quantum neural network" → "Jaringan saraf kuantum" both read as native Indonesian technical usage and match how the body already renders "jaringan saraf" (line 122 ff.). The one slip is the H2 at line 39: "Support vector machines" → "Mesin vektor pendukung", a full calque of a term the Indonesian ML field keeps in English — and this same file keeps it in English everywhere else ("kelas algoritma yang disebut support vector machines", line 41; "disebut support vectors", line 45; "menjalankan algoritma support vector machine", line 68; "optimasi SVM", line 112). The result is a heading whose term appears nowhere in the section it introduces; "mesin" also pulls toward the physical-machine sense rather than the ML sense. Nothing here misleads — the concept stays identifiable — so this is a consistency/naturalness fix, not a semantic one: either keep "Support vector machines" in the heading or gloss it, e.g. "Support vector machine (mesin vektor pendukung)", matching the pattern the file already uses for "Supervised learning (Pembelajaran terarah)" at line 23.

examples.source: Support vector machines {#support-vector-machines}
examples.translation: Mesin vektor pendukung {#support-vector-machines}
examples.suggested: Support vector machines  — or, matching the file's own gloss pattern, "Support vector machines (mesin vektor pendukung)"
examples.why: Calqued rendering of a term Indonesian ML practice keeps in English, and it contradicts the rest of the file, which uses "support vector machines" (line 41), "support vectors" (line 45), "algoritma support vector machine" (line 68) and "optimasi SVM" (line 112). The heading therefore introduces a section in which its own term never reappears; "mesin" also skews toward the physical-machine reading. Recognizable, not misleading — a within-file consistency slip.

examples.source: Quantum kernels {#quantum-kernels}
examples.translation: Kernel kuantum {#quantum-kernels}
examples.suggested: (no change)
examples.why: Correct and natural; "kernel" is retained as the field does and "kuantum" is the established adjective used throughout the file. Listed only to record that this delta entry was checked and is fine.

examples.source: Quantum neural network {#quantum-neural-network}
examples.translation: Jaringan saraf kuantum {#quantum-neural-network}
examples.suggested: (no change)
examples.why: Accurate and consistent with the body's "jaringan saraf klasik" / "jaringan saraf" (lines 116, 122, 130); the English "Quantum neural network (QNN)" is still introduced in the first sentence under the heading, so the acronym stays anchored. Listed only to record that this delta entry was checked and is fine.

editor_note: The physics is faithful throughout — every quantity, condition and caveat survives (n ≥ log2(N) qubits, α = √105 / √270, depth-2 phase encoding, θ_{q,p} = 2(π−x_q)(π−x_p), the "darker CZ shades are better / longer T1 is better" polarity in the last figure caption, and the "neither sufficient nor well-matched" hedge about efficient_su2), and the informal "kamu/kita" register holds end to end. The one passage that needs rewriting is line 704: "neither consistent nor inconsistent with little-endian notation" became "Ini tidak konsisten maupun tidak konsisten dengan notasi little-endian" — a stuttered double "tidak konsisten" that a reader will first parse as a flat "this is inconsistent with little-endian" before reconstructing the intended neutrality; suggest "Hal ini tidak dapat dikatakan konsisten maupun bertentangan dengan notasi little-endian". Secondary: the section headings translate the key term ("Pengodean basis/amplitudo/sudut/fase", lines 57/156/334/478/556) while the whole body and the later heading "Encoding dengan feature map bawaan" (line 624) keep "encoding"; "unitary" is split between "uniter" (721, 858) and "unitary" (875); and "Circuit" slips to "sirkuit" once at line 968. Line 1019 calques the English "It is one thing to say… It is quite another thing for…" into "Satu hal untuk mengatakan… Hal yang sama sekali berbeda adalah…", which flattens the contrast the paragraph is teaching.

examples.source: This is neither consistent nor inconsistent with little-endian notation, since here the data features cannot be ordered by qubit a priori
examples.translation: Ini tidak konsisten maupun tidak konsisten dengan notasi little-endian, karena di sini fitur data tidak dapat diurutkan berdasarkan qubit *a priori*
examples.suggested: Hal ini tidak dapat dikatakan konsisten maupun bertentangan dengan notasi little-endian, karena di sini fitur data tidak dapat diurutkan berdasarkan qubit *a priori*
examples.why: The repeated "tidak konsisten … tidak konsisten" reads as a stutter; on first pass it lands as the flat claim "this is inconsistent with little-endian", the opposite half of the English's deliberately neutral "neither/nor". Not confidently false (the reader will notice the sentence is broken), but it must be rewritten.

examples.source: Basis encoding / Amplitude encoding / Angle encoding / Phase encoding / Dense angle encoding (headings)
examples.translation: Pengodean basis / Pengodean amplitudo / Pengodean sudut / Pengodean fase / Pengodean sudut padat — while the body and heading 624 keep "encoding" ("Encoding dengan feature map bawaan", "basis encoding", "amplitude encoding")
examples.suggested: Keep one convention: headings "Basis encoding", "Amplitude encoding", "Angle encoding", "Phase encoding", "Dense angle encoding" to match the body
examples.why: The five method headings are the only places the term is Indonesianized; every reference to the same method in the prose below uses the English form, so the table of contents and the text disagree.

examples.source: unitary operator / unitary evolution operator; "all gates in a circuit"
examples.translation: "operator uniter" (721, 858) vs "operator evolusi unitary" / "operator unitary" (875); "jumlah semua Gate dalam sebuah sirkuit" (968) vs "Circuit" everywhere else
examples.suggested: Pick "uniter" (or "unitary") throughout; change "sebuah sirkuit" to "sebuah Circuit"
examples.why: Within-file inconsistency for one concept; recognizable either way, but a native editor would unify it.

examples.source: It is one thing to say that the zz_feature_map, for example, is difficult to simulate classically, and therefore interesting. It is quite another thing for the zz_feature_map to be ideally suited to your machine learning task or data set.
examples.translation: Satu hal untuk mengatakan bahwa `zz_feature_map`, misalnya, sulit untuk disimulasikan secara klasik, dan karena itu menarik. Hal yang sama sekali berbeda adalah `zz_feature_map` yang idealnya cocok untuk tugas machine learning atau dataset __kamu__.
examples.suggested: Mengatakan bahwa `zz_feature_map`, misalnya, sulit disimulasikan secara klasik — dan karena itu menarik — adalah satu hal. Apakah `zz_feature_map` benar-benar cocok untuk tugas machine learning atau dataset __kamu__ adalah soal yang sama sekali lain.
examples.why: The English "one thing … quite another thing" contrast is calqued into a noun phrase that reads as if it were describing a zz_feature_map which IS ideally suited; the rhetorical point (classical hardness ≠ fitness for your data) is blunted.

examples.source: But we have with just four computational basis states.
examples.translation: Tapi kita hanya punya empat basis komputasi.
examples.suggested: Tapi kita hanya punya empat computational basis state.
examples.why: "empat basis komputasi" says "four computational bases" rather than "four basis states"; the surrounding argument (eight parameters spread over four complex prefactors) makes the intent recoverable, but the noun is wrong.

editor_note: No semantic drift anywhere: the exam facts (20 pertanyaan, "minimal 16 dengan benar", "dua percobaan" → "terkunci sementara"), the maintenance notice and the whole Credly privacy paragraph all match the English exactly, and the informal "kamu/-mu" convention holds throughout. What a native editor would still change are three translationese slips: "klik tombol di bawah untuk navigasi ke IBM Training" uses the noun "navigasi" as if it were a verb (native: "untuk menuju ke" / "untuk membuka"); the privacy paragraph's "Itu akan ditangani secara konsisten dengan praktik privasi IBM" opens with a bare pronoun "Itu" for "It" — Indonesian needs "Informasi tersebut akan ditangani sesuai dengan praktik privasi IBM"; and the final link is written "[di sini.](…)" with the full stop pulled inside the link text, so the period renders as part of the hyperlink (EN has "[here](…)."). "penawaran konten" for "content offering" is a mild calque but defensible and not counted.

examples.source: click the button below to navigate to IBM® Training, where you can take the badging exam
examples.translation: klik tombol di bawah untuk navigasi ke IBM® Training, di mana kamu bisa mengikuti ujian lencana
examples.suggested: klik tombol di bawah untuk menuju ke IBM® Training, tempat kamu bisa mengikuti ujian lencana
examples.why: "untuk navigasi ke" uses the noun navigasi in a verb slot — a direct calque of "to navigate to"; a native technical writer writes "untuk menuju ke" or "untuk membuka". "di mana" as a relative pronoun is the classic English-"where" calque; "tempat" is the idiomatic choice.

examples.source: It will be handled in a manner consistent with IBM privacy practices.
examples.translation: Itu akan ditangani secara konsisten dengan praktik privasi IBM.
examples.suggested: Informasi tersebut akan ditangani sesuai dengan praktik privasi IBM.
examples.why: Sentence-initial bare "Itu" for English "It" is not idiomatic Indonesian — the referent (the personal information) must be named or carried by "tersebut". "secara konsisten dengan" is also a literal rendering of "in a manner consistent with"; "sesuai dengan" is the normal phrasing.

examples.source: The IBM Privacy Statement can be viewed [here](https://www.ibm.com/privacy/us/en/).
examples.translation: Pernyataan Privasi IBM dapat dilihat [di sini.](https://www.ibm.com/privacy/us/en/)
examples.suggested: Pernyataan Privasi IBM dapat dilihat [di sini](https://www.ibm.com/privacy/us/en/).
examples.why: The full stop was moved inside the link label, so the rendered hyperlink text becomes "di sini." including the period — the English keeps punctuation outside the link. Cosmetic, but it is a rendering difference a native editor would fix.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat: the overview keeps "will offer some review … but will also assume some familiarity" intact ("akan menawarkan beberapa ulasan … tapi juga mengasumsikan kamu sudah familiar"), the Credly notice preserves every element of the disclosure (name/email/badge shared, Credly email with claim instructions, global sharing with subsidiaries and third parties), and the informal "kamu" register holds consistently. Two spots read as translationese a native technical editor would rewrite: "menawarkan beberapa ulasan pendekatan machine learning klasik" is a word-for-word calque of "offer some review of" (Indonesian would use "memberikan sedikit tinjauan/ulasan tentang"), and the Credly sentence opens with the bare pronoun "Itu akan ditangani secara konsisten dengan praktik privasi IBM", where Indonesian needs an explicit antecedent ("Informasi tersebut akan ditangani sesuai dengan praktik privasi IBM"). Domain terms are handled by a defensible keep-in-English convention (quantum kernels, variational quantum circuits, machine learning) with "pengkodean data" for data encoding; neither issue misleads the learner.

examples.source: The course will offer some review of classical machine learning approaches, but will also assume some familiarity with these methods.
examples.translation: Kursus ini akan menawarkan beberapa ulasan pendekatan machine learning klasik, tapi juga mengasumsikan kamu sudah familiar dengan metode-metode ini.
examples.suggested: Kursus ini akan memberikan sedikit tinjauan tentang pendekatan machine learning klasik, tapi juga mengasumsikan kamu sudah cukup familiar dengan metode-metode tersebut.
examples.why: "menawarkan beberapa ulasan" is a literal calque of "offer some review"; in Indonesian "beberapa ulasan" counts discrete reviews (like product reviews) rather than conveying "some amount of review", and "menawarkan" is commercial. Meaning is still recoverable, so MINOR.

examples.source: It will be handled in a manner consistent with IBM privacy practices.
examples.translation: Itu akan ditangani secara konsisten dengan praktik privasi IBM.
examples.suggested: Informasi tersebut akan ditangani sesuai dengan praktik privasi IBM.
examples.why: Sentence-initial bare "Itu" as a stand-in for an abstract antecedent is English syntax; Indonesian technical prose repeats the noun ("Informasi tersebut"). Also "secara konsisten dengan" is a calque of "in a manner consistent with" — idiomatic Indonesian is "sesuai dengan".

editor_note: Delta entry 48 is faithful and natural: "Keadaan kuantum yang sangat terjerat memungkinkan kita menyelesaikan sebagian besar masalah machine learning secara lebih efisien" keeps the quantifier "most" as "sebagian besar" (not softened/strengthened) and the claim un-negated, so it still sets up the "Salah." answer that follows; "sangat terjerat" matches the file's own "keterjeratan"/"terjerat" convention.

No semantic drift found: every quantitative and conditional claim survives intact — the 0.90^10 ≈ 35% answer, "kedalaman dua-qubit lebih dari 100, bahkan sebelum transpilasi, sudah tidak layak dipakai", the (1-p)^N degradation argument, "Dimensi matriks kernel ditentukan oleh jumlah titik dalam data pelatihanmu, bukan jumlah fitur", and the caveat that classical kernels would likely also reach 100% ("Tapi itu sangat berbeda dari keunggulan kuantum") are all faithful; the informal "kamu" register holds throughout. What a native editor would change is consistency and calques: "feature map" is rendered "peta fitur" in the first two thirds (lines 34, 85, 380) but left as English "feature map" in the last third (lines 656, 818, 828, 835, 839), and the Step-4 headings alternate between "Post-processing" (480) and "Pasca-proses" (806), with "Pemetaan input klasik" (335) vs "Peta input klasik" (522). Several sentences are word-for-word English syntax rather than Indonesian: "kita bermaksud melangkah ke semua titik data" for "step over all data points", "dengan struktur tersebut dalam pikiran" for "with that structure in mind", "mengadvokasi satu metode di atas yang lain", and "di antara alat-alat lain" for "among other tools". There is also one untranslated inline English word ("10 pengukuran paling probable teratas", line 267) and the calque "tidak traktabel" used twice where "sulit ditangani"/"tidak praktis" is the idiomatic rendering.

examples.source: pre-made feature map / custom feature maps / Try different feature maps
examples.translation: "peta fitur yang sudah jadi" … then "feature map kustom", "Coba berbagai feature map dan skema entanglement"
examples.suggested: Pick one and keep it: "peta fitur" everywhere (or "feature map" everywhere), e.g. "Coba berbagai peta fitur dan skema entanglement."
examples.why: The same core concept is named two different ways, splitting across the first and last thirds of the lesson; recognizable, but a learner scanning the Review section sees a term that never appeared in the body.

examples.source: But in this case, we intend to step over all data points and calculate the full kernel matrix.
examples.translation: Namun dalam kasus ini, kita bermaksud melangkah ke semua titik data dan menghitung matriks kernel penuh.
examples.suggested: Namun dalam kasus ini, kita akan melakukan iterasi atas seluruh titik data dan menghitung matriks kernel penuh.
examples.why: "melangkah ke semua titik data" is a literal calque of "step over"; in Indonesian it reads as physically stepping toward the points, not looping over them. A native writer uses "melakukan iterasi atas" / "menelusuri".

examples.source: you should design an entanglement map with that structure in mind
examples.translation: kamu sebaiknya merancang peta entanglement dengan struktur tersebut dalam pikiran
examples.suggested: kamu sebaiknya merancang peta entanglement berdasarkan struktur tersebut
examples.why: "dengan … dalam pikiran" is a word-for-word transfer of the English idiom "with … in mind" and is not idiomatic Indonesian.

examples.source: to look only at the top 10 most probable measurements
examples.translation: untuk hanya melihat 10 pengukuran paling probable teratas
examples.suggested: untuk melihat hanya 10 hasil pengukuran dengan probabilitas tertinggi
examples.why: The English adjective "probable" is left untranslated mid-sentence, and "paling … teratas" is redundant; the sentence reads as unfinished machine output.

examples.source: Step 4: Post-process, return result in classical format
examples.translation: "Langkah 4: Post-processing, kembalikan hasil dalam format klasik" (three times) vs "Langkah 4: Pasca-proses, kembalikan hasil dalam format klasik" (last occurrence)
examples.suggested: Use the same wording in all four Step-4 headings (and align "Pemetaan input klasik" at line 335 with "Peta input klasik" at line 522).
examples.why: The four parallel Qiskit-patterns headings are the lesson's navigational spine; renaming one of them makes the repeated structure look like a different step.

examples.source: How is the accuracy affected by increasing/decreasing the amount of training data?
examples.translation: Bagaimana akurasi dipengaruhi oleh meningkatkan/mengurangi jumlah data pelatihan?
examples.suggested: Bagaimana akurasi dipengaruhi oleh penambahan/pengurangan jumlah data pelatihan?
examples.why: "dipengaruhi oleh" requires a nominalization, not a bare verb; the same pattern recurs in the next bullet ("dipengaruhi oleh meningkatkan jumlah fitur"), giving the closing checklist a distinctly machine-translated feel.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination found: every load-bearing claim survives intact, including the tricky ones (the "if a horizontal line is *not* detected, then it is a vertical line" binary-classification reasoning, the CNOT pairs 0-1/1-2/2-3 vs. the extension to 4-5/5-6/6-7, the "~60% lebih rendah" loss claim, the 32-qubit non-Clifford simulation limit, and the 72 free parameters reducible "setidaknya faktor 2-3"). The informal register ("kamu", "masalahmu", "ansatz-mu") holds throughout. What a native editor would change: (1) the file splits its core vocabulary in two — the first ~60% writes "komputer quantum", "Circuit variational", "quantum Circuit", while everything from "Langkah 1 ditinjau ulang" onward switches to "komputer kuantum", "Circuit variasional", and one lone "sirkuit kuantum" (line ~651); the concept stays identifiable, but the seam is visible. (2) "Mengentanglement qubit yang berdekatan… agar bisa saling direntanglement" (line ~173) is an invented Indonesian morphology no technical writer would produce. (3) Several English calques survive: "layer-layer tersebut datang dalam urutan ini", "Seseorang bisa memiliki beberapa layer" / "seseorang mungkin menemui barren plateaus" (English impersonal "one", which Indonesian renders as "kita"), and the inverted "Kita harus sekarang memutuskan…". (4) "melewati seluruh dataset dalam batch" for "go over the entire dataset" picks a verb whose commoner sense is "to skip"; "menelusuri"/"mengiterasi" is what is meant and is disambiguated only by the surrounding clause.

examples.source: Entangling adjacent qubits does not increase the depth by too much, but entangling very distant qubits can increase depth substantially, as we must insert swap gates to move information onto qubits that are adjacent in order for them to be entangled.
examples.translation: Mengentanglement qubit yang berdekatan tidak terlalu meningkatkan kedalaman, tetapi mengentanglement qubit yang sangat jauh bisa meningkatkan kedalaman secara substansial, karena kita harus menyisipkan swap Gate untuk memindahkan informasi ke qubit yang berdekatan agar bisa saling direntanglement.
examples.suggested: Meng-entangle qubit yang berdekatan tidak terlalu menambah kedalaman, tetapi meng-entangle qubit yang berjauhan bisa menambah kedalaman secara substansial, karena kita harus menyisipkan Gate SWAP untuk memindahkan informasi ke qubit yang bertetangga agar keduanya bisa di-entangle.
examples.why: 'Mengentanglement' and especially 'direntanglement' are invented Indonesian affixations on an English noun; no native technical writer produces them. Meaning survives, so MINOR.

examples.source: This variational circuit is sometimes called the "ansatz". / Our previous variational circuit contained CNOT gates…
examples.translation: Circuit variational ini kadang disebut "ansatz". … Circuit variasional sebelumnya berisi Gate CNOT … revisi Circuit variasional kita
examples.suggested: Pick one: 'Circuit variasional' (or 'variational') throughout; likewise 'komputer kuantum' vs. the earlier 'komputer quantum', and drop the single 'sirkuit kuantum' at line ~651 in favour of the file's 'Circuit kuantum'.
examples.why: Three parallel term splits (variational/variasional, quantum/kuantum, Circuit/sirkuit) divide the file roughly at the 'Langkah 1 ditinjau ulang' seam. The concept stays identifiable, so MINOR per the calibration rule.

examples.source: There is no constraint that forces the layers to come in this order, or even to be fully separate. One could have multiple variational and/or encoding layers in any order that is technically motivated.
examples.translation: Tidak ada batasan yang memaksa layer-layer tersebut datang dalam urutan ini, atau bahkan harus sepenuhnya terpisah. Seseorang bisa memiliki beberapa layer variational dan/atau encoding dalam urutan apapun yang dimotivasi secara teknis.
examples.suggested: Tidak ada batasan yang mengharuskan layer-layer tersebut tersusun dalam urutan ini, atau bahkan harus sepenuhnya terpisah. Kita bisa memakai beberapa layer variasional dan/atau encoding dalam urutan apa pun yang punya alasan teknis.
examples.why: 'datang dalam urutan ini' is a word-for-word calque of 'come in this order'; English impersonal 'one' is rendered as 'Seseorang' (a person), where Indonesian technical prose uses 'kita'. Same calque recurs at 'seseorang mungkin menemui barren plateaus' and 'seseorang bisa saja beranggapan'.

examples.source: We can now go over the entire dataset in batches in desired number of epochs to train our quantum neural network.
examples.translation: Kita sekarang bisa melewati seluruh dataset dalam batch dengan jumlah epoch yang diinginkan untuk melatih quantum neural network kita.
examples.suggested: Kita sekarang bisa menelusuri seluruh dataset dalam batch dengan jumlah epoch yang diinginkan untuk melatih quantum neural network kita.
examples.why: 'melewati' most commonly reads as 'to skip/pass by', the opposite of iterating over the data; only the trailing 'untuk melatih' and the section heading ('Iterasi dataset…') rescue it. Imperfect-but-recoverable verb choice, so MINOR.

examples.source: We must now decide on an ansatz to be trained. / We must now define an observable, so we can use it in our cost function.
examples.translation: Kita harus sekarang memutuskan ansatz yang akan dilatih. / Kita harus mendefinisikan observable sekarang, agar bisa menggunakannya dalam fungsi biaya kita.
examples.suggested: Sekarang kita harus memutuskan ansatz yang akan dilatih. / Sekarang kita harus mendefinisikan observable, agar bisa menggunakannya dalam fungsi biaya kita.
examples.why: English adverb placement carried over literally; Indonesian fronts 'Sekarang'. Grammatical but audibly translated — stiffness only, never a FAIL.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted negation, no swapped quantity, no hallucinated sentence; the Bell-state, shots, noise and queue-time passages all carry the English claims intact, and the informal "kamu" register holds from start to finish. The defects are lexical and stylistic: "counts" is rendered three ways — "perhitungan" (= calculations, the wrong word) in the helper-function paragraph, "jumlah" in the QPU/simulator paragraphs, "hitungan" in the quiz — and "extracting the counts" therefore reads as "extracting the calculations". The clause "stronger than any purely classical correlation or shared randomness can explain" is re-hinged as a relative clause ("...korelasi klasik atau keacakan bersama mana pun yang bisa menjelaskannya"), which drops "purely" and half-implies that something does explain it. Remaining slips are translationese a native technical writer would rewrite: "pengenalan praktis yang lembut" for "gentle introduction", "menyeret Gate ke kabel" for dragging gates onto wires, "kamu akan pernah melihat" calquing "you'll ever see", and the ungrammatical "saat kita skala ke lebih banyak qubit". None of these would give a learner a false belief about the physics.

examples.source: extracting the counts from the results
examples.translation: mengekstrak perhitungan dari hasilnya
examples.suggested: mengekstrak cacahan (counts) dari hasilnya
examples.why: "perhitungan" means calculations, not measurement counts; the same concept is later rendered "jumlah" (line 179, 215) and "hitungan" (line 243) — three renderings of one core term inside one file.

examples.source: This link is stronger than independent randomness and stronger than any purely classical correlation or shared randomness can explain.
examples.translation: Hubungan ini lebih kuat dari keacakan independen dan lebih kuat dari korelasi klasik atau keacakan bersama mana pun yang bisa menjelaskannya.
examples.suggested: ...lebih kuat daripada yang bisa dijelaskan oleh korelasi klasik murni atau keacakan bersama mana pun.
examples.why: The English says no classical correlation can explain the link; the Indonesian relative clause "yang bisa menjelaskannya" reads as "any classical correlation that can explain it", presupposing an explanation exists, and "purely" is dropped.

examples.source: Superposition doesn't mean you'll ever see both results in one measurement
examples.translation: Superposisi tidak berarti kamu akan pernah melihat kedua hasil dalam satu pengukuran
examples.suggested: Superposisi bukan berarti kamu akan melihat kedua hasil sekaligus dalam satu pengukuran
examples.why: "akan pernah melihat" is a word-for-word calque of "will ever see"; Indonesian does not stack "akan pernah" this way, and the intended "both at once" force is carried better by "sekaligus".

examples.source: lets you build circuits by dragging gates onto wires / as we scale to more qubits
examples.translation: membangun Circuit dengan cara menyeret Gate ke kabel / saat kita skala ke lebih banyak qubit
examples.suggested: menyeret Gate ke jalur qubit / saat kita meningkatkan skala ke lebih banyak qubit
examples.why: "kabel" is a physical cable, not a circuit-diagram wire; "kita skala ke" uses the noun "skala" as a verb, which is ungrammatical in Indonesian and reads as raw MT.

editor_note: Placeholder stub page whose only prose line, "Lesson coming soon!", is rendered idiomatically as "Pelajaran segera hadir!"; the title/sidebar_label "Lanjutkan perjalanan belajarmu" and description "Tur kursus dan jalur pembelajaran lain di IBM Quantum Platform" are faithful and keep the informal -mu register with no drift or added claims.

Semantically faithful throughout — the load-bearing facts all survive intact: "20 soal", "minimal 16 dengan benar untuk lulus", "dalam dua percobaan, ujian akan terkunci sementara", and the full Credly notice (third-party processor, US location, name/email/badge shared, global subsidiary sharing). Informal register holds consistently ("kamu", "kemampuanmu", "lencanamu") with no deferential slips. Two stylistic blemishes a native technical editor would still change: the Credly paragraph's closing "Ini akan ditangani dengan cara yang konsisten dengan praktik privasi IBM" is a word-for-word calque of "in a manner consistent with" with a vague bare "Ini" as subject, and line 18 uses the locative relative "di mana" for English "where" referring to a website rather than a place. Also a mild internal inconsistency: the course name is localized in the frontmatter title ("Gunakan komputer kuantum hari ini") but kept in English twice in the body — defensible as a proper noun, but not uniform.

examples.source: It will be handled in a manner consistent with IBM privacy practices.
examples.translation: Ini akan ditangani dengan cara yang konsisten dengan praktik privasi IBM.
examples.suggested: Informasi tersebut akan ditangani sesuai dengan praktik privasi IBM.
examples.why: "dengan cara yang konsisten dengan" is a literal calque of "in a manner consistent with" that no Indonesian legal/technical writer would produce; "sesuai dengan" is the idiomatic rendering. The bare anaphoric "Ini" also leaves the subject vague after a long sentence about IBM sharing data — "Informasi tersebut" pins it back to the personal information. Meaning is unchanged, so this is cosmetic.

examples.source: click the button below to navigate to IBM Training, where you can take the badging exam
examples.translation: klik tombol di bawah untuk menuju ke IBM Training, di mana kamu bisa mengikuti ujian lencana
examples.suggested: klik tombol di bawah untuk menuju ke IBM Training, tempat kamu bisa mengikuti ujian lencana
examples.why: "di mana" as an English-style relative pronoun is a well-known calque flagged by Indonesian style guidance; a native writer would use "tempat" or simply split the clause. Fully understandable and not misleading, hence minor.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: the welcome, exam and full Credly privacy notice all match the English clause for clause (third-party processor, data shared, email notification, IBM subsidiaries/global sharing all intact), and the informal "kamu/-mu" register holds throughout ("lencanamu", "informasi pribadimu"). Two things a native technical editor would change, both stylistic. (1) "Ujian ini dimaksudkan untuk diambil setelah membaca pelajaran" is a calque of "intended to be taken"; Indonesian collocates ujian with "mengikuti/diikuti", not "diambil" — and the same sentence's own preceding clause already uses the right verb ("ikuti ujian di IBM Training"), so the file contradicts itself within two lines. (2) "Kalau kamu bisa mengikuti notebook dan klik \"Run\"" is too terse for "follow along with a notebook"; "mengikuti langkah-langkah di notebook" is what a native writer would put. Neither misleads a learner.

examples.source: This exam is intended to be taken after reading the lessons in this course.
examples.translation: Ujian ini dimaksudkan untuk diambil setelah membaca pelajaran dalam kursus ini.
examples.suggested: Ujian ini sebaiknya diikuti setelah kamu membaca pelajaran dalam kursus ini.
examples.why: "diambil" is a word-for-word calque of "to be taken"; Indonesian says "mengikuti ujian". The same sentence's earlier clause already renders it correctly as "ikuti ujian di IBM Training", so the verb is inconsistent within one paragraph.

examples.source: If you can follow along with a notebook and click "Run," you're ready.
examples.translation: Kalau kamu bisa mengikuti notebook dan klik "Run," kamu sudah siap.
examples.suggested: Kalau kamu bisa mengikuti langkah-langkah di notebook dan klik "Run", kamu sudah siap.
examples.why: "mengikuti notebook" reads as following the notebook itself rather than following along with its steps; the English "follow along with" needs the object spelled out in Indonesian to sound like a human wrote it.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I found no inverted conditions, swapped quantities or hallucinated claims: the CNOT rule ("membalik qubit 1 (disebut qubit target) hanya jika qubit 0 (disebut qubit kontrol) berada dalam keadaan |1⟩"), the little-endian note, the 50/50 probabilities, the "superposition is not literally both states at once" caveat and the coin-glued-together analogy all land correctly, and the informal "kamu" register holds from start to finish. What a native technical editor would still change is vocabulary, not content: "entanglement" is split between the verb family "terjerat/menjerat" and the noun "keterikatan kuantum" (the concept stays identifiable, but "keterjeratan" would keep one family), and two physics collocations are literal rather than idiomatic — "Gate tidak memperpanjang atau mempersingkat vektor" uses "mempersingkat" (shorten in *duration*) where vector length needs "memperpendek", and interfering waves that "saling memperkuat atau membatalkan" should be "saling meniadakan" ("membatalkan" = cancel an appointment). Also a small relational slip in the gate-matrix list: "di mana $N$ juga merupakan dimensi vektor keadaan yang diterapkan" reads as "the state vector that is applied", losing EN's "the state vector it is applied to". None of these would mislead a learner about the physics.

examples.source: We saw that this is a hallmark of quantum entanglement. / With entangled qubits, the situation is fundamentally different.
examples.translation: Kita melihat bahwa ini adalah ciri khas keterikatan kuantum. / Dengan qubit yang terjerat, situasinya secara fundamental berbeda.
examples.suggested: Pick one family: "keterjeratan kuantum" + "qubit yang terjerat" (or consistently "keterikatan" + "terikat").
examples.why: The noun (keterikatan) and the verb/participle (terjerat) come from different roots, so the reader must infer that the section heading "Lebih lanjut tentang keterikatan kuantum" is about the same phenomenon as "qubit yang terjerat" two lines below. Recognizable, hence minor.

examples.source: The gates do not lengthen or shorten them, but simply rotate them.
examples.translation: Gate tidak memperpanjang atau mempersingkat vektor, tapi hanya merotasinya.
examples.suggested: Gate tidak memperpanjang atau memperpendek vektor, tapi hanya merotasinya.
examples.why: "mempersingkat" is shortening in time (a meeting, a trip); the length of a vector takes "memperpendek". A physics reader notices immediately.

examples.source: like overlapping waves that can amplify or cancel each other
examples.translation: seperti gelombang yang bertumpang tindih yang dapat saling memperkuat atau membatalkan
examples.suggested: seperti gelombang yang saling bertumpang tindih dan dapat saling memperkuat atau meniadakan
examples.why: "membatalkan" is cancel-as-in-call-off; destructive interference in Indonesian physics prose is "saling meniadakan" (or "saling melemahkan"). The double "yang ... yang" is also stiff.

examples.source: They are always square, $N \times N$ matrices, where $N$ is also the dimension of the state vector it is applied to.
examples.translation: Matriks ini selalu persegi, berukuran $N \times N$, di mana $N$ juga merupakan dimensi vektor keadaan yang diterapkan.
examples.suggested: ... di mana $N$ juga merupakan dimensi vektor keadaan yang dikenai matriks tersebut.
examples.why: EN says the matrix is applied TO the state vector; the Indonesian relative clause reads as "the state vector that is applied", flipping which object acts on which. The surrounding 2x2 example still makes the intent recoverable, so this is a dropped relation rather than a misleading claim.

examples.source: you can [learn how to do matrix multiplication]
examples.translation: kamu bisa [pelajari cara melakukan perkalian matriks]
examples.suggested: kamu bisa [mempelajari cara melakukan perkalian matriks]
examples.why: After "bisa", Indonesian takes the meN- form (mempelajari), not the bare imperative stem (pelajari). Small grammatical slip inside the link text.

editor_note: No misleading drift: the physics (antiferromagnetic anti-alignment, transverse field forcing a superposition ground state, J/h_x roles, Sampler=histogram vs Estimator=single expectation number, the counts 01/10 reading, the final energy) all track the English faithfully, and the informal "kamu" register holds throughout. What a native technical editor would change is wording: "variational" is rendered as "variatif" three times (lines ~56, 354, 356 — "algoritma variatif", "metode variatif", "teknik variatif"), but "variatif" in Indonesian means "varied/diverse"; the field's term is "variasional" — recognizable here only because the linked course title stays in English. Two calques read as raw MT: "As he famously put it" → "Seperti yang terkenalnya:" (ungrammatical) and "the trickiest and most involved part" → "bagian ... paling banyak terlibat", which in Indonesian says "most participated-in", not "most elaborate". Minor inconsistencies: the heading "Post-process" is "Proses pasca" (lines 80, 218, 332) but the body says "langkah pasca-pemrosesan" (line 334), and "Circuit" is kept in English everywhere except one lone "setiap sirkuit kuantum" (line 124); also "in a later lesson" became "dalam pelajaran berikutnya" (next lesson) with "broader" dropped from "broader landscape".

examples.source: such as variational algorithms / the essence of variational methods / beyond variational techniques
examples.translation: seperti algoritma variatif / inti dari metode variatif / melampaui teknik variatif
examples.suggested: algoritma variasional / metode variasional / teknik variasional
examples.why: "Variatif" is a false friend meaning "varied/diverse"; the established Indonesian rendering of the physics term is "variasional". Consistent within the file and disambiguated by the adjacent English course title "Variational Quantum Algorithms", so recognizable — but still the wrong domain word.

examples.source: As he famously put it: "Nature isn't classical, dammit..."
examples.translation: Seperti yang terkenalnya: "Alam itu tidak klasik, sial, ..."
examples.suggested: Seperti ucapannya yang terkenal: "Alam itu tidak klasik, sialan, ..."
examples.why: "Seperti yang terkenalnya" is not grammatical Indonesian — it is a word-for-word transposition of "as he famously put it" with no noun for the clause to attach to. A native writer would write "Seperti ucapannya yang terkenal" or "Dalam kata-katanya yang terkenal".

examples.source: In many applications, this is the trickiest and most involved part of the workflow
examples.translation: Dalam banyak aplikasi, ini adalah bagian alur kerja yang paling rumit dan paling banyak terlibat
examples.suggested: ... bagian alur kerja yang paling rumit dan paling memakan usaha / paling berbelit
examples.why: "Most involved" (= elaborate, laborious) is calqued as "paling banyak terlibat", which in Indonesian means "the most involved as a participant" — the sentence ends up saying the mapping step participates the most, not that it is the most intricate.

examples.source: Post-process the raw measurement data ... in the post-processing step / every quantum circuit
examples.translation: Proses pasca data pengukuran mentah ... dalam langkah pasca-pemrosesan / setiap sirkuit kuantum
examples.suggested: Use one form consistently ("Pascapemrosesan" for the heading and body); and keep "Circuit" as elsewhere in the file, i.e. "setiap Circuit kuantum"
examples.why: Two within-file inconsistencies: "Post-process" is "Proses pasca" in the headings but "pasca-pemrosesan" in the prose, and the file's own convention of keeping "Circuit" in English breaks once with "sirkuit kuantum". Neither misleads, but an editor would unify them.

examples.source: We'll explore the broader landscape of quantum-suitable problems in a later lesson.
examples.translation: Kita akan menjelajahi lanskap masalah yang cocok untuk kuantum dalam pelajaran berikutnya.
examples.suggested: Kita akan menjelajahi lanskap yang lebih luas dari masalah yang cocok untuk kuantum dalam pelajaran selanjutnya.
examples.why: "A later lesson" is narrowed to "pelajaran berikutnya" (the next lesson), and the qualifier "broader" is dropped. A dropped qualifier plus a slightly over-specific pointer — no false physics, so MINOR.

editor_note: No sentence here would mislead a learner: the physics is faithful throughout (CNOT "membalik qubit target hanya ketika qubit kontrol berada dalam keadaan |1⟩", the 75%-chance example, Little Endian "qubit 0 adalah bit paling kanan", depth 4/5 and the "Circuit yang sangat dalam tidak demikian" contrast all land correctly), and the informal "kamu" register holds end to end. The main defect is a within-file split on the single most frequent term: "state" is "kondisi" through §1–3.3 ("Kondisi kuantum dan Bloch sphere", "kondisi superposisi", "kondisi awal") and then silently becomes "keadaan" from §4.1 onward ("keadaan kuantum", "keadaan awal Qiskit"); "keadaan" is the conventional Indonesian physics term, so the earlier "kondisi" is also the weaker of the two. "Entangled state" is rendered "keadaan terjalin" (literally "interwoven"), non-standard but always glossed with "(entangled)", so still recognizable. Smaller slips: "equal superposition" becomes "superposisi yang sama" (§|−⟩, readable as "the same superposition") and "superposisi yang setara" (§4.1), and a few calques — "seiring kita berjalan" for "as we go", the heading "Langkah 4. Proses pasca hasil" whose word order garbles "post-process the results".

examples.source: A qubit's state is represented as a superposition … / the quantum state of the above circuit can be written as a tensor product
examples.translation: Kondisi sebuah qubit direpresentasikan sebagai superposisi … / keadaan kuantum pada Circuit di atas bisa ditulis sebagai tensor product
examples.suggested: Use "keadaan" for "state" throughout (Keadaan sebuah qubit …, keadaan kuantum, keadaan superposisi, keadaan awal)
examples.why: "state" is rendered "kondisi" in §1–3.3 and "keadaan" from §4 onward — the same concept under two names in one lesson, and "keadaan" is the established Indonesian physics term while "kondisi" reads as "condition".

examples.source: An entangled state is a state |ψ_AB⟩ … / a maximally entangled state of three or more qubits
examples.translation: Keadaan terjalin (entangled) adalah keadaan |ψ_AB⟩ … / keadaan terjalin maksimal dari tiga qubit atau lebih
examples.suggested: keadaan terbelit (entangled) / keadaan entangled — or keep the English term as the file already does for "entanglement"
examples.why: "terjalin" (interwoven, as of threads) is not the conventional rendering; the file elsewhere keeps "entanglement" untranslated, so the noun and adjective drift apart. Glossed each time, so recognizable — MINOR, not misleading.

examples.source: Applying the H gate on |1⟩ results in an equal superposition of |0⟩ and |1⟩, but the sign of |1⟩ is negative.
examples.translation: Menerapkan gate $H$ pada $|1\rangle$ menghasilkan superposisi yang sama dari $|0\rangle$ dan $|1\rangle$, tapi tanda dari $|1\rangle$ adalah negatif.
examples.suggested: … menghasilkan superposisi seimbang antara $|0\rangle$ dan $|1\rangle$, tapi tanda $|1\rangle$ negatif.
examples.why: "superposisi yang sama" first parses as "the same superposition" rather than "equal-weight superposition"; the contrast clause rescues it, but a native technical writer would write "seimbang" (and "setara" at line 685 is a third variant of the same idea).

examples.source: We'll construct an empty circuit and then add quantum operations, discussing the gates and visualizing their effects as we go.
examples.translation: Kita akan membuat circuit kosong lalu menambahkan operasi kuantum, membahas gate dan memvisualisasikan efeknya seiring kita berjalan.
examples.suggested: … membahas gate dan memvisualisasikan efeknya sambil kita jalan / di sepanjang prosesnya.
examples.why: "seiring kita berjalan" is a word-for-word calque of "as we go" and reads as translationese; an Indonesian technical writer would use "sambil berjalan" or drop the phrase entirely.

examples.source: Step 4. Post-process the results — Finally, we must post-process our results to create outputs in the expected format
examples.translation: Langkah 4. Proses pasca hasil — Terakhir, kita harus memproses hasil kita untuk membuat output dalam format yang diharapkan
examples.suggested: Langkah 4. Pascaproses hasilnya — Terakhir, kita harus melakukan pascaproses terhadap hasil kita …
examples.why: The heading's word order ("Proses pasca hasil") reads as "post-result process" instead of the imperative "post-process the results", and the body drops "post-" entirely; the Qiskit-patterns step name loses its identity, though the step's content still explains it.

editor_note: Short stub page (title, attribution line, one sentence) rendered faithfully and naturally: "Modulnya dihosting di GitHub" and "Pelajaran ini bisa dianggap opsional, tetapi sangat direkomendasikan" preserve both the optional-but-recommended hedge and the Prof. Kawase / Universitas Tokyo attribution, with no drift or added claims.

No semantic drift, no hallucination, and every number, condition and caveat survives intact (25x shots = 10_000, 4k lapisan Gate dua-Qubit, hasil ideal = state input |000000⟩ with ⟨IIIIIZ⟩ = 1, "per 2024/06/28"); core terms are correct and consistent (nilai ekspektasi, langkah waktu, observable/shots/Backend/Estimator kept in English, "men-transpile"). Three editorial slips remain. (1) "noisy" is rendered "berisik" throughout ("Simulasi berisik", "Sampler berisik") while the noun "noise" is deliberately kept in English everywhere else ("model noise", "efek noise", "profil noise") — "berisik" is the colloquial acoustic sense of loud/noisy and clashes with the file's own convention; "simulasi ber-noise" / "simulasi dengan noise" is what an Indonesian quantum engineer would write. (2) §3 "melihat bagaimana error skalanya terhadap jumlah langkah waktu" is not idiomatic Indonesian — "skalanya" is pressed into service as a verb calquing "scales with respect to". (3) Two calqued constructions a native technical editor would rewrite: "Kita pertimbangkan Circuit 1-Qubit sederhana" (literal "We consider") and the agentless passive "pastikan plot yang lebih mulus diperoleh". None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: Noisy simulation without error mitigation / Build a noisy sampler with the noise model
examples.translation: Simulasi berisik tanpa mitigasi error / Buat Sampler berisik dengan model noise
examples.suggested: Simulasi ber-noise tanpa mitigasi error / Buat Sampler ber-noise dengan model noise
examples.why: The file keeps the noun 'noise' in English ('model noise', 'efek noise', 'profil noise') but renders the adjective 'noisy' as 'berisik', which in Indonesian primarily means acoustically loud/rowdy. The split is internally inconsistent with the file's own convention and reads colloquially in a technical heading; the concept is still recoverable from context, so it is MINOR.

examples.source: We consider 6-qubit Trotterized circuits for simulating the time evolution of one dimensional Ising model and see how the error scales with respect to the number of time steps.
examples.translation: Kita mempertimbangkan Circuit Trotterisasi 6-Qubit untuk mensimulasikan evolusi waktu model Ising satu dimensi dan melihat bagaimana error skalanya terhadap jumlah langkah waktu.
examples.suggested: ...dan melihat bagaimana error meningkat seiring bertambahnya jumlah langkah waktu.
examples.why: 'error skalanya terhadap' is a word-for-word calque of 'the error scales with respect to'; 'skalanya' (a noun + possessive) cannot carry the verbal sense 'scales'. Grammatically odd and reads as raw MT in an otherwise clean paragraph.

examples.source: We consider toy 1-qubit circuits which just repeat X gates `d` times ... / ensure that a smoother plot is obtained
examples.translation: Kita pertimbangkan Circuit 1-Qubit sederhana yang hanya mengulang Gate X sebanyak `d` kali ... / pastikan plot yang lebih mulus diperoleh
examples.suggested: Kita tinjau Circuit 1-Qubit sederhana ... / pastikan Anda memperoleh plot yang lebih mulus
examples.why: Two English-shaped constructions: 'Kita pertimbangkan' literalizes 'We consider' where Indonesian technical prose uses 'kita tinjau/kita gunakan', and the agentless passive 'plot ... diperoleh' in an exercise instruction is stiffer than the direct 'Anda memperoleh'. Meaning is intact; style only.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every numeric and conditional claim tracks the source — the O(N)/O(√N) contrast, "empat komponen utama" followed by only three items (the source's own bug, faithfully carried), "dua iterasi adalah optimal", "probabilitas ... tidak 100%", and the 3-/4-iteration degradation sentences ("sedikit berkurang" / "semakin berkurang", "probabilitas terendah") are all correct. What a native technical editor would change is terminology and calque: "equal superposition" is rendered "superposisi setara" (= "equivalent/on-par superposition") in both places it occurs (lines 73 and 149), where Indonesian quantum writing uses "superposisi seragam" or "superposisi merata"; "inversion about the average amplitude" becomes the spatial calque "inversi di sekitar amplitudo rata-rata" ("around the average") instead of "inversi terhadap nilai rata-rata"; and the "Post-processing the results" heading loses its "post-" as plain "Pemrosesan hasil". Register is consistently "kita"-based with no deferential slips, and domain terms (qubit, oracle, operator difusi, amplifikasi amplitudo, phase kickback, transpile) are correct and consistent.

examples.source: which will result in an equal superposition of $2^n$ states
examples.translation: yang akan menghasilkan superposisi setara dari $2^n$ state
examples.suggested: yang akan menghasilkan superposisi seragam dari $2^n$ state
examples.why: "setara" means equivalent/on a par, not equal-amplitude. The conventional Indonesian term for the uniform superposition is "superposisi seragam" (or "merata"). Recognizable from the accompanying formula, so MINOR, but it is used the same way again at line 149 ("state superposisi setara" for "the equal superposition state").

examples.source: which effectively performs an inversion about the average amplitude
examples.translation: yang secara efektif melakukan inversi di sekitar amplitudo rata-rata
examples.suggested: yang secara efektif melakukan inversi terhadap amplitudo rata-rata
examples.why: "about" here means "with respect to / reflected in", not spatial proximity; "di sekitar" reads as "in the vicinity of the average" and is a calque a native writer would not use for a reflection operator.

examples.source: Step 4: Post-processing the results.
examples.translation: Langkah 4: Pemrosesan hasil.
examples.suggested: Langkah 4: Pascapemrosesan hasil.
examples.why: The "post-" is dropped, so the heading reads as generic "processing the results" and loses the four-step Qiskit patterns framing (map / optimize / execute / post-process) that the course reuses across notebooks.

editor_note: The one re-written entry, the heading "2.2 Coupling map" → "2.2 Peta coupling", is accurate and not misleading — "peta" is the right word for "map" and a learner reaches the same concept. The only thing a native technical editor would change is consistency: the heading half-translates the term ("Peta coupling") while the very next sentence of the same section leaves it wholly in English ("Kita sekarang menggambar coupling map dari perangkat"), and the page elsewhere keeps hardware terms untranslated (Backend, Target, Gate, qubit, readout, "kisi heavy-hex"). Either "Coupling map" in the heading or "peta coupling" in the body would align the two; nothing here teaches a false concept, and the informal "kamu/-mu" register holds throughout.

examples.source: ### 2.2 Coupling map … We now draw the coupling map of the device.
examples.translation: ### 2.2 Peta coupling … Kita sekarang menggambar coupling map dari perangkat.
examples.suggested: ### 2.2 Coupling map … Kita sekarang menggambar coupling map dari perangkat.
examples.why: The heading half-translates the term while the first body sentence of the same section keeps it fully in English; aligning them (the untranslated form matches the rest of the page's hardware vocabulary: Backend, Target, Gate, readout) removes the split. Meaning is unaffected — MINOR only.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout this very short overview page — the 14 lessons/labs, the IBM Quantum–University of Tokyo collaboration, the "building toward a utility-scale calculation" framing and the June 2023 Nature cover reference all survive intact, with no drift, no dropped caveat and no hallucinated claim; "skala utilitas" for utility-scale is used consistently in both frontmatter and body. Two things a native technical editor would still change: the frontmatter writes "kursus 14-pelajaran", an orthographic calque of the English compound modifier "14-lesson course" (Indonesian does not hyphenate this way — "kursus 14 pelajaran" or "kursus yang terdiri dari 14 pelajaran"), and the body renders "the cover of Nature" as "sampul majalah Nature", adding the word "majalah" (magazine) which is not in the source and mis-types Nature — Indonesian scientific writing calls it "jurnal Nature". "Kursus replay acara ini" for "This event replay course" is borderline translationese (word order calqued from English) but remains understandable, so I am not counting it. Neither issue could mislead a learner about any quantum concept.

examples.source: The result is very similar to work published on the cover of Nature in June 2023.
examples.translation: Hasilnya sangat mirip dengan karya yang diterbitkan di sampul majalah Nature pada Juni 2023.
examples.suggested: Hasilnya sangat mirip dengan karya yang diterbitkan di sampul jurnal Nature pada Juni 2023.
examples.why: "majalah" (magazine) is added and not in the source; Nature is a scientific journal and is conventionally "jurnal Nature" in Indonesian technical writing.

examples.source: A collection of learning assets from a 14-lesson course on utility-scale quantum computing.
examples.translation: Kumpulan aset pembelajaran dari kursus 14-pelajaran tentang komputasi kuantum skala utilitas.
examples.suggested: Kumpulan aset pembelajaran dari kursus 14 pelajaran tentang komputasi kuantum skala utilitas.
examples.why: "14-pelajaran" copies the English hyphenated compound modifier; Indonesian does not hyphenate a numeral+noun modifier this way.

examples.source: This event replay course consists of 14 lessons and labs...
examples.translation: Kursus replay acara ini terdiri dari 14 pelajaran dan lab...
examples.suggested: Kursus tayang ulang acara ini terdiri dari 14 pelajaran dan lab...
examples.why: Borderline (not counted): the English noun-stack order is carried over verbatim; "replay acara" reads as MT, though a reader still understands it.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — lesson numbering (2-6, 7-8, 9, 10-11, 12-14), the Kawase/University of Tokyo attribution, the "no quiz or badge" caveat and the deprecated-code-snippets warning all survive intact, so nothing here would mislead a learner. Three editorial slips: (1) the second-person register is split within the file — formal "Anda" in "Jika Anda baru mengenal komputasi kuantum" and "berguna bagi Anda" versus the clitic "-mu" in "perhitunganmu" and "mahasiswamu", sometimes in the same sentence; (2) "Ini tak terbantahkan penting" is a stiff calque of "undeniably important" that no Indonesian technical writer would produce (natural: "Algoritma-algoritma ini jelas penting"); (3) "you should definitely work through these" is softened to plain "Anda sebaiknya mengerjakan ini semua", losing the emphatic "definitely". Also "the labs are sparse" is rendered "lab-nya ringkas" (concise) rather than the intended sense of minimal/bare ("minim" / "seadanya").

examples.source: your calculations might vary slightly … useful to you and your students
examples.translation: perhitunganmu mungkin sedikit berbeda … berguna bagi Anda dan mahasiswamu
examples.suggested: perhitungan Anda mungkin sedikit berbeda … berguna bagi Anda dan mahasiswa Anda
examples.why: The file mixes formal "Anda" (lines 17, 27) with the informal clitic "-mu", even inside a single sentence ("bagi Anda dan mahasiswamu"). Pick one convention; the file's dominant one is "Anda".

examples.source: These are undeniably important to our understanding of the potential power of quantum computing
examples.translation: Ini tak terbantahkan penting untuk pemahaman kita tentang potensi kekuatan komputasi kuantum
examples.suggested: Algoritma-algoritma ini jelas penting bagi pemahaman kita tentang potensi kekuatan komputasi kuantum
examples.why: "tak terbantahkan penting" is a word-for-word calque of "undeniably important"; Indonesian does not stack the adverbial that way. Bare "Ini" also loses the antecedent that the English plural "These" carries.

examples.source: If you are new to quantum computing, you should definitely work through these.
examples.translation: Jika Anda baru mengenal komputasi kuantum, Anda sebaiknya mengerjakan ini semua.
examples.suggested: Jika Anda baru mengenal komputasi kuantum, Anda benar-benar perlu mengerjakan semuanya.
examples.why: "definitely" is dropped and "should" weakened to "sebaiknya" (preferably), turning a firm recommendation into an optional suggestion. Not misleading about facts, but the pedagogical emphasis flattens.

examples.source: the labs are sparse and merely show a workflow
examples.translation: lab-nya ringkas dan hanya menampilkan alur kerja
examples.suggested: lab-nya minim dan hanya menampilkan alur kerja
examples.why: "ringkas" means concise/well-condensed, a positive quality; the English "sparse" signals the lab deliberately omits explanation (which lives in the PDF). "minim" or "seadanya" carries that sense.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, swapped quantities or hallucinated claims; the load-bearing heavy-hex explanation (degree-4 star node vs. "node dengan degree maksimal 3", SWAP insertion raising the gate count) and the optimization_level 0–3 description are both accurate, and the informal "kamu" register holds consistently ("apa yang bisa kamu lakukan", "kalau kamu menemukan Circuit-mu"). Three editorial slips: (1) "optimization" is rendered two ways inside one file — the §2.1 heading says "Level optimasi" while its own body switches to "optimisasi"/"tingkat optimisasi" four times, then §3.4 goes back to "Tahap Optimasi"; (2) the English observation-then-question pair "The new synthesis produces a shallower circuit. Why?" is collapsed into a single presupposing question, flattening the pedagogical beat where the reader is first shown the result; (3) "for more optimization" is softened/shifted to "untuk optimasi yang lebih baik" (better, not more), and "coupling constraint-aware" is left as the stiff calque "sadar batasan kopling". None of these would teach a learner something false.

examples.source: ### 2.1 Optimization level — `optimization_level` has four options... The higher the optimization level, the more computational effort... Level 1 is the default optimization level.
examples.translation: ### 2.1 Level optimasi — ... Semakin tinggi tingkat optimisasi, semakin banyak upaya komputasional... Level 1 adalah tingkat optimisasi default.
examples.suggested: Pick one form and keep it: heading "Level optimasi" with body "tingkat optimasi" / "tanpa optimasi" / "dengan optimasi", matching §3.4 "Tahap Optimasi" and §4.1 "Optimasi blok dua-Qubit".
examples.why: The same concept alternates between "optimasi" and "optimisasi" within a single section — and the section heading uses the other form than its own body. Recognizable either way, so MINOR, but a native technical editor would normalize it.

examples.source: The new synthesis produces a shallower circuit. Why?
examples.translation: Kenapa sintesis baru menghasilkan Circuit yang lebih dangkal (shallower)?
examples.suggested: Sintesis baru menghasilkan circuit yang lebih dangkal (shallower). Kenapa?
examples.why: English first states the observed result, then asks the reader to explain it — the setup for the heavy-hex paragraph that follows. The Indonesian merges both into one question that presupposes the result, so the reader is no longer handed the observation before being asked to account for it. Meaning survives; the teaching beat does not.

examples.source: For level 2 and 3, we have more passes (`Collect2qBlocks`, `ConsolidateBlocks`, `UnitarySynthesis`) for more optimization, namely two-qubit block optimization.
examples.translation: Untuk level 2 dan 3, ada lebih banyak pass (`Collect2qBlocks`, `ConsolidateBlocks`, `UnitarySynthesis`) untuk optimasi yang lebih baik, yaitu optimasi blok dua-Qubit.
examples.suggested: ...untuk optimasi yang lebih banyak, yaitu optimasi blok dua-Qubit.
examples.why: "more optimization" (extra optimization work, matching "more passes") becomes "optimasi yang lebih baik" (better optimization) — a quality claim the English does not make. The surrounding sentence still makes the point clear, so this does not mislead, but it is a dropped parallel between "more passes" and "more optimization".

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — every quantity, condition and caveat survives (5/16 vs 10/16 turns and the "digandakan untuk qubit berikutnya" chain, "qubit paling kiri ... frekuensi terendah", "hanya jika bit kontrolnya adalah |1⟩", θ = 1/2³ = 1/8, and the T-gate/λ = 2π/3 setups all match), the informal "kamu" register holds, and I found no hallucinated sentence. What a native technical editor would change is consistency: "unitary" is rendered three ways in the same file — "matriks unitari" (§2, §2.2), "operator/operasi uniter" (§3, §3.1), and left English in "operasi unitary terkontrol" (§3.2); the counting register alternates between "register pencacah" (§3.1 Persiapan/Superposisi) and "register penghitung"/"qubit penghitung" (§3.2); and "kuantum" silently becomes English "quantum" in §4 ("perangkat quantum nyata", "Circuit dan operator quantum") after being translated everywhere before. One calque also stands out: "yang diterjemahkan ke desimal" for "which translates to the decimal" — an Indonesian writer would say "yang setara dengan desimal". None of these mislead; the concepts stay identifiable.

examples.source: unitary matrix representation … U is a unitary operator … We perform the controlled unitary operations
examples.translation: representasi matriks unitari … operator uniter $U$ … Kita melakukan operasi unitary terkontrol
examples.suggested: Pick one: "uniter" throughout — "representasi matriks uniter", "operator uniter", "operasi uniter terkontrol".
examples.why: One core term ('unitary') appears in three different forms within a single file (unitari / uniter / unitary), which reads as inconsistent editing rather than a settled convention.

examples.source: the counting register … Hadamard gates to the counting qubits … measure the counting register
examples.translation: register pencacah … gate Hadamard pada qubit penghitung … mengukur register penghitung
examples.suggested: Use "register pencacah" / "qubit pencacah" consistently (or "penghitung" consistently), including §3.3 "3 qubit untuk pencacahan".
examples.why: The same register is named pencacah in §3.1 and penghitung in §3.2; a learner tracking the algorithm's two registers has to infer they are the same thing.

examples.source: using the real quantum device … Map the problem to a quantum-native format … Map problem to quantum circuits and operators
examples.translation: menggunakan perangkat quantum nyata … Petakan masalah ke format quantum-native … Petakan masalah ke Circuit dan operator quantum
examples.suggested: menggunakan perangkat kuantum nyata … format native-kuantum … Circuit dan operator kuantum
examples.why: 'quantum' is translated as 'kuantum' consistently in sections 1–3 (e.g. 'keadaan kuantum', 'algoritma kuantum') but reverts to untranslated English in section 4, breaking the file's own convention.

examples.source: We see we get one result (`001`) with certainty, which translates to the decimal: `1`.
examples.translation: Kita melihat kita mendapatkan satu hasil (`001`) dengan pasti, yang diterjemahkan ke desimal: `1`.
examples.suggested: Kita mendapatkan satu hasil (`001`) dengan pasti, yang setara dengan desimal `1`.
examples.why: 'diterjemahkan' is a literal calque of 'translates' in the linguistic sense; for base conversion Indonesian uses 'setara dengan' or 'dikonversi ke'. 'Kita melihat kita mendapatkan' also doubles the subject in a way no native technical writer would.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination; the hardest passages survive intact (the ±45° paragraph keeps "pertukaran spin menjadi yang paling mungkin dengan probabilitas 67%", the longitudinal-field caveat "tidak akan ada evolusi, sehingga kita akan mengukur sistem persis seperti saat disiapkan, ↓↑", and the right-to-left label note). Two things a native technical editor would still change: (1) "circuit" is rendered as Indonesian "sirkuit" exactly once, in §2.4 ("kita membangun sebuah sirkuit untuk satu langkah waktu"), while every other occurrence in the file keeps "Circuit" — a one-off split in the file's own convention; (2) "near-term quantum devices" (§1) is flattened to "perangkat kuantum masa kini" (present-day devices), which drops the near-future/NISQ-era sense the English carries — not misleading, since the same paragraph still says error accumulation is a real concern, but "jangka pendek"/"era NISQ" would carry the nuance. Terminology is otherwise correct and consistent (qubit, gate, nilai ekspektasi, observabel, transpilasi, primitif, Hamiltonian, irisan waktu, orde pertama/kedua/keempat), and the informal "kamu" register in §1.1–1.2 holds.

examples.source: We here construct a circuit for a single time step using Lie–Trotter.
examples.translation: Di sini kita membangun sebuah sirkuit untuk satu langkah waktu menggunakan Lie–Trotter.
examples.suggested: Di sini kita membangun sebuah Circuit untuk satu langkah waktu menggunakan Lie–Trotter.
examples.why: Sole use of Indonesian "sirkuit" in a file that otherwise keeps "Circuit" everywhere (§2.3, §2.4 heading, §3.1, §4.2, §4.4). Within-file inconsistency only — the concept stays identifiable.

examples.source: ...leads to more error accumulation (a non-negligible concern on near-term quantum devices).
examples.translation: ...menyebabkan lebih banyak akumulasi kesalahan (suatu kekhawatiran yang tidak bisa diabaikan pada perangkat kuantum masa kini).
examples.suggested: ...(suatu kekhawatiran yang tidak bisa diabaikan pada perangkat kuantum jangka pendek / era NISQ).
examples.why: "near-term" is a term of art about the coming NISQ generation; "masa kini" narrows it to present-day hardware. A dropped qualifier, not a false statement.

editor_note: No semantic drift: every numbered protocol step is faithful (teleportasi "01"→Gate X / "10"→Gate Z; superdense "01"→Gate Z / "10"→Gate X both match the source), the little-endian/100%-|0⟩ paragraph, the no-cloning Q&A, and the "dynamic circuits have a higher error rate" caveat all survive intact. What a native technical editor would change: (1) "classical" is rendered throughout as "klasikal" ("informasi klasikal", "berkomunikasi secara klasikal", "komunikasi klasikal") — in Indonesian *klasikal* means "in a class/collectively"; the standard adjective is "klasik", which the file itself uses once at line 33 ("komunikasi klasik tambahan"), so it is also internally inconsistent.
