(2) "entangled/entanglement" is split four ways — "state belitan bersama" (l.33), "state terkait"/"pasangan terkait" (ll.377, 380, 443, 769, 773), "keterkaitan (entanglement)" (l.976), plus the verb "meng-entangle" (ll.383, 457); the bare "terkait" ("related") is weak, though the English gloss at first use keeps the concept identifiable. (3) "Post-process the results" → "Proses pasca hasil" (ll.566, 730) is a word-order calque; Indonesian would be "Pascaproses hasilnya". (4) "trace out Bob's results" → "menelusuri hasil Bob" (l.741) reads as "follow/explore", losing the marginalization sense of *trace out*. (5) Typo "teman-teman yang berjauh" (l.974) for "berjauhan". Informal register ("kamu") holds consistently.

examples.source: Assume they can only communicate with classical communication … she has no means of classical communication with Bob
examples.translation: Asumsikan mereka hanya bisa berkomunikasi secara klasikal … dia tidak punya cara komunikasi klasikal dengan Bob
examples.suggested: …berkomunikasi secara klasik … komunikasi klasik…
examples.why: In Indonesian *klasikal* means "collective / classroom-style", not "classical" in the physics sense; the correct adjective is *klasik*. The file already uses "komunikasi klasik" once (l.33), so the rendering is both imperfect and inconsistent within the file — recognizable from context, hence MINOR.

examples.source: a shared entangled state (sometimes called an e-bit) … Alice and Bob shares a 2-qubit entangled state … by having shared entanglement
examples.translation: state belitan bersama (kadang disebut e-bit) … Alice dan Bob berbagi state terkait 2-Qubit … dengan memiliki keterkaitan (entanglement) yang dibagikan
examples.suggested: Pick one: "state terbelit" / "keterbelitan" (or keep "entangled"/"entanglement") and use it everywhere.
examples.why: Four competing renderings for one core concept — belitan, terkait, keterkaitan, and the hybrid verb meng-entangle. "terkait" alone only means "related", which under-specifies entanglement; the parenthetical English glosses at ll.377 and 976 keep it identifiable, so this is inconsistency rather than a false concept.

examples.source: Step 4: Post-process the results
examples.translation: Langkah 4: Proses pasca hasil
examples.suggested: Langkah 4: Pascaproses hasilnya
examples.why: Calqued word order: "Proses pasca hasil" parses as "the post-result process", not "post-process the results". A native technical writer would write "pascaproses hasilnya" or "olah hasilnya setelah eksekusi". Stiff, not misleading.

examples.source: Or, using `marginal_count`, you can trace out Bob's results on qubit 2.
examples.translation: Atau, menggunakan `marginal_count`, kamu bisa menelusuri hasil Bob pada qubit 2.
examples.suggested: …kamu bisa memarginalkan hasilnya sehingga hanya menyisakan hasil Bob pada qubit 2.
examples.why: "menelusuri" = "follow/trace through", the everyday sense of *trace*, whereas *trace out* here means marginalizing over the other two qubits. The surrounding code (`marginal_counts`) and the histogram keep the learner on track, so it is an imperfect term rather than a false concept.

examples.source: Although the scenarios for both involving distant friends are somewhat removed from quantum computing on a single QPU
examples.translation: Meski skenario keduanya yang melibatkan teman-teman yang berjauh agak berbeda dari komputasi kuantum pada satu QPU
examples.suggested: Meski skenario keduanya — yang melibatkan teman-teman yang berjauhan — agak jauh dari komputasi kuantum pada satu QPU
examples.why: "berjauh" is not a word (should be "berjauhan", the form used correctly at ll.31/33/35); the rest of the file gets this right, so it reads as a typo in the final summary paragraph.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — all quantities (127-Qubit × 60-lapisan, 20 langkah Trotter, $\langle Z_{62}\rangle$, 28 tepi, 144 tepi, 2 menit 19 detik), the "tanpa mitigasi" vs "yang dimitigasi" distinction, and the "tidak (__tidak seharusnya__) meminta Transpiler" caveat all survive intact, so nothing here would mislead a learner. The main editorial defect is that "noise/noisy" is rendered four different ways inside one file: "bising" (sec. 1: "komputer kuantum yang bising"), "bergangguan" (sec. 4.3: "simulasi bergangguan"), "gangguan" (sec. 4.4: "efek gangguan yang parah") and "kebisingan" (closing paragraph: "di tengah kebisingan") — the last is the acoustic sense and is the weakest choice for a hardware-noise context. Second, the concessive connector "Having said this," (sec. 2.2) is turned into the consequential "Dengan demikian," which reverses the logical relation to the preceding "tidak dijamin menemukan pewarnaan minimal" sentence, making the reasoning read as a non sequitur. Remaining slips are translationese: "Plot ini bersama dengan hasilmu" (parses as a noun phrase, not the imperative "Plot nilai-nilai ini…") and "Jika kursus ini menghasilkan kamu bergabung dalam pencarian ini" (calqued from "results in your joining"). Informal register ("kamu"/"kita") holds consistently.

examples.source: noisy simulation … the severe effects of noise … even in the presence of noise
examples.translation: simulasi bergangguan … efek gangguan yang parah … di tengah kebisingan
examples.suggested: simulasi berderau … efek derau yang parah … bahkan dengan adanya derau (or keep "bising" from sec. 1 throughout)
examples.why: "noise" is rendered four ways in one file (bising / bergangguan / gangguan / kebisingan); "kebisingan" in particular is the acoustic-loudness sense and is the wrong register for hardware noise. Concept stays identifiable, so MINOR.

examples.source: Having said this, since heavy-hex graphs are bipartite, we pick up graph_bipartite_edge_color
examples.translation: Dengan demikian, karena graf heavy-hex bersifat bipartit, kita memilih graph_bipartite_edge_color
examples.suggested: Meski begitu, karena graf heavy-hex bersifat bipartit, kita memilih graph_bipartite_edge_color
examples.why: "Having said this" is concessive (contrasting with the preceding "tidak dijamin menemukan pewarnaan minimal"); "Dengan demikian" means "therefore", inverting the discourse relation and turning the argument into a non sequitur. The technical claim itself is unchanged.

examples.source: Plot these together with your results.
examples.translation: Plot ini bersama dengan hasilmu.
examples.suggested: Plot nilai-nilai ini bersama hasilmu.
examples.why: Without an explicit object, "Plot ini" reads most naturally as the noun phrase "this plot" rather than the intended imperative, momentarily obscuring the instruction.

examples.source: If this course results in your joining the quest, which is full of challenge and fun, we would be more than happy.
examples.translation: Jika kursus ini menghasilkan kamu bergabung dalam pencarian ini, yang penuh tantangan dan kesenangan, kami akan sangat senang.
examples.suggested: Jika kursus ini membuat kamu ikut bergabung dalam pencarian ini, yang penuh tantangan dan keseruan, kami akan sangat senang.
examples.why: "menghasilkan kamu bergabung" is a direct calque of "results in your joining"; no native technical writer would use menghasilkan with a clausal complement here.

examples.source: Heavy-hexagonal graphs should be painted in three colors.
examples.translation: Graf heavy-hexagonal harus diwarnai dengan tiga warna.
examples.suggested: Graf heavy-hexagonal semestinya dapat diwarnai dengan tiga warna.
examples.why: "should" here is an expectation about the result of the coloring algorithm; "harus" states an obligation, slightly strengthening the claim into a prescription. The very next line ("Ya, memang begitu!") confirms the expectation reading.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every quantity and condition survives intact ($N=2$/$N=6$ sites, $N=20$/$N=70$, "medan eksternal membentuk sudut $\alpha$ terhadap arah transversal", "+1 dan -1 masing-masing", the caveat about deeper circuits and error accumulation, the "coba sendiri; gulir ke bawah" activity framing). What a native technical editor would change is wording, not meaning: line 361 renders numerical agreement between simulators with "sepakat" (a human-consensus verb — a calque of "agree"; "sesuai"/"bersesuaian" is the domain wording); line 33 has an English-shaped adverb placement, "jika kamu sudah baru-baru ini meninjau pelajaran 7" instead of "jika kamu baru saja meninjau pelajaran 7"; "commute" is split within the file between "saling komutasi" (l.41) and "berkomutasi" (l.53, l.59); "exponential" is rendered "eksponen" (the exponent, i.e. the power) at l.41/47 where "eksponensial"/"fungsi eksponensial" is meant; and "utility-scale" appears as "skala utility" in the H1 (l.17) but "skala utilitas" in the closing line (l.861). The informal "kamu/kita" register holds throughout, with no deferential bapak/ibu slips.

examples.source: Confirm that the results from statevector and matrix product space simulators agree.
examples.translation: Konfirmasi bahwa hasil dari simulator statevector dan matrix product space sepakat.
examples.suggested: Pastikan bahwa hasil dari simulator statevector dan matrix product state saling bersesuaian.
examples.why: "sepakat" is agreement between people/parties; for two numerical results Indonesian technical prose uses "sesuai"/"bersesuaian"/"cocok". Meaning is still recoverable, so MINOR.

examples.source: Feel free to skip to the code cells below if you have recently reviewed lesson 7.
examples.translation: Silakan lewati ke sel kode di bawah jika kamu sudah baru-baru ini meninjau pelajaran 7.
examples.suggested: Silakan langsung lompat ke sel kode di bawah jika kamu baru saja meninjau pelajaran 7.
examples.why: "sudah baru-baru ini meninjau" mirrors the English present-perfect word order; a native writer says "baru saja meninjau". Also "lewati ke" is an odd pairing ("lewati" = skip over, not skip to).

examples.source: these Pauli terms might commute with one another … When $H_1$ and $H_2$ commute … when operators do not commute
examples.translation: suku-suku Pauli ini mungkin saling komutasi … Ketika $H_1$ dan $H_2$ berkomutasi … ketika operator tidak berkomutasi
examples.suggested: use "saling berkomutasi" (or "komut") consistently in all three places
examples.why: The same core concept is rendered with a noun form ("saling komutasi") once and the verb form ("berkomutasi") twice within a few paragraphs. Recognizable, so MINOR, but a technical editor would unify it.

examples.source: The exponential of an operator can be most easily understood through its Taylor series … Some very basic exponentials, like $e^{iZ}$
examples.translation: Eksponen dari sebuah operator paling mudah dipahami melalui deret Taylornya … Beberapa eksponen yang sangat dasar, seperti $e^{iZ}$
examples.suggested: Eksponensial dari sebuah operator … Beberapa eksponensial yang sangat dasar
examples.why: "eksponen" normally denotes the exponent (the power itself), not the exponential $e^{X}$ of an operator; "eksponensial" is the conventional rendering (used correctly later as "eksponen matriks" would also be better as "eksponensial matriks", l.205).

examples.source: Utility-scale experiment II … your utility-scale quantum journey
examples.translation: Eksperimen skala utility II … perjalanan quantum skala utilitas
examples.suggested: pick one rendering of "utility-scale" (e.g. "skala utilitas") and use it in both the H1 and the closing line
examples.why: The course's own banner concept is named two different ways in the same file — half-English in the title, fully Indonesian at the end. Not misleading, but inconsistent.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — every quantity, condition and caveat survives (depth 5→6 vs two-qubit 9→8 in §3.2, the ">0.5" fidelity criterion, "Eagle device / 40.000 shots", the "Pastikan kamu menjalankan sel berikutnya setelah status job … menjadi 'DONE'" caveat), and the informal "kamu" register holds from top to bottom. Three things a native technical editor would still change: (1) "atau kamu bisa datang dengan ide sendiri" (§4 closing) is a word-for-word calque of "come up with"; Indonesian would say "memunculkan/mencetuskan ide sendiri" — "datang dengan ide" is not idiomatic. (2) The head-noun order for the two central terms flips within the file: "GHZ state" / "GHZ Circuit" (§1.1, §1.2, §2.1) vs "state GHZ 16-Qubit" and "state GHZ yang lebih besar" (§3) and "Circuit GHZ yang lebih baik" (§4) — the concept stays identifiable, but the inconsistency is visible. (3) "state $|0\rangle$ semua dan $|1\rangle$ semua" (§1.1) calques English "all |0⟩'s and all |1⟩'s" with the quantifier postposed; Indonesian puts it in front ("state semua-$|0\rangle$ dan semua-$|1\rangle$"). None of these mislead a learner.

examples.source: You can combine and expand these ideas or you come up with your own ideas to create a better GHZ circuit.
examples.translation: Kamu bisa menggabungkan dan mengembangkan ide-ide ini, atau kamu bisa datang dengan ide sendiri untuk membuat Circuit GHZ yang lebih baik.
examples.suggested: Kamu bisa menggabungkan dan mengembangkan ide-ide ini, atau memunculkan idemu sendiri untuk membuat GHZ Circuit yang lebih baik.
examples.why: "datang dengan ide" is a literal calque of English "come up with"; no Indonesian technical writer would use it. Idiomatic options: memunculkan / mencetuskan / merancang ide sendiri.

examples.source: We try to create a 16-qubit GHZ state as before. / a 30-qubit GHZ state / a better GHZ circuit
examples.translation: Kita akan mencoba membuat state GHZ 16-Qubit seperti sebelumnya. / state GHZ 30-Qubit / Circuit GHZ yang lebih baik
examples.suggested: … membuat GHZ state 16-qubit … / GHZ state 30-qubit … / GHZ Circuit yang lebih baik
examples.why: The file elsewhere consistently uses the kept-English order "GHZ state" (§1.1, §1.2, §1 intro) and "GHZ Circuit" (§1.2, §2.1, §5); §3 and §4 flip to "state GHZ" / "Circuit GHZ". Within-file inconsistency only — the concept stays identifiable.

examples.source: the states of all $|0\rangle$'s and all $|1\rangle$'s do dominate, but the errors are substantial
examples.translation: state $|0\rangle$ semua dan $|1\rangle$ semua memang mendominasi, tapi errornya cukup besar
examples.suggested: state semua-$|0\rangle$ dan semua-$|1\rangle$ memang mendominasi, tapi errornya cukup besar
examples.why: Postposed "semua" copies the English possessive-plural construction; in Indonesian the quantifier precedes the thing quantified, so the current order reads as MT rather than as written Indonesian. Meaning is still recoverable.

editor_note: No misleading content: the whole QAOA/max-cut derivation (QUBO → Hamiltonian biaya, x_i=(1-z_i)/2, "jika $x_i$ bernilai $0$, maka $z_i$ harus bernilai $1$", the dropped 1/4 factor and $n^2$ offset, "nilai potongan dari solusi optimal adalah 5") is faithful, and the informal "kamu"/"kita" register holds throughout. Four things a native technical editor would still change. (1) "variational" is consistently rendered "variatif" ("Algoritma kuantum variatif", "parameter variatif", "bentuk variatif"); in Indonesian "variatif" means "beragam/bervariasi" — the established domain term is "variasional" (metode/prinsip variasional); it is recognizable (and "variational quantum eigensolver (VQE)" is kept in English in §1) so it does not teach a false concept, but it is the wrong convention. (2) "primitive" is split within the file: heading 3.4 says "primitif IBM Quantum" while §"Tentukan Backend dan primitive eksekusi" and its body keep "primitive"; likewise "optimasi" (§1) vs "optimisasi" (§3 onward). (3) "We start with arbitrary chosen parameters" became "parameter yang dipilih secara acak" (randomly chosen) — the values are π and π/2, deliberately arbitrary, not random; "sembarang" is the right word. (4) The Sampler sentence in §3.4 lost its predicate and reads as a fragment.

examples.source: Variational quantum algorithms / a circuit with gates that take variational parameters
examples.translation: Algoritma kuantum variatif / Circuit dengan Gate yang mengambil parameter variatif
examples.suggested: Algoritma kuantum variasional / parameter variasional
examples.why: "Variatif" is everyday Indonesian for "varied/diverse"; the conventional physics term for the variational principle/method is "variasional". Consistent within the file and still recognizable, so MINOR, but it is the wrong domain convention and weakens the link to the variational principle the whole lesson rests on.

examples.source: We start with arbitrary chosen parameters.
examples.translation: Kita mulai dengan parameter yang dipilih secara acak.
examples.suggested: Kita mulai dengan parameter yang dipilih secara sembarang.
examples.why: "Secara acak" says the initial γ, β were generated randomly; the code sets them deterministically to π and π/2, chosen arbitrarily. The same file already uses "nilai parameter acak" for genuinely random values, so the distinction the English draws is lost.

examples.source: Here is where the Sampler primitive should be used since it is the probability distribution of bitstring measurements which correspond to the optimal cut of the graph.
examples.translation: Di sinilah primitive *Sampler* harus digunakan karena distribusi probabilitas pengukuran bitstring yang berkorespondensi dengan potongan optimal dari graf.
examples.suggested: … karena yang kita inginkan adalah distribusi probabilitas pengukuran bitstring, yang berkorespondensi dengan potongan optimal dari graf.
examples.why: The subordinate clause after "karena" has no predicate — dropping "it is" leaves a noun phrase dangling, so the sentence stops mid-thought. A native technical writer would not leave the reason clause unfinished.

examples.source: primitives / optimization
examples.translation: "primitif IBM Quantum" (heading 3.4) vs "primitive eksekusi", "Dua primitive tersebut" (§3.4 body); "masalah optimasi" (§1) vs "masalah optimisasi" (§3)
examples.suggested: Pick one per term: "primitive" throughout (and "optimisasi" throughout, matching the majority usage).
examples.why: Two core terms each rendered two ways inside one page. Both variants are understandable, so the concept stays identifiable, but the inconsistency is the kind of thing a reviewer normalizes.

editor_note: The three rewritten entries are semantically faithful — nothing misleads: the alt text (entry 8) reproduces "key components … heuristic and problem-specific ansaetze" exactly as "komponen kunci dari diskusi ansatz, termasuk ansatz heuristik dan ansatz spesifik-masalah". The two rewritten headings are each defensible but clash with how the rest of the file renders the same terms. "Pembelajaran Mesin Kuantum" (entry 60) is a correct Indonesian rendering, yet the prose directly beneath it and in the Efficient SU2 section keeps "machine learning" untranslated ("Dalam machine learning, aplikasi umum adalah…", "pendekatan machine learning klasik"), and every other H2/H3 in the file keeps its English form ("Parameterized Quantum Circuit", "Variational Form dan Ansatz", "N-local circuit", "Heuristic ansaetze dan trade-off") — so this one fully-Indonesian heading is the odd one out. Likewise "Ansatz spesifik-masalah" (entry 50) uses a hyphenated calque of the English compound, while the body under it writes "pengetahuan spesifik masalah" without the hyphen and the Summary bullet still reads "Problem-specific ansaetze" in English. Both are consistency/style slips only; drop the hyphen and either keep the QML heading in English or translate "machine learning" throughout.

examples.source: Quantum Machine Learning {#quantum-machine-learning}
examples.translation: Pembelajaran Mesin Kuantum {#quantum-machine-learning}
examples.suggested: Quantum Machine Learning — or translate "machine learning" in the body prose too
examples.why: The rendering itself is correct Indonesian, but the paragraph immediately below keeps "machine learning" in English twice, and every other heading in the file keeps its English technical form; the fully-translated heading is inconsistent with both.

examples.source: Problem-specific ansaetze {#problem-specific-ansaetze}
examples.translation: Ansatz spesifik-masalah {#problem-specific-ansaetze}
examples.suggested: Ansatz spesifik masalah (or: Ansatz khusus masalah)
examples.why: The hyphen is a calque of the English compound; Indonesian does not hyphenate a postposed modifier, and the body text three lines later already writes "pengetahuan spesifik masalah" unhyphenated, while the Summary bullet leaves "Problem-specific ansaetze" in English — three renderings of one term.

examples.source: A diagram showing key components of the ansatz discussion, including heuristic ansaetze and problem-specific ansaetze.
examples.translation: Diagram yang menunjukkan komponen kunci dari diskusi ansatz, termasuk ansatz heuristik dan ansatz spesifik-masalah.
examples.why: No defect — listed to record that this rewritten entry was checked: both listed ansatz families and the "key components of the ansatz discussion" framing survive intact, with no added or dropped content.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I found no inverted condition, swapped quantity, softened claim or hallucinated sentence; the delicate passages (sparse vs dense Pauli decomposition, "probabilitas diambil dari keadaan V|ψ⟩ bukan dari |ψ⟩", the max-cut sign flip "alih-alih memaksimalkan C(z) kita akan meminimalkan", the bias/variance trade-off and the Open Plan / error-code-1217 caveat) all survive intact, and the informal "kita/kamu" register is consistent. Three editorial defects remain. (1) One full source paragraph in "Ketelitian matematis (opsional)" is left in English verbatim — "Since we do not know the eigenvalues or eigenstates of the target observable Ĥ, first we need to consider its diagonalization…" — so the Indonesian reader loses the sentence that motivates the whole diagonalization derivation that follows. (2) The core term "observable" is split within the file: "observabel" in the Primitives/Estimator sections (lines 32–92) but bare English "observable" from "Fungsi biaya" onward (lines 359, 510, 555, 723, 751, 870); "sirkuit" likewise appears once (line 844) amid the otherwise uniform "Circuit". (3) Two small prose slips: the relative clause "yang harus kita tambahkan suku konstanta setelahnya" is ungrammatical as written, and "Di kursus berikutnya" states the next course where the English says only "In a later course".

examples.source: Since we do not know the eigenvalues or eigenstates of the target observable $\hat{H}$, first we need to consider its diagonalization. Given that $\hat{H}$ is Hermitian, there exists a unitary transformation $V$ such that $\hat{H}=V^\dagger \Lambda V$…
examples.translation: Since we do not know the eigenvalues or eigenstates of the target observable $\hat{H}$, first we need to consider its diagonalization. Given that $\hat{H}$ is Hermitian, there exists a unitary transformation $V$ such that $\hat{H}=V^\dagger \Lambda V$… (left untranslated)
examples.suggested: Karena kita tidak mengetahui nilai eigen maupun eigenstate dari observabel target $\hat{H}$, pertama-tama kita perlu meninjau diagonalisasinya. Mengingat $\hat{H}$ bersifat Hermitian, terdapat transformasi uniter $V$ sedemikian sehingga $\hat{H}=V^\dagger \Lambda V$, di mana $\Lambda$ adalah matriks diagonal nilai eigen, sehingga $\langle j | \Lambda | k \rangle = 0$ jika $j\neq k$, dan $\langle j | \Lambda | j \rangle = \lambda_j$.
examples.why: A whole source paragraph is still English. It is the bridge sentence that explains WHY the diagonalization $V^\dagger \Lambda V$ is introduced, and the next Indonesian line ('Ini berarti nilai ekspektasi bisa ditulis ulang sebagai:') refers back to it, so an Indonesian-only reader loses the motivation for the derivation that follows.

examples.source: the observable representing energy … the observables that Qiskit admits natively … sinusoidal expectation values of the observable given
examples.translation: observable yang merepresentasikan energi … observable yang diterima Qiskit secara native … nilai ekspektasi sinusoidal dari observable yang diberikan
examples.suggested: observabel yang merepresentasikan energi … observabel yang diterima Qiskit secara native … nilai ekspektasi sinusoidal dari observabel yang diberikan
examples.why: The first half of the file consistently uses the Indonesian form 'observabel' (lines 32, 34, 65, 71, 73, 90, 92); from the 'Fungsi biaya' section onward it switches to bare English 'observable'. The concept stays identifiable, so this is minor, but a native technical editor would pick one form for the whole lesson.

examples.source: to which we will have to add the independent term afterwards:
examples.translation: yang harus kita tambahkan suku konstanta setelahnya:
examples.suggested: yang kemudian harus kita tambahi suku bebas berikut:
examples.why: As written the relative clause has no grammatical subject-object fit ('yang harus kita tambahkan suku konstanta setelahnya' reads as if the operator is being added to the constant term). A native writer would restructure it; the meaning is still recoverable from the formula that follows.

examples.source: In a later course, we will delve into different circuit construction methods to improve results
examples.translation: Di kursus berikutnya, kita akan mendalami berbagai metode konstruksi Circuit untuk meningkatkan hasil
examples.suggested: Di salah satu kursus berikutnya, kita akan mendalami berbagai metode konstruksi Circuit untuk meningkatkan hasil
examples.why: 'kursus berikutnya' promises the immediately next course; the English deliberately says only 'a later course'. A dropped hedge rather than a misstatement, so minor.

editor_note: Meaning is fully faithful — the 20-question / minimum-16-correct pass rule, the automatic badge email to the IBM Training registration address, the two-attempt temporary lock ("terkunci sementara"), the maintenance notice and the entire Credly privacy paragraph all survive with no drift, no dropped caveat and nothing hallucinated; informal "kamu"/"-mu" register is consistent throughout. What an editor would change is purely surface: "klik tombol di bawah untuk navigasi ke IBM Training" is a calque of "to navigate to" ("navigasi" is a noun here — natural Indonesian is "untuk menuju ke" or "untuk membuka"), and the Credly paragraph's "Itu akan ditangani secara konsisten dengan praktik privasi IBM" carries "your personal information" with a bare English-style pronoun "Itu" where Indonesian restates the noun ("Informasi tersebut akan ditangani sesuai dengan praktik privasi IBM"). One formatting slip: the final sentence's period was moved inside the link text — "dapat dilihat [di sini.](…)" — so the rendered hyperlink reads "di sini." with a trailing dot, unlike EN's "[here](…)." None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: click the button below to navigate to IBM® Training, where you can take the badging exam
examples.translation: klik tombol di bawah untuk navigasi ke IBM® Training, di mana kamu bisa mengikuti ujian lencana
examples.suggested: klik tombol di bawah untuk menuju ke IBM® Training, tempat kamu bisa mengikuti ujian lencana
examples.why: "untuk navigasi ke" is a direct calque of "to navigate to"; "navigasi" is a noun, so the phrase reads ungrammatically stiff. A native technical writer would use the verb "menuju"/"membuka".

examples.source: It will be handled in a manner consistent with IBM privacy practices.
examples.translation: Itu akan ditangani secara konsisten dengan praktik privasi IBM.
examples.suggested: Informasi tersebut akan ditangani sesuai dengan praktik privasi IBM.
examples.why: Opening a sentence with a bare "Itu" to carry over "your personal information" is English pronoun syntax; Indonesian restates the noun. "secara konsisten dengan" is also a literal rendering where "sesuai dengan" is the idiomatic phrase.

examples.source: The IBM Privacy Statement can be viewed [here](https://www.ibm.com/privacy/us/en/).
examples.translation: Pernyataan Privasi IBM dapat dilihat [di sini.](https://www.ibm.com/privacy/us/en/)
examples.suggested: Pernyataan Privasi IBM dapat dilihat [di sini](https://www.ibm.com/privacy/us/en/).
examples.why: The sentence-final period was pulled inside the link label, so the rendered hyperlink text is "di sini." with a trailing dot and the sentence ends with an unpunctuated URL — a visible formatting slip versus EN.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I checked the load-bearing reasoning passages line by line and they survive intact: the betas-too-small explanation ("beta terlalu kecil untuk memberi penalti pada eigenstate minimum... ia tidak dikecualikan dari ruang pencarian efektif"), the Step-4 convergence caveat ("gagal konvergen dalam 200 iterasi. Di sini, kita berhasil konvergen... tapi dengan toleransi berapa?"), and the whole final cautionary argument about orthogonality against an inaccurate ground state (§1160-1164) all preserve the English logic, direction and hedging, with no inverted condition, swapped quantity or hallucinated claim. What a native technical editor would still change: (1) the second-person register is split within one file — "Seperti yang bisa Anda lihat" (§205) against "kamu" everywhere else (§301, §364, §885, §1164, §1424); (2) "excited state" is kept in English on every occurrence except the heading "Keadaan Tereksitasi" (§984), and "Qiskit patterns" appears both translated ("framework pola Qiskit", §26) and untranslated ("framework Qiskit patterns", §396); (3) a few calques/odd word choices — "solusinya tersandi dalam distribusi output" (§1329, where "terenkode"/"dikodekan" is the domain-normal verb) and "harus dilewatkan sebagai argumen" (§411, for "must be passed"). None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: As you can see, the result is extremely close to the ideal.
examples.translation: Seperti yang bisa Anda lihat, hasilnya sangat dekat dengan nilai ideal.
examples.suggested: Seperti yang bisa kamu lihat, hasilnya sangat dekat dengan nilai ideal.
examples.why: This is the only "Anda" in the file; every other second-person address uses "kamu" ("Tergantung sistem spesifik kamu", "kamu mungkin bisa mencapai konvergensi lebih cepat", "Lihat apakah kamu bisa menjelaskan", "kamu sudah mempelajari"). Pick one and hold it.

examples.source: ### Excited States
examples.translation: ### Keadaan Tereksitasi {#excited-states}
examples.suggested: ### Excited state {#excited-states}
examples.why: The term is kept in English in every body occurrence ("energi excited state pertama", "ground state dan excited state pertama", "estimasi energi kita untuk excited state"); only this heading is translated, so the section title does not visually match the concept the prose teaches. Concept stays identifiable, so MINOR.

examples.source: Note that the Qiskit patterns framework can be applied to all the problems… / Here we implement the Qiskit patterns framework, explicitly.
examples.translation: Perhatikan bahwa framework pola Qiskit bisa diterapkan… / Di sini kita mengimplementasikan framework Qiskit patterns secara eksplisit.
examples.suggested: Use "framework Qiskit patterns" in both places (it is a product name, not a descriptive phrase).
examples.why: "Qiskit patterns" is a named framework; translating it to "pola Qiskit" in the intro and leaving it in English 370 lines later makes the two sentences look like they refer to different things.

examples.source: for QAOA, the solution is encoded in the output distribution of the ansatz circuit bound with the optimal parameters from the minimization
examples.translation: untuk QAOA, solusinya tersandi dalam distribusi output dari Circuit ansatz yang diikat dengan parameter optimal dari minimasi
examples.suggested: untuk QAOA, solusinya terenkode dalam distribusi keluaran Circuit ansatz yang telah diisi dengan parameter optimal hasil minimasi
examples.why: "tersandi" is a literary/cryptographic word no Indonesian quantum engineer would use for "encoded" here; "terenkode"/"dikodekan" is the conventional technical rendering. "diikat" for "bound (parameters)" is also stiff — "diisi"/"di-assign" reads more naturally.

editor_note: Nothing here misleads: every claim matches the English (badge/exam flow, Credly data-sharing notice, IBM privacy links all intact), and the core term is rendered correctly and consistently as "algoritma variasional". Three editorial slips remain. (1) Second-person register splits inside the file: the Exam section uses formal "Anda" ("Setelah Anda lulus ujian, Anda akan diberitahu"), while the Credly section switches to "kamu/-mu" ("untukmu", "informasi pribadimu", "Kamu akan menerima notifikasi email") — pick one; the file's own convention is "Anda". (2) "some experience with quantum computing" is calqued as "memiliki beberapa pengalaman dengan komputasi kuantum"; "beberapa pengalaman" counts experiences rather than meaning "a certain amount of", so a native writer would say "sudah memiliki sedikit pengalaman di bidang komputasi kuantum". (3) "Itu akan ditangani secara konsisten dengan praktik privasi IBM" uses a bare pronoun subject where Indonesian legal prose would name the referent ("Informasi tersebut akan ditangani sesuai dengan praktik privasi IBM"), and "secara konsisten dengan" is a literal rendering of "in a manner consistent with".

examples.source: After you pass the exam, you will be notified by Credly … / In order to issue you an IBM Digital Badge, your personal information …
examples.translation: Setelah Anda lulus ujian, Anda akan diberitahu oleh Credly … / Agar dapat menerbitkan IBM Digital Badge untukmu, informasi pribadimu … Kamu akan menerima notifikasi email
examples.suggested: Keep "Anda" throughout: "Agar dapat menerbitkan IBM Digital Badge untuk Anda, informasi pribadi Anda … Anda akan menerima notifikasi email"
examples.why: The same reader is addressed formally in one section and informally in the next; within-file register inconsistency, not a meaning change.

examples.source: individuals who have some experience with quantum computing
examples.translation: individu yang memiliki beberapa pengalaman dengan komputasi kuantum
examples.suggested: individu yang sudah memiliki sedikit pengalaman di bidang komputasi kuantum
examples.why: "beberapa pengalaman" reads as "several experiences" (countable) — a calque of English "some"; also "pengalaman dengan" should be "pengalaman di bidang/dalam".

examples.source: It will be handled in a manner consistent with IBM privacy practices.
examples.translation: Itu akan ditangani secara konsisten dengan praktik privasi IBM.
examples.suggested: Informasi tersebut akan ditangani sesuai dengan praktik privasi IBM.
examples.why: Bare "Itu" as sentence subject is un-idiomatic in Indonesian formal/legal prose, and "secara konsisten dengan" is a word-for-word rendering of "in a manner consistent with".

editor_note: The three rewritten section headings are semantically exact and idiomatic Indonesian noun-phrase order with the acronym preserved: "Eigensolver Kuantum Variasional (VQE)", "Pencarian Subruang VQE (SSVQE)" and "Deflasi Kuantum Variasional (VQD)" — "variational" correctly renders as "variasional" (not, say, "permutasional"), "subspace search" as "pencarian subruang" matching the body's "subruang yang bersesuaian" in the VQD section, and "deflation" as "deflasi"; keeping the English paper titles in the arXiv bullet list at the top while translating the headings is a defensible convention since the VQE/SSVQE/VQD acronyms anchor identity in both places.

This page is a bare index (title + "Kursus"/"Modul" headings + 16 link labels); there is no running prose, so no semantic drift, dropped caveat or hallucination is possible, and none is present. All fourteen course titles map one-to-one onto the English and the domain terms are correct and conventional: "Variational Algorithm Design" → "Desain Algoritma Variasional" (not the false-concept "permutasional"), "Quantum Diagonalization Algorithms" → "Algoritma Diagonalisasi Kuantum", "Utility Scale Quantum Computing" → "Komputasi Kuantum Skala Utilitas", "Quantum Chem With Vqe" → "Kimia Kuantum dengan VQE" (VQE kept, correctly, in English). The single editorial slip is the HPC course: "Integrating Quantum And High Performance Computing" → "Mengintegrasikan Komputasi Kuantum dan Kinerja Tinggi", which relies on a shared head noun ("Komputasi [Kuantum dan Kinerja Tinggi]") that most Indonesian readers will not recover, because "Komputasi Kuantum" is a heavily lexicalised collocation — the tail then reads as a dangling "and high performance". Repeating the head ("…Komputasi Kuantum dan Komputasi Kinerja Tinggi") removes the ambiguity; it is a clarity slip in a link label, not a misleading claim. Register is not at issue (no second-person prose on the page).

examples.source: [Integrating Quantum And High Performance Computing](/learning/courses/integrating-quantum-and-high-performance-computing)
examples.translation: [Mengintegrasikan Komputasi Kuantum dan Kinerja Tinggi](/learning/courses/integrating-quantum-and-high-performance-computing)
examples.suggested: [Mengintegrasikan Komputasi Kuantum dan Komputasi Kinerja Tinggi](/learning/courses/integrating-quantum-and-high-performance-computing)
examples.why: The rendering coordinates two modifiers under one head noun ("Komputasi"), but "Komputasi Kuantum" is such an entrenched unit in Indonesian that the phrase is naturally parsed as "quantum computing and high performance", leaving "Kinerja Tinggi" dangling instead of reading as HPC ("Komputasi Kinerja Tinggi"). Repeating the head noun makes the two-field pairing explicit. Clarity only — the link target and course scope are still recoverable, so it does not mislead.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I checked the quantitative and logic-bearing passages line by line (N/2 vs π√N/4 queries, the ψ0→ψ5 two-qubit walkthrough including "Z_OR membalik tanda pada semua state kecuali |00⟩", the odd/even parity argument "mengembalikan true ketika jumlah *ganjil* … kita ingin jumlah *genap* (khususnya dua)", t ≈ (π/4)√(N/|A₁|) − 1/2, the over-rotation caveat, and the 20-qubit "hanya sekitar 10% kemungkinan" answer) and found no inverted condition, swapped quantity or hallucinated claim. The defects are editorial: one full prose paragraph is left untranslated in English (line 111, the "Grover operator" caption after the circuit diagram); several English calques survive — "Tetapi pengambilan nyata adalah tekniknya" for "the real takeaway" (line 898, near-nonsensical in Indonesian; should be "inti pelajarannya"), "mari kita berjalan melalui" for "work through" (lines 165, 289), "Perlakuan singkat" for "A condensed treatment" (line 101), "tampak melingkar" for "seems circular" (line 281), "membiarkan yang lainnya sendiri" for "leaves everything else alone" (line 234); terminology splits within the file: kueri/mengkueri in the Theory section vs query later ("model query", "jumlah query", lines 587/905/913) and subrutin (line 66) vs subroutine (lines 281, 908); and line 45 adds an intensifier, "yang sangat signifikan untuk dataset besar" where the English is plain "which is significant". Register is consistently informal kamu/kita, no bapak/ibu slips.

examples.source: Often, the marking gate $Z_f$ and the diffusion layers consisting of $H$, $Z_{\text{OR}}$, and $H$ are collectively referred to as the "Grover operator". In this diagram, only a single repetition of the Grover operator is shown.
examples.translation: Often, the marking gate $Z_f$ and the diffusion layers consisting of $H$, $Z_{\text{OR}}$, and $H$ are collectively referred to as the "Grover operator". In this diagram, only a single repetition of the Grover operator is shown.
examples.suggested: Sering kali, gate penanda $Z_f$ dan lapisan difusi yang terdiri dari $H$, $Z_{\text{OR}}$, dan $H$ secara kolektif disebut "operator Grover". Dalam diagram ini, hanya satu pengulangan operator Grover yang ditampilkan.
examples.why: An entire body paragraph — the one that first defines the term "operator Grover" used for the rest of the module — is left in English. It does not mislead, but an Indonesian reader loses the definition of the central term at the point it is introduced.

examples.source: But the real takeaway is the technique: encoding problem constraints into a quantum oracle is a powerful pattern…
examples.translation: Tetapi pengambilan nyata adalah tekniknya: mengkodekan batasan masalah ke dalam oracle kuantum adalah pola yang kuat…
examples.suggested: Tetapi inti pelajarannya adalah tekniknya: mengkodekan batasan masalah ke dalam oracle kuantum adalah pola yang ampuh…
examples.why: "pengambilan nyata" is a word-for-word calque of "takeaway" and means "the real act of taking" in Indonesian; the closing sentence of the whole module reads as raw MT where it should carry the module's punchline.

examples.source: …requires a number of queries that is linear in $N$ … a number of queries that scales like $\sqrt{N}$.
examples.translation: …membutuhkan jumlah kueri yang linier terhadap $N$ … (later) algoritma Grover membutuhkan jumlah query yang berskala seperti $\sqrt{N}.$
examples.suggested: Pick one: use "kueri" throughout (…jumlah kueri yang berskala seperti $\sqrt{N}$; "model kueri") or keep "query" throughout.
examples.why: The file's single most important countable quantity is called kueri in Theory and query in the summary/T-F questions (lines 587, 905, 908, 913); same split for subrutin (line 66) vs subroutine (lines 281, 908). Concept stays identifiable, so MINOR, but a reader comparing the summary to the derivation sees two different words.

examples.source: …and the operator acts on each accordingly — which is exactly a reflection about $|v\rangle$.
examples.translation: …dan operator bertindak pada masing-masing sesuai — yang merupakan refleksi tentang $|v\rangle$ persis.
examples.suggested: …dan operator bekerja pada masing-masing komponen tersebut — yang persis merupakan refleksi terhadap $|v\rangle$.
examples.why: "sesuai" is left dangling without its object, "refleksi tentang" contradicts the "refleksi terhadap" used everywhere else in the same section, and "persis" is stranded sentence-finally in English word order.

examples.source: This represents a *quadratic speedup* over classical methods, which is significant for large datasets.
examples.translation: Ini merupakan *percepatan kuadratik* dibandingkan metode klasik, yang sangat signifikan untuk dataset besar.
examples.suggested: …yang signifikan untuk dataset besar.
examples.why: "sangat" strengthens a plain claim; harmless here but the module elsewhere is careful to keep the quadratic-vs-exponential speedup un-oversold, so the added intensifier works against that emphasis.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat; the Open Plan sentence, the simulator fallback caveat and the two background bullets all track the English, and the informal register ("bisa", "kalau-kalau", no deferential bapak/ibu) is consistent. Two things a native technical editor would change. (1) In the instructor paragraph the demonstrative "ini" dangles at the very end of the sentence ("mengisi [survei singkat] tentang cara notebook digunakan ini"), where it appears to modify "cara notebook digunakan" instead of the survey; it belongs right after the link ("mengisi [survei singkat] ini tentang bagaimana notebook digunakan"). (2) "Some linear algebra background" is calqued as "Beberapa latar belakang aljabar linear" — "beberapa" quantifies countable items and reads wrong with an uncountable "latar belakang"; the very next bullet correctly uses "Sedikit" for the same English "Some", so the file is also internally inconsistent on that quantifier.

examples.source: by filling out this [quick survey](...) on how the notebooks are being used.
examples.translation: dengan mengisi [survei singkat](...) tentang cara notebook digunakan ini.
examples.suggested: dengan mengisi [survei singkat](...) ini tentang bagaimana notebook digunakan.
examples.why: The stranded sentence-final "ini" attaches to "cara notebook digunakan" rather than to the survey; Indonesian puts the demonstrative directly after the noun it modifies. Also "versi notebook" drops the "these" of "these notebooks" ("versi notebook ini").

examples.source: Some linear algebra background ( $2 \times 2$ matrices should be sufficient)
examples.translation: Beberapa latar belakang aljabar linear (matriks $2 \times 2$ sudah cukup)
examples.suggested: Sedikit latar belakang aljabar linear (matriks $2 \times 2$ sudah cukup)
examples.why: "Beberapa" is a countable-plural quantifier and is a direct calque of English "some" here; with the uncountable "latar belakang" a native writer uses "sedikit" or "dasar-dasar". The next bullet already renders the same English "Some" as "Sedikit", so the two parallel bullets are inconsistent.

editor_note: Entry 76 ("Superposisi keadaan komputasi apa yang akan menghasilkan QFT dengan puncak pada setiap bilangan biner ganjil?") is faithful and idiomatic: "menghasilkan" for "would correspond to" is the natural Indonesian phrasing for this prompt and matches the accompanying answer ("Jika kamu mengambil QFT dari state $\psi = |0\rangle - |N/2\rangle$, maka kamu akan melihat puncak pada setiap state bernomor biner ganjil"), "puncak" is consistent with the earlier frequency-spectrum passages, "bilangan biner ganjil" correctly renders "odd binary number", and the parallel question above it ("keadaan basis genap") keeps the even/odd contrast intact.

Meaning is faithful throughout — the CNOT control/target and little-endian conventions, the four-outcome table with its X/Z corrections, the "~95% |0⟩ means success" reading of the histogram, and the no-faster-than-light argument all land exactly as in the English, and the informal "kamu/-mu" register holds everywhere. The defects are consistency and calque, not accuracy. Two core terms split mid-file: "entanglement" is "keterikatan/terikat" through the theory and both experiments but becomes "keterjeratan/terjerat" in the "Konsep kritis" and quiz sections, and "state" is "keadaan" up to Experiment 1 Step 4 then switches to the English "state" for the rest of the page ("keadaan rahasia" → "state rahasia" for the same object). Separately, "we expect to encounter some errors" and "the more errors you can expect" are both rendered with "berharap/harapkan" ("hope"), and several English idioms are calqued literally ("By all means" → "Dengan segala cara", "solid-state qubits" → "qubit keadaan padat", "heads twice in a row" → "kepala dua kali berturut-turut"); the hedge "Arguably" is dropped at the top of Experiment 2.

examples.source: Another key feature is that quantum bits can be "entangled" … / Qubits can be entangled … / Entanglement differs from classical correlations
examples.translation: bit kuantum bisa "terikat satu sama lain" (entangled) … Keterikatan qubit seperti ini … / Qubit dapat terjerat … Keterjeratan berbeda dari korelasi klasik
examples.suggested: Pick one convention for the whole file — either keterikatan/terikat or keterjeratan/terjerat — and use it in the Konsep kritis and quiz sections too.
examples.why: The single core concept of the module is named two different ways, with the split falling exactly on the summary/quiz sections a learner reviews last; still recognizable, so MINOR.

examples.source: quantum states denoted |0⟩ and |1⟩ … The secret state is prepared on qubit Q … states … are all consistent with successful teleportation
examples.translation: keadaan kuantum yang dilambangkan … Keadaan rahasia dipersiapkan pada qubit Q … State $|000\rangle,$ … konsisten dengan teleportasi yang berhasil
examples.suggested: Keep "keadaan" (already used for the first two thirds) throughout, or keep English "state" throughout — not both for the same object.
examples.why: "keadaan rahasia" and "state rahasia" denote the same thing in the same document; the switch happens mid-page without explanation.

examples.source: keep in mind as a caveat that we expect to encounter some errors when we move quantum information around a lot / the more errors and noise you can expect
examples.translation: kita berharap mengalami beberapa kesalahan ketika memindahkan informasi kuantum ke mana-mana / semakin banyak error dan noise yang bisa kamu harapkan
examples.suggested: kita perkirakan akan muncul sejumlah galat … / semakin banyak error dan noise yang harus kamu perkirakan
examples.why: "berharap/harapkan" means *hope for*, not *expect*; the sentence reads as wanting errors. Meaning is still recoverable from context, so MINOR, but it is a wrong sense of the verb.

examples.source: By all means, keep questioning and probing scientific rules, but unfortunately this won't allow us to send information faster than light
examples.translation: Dengan segala cara, teruslah mempertanyakan dan menyelidiki aturan ilmiah, tapi sayangnya ini tidak akan memungkinkan kita mengirim informasi lebih cepat dari cahaya
examples.suggested: Silakan saja, teruslah mempertanyakan dan menguji aturan-aturan ilmiah, …
examples.why: "Dengan segala cara" is a word-for-word calque of "by all means" and reads as "by any means necessary" in Indonesian — a native technical writer would never open the sentence this way.

examples.source: Arguably, the most interesting part of quantum teleportation is that a quantum state can be teleported over long distances instantly
examples.translation: Yang paling menarik dari teleportasi kuantum adalah bahwa state kuantum dapat diteleportasikan jarak jauh secara instan
examples.suggested: Bisa dibilang, bagian paling menarik dari teleportasi kuantum adalah …
examples.why: The author's hedge is dropped, turning an explicitly arguable opinion into a flat assertion; a dropped qualifier, not a technical caveat.

examples.source: Adds a "phase" to a state (a prefactor, which in the cases of the Z eigenstates |0⟩ and |1⟩ either a 1, or -1, respectively)
examples.translation: Menambahkan "fase" ke suatu keadaan (faktor prefaktor, yang dalam kasus eigenstate Z $|0\rangle$ dan $|1\rangle$ berupa 1, atau -1, masing-masing)
examples.suggested: (sebuah prefaktor, yang untuk eigenstate Z $|0\rangle$ dan $|1\rangle$ masing-masing bernilai 1 dan -1)
examples.why: "faktor prefaktor" is a redundant doubling; "prefaktor" alone is the term, and the trailing "masing-masing" placement is stiff.

editor_note: The judged delta entry (heading "4. Post-process" → "4. Pascaproses") is faithful and uses the correct KBBI-conformant bound-prefix spelling "pascaproses"; it matches the step-4 body text below it, which keeps the English term "post-processing" in quotes exactly as the source does, and the surrounding prose (orde/pencarian orde, estimasi fase, qubit kontrol) reads naturally with the informal "kamu" register.

examples.source: 4. Post-process {#4-post-process}
examples.translation: 4. Pascaproses {#4-post-process}
examples.why: Correct and idiomatic: 'pasca-' is a bound prefix written solid in Indonesian (cf. pascasarjana, pascapanen), so 'Pascaproses' is the right rendering of 'Post-process'; the anchor is untouched and the following section keeps the quoted English term "post-processing" just as the English does.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I checked every quantitative and conditional claim (variational bound "selalu sama dengan atau lebih tinggi dari energi ground state ($E_0$)", "karena qubit dapat dibedakan", 5000 state acak, 0.735 Å, -0,5 Hartree, "batas atas terhadap energi ground state yang sebenarnya", ansatz 2 near the poles vs ansatz 3 uniform) and found no drift, no dropped caveat and no hallucinated sentence. What a native technical editor would still change is vocabulary and consistency: "occupation (of a spin-orbital)" is rendered "hunian" (line 229), which in Indonesian means residence/housing, not physical occupancy (keterisian/okupansi); "intractable" appears twice as two different non-idiomatic renderings — "tidak dapat diatasi" (line 86) and "tidak traktabel" (line 1157); and "established wave mechanics" becomes "ia menegakkan mekanika gelombang" (line 53), where "menegakkan" means uphold/enforce. Several terms also split within the file: "Cek pemahamanmu" (lines 92/191/249) vs "Periksa pemahamanmu" (727/871); "basis set" vs "kumpulan basis" (734); "fungsi gelombang trial" vs "fungsi gelombang percobaan" (389); "optimasi" vs "optimisasi" (appendix/conclusion); "inti" vs the Latinate "nuklei" (881/885). Finally two small register/word-order slips: "hidrogen atom ($H$)" instead of "atom hidrogen" (1039) and the untranslated English adjective in "algoritma kuantum near-term yang powerful" (1043). Informal "kamu" register is held consistently; none of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: it maps the occupation of one spin-orbital to the occupation of one qubit
examples.translation: ia memetakan hunian satu spin-orbital ke hunian satu qubit
examples.suggested: ia memetakan keterisian (okupansi) satu spin-orbital ke keterisian satu qubit
examples.why: "hunian" is the everyday word for housing/residence; Indonesian physics texts use "keterisian" or "okupansi" for orbital occupation. Recognizable from context, so MINOR, but a native writer would not choose it — and it recurs later in the same paragraph as "hunian spin".

examples.source: the theoretically "exact" but intractable full molecular orbitals / The optimization process becomes intractable
examples.translation: orbital molekul penuh yang secara teoritis "eksak" namun tidak dapat diatasi / Proses optimisasi menjadi tidak traktabel
examples.suggested: … namun tidak terselesaikan secara komputasi / Proses optimisasi menjadi tak tertangani (intractable)
examples.why: The same source term gets two renderings, one of which ("tidak dapat diatasi" = cannot be overcome) misses the computational sense and the other ("traktabel") is a non-word borrowing. Neither teaches a false concept, but both read as MT.

examples.source: fundamentally, he established wave mechanics by developing the famous time-dependent Schrödinger equation
examples.translation: secara fundamental, ia menegakkan mekanika gelombang dengan mengembangkan persamaan Schrödinger terkenal yang bergantung waktu
examples.suggested: secara fundamental, ia meletakkan dasar mekanika gelombang dengan mengembangkan persamaan Schrödinger bergantung waktu yang terkenal
examples.why: "menegakkan" means to uphold or enforce (used of law/justice), not to found a field. Also "persamaan Schrödinger terkenal yang bergantung waktu" attaches "terkenal" awkwardly mid-phrase; the modifier order is calqued from English.

examples.source: Check your understanding / trial wave function
examples.translation: "Cek pemahamanmu" (92, 191, 249) vs "Periksa pemahamanmu" (727, 871); "fungsi gelombang trial" (93) vs "fungsi gelombang percobaan" (389)
examples.suggested: Pick one per term: "Cek pemahamanmu" for every section heading, "fungsi gelombang trial" throughout (matching the $\Psi_\text{trial}$ notation)
examples.why: The same recurring heading and the same core term are rendered two ways within one file. The concept stays identifiable, so MINOR, but the split is visible in the sidebar/TOC and in the ansatz discussion where $\Psi_\text{trial}$ is referenced by name.

examples.source: VQE is a powerful near-term quantum algorithm … ground state energies for atomic hydrogen ($H$)
examples.translation: VQE adalah algoritma kuantum near-term yang powerful … energi ground state untuk hidrogen atom ($H$)
examples.suggested: VQE adalah algoritma kuantum near-term yang ampuh … energi ground state untuk atom hidrogen ($H$)
examples.why: "powerful" is left as an English adjective inside Indonesian prose (unlike the kept technical nouns, an ordinary adjective has a natural equivalent), and "hidrogen atom" reverses Indonesian head-modifier order — the correct "atom hidrogen" is used everywhere else in the file.

editor_note: Two-link index page rendered faithfully and idiomatically: title "Modules" → "Modul", and the link labels use the standard Indonesian domain terms "Ilmu Komputer" and "Mekanika Kuantum" with URLs and the #modules anchor intact; nothing a native technical editor would change.

Both rewritten entries are semantically faithful — no drift, no hallucination. Entry 26 (Born's Option 2) keeps every load-bearing element: "bukan sekadar tidak diketahui, tetapi tidak terdefinisi secara fisik" for "not merely unknown, but ill-defined physically", the collapse of "ruang semua kemungkinan" onto a single determined state, the electron's projection "tepat berlawanan dengan spin positron", and the "aksi seram dari jarak jauh" / "fisika non-lokal" contrast. Entry 26 registers correctly against Option 1 above it ("Pilihan 2" matching "Pilihan 1", informal "kamu" register maintained). Entry 29 is exact, including the "butuh waktu beberapa dekade bagi manusia" concession. The single editorial change a native technical writer would make is the correlative in "baik sepanjang sumbu +z atau -z": Indonesian "baik…" pairs with "maupun" (both/and); the English "either…or" here needs "entah sepanjang sumbu +z atau -z" (or simply "sepanjang sumbu +z atau -z"). It does not mislead — the physics reads correctly either way.

examples.source: Measuring the positron spin “collapses” the space of all possibilities down to a single determined state, either along the +z or -z axes.
examples.translation: Mengukur spin positron "meruntuhkan" ruang semua kemungkinan menjadi satu keadaan yang ditentukan, baik sepanjang sumbu +z atau -z.
examples.suggested: Mengukur spin positron "meruntuhkan" ruang semua kemungkinan menjadi satu keadaan yang ditentukan, entah sepanjang sumbu +z atau -z.
examples.why: Correlative mismatch: Indonesian "baik…" takes "maupun" (both/and); the exclusive "either…or" of the English is carried by "entah … atau". Grammar nit only — the meaning (one of the two, not both) still comes through from context, so it does not mislead.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I found no semantic drift or hallucination: the CNOT control/target ordering ("qubit $A$ (qubit paling kanan) adalah kontrol"), the double-CNOT sum explanation ("keadaan $S$ akan dibalik dua kali, membawanya kembali ke keadaan $\vert 0\rangle$"), the little-endian answer, the measurement-collapse probability ($\vert c_i\vert^2$) and the deliberately-false True/False items (#2 independence, #4 leftmost $q_0$, #8 $2N$) are all correctly preserved, and the informal "kamu" register holds everywhere. What a native editor would change is consistency and a few calques. The recurring heading "Check your understanding" is rendered three different ways in one file — "Cek pemahamanmu" (l.69, 462, 575, 734), "Periksa pemahamanmu" (l.157, 220, 246, 282) and "Uji pemahamanmu" (l.417); the entanglement concept appears as "entanglement" (l.202), "terjerat" (l.774) and "Keterikatan" (l.794); and the Qiskit-patterns step named "Pemetaan" at l.548/559 becomes the noun "Peta" ("a map") in the summary list at l.784, where a verbal "Petakan"/"Pemetaan" is needed. Two sentences read as English syntax carried over: "Ini bertentangan dengan gate klasik…" (l.390, "bertentangan" = contradicts, not "stands in contrast to") with its trailing "diberikan output, kamu tidak dapat menentukan input secara unik", and "menulis ulang Gate dalam hal set Gate native-nya sendiri" (l.628, calqued "in terms of").

examples.source: ### Check your understanding
examples.translation: "Cek pemahamanmu" (l.69, 462, 575, 734) / "Periksa pemahamanmu" (l.157, 220, 246, 282) / "Uji pemahamanmu" (l.417)
examples.suggested: Pick one form and use it for all eight occurrences, e.g. "Cek pemahamanmu".
examples.why: The same recurring section heading is rendered three ways in one page; a learner scanning for the exercise blocks loses the visual anchor the English keeps constant.

examples.source: we use the four steps in the **Qiskit patterns** workflow: **Map**, **Optimize**, **Execute**, **Post-process**.
examples.translation: kita menggunakan empat langkah dalam alur kerja **Qiskit patterns**: **Peta**, **Optimasi**, **Eksekusi**, **Pasca-proses**.
examples.suggested: …: **Pemetaan**, **Optimasi**, **Eksekusi**, **Pasca-pemrosesan**.
examples.why: "Peta" is the concrete noun "a map/chart", not the process step; the body text already uses "Pemetaan" (l.548, 559) and "Pasca-pemrosesan" (l.554, 715), so the summary contradicts the section it summarizes.

examples.source: entanglement … entangled … Entanglement means the state of one qubit is independent…
examples.translation: "entanglement" (l.202), "terjerat" (l.774), "Keterikatan" (l.794)
examples.suggested: Keep one convention, e.g. "keterjeratan" for the noun and "terjerat" for the adjective, throughout (including the True/False item).
examples.why: Three renderings of the single core concept within one file; the quiz item in particular uses a term ("Keterikatan") that appears nowhere in the teaching sections, so the student may not connect it to what was taught.

examples.source: This stands in contrast to the classical gates we saw above such as AND or OR, which lose information and are irreversible — given an output, you cannot uniquely determine the input.
examples.translation: Ini bertentangan dengan gate klasik yang kita lihat di atas seperti AND atau OR, yang kehilangan informasi dan tidak dapat dibalik — diberikan output, kamu tidak dapat menentukan input secara unik.
examples.suggested: Ini berbeda dengan gate klasik yang kita lihat di atas seperti AND atau OR, yang membuang informasi dan tidak dapat dibalik — jika hanya output-nya yang diketahui, kamu tidak bisa menentukan input-nya secara unik.
examples.why: "bertentangan" means "contradicts", not "contrasts with", and the absolute-construction "diberikan output" is a literal calque of "given an output" that no Indonesian technical writer would use.

examples.source: rewrites the gates in terms of its own native set of gates that have been optimized to run on the quantum computer
examples.translation: menulis ulang Gate dalam hal set Gate native-nya sendiri yang telah dioptimalkan untuk dijalankan pada komputer kuantum
examples.suggested: menulis ulang gate menjadi set gate native milik prosesor itu sendiri, yang telah dioptimalkan untuk dijalankan pada komputer kuantum
examples.why: "dalam hal" is a word-for-word calque of "in terms of" and reads as machine output; "menjadi" carries the actual rewriting sense.

examples.source: produces opposite outcomes every time
examples.translation: menghasilkan hasil yang berlawanan setiap saat
examples.suggested: selalu menghasilkan keluaran yang berlawanan
examples.why: "menghasilkan hasil" is a stem repetition a native editor would remove, and "setiap saat" reads as "at all times" rather than "every time (you measure)".

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every claim (Open Plan free time, simulator fallback, instructor answer-key survey, 2x2 linear algebra prerequisite) matches the English, and the informal register ("bisa", "tapi", "kalau-kalau", no bapak/ibu) holds throughout. Three editorial slips remain. (1) Line 15 strands the demonstrative at the end of the clause — "mengisi [survei singkat] tentang cara notebook digunakan ini" — where "ini" belongs on the survey ("survei singkat ini"), so it reads as if it modifies "cara notebook digunakan"; "versi notebook" also drops "these". (2) The first bullet calques English "Some" as the countable "Beberapa latar belakang aljabar linear" instead of "Sedikit"/"Dasar", and is inconsistent with the very next bullet, which correctly uses "Sedikit". (3) "keakraban dengan Python" is a literal rendering of "familiarity" that a native technical writer would replace with "pengalaman"/"sudah kenal Python"; relatedly "Kumpulan modul dalam kelas Qiskit ini" reads as "modules in the Qiskit class" rather than as the "Qiskit in classrooms" program name.

examples.source: by filling out this [quick survey](...) on how the notebooks are being used
examples.translation: dengan mengisi [survei singkat](...) tentang cara notebook digunakan ini
examples.suggested: dengan mengisi [survei singkat](...) ini tentang bagaimana notebook digunakan
examples.why: The demonstrative "ini" is stranded at the end of the sentence, where it attaches to "cara notebook digunakan" instead of to the survey; a native writer places it directly after the noun it points at.

examples.source: Some linear algebra background ( $2 \times 2$ matrices should be sufficient)
examples.translation: Beberapa latar belakang aljabar linear (matriks $2 \times 2$ sudah cukup)
examples.suggested: Sedikit latar belakang aljabar linear (matriks $2 \times 2$ sudah cukup)
examples.why: "Beberapa" is the countable "several", a calque of English mass-quantifier "Some"; it is also inconsistent with the next bullet, which correctly renders the same "Some" as "Sedikit".

examples.source: Some Python familiarity, though most notebooks can simply be run as written
examples.translation: Sedikit keakraban dengan Python, meskipun sebagian besar notebook bisa langsung dijalankan seperti apa adanya
examples.suggested: Sedikit pengalaman dengan Python, meskipun sebagian besar notebook bisa langsung dijalankan apa adanya
examples.why: "keakraban dengan Python" is a literal mapping of "familiarity" that reads as translationese in Indonesian technical prose; "pengalaman"/"sudah kenal" is the idiomatic choice, and "seperti apa adanya" doubles the adverb.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I checked every quantitative and conditional claim (50/50 vs 100% along X, "tidak lagi sama dengan koefisiennya… kuadrat dari koefisien", ⟨X⟩=1 so "**tidak** ada probabilitas 50-50", the 0/−1/0 triple for X/Y/Z, "selalu $|+\rangle$ dan tidak pernah $|-\rangle$", global phase $-\phi_1$ so $c_1$ murni real) and found no drift, inversion or hallucination; the last 40% (√NOT thought experiment, Bloch vector, conclusion) is accurate, and "in the eye of the beholder" → "hanya bergantung pada sudut pandang pengamat" is a genuinely good idiomatic call. What a native technical editor would still change: (1) "equal superposition" is rendered two ways — "superposisi yang sama" (§Koin kuantum, twice) and "superposisi setara" (§Fase kuantum, §analogi koin) — where "superposisi setara/seimbang" is the better convention and "yang sama" is ambiguously readable as "the same superposition"; (2) "observable" is kept English in §nilai ekspektasi but Indonesianized as "observabel" later in the same file; (3) "Bell's Inequality module" → "modul Ketidaksetaraan Bell", which is the social-inequity sense — the field says "Ketaksamaan Bell" / "Pertidaksamaan Bell"; (4) "squashing it with your hand" → "menepuk" (patting/clapping) twice, which weakens the press-it-flat image the measurement analogy depends on. None of these would cause a learner to form a false belief.

examples.source: This puts it in an equal superposition of $|0\rangle$ and $|1\rangle$.
examples.translation: Ini menempatkannya dalam superposisi yang sama antara $|0\rangle$ dan $|1\rangle$.
examples.suggested: Ini menempatkannya dalam superposisi setara antara $|0\rangle$ dan $|1\rangle$.
examples.why: "superposisi yang sama" can be parsed as "the same superposition" rather than "an equal superposition"; the file itself uses the clearer "superposisi setara" later (H|1⟩ paragraph and the Bloch-analogy paragraph), so the split is internal inconsistency on a core concept.

examples.source: …how the quantum phenomenon of entanglement can help us elucidate this, in the Bell's Inequality module.
examples.translation: …bagaimana fenomena kuantum berupa keterikatan (entanglement) dapat membantu kita menjelaskan hal ini, di modul Ketidaksetaraan Bell.
examples.suggested: …di modul Ketaksamaan Bell.
examples.why: "Ketidaksetaraan" is the socio-economic sense of "inequality"; the mathematical/physics term is "ketaksamaan" or "pertidaksamaan". A learner searching for the concept in Indonesian sources would be pointed at the wrong word, though the English name is recoverable from context.

examples.source: …collapsing the coin along the measurement axis (by squashing it with your hand so that it's lying flat)
examples.translation: …runtuhkan koin sepanjang sumbu pengukuran (dengan menepuk koin dengan tanganmu sehingga tergeletak datar)
examples.suggested: …dengan menekan/memipihkan koin dengan tanganmu sehingga tergeletak datar
examples.why: "menepuk" means to pat or clap, not to press flat; the whole measurement analogy rests on the image of forcing the edge-standing coin down onto a face, and the weaker verb flattens that intuition. Same verb recurs in the Kesimpulan paragraph.

examples.source: …the so-called *expectation value* of an *observable* of the state. / …check the expectation value of the three observables, X, Y, and Z.
examples.translation: …*nilai ekspektasi* dari sebuah *observable* pada keadaan tersebut. / …nilai ekspektasi dari tiga observabel: X, Y, dan Z.
examples.suggested: Pick one: keep "observable" in both places, or use "observabel" in both.
examples.why: The same core term is kept in English in the first, definitional occurrence and Indonesianized in the second; a reader meeting "observabel" for the first time in the √NOT section has to reconnect it to the term that was introduced and italicized earlier.

examples.source: The state of a single, isolated qubit can be visualized as a point on the so-called "Bloch sphere,"
examples.translation: Keadaan satu qubit terisolasi bisa divisualisasikan sebagai sebuah titik di atas yang disebut "bola Bloch,"
examples.suggested: …sebagai sebuah titik pada apa yang disebut "bola Bloch,"
examples.why: "di atas yang disebut" is a word-for-word calque of "on the so-called" and reads broken in Indonesian — the noun the preposition governs is missing. This is in the Konsep kritis summary list, the part students reread.

examples.source: 2. The Bloch sphere describes a qubit's: (select all that apply)
examples.translation: 2. Bola Bloch menggambarkan: (pilih semua yang berlaku)
examples.suggested: 2. Bola Bloch menggambarkan hal-hal berikut dari sebuah qubit: (pilih semua yang berlaku)
examples.why: The possessive "a qubit's" is dropped, so the stem no longer states what the listed properties belong to; option (b) "keterikatan (entanglement) dengan qubit lain" only partly restores it. A dropped qualifier in a quiz stem, not a wrong claim.

editor_note: No semantic drift and no hallucination: the counterfactual in "Ini adalah Circuit yang akan kita gunakan seandainya kita tidak menggunakan jumlah langkah Trotter yang banyak untuk Circuit target", the comparative claim "state tersebut sebenarnya memiliki error Trotter yang lebih kecil dibanding Circuit pembanding", and the stopping-point paragraph ("error Trotter yang lebih kecil _dan_ kedalaman yang lebih rendah") all track the English exactly; terminology (fidelitas, ansatz, observable, state, error Trotter, kedalaman, men-transpile) is correct and consistent, and the "kita" register holds throughout. Two nuance flattenings a native technical editor would still fix: "we might as well use a generous number of layers" becomes the merely permissive "jadi kita bisa menggunakan jumlah layer yang lebih banyak", which loses the pedagogical point that layers are essentially free here (and leaves "lebih banyak" comparative with no referent), and the same idea is rendered later as "jumlah langkah Trotter yang banyak" — a small within-file inconsistency for "generous". Also "it is desirable to use as few Trotter layers as possible" is strengthened to "disarankan" (it is recommended). Neither would mislead a learner about the physics or the workflow.

examples.source: Because this is being simulated by a tensor-network simulator, the number of layers affects execution time only by a constant factor, so we might as well use a generous number of layers to minimize Trotter error.
examples.translation: Karena ini disimulasikan oleh simulator tensor-network, jumlah layer hanya mempengaruhi waktu eksekusi dengan faktor konstan, jadi kita bisa menggunakan jumlah layer yang lebih banyak untuk meminimalkan error Trotter.
examples.suggested: ... jadi tidak ada salahnya kita memakai jumlah layer yang banyak (berlebih) untuk meminimalkan error Trotter.
examples.why: "we might as well" carries the teaching point that extra layers cost essentially nothing, so be lavish; "kita bisa" reduces it to bare permission, and "lebih banyak" is a comparative with no stated referent. Not misleading, but the emphasis is flattened.

examples.source: a generous number of layers / a generous number of Trotter steps
examples.translation: jumlah layer yang lebih banyak / jumlah langkah Trotter yang banyak
examples.suggested: pick one rendering for "generous", e.g. "jumlah ... yang banyak" (or "berlimpah") in all three places
examples.why: The same qualifier that ties the target circuit, the comparison circuit and the fidelity argument together is rendered two ways within the file; the concept stays identifiable, so this is minor, but consistency would make the comparison thread easier to follow.

examples.source: Because this is being run on quantum hardware, it is desirable to use as few Trotter layers as possible.
examples.translation: Karena ini akan dijalankan pada hardware kuantum, disarankan menggunakan sesedikit mungkin layer Trotter.
examples.suggested: ... sebaiknya kita menggunakan layer Trotter sesedikit mungkin.
examples.why: "it is desirable" is a statement of what you want; "disarankan" turns it into an impersonal recommendation, mildly strengthening it and dropping the first-person framing the rest of the page uses. Defensible but a shade off.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every prose paragraph tracks the English (the sampling-overhead $9^2$ / two CNOT cuts, the caveat that observable coefficients and phases are ignored during decomposition but "bisa diterapkan kembali saat rekonstruksi", the joint-quasiprobability sentence, and the local-mode note are all faithful), and the register is the correct informal "kita" throughout. Three editorial slips remain. (1) "circuit" is rendered two ways in the same sentence — "mengurangi jumlah qubit dalam sebuah sirkuit ... sirkuit empat qubit" in the intro and "Petakan hamiltonan ke sebuah sirkuit kuantum", versus the kept "Circuit" everywhere else ("Potong Circuit dan observable", "Buat Circuit yang akan dipotong", "Circuit berukuran penuh"); the concept stays identifiable, but a native editor would pick one. (2) "hamiltonian" is spelled "hamiltonan" (lowercase, non-standard); Indonesian physics writing uses "Hamiltonian". (3) "fake backend" → "Backend palsu" reads as "counterfeit" rather than "simulated/tiruan"; recognizable but not the phrasing an Indonesian quantum engineer would write.

examples.source: reduce the number of qubits in a circuit … Map the hamiltonian onto a quantum circuit. … Cut the circuit and observable.
examples.translation: mengurangi jumlah qubit dalam sebuah sirkuit … Petakan hamiltonan ke sebuah sirkuit kuantum. … Potong Circuit dan observable.
examples.suggested: Use one convention for "circuit" throughout (either "sirkuit" everywhere in prose, or the kept "Circuit" everywhere).
examples.why: Within-file inconsistency: the same term appears as "sirkuit" in the intro/Step-1 prose and as "Circuit" in the step list, headings and the Step-2 paragraph. Not misleading, but a native editor would normalize it.

examples.source: Map the hamiltonian onto a quantum circuit.
examples.translation: Petakan hamiltonan ke sebuah sirkuit kuantum.
examples.suggested: Petakan Hamiltonian ke sebuah sirkuit kuantum.
examples.why: "hamiltonan" is a non-standard spelling of the eponym; Indonesian technical writing uses "Hamiltonian" (capitalized, named after Hamilton). Recognizable, so MINOR, but it reads as a typo to a physicist.

examples.source: Here we are using a fake backend, which will result in Qiskit Runtime running in local mode (i.e., on a local simulator).
examples.translation: Di sini kita menggunakan Backend palsu, yang akan membuat Qiskit Runtime berjalan dalam mode lokal (yaitu, pada simulator lokal).
examples.suggested: Di sini kita menggunakan fake backend (backend tiruan), yang akan membuat Qiskit Runtime berjalan dalam mode lokal …
examples.why: "palsu" carries the sense of counterfeit/bogus; the technical meaning here is a stand-in model of real hardware, better served by "tiruan" or by keeping the API term "fake backend" (which matches the class name FakeManilaV2 in the code below).

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the layout/two-swaps setup, the $9^3$ sampling overhead, the "depth reduced by more than half" claim, and the Note about observable coefficients/phases being ignored during decomposition and re-applied during reconstruction all match the English, and core terms are correct and consistent (nilai ekspektasi, subeksperimen, distribusi kuasiprobabilitas, suku observable, primitif Sampler; informal "Kamu" register holds). Three editorial slips remain, none misleading. (1) In the opening sentence "swap gate yang biasanya diperkenalkan oleh proses routing": "diperkenalkan" is a literal calque of "introduced" — in Indonesian it means introducing a person or concept, not inserting gates; a native writer would say "ditambahkan"/"disisipkan oleh proses routing". (2) The same sentence renders "would otherwise be introduced" as "biasanya" (usually), dropping the counterfactual "otherwise" that ties the swaps to the not-cutting case. (3) "an arbitrarily chosen subexperiment" becomes "dipilih secara acak" (chosen at random) — the code picks a fixed index 100, so "sembarang"/"dipilih sembarang" is the accurate sense.

examples.source: avoiding the swap gates that would otherwise be introduced by routing
examples.translation: sehingga menghindari swap gate yang biasanya diperkenalkan oleh proses routing
examples.suggested: sehingga menghindari swap gate yang jika tidak demikian akan disisipkan oleh proses routing
examples.why: "diperkenalkan" is a calque of "introduced"; in Indonesian it means introducing a person/concept, not inserting gates into a circuit. A native technical writer uses "disisipkan"/"ditambahkan".

examples.source: the swap gates that would otherwise be introduced by routing
examples.translation: swap gate yang biasanya diperkenalkan oleh proses routing
examples.suggested: swap gate yang seharusnya disisipkan oleh routing jika Gate tersebut tidak dipotong
examples.why: "otherwise" is counterfactual (if we did not cut), but "biasanya" (usually) turns it into a general habit and loses the causal link to cutting. Not misleading, but a dropped nuance.

examples.source: Here is an example of an arbitrarily chosen subexperiment generated from the QPD circuit.
examples.translation: Berikut adalah contoh salah satu subeksperimen yang dipilih secara acak dari Circuit QPD.
examples.suggested: Berikut adalah contoh subeksperimen sembarang yang dihasilkan dari Circuit QPD.
examples.why: "secara acak" says randomly selected, but the code deterministically takes subexperiments[100]; "arbitrarily" means "any one will do", best rendered "sembarang".
